targets.label: Theorem 6
targets.statement:
Theorem 6 Suppose that $\| \pmb{w}_{t}- \pmb{w}^{\star}\| \leq D$ holds at every iteration, and that G is an upper bound on the norms of the subgradient sets $\partial f_{t}$ and $\partial r$. Fix an arbitrary scalar $c > 0$. Then FoBoS run with step sizes $\eta_{t}= c / \sqrt{t}$ has a regret bound of the form

$$
R_{f+r}(T)\leq 2GD+\left({\frac{D^{2}}{2c}}+7G^{2}c\right)\sqrt{T}.
$$

targets.label: Theorem 8
targets.statement:
Theorem 8 As in Theorem 6, suppose that $\| \pmb{w}_{t}- \pmb{w}^{\star}\| \leq D$ and that G bounds $\partial f_{t}$ and $\partial r$ from above. In addition, suppose that for every t the function $f_{t}+ r$ is H-strongly convex on the region $\| \pmb{w}- \pmb{w}^{\star}\| \leq D$. Then, with the step sizes $\eta_{t}=1/(Ht)$, FoBoS has regret

$$
R_{f+r}(T)\leq 2GD+HD^{2}+\frac{7G^{2}}{2H}(1+\log T).
$$

targets.label: Proposition 11
targets.statement:
Proposition 11 For $t=1,\ldots,T$, solve one after another the T self-similar optimization problems

$$
\mathcal{P}.1:~{\pmb w}_{t}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{{\pmb w}}\frac{1}{2}\|{\pmb w}-{\pmb w}_{t-1}\|^{2}+\lambda_{t}\|{\pmb w}\|_{q}\enspace .\tag{28}
$$

and let $\pmb{w}_{T}$ be the vector obtained at the end. Denote by $\pmb{w}^{\star}$ the optimal solution of the problem

$$
\mathcal{P}. 2:\pmb{w}^{\star}=\underset{\pmb{w}}{\mathrm{argmin}}\frac{1}{2}\|\pmb{w}-\pmb{w}_{0}\|^{2}+\left(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\lambda_{t}\right)\|\pmb{w}\|_{q}.
$$

Then, for $q\in\{1,2,\infty\}$, the two vectors $\pmb{w}_{T}$ and $\pmb{w}^{\star}$ coincide.

nl_proof:
### Proof of Theorem 6

Proof of Theorem 6 When $\| \partial f \|$ and $\| \partial r \|$ are bounded by G, Lemma 1 gives at once

$$
f_{t}(\boldsymbol{w}_{t})-f_{t}(\boldsymbol{w}^{\star})+r(\boldsymbol{w}_{t+1})-r(\boldsymbol{w}^{\star})\leq\frac{1}{2\eta_{t}}\left(\|\boldsymbol{w}_{t}-\boldsymbol{w}^{\star}\|^{2}-\|\boldsymbol{w}_{t+1}-\boldsymbol{w}^{\star}\|^{2}\right)+\frac{7}{2}G^{2}\eta_{t}.\tag{36}
$$

Applying Eq. (36), we find

$$
\begin{array}{r c l}{R_{f+r}(T)}&{=}&{\displaystyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left(f_{t}(w_{t})-f_{t}(w^{\star})+r(w_{t})-r(w^{\star})\right)+r(w_{T+1})-r(w^{\star})-r(w_{1})+r(w^{\star})}\\ &{\le}&{\displaystyle GD+\displaystyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\frac{1}{2\eta_{t}}\left(\|w_{t}-w^{\star}\|^{2}-\|w_{t+1}-w^{\star}\|^{2}\right)+\displaystyle\frac{7G^{2}}{2}\displaystyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\eta_{t}}\end{array}
$$

because $r(\pmb{w})\leq r(\mathbf{0})+G\|\pmb{w}\|\leq GD$. Rearranging this bound gives

$$
\begin{array}{r c l}{{R_{f+r}(T)}}&{{\le}}&{{\displaystyle GD+\frac{1}{2\eta_{1}}\|w_{1}-w^{\star}\|^{2}+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{t=2}^{T}\|w_{t}-w^{\star}\|^{2}\left(\frac{1}{\eta_{t}}-\frac{1}{\eta_{t-1}}\right)+\frac{7G^{2}}{2}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\eta_{t}}}\\ {{}}&{{\le}}&{{\displaystyle GD+\frac{D^{2}}{2\eta_{1}}+\frac{D^{2}}{2}\sum_{t=2}^{T}\left(\frac{1}{\eta_{t}}-\frac{1}{\eta_{t-1}}\right)+\frac{7G^{2}}{2}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\eta_{t}~,}}\end{array}
$$

where the final inequality once more uses the bound on the distance from each ${\pmb w}_{t}$ to $\pmb{w}^{\star}$. Finally, the sum $\frac{1}{\eta_{1}}+\sum_{t=2}^{T}\big(\frac{1}{\eta_{t}}-\frac{1}{\eta_{t-1}}\big)$ telescopes, which yields

$$
R_{f+r}(T)\leq GD+{\frac{D^{2}}{2\eta_{T}}}+{\frac{7G^{2}}{2}}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\eta_{t}.
$$

The proof is finished by taking $\eta_{t}= c / \sqrt{t}$ and noting that $\sum_{t = 1}^{T}\eta_{t}\leq 2 c \sqrt{T}$.

### Proof of Theorem 8

Proof of Theorem 8 The argument is a direct extension of Theorem 1 of Hazan et al. (2006) together with our proof of Theorem 6. Adding up Eq. (17) over $t = 1$ to T, we get

$$
\begin{array}{r c l}{{R_{f+r}(T)}}&{{\le}}&{{\displaystyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left(\left\langle g_{t}^{f}+g_{t}^{r},w_{t}-w^{\star}\right\rangle-\displaystyle\frac{H}{2}\|w_{t}-w^{\star}\|^{2}\right)}}\\ {{}}&{{\le}}&{{\displaystyle 2GD+\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\left(\displaystyle\frac{1}{\eta_{t}}\|w_{t}-w^{\star}\|^{2}-\displaystyle\frac{1}{\eta_{t}}\|w_{t+1}-w^{\star}\|^{2}-H\|w_{t}-w^{\star}\|^{2}\right)+\displaystyle\frac{7G^{2}}{2}\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\displaystyle\eta_{t}}}\\ {{}}&{{\le}}&{{\displaystyle 2GD+\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\sum_{t=2}^{T-1}\|w_{t}-w^{\star}\|^{2}\left(\displaystyle\frac{1}{\eta_{t}}-\displaystyle\frac{1}{\eta_{t-1}}-H\right)+\displaystyle\frac{1}{\eta_{1}}\|w_{1}-w^{\star}\|^{2}+\displaystyle\frac{7G^{2}}{2}\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\displaystyle\eta_{t}.}}\end{array}
$$

Eq. (36) gives the second inequality; the third comes from reordering the sum and discarding the negative term $\big(1/\eta_{T-1}\big)\big\|\pmb{w}_{T}-\pmb{w}^{\star}\big\|^{2}$. With the choice $\eta_{t}= \frac{1}{H t}$ we have $1/\eta_{t}-1/\eta_{t-1}-H=Ht-H(t-1)-H=0$, and therefore the regret is at most

$$
R_{f+r}(T)\leq 2GD+HD^{2}+{\frac{7G^{2}}{2}}\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}{\frac{1}{Ht}}\leq 2GD+HD^{2}+{\frac{7G^{2}}{2H}}(1+\log T)=O\left({\frac{G^{2}}{H}}\log T\right)~.
$$

### Proof of Proposition 11

Proof Since the claim is trivially true for $T = 1$, it is enough to establish it for $T = 2$ and then argue by induction. For each norm we give a separate, direct proof, examining the updates derived in Sec. 5 and verifying that $\pmb{w}_{2}= \pmb{w}^{\star}$.

For $q = 1$ the objectives are separable. Hence, for $\ell_{1}$-regularization, proving the proposition for an arbitrary single component of the vector w suffices. Dropping the component index, we write $w_{0}, w_{1}, w_{2}, w_{3}, \ldots$ for one coordinate of w across the iterations of P.1, and $w^{\star}$ for the same coordinate of the solution of P.2. What must be shown is $w^{\star}= w_{2}$. Unrolling the $\ell_{1}$-update of Eq. (19) for two iterations gives

$$
w_{2}=\mathrm{sign}(w_{1})\left[\left|w_{1}\right| -\lambda_{2}\right]_{+}=\mathrm{sign}(w_{1})\left[\left|\mathrm{sign}(w_{0})\left[\left|w_{0}\right| -\lambda_{1}\right]_{+}\right| -\lambda_{2}\right]_{+}=\mathrm{sign}(w_{0})\left[\left|w_{0}\right| -\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}\right]_{+}\ ,
$$

where the positivity of | · | was used. Turning to P.2 and applying Eq. (19) once more,

$$
w^{\star}=\mathrm{sign}(w_{0})\left[|w_{0}| -\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}\right]_{+}~.
$$

Consequently $w^{\star}= w_{2}$, as asserted.

We next prove the proposition for $\ell_{2}$, now working with the whole vector rather than a single coordinate, by means of the explicit $\ell_{2}$-update from Eq. (20); the norm of the vector ${\pmb w}_{1}$ produced by program P.1 then expands as

$$
\| \pmb{w}_{1}\| = \bigg [ 1 - \frac{\lambda_{1}}{\| \pmb{w}_{0}\|}\bigg ]_{+}\| \pmb{w}_{0}\| = \big [ \| \pmb{w}_{0}\| - \lambda_{1}\big ]_{+}.
$$

In the same way, $\| \pmb{w}_{2}\| = [ \| \pmb{w}_{1}\| - \lambda_{2}]_{+}$. Putting the two norm identities together, the norm of $\pmb{w}_{2}$ obtained from the two successive updates is

$$
\left\| w_{2}\right\| = \left[ \left[ \left\| w_{0}\right\| - \lambda_{1}\right]_{+}- \lambda_{2}\right]_{+}= \left[ \left\| w_{0}\right\| - \lambda_{1}- \lambda_{2}\right]_{+}.
$$

On the other hand, computing the norm of $\pmb{w}^{\star}$ directly from the update given by Eq. (20) gives

$$
\| \pmb{w}^{\star}\| = \biggl [ 1 - \frac{\lambda_{1}+ \lambda_{2}}{\| \pmb{w}_{0}\|}\biggr ]_{+}\| \pmb{w}_{0}\| = [ \| \pmb{w}_{0}\| - \lambda_{1}- \lambda_{2}]_{+}.
$$

Hence $\pmb{w}^{\star}$ and ${\pmb w}_{2}$ have equal norms. As the update keeps the direction of the original vector $\pmb{w}_{0}$, we get that ${\pmb w}^{\star}={\pmb w}_{2}$, which is what we needed.

We come now to the $\ell_{\infty}$ norm, whose update and proof are the most involved of the three norms. First we restate the programs P.1 and $\mathcal{P}. 2$ for $T = 2$ and $q = \infty$:

$$
\mathcal{P}.1:\quad\pmb{w}_{1}\ =\ \operatorname*{argmin}_{\pmb{w}}\left\{\frac{1}{2}\|\pmb{w}-\pmb{w}_{0}\|^{2}+\lambda_{1}\|\pmb{w}\|_{\infty}\right\}\tag{29}
$$

$$
\begin{array}{r c l}{{\pmb w}_{2}}&{{=}}&{{\displaystyle\operatorname*{argmin}_{\pmb{w}}\left\{\frac{1}{2}\|{\pmb w}-{\pmb w}_{1}\|^{2}+\lambda_{2}\|{\pmb w}\|_{\infty}\right\}\ \ ,}}\end{array}\tag{30}
$$

$$
\mathcal{P}.2:\quad\pmb{w}^{\star}\ =\ \operatorname*{argmin}_{\pmb{w}}\left\{\frac{1}{2}\|\pmb{w}-\pmb{v}\|_{2}^{2}+\left(\lambda_{1}+\lambda_{2}\right)\|\pmb{w}\|_{\infty}\right\}\ .\tag{31}
$$

The equivalence of the two programs is established in two stages: we treat first the case $\| \pmb{w}_{0}\|_{1}> \lambda_{1}+ \lambda_{2}$, and afterwards the complementary case $\| \pmb{w}_{0}\|_{1}\le \lambda_{1}+ \lambda_{2}$. To keep things concrete and simple we take ${\pmb w}_{0}\succeq{\bf 0}$; this is clearly allowed because the objective is symmetric under replacing $\pmb{w}_{0}$ by $-{\pmb w}_{0}$. So every entry of $\pmb{w}_{0}$ may be assumed non-negative. The proof uses the following operators: $[{\pmb v}]_{+}$ now stands for the entrywise positive part of $v$; $\min\{v,\theta\}$ is the entrywise minimum of the elements of v and $\theta$; and similarly $\max\{v,\theta\}$ is the entrywise maximum. We begin with the case $\left\| \pmb{w}_{0}\right\|_{1}> \lambda_{1}+ \lambda_{2}$ and look at Eq. (29). Lagrange duality tells us that ${\pmb w}_{1}={\pmb w}_{0}-{\pmb \alpha}_{1}$, with $\pmb{\alpha}_{1}$ the solution of

$$
\operatorname*{minimize}_{\alpha}\frac{1}{2}\|\alpha-\pmb{w}_{0}\|_{2}^{2}\ \mathrm{s . t .}\ \|\pmb{\alpha}\|_{1}\leq\lambda_{1}.
$$

Following Duchi et al. (2008), as already reviewed in Sec. 5, $\pmb{\alpha}_{1}= [ \pmb{w}_{0}- \pmb{\theta}_{1}]_{+}$ for some $\theta_{1}\in \mathbb{R}_{+}$. This form of $\pmb{\alpha}_{1}$ translates directly into the form $\pmb{w}_{1}= \pmb{w}_{0}- \pmb{\alpha}_{1}= \min\{ \pmb{w}_{0}, \theta_{1}\}$ for $\pmb{w}_{1}$. The same reasoning applied to the second step of P.1 gives $\pmb{w}_{2}= \pmb{w}_{1}- \pmb{\alpha}_{2}= \pmb{w}_{0}- \pmb{\alpha}_{1}- \pmb{\alpha}_{2}$, with $\pmb{\alpha}_{2}$ the minimizer of

$$
\frac{1}{2}\left\|\alpha-\pmb{w}_{1}\right\|_{2}^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\left\|\alpha-\left(\pmb{w}_{0}-\pmb{\alpha}_{1}\right)\right\|_{2}^{2}\mathrm{s.t.}\left\|\pmb{\alpha}\right\|_{1}\leq\lambda_{2}\mathrm{.}
$$

Once again $\pmb{\alpha}_{2}= [ \pmb{w}_{1}- \pmb{\theta}_{2}]_{+}= [ \pmb{w}_{0}- \pmb{\alpha}_{1}- \pmb{\theta}_{2}]_{+}$ for some $\theta_{2}\in \mathbb{R}_{+}$. Combining the two successive steps,

$$
{\pmb w}_{2}=\operatorname*{min}\{{\pmb w}_{1},{\theta}_{2}\}=\operatorname*{min}\left\{\operatorname*{min}\{{\pmb w}_{0},{\theta}_{1}\},{\theta}_{2}\right\}\mathrm{~.~}
$$

Our next claim is that $\theta_{2}\leq \theta_{1}$, whatever the 1-norm of $w_{0}$. The intuition is that if $\theta_{2}> \theta_{1}$, the second minimization step of P.1 would apply no shrinkage to $\pmb{w}_{1}$ in producing $\pmb{w}_{2}$. To make this rigorous, suppose toward a contradiction that $\theta_{2}> \theta_{1}$. Then ${\pmb w}_{2}=\mathrm{min}\{\mathrm{min}\{{\pmb w}_{0},{\pmb\theta}_{1}\},{\pmb\theta}_{2}\}=\mathrm{min}\{{\pmb w}_{0},{\pmb\theta}_{1}\}={\pmb w}_{1}$. It follows that the subgradient set of Eq. (30) at ${\pmb w}={\pmb w}_{1}$ contains 0, that is,

$$
\mathbf{0}\in{\pmb w}_{1}-{\pmb w}_{1}+ \lambda_{2}\partial \left\|{\pmb w}_{1}\right\|_{\infty}= \lambda_{2}\partial \left\|{\pmb w}_{1}\right\|_{\infty}.
$$

But the set $\partial \| \pmb{w}_{1}\|_{\infty}$ obviously contains 0 only if ${\pmb w}_{1}={\bf 0}$. Because we assumed $\lambda_{1}< \| w_{0}\|_{1}$, so that $\pmb{\alpha}_{1}\preceq{w_{0}}$ and $\pmb{\alpha}_{1}\neq \pmb{w}_{0}$, it follows that $\pmb{w}_{1}= \pmb{w}_{0}- \pmb{\alpha}_{1}\neq \pmb{0}$. This contradiction shows $\theta_{2}\leq \theta_{1}$.

Consider now $\pmb{\alpha}_{1}$ and $\pmb{\alpha}_{2}$, the solution vectors of the dual problems of $\mathcal{P}. 1$. Since $\| \pmb{\alpha}_{1}\|_{1}= \lambda_{1}$, we have $\left\| \pmb{w}_{0}- \pmb{\alpha}_{1}\right\|_{1}> \lambda_{2}$, and so $\pmb{\alpha}_{2}$ lies on the boundary, $\| \pmb{\alpha}_{2}\|_{1}= \lambda_{2}$ (again see Duchi et al. 2008). In addition, these vectors add up to

$$
\alpha_{1}+ \alpha_{2}= \left[{\pmb w}_{0}-{\pmb \theta}_{1}\right]_{+}+ \left[{\pmb w}_{0}- \left[{\pmb w}_{0}-{\pmb \theta}_{1}\right]_{+}-{\pmb \theta}_{2}\right]_{+}.\tag{32}
$$

Let $v$ be any component of $\pmb{w}_{0}$ exceeding $\theta_{1}$. For such a component, the right-hand side of Eq. (32) equals

$$
\left[v-(v-\theta_{1})-\theta_{2}\right]_{+}+\left[v-\theta_{1}\right]_{+}=\left[\theta_{1}-\theta_{2}\right]_{+}+v-\theta_{1}=v-\theta_{1}=\left[v-\theta_{1}\right]_{+}\ ,
$$

where the term $\left[ \theta_{1}- \theta_{2}\right]_{+}$ was removed using $\theta_{2}\leq \theta_{1}$. Now let u be a component of $\pmb{w}_{0}$ below $\theta_{1}$. For such a component the right-hand side of Eq. (32) equals $[ u - 0 - \theta_{2}]_{+}+ 0 = [ u - \theta_{2}]_{+}$. To summarize, the vector sum $\pmb{\alpha}_{1}+ \pmb{\alpha}_{2}$ is equal to $[{\pmb w}_{0}-{\theta}_{2}]_{+}$. Furthermore, $\pmb{\alpha}_{1}$ and $\pmb{\alpha}_{2}$ lie in $\mathbb{R}^{n}_{+}$ since we assumed ${\pmb w}_{0}\succeq{\bf 0}$, and hence

$$
\| \left[{\pmb w}_{0}-{\pmb \theta}_{2}\right]_{+}\|_{1}= \|{\pmb \alpha}_{1}+{\pmb \alpha}_{2}\|_{1}= \lambda_{1}+ \lambda_{2}\enspace .\tag{33}
$$

We next verify that P.2 has the same dual solution as the sequential updates just analyzed. The dual of P.2 reads

$$
\operatorname*{minimize}_{\alpha}\frac{1}{2}\left\|\alpha-\pmb{w}_{0}\right\|_{2}^{2}\mathrm{s . t .}\left\|\pmb{\alpha}\right\|_{1}\leq\lambda_{1}+\lambda_{2}.
$$

Writing $\pmb{\alpha}_{0}$ for the solution of this dual problem, we have $\pmb{w}^{\star}= \pmb{w}_{0}- \pmb{\alpha}_{0}$ and $\pmb{\alpha}_{0}= [ \pmb{w}_{0}- \pmb{\theta}]_{+}$ for some $\theta \in \mathbb{R}_{+}$. Its norm satisfies

$$
\| \pmb{\alpha}_{0}\|_{1}= \big \| [ \pmb{w}_{0}- \pmb{\theta}]_{+}\big \|_{1}= \lambda_{1}+ \lambda_{2}\tag{34}
$$

as a consequence of the assumption $\| \pmb{w}_{0}\|_{1}> \lambda_{1}+ \lambda_{2}$. Regard $\left\| \left[{\pmb w}_{0}-{\pmb \theta}_{2}\right]_{+}\right\|_{1}$ in Eq. (33) as a function of $\theta_{2}$, and $\left\| \left[ \pmb{w}_{0}- \pmb{\theta}\right]_{+}\right\|_{1}$ in Eq. (34) as a function of θ. On the interval $[0,\|\pmb{w}_{0}\|_{\infty}]$ both are strictly decreasing functions of θ and $\theta_{2}$, so they are invertible for $0 < \lambda_{1}+ \lambda_{2}< \| \pmb{w}_{0}\|_{1}$. As $\left\| [ \pmb{w}_{0}- \pmb{\theta}]_{+}\right\|_{1}= \left\| [ \pmb{w}_{0}- \pmb{\theta}_{2}]_{+}\right\|_{1}$, necessarily $\theta_{2}= \theta$. Recall that Eq. (31) is solved by $w^{\star}= \min\{w_{0}, \theta \}$, whereas the sequential update defined by Eq. (29) and Eq. (30) produces $\min\{ \min\{w_{0}, \theta_{1}\}, \theta_{2}\}= \min\{w_{0}, \theta_{2}\}$. Thus P.1 and P.2 lead to the same vector $\min\{w_{0}, \theta_{2}\}= \min\{w_{0}, \theta \}$, and the updates they induce are equivalent.

It remains to handle the case $\lVert \boldsymbol{w}_{0}\rVert_{1}\leq \lambda_{1}+ \lambda_{2}$. If moreover the 1-norm of $\pmb{w}_{0}$ is below $\lambda_{1}$, i.e. $\| \pmb{w}_{0}\|_{1}\le \lambda_{1}$, then the dual solution of the first step of P.1 is $\pmb{\alpha}_{1}= \pmb{w}_{0}$, so $\pmb{w}_{1}= \pmb{w}_{0}- \pmb{\alpha}_{1}= \pmb{0}$ and consequently ${\pmb w}_{2}={\bf 0}$. For the combined problem the dual solution is clearly $\pmb{\alpha}_{0}= \pmb{w}_{0}$, and once more $\pmb{w}^{\star}= \pmb{w}_{0}- \pmb{\alpha}_{0}= \pmb{0}$. What is left is the case $\lambda_{1}< \| \pmb{w}_{0}\|_{1}\leq \lambda_{1}+ \lambda_{2}$. Here it is immediate that Eq. (31) is solved by $\boldsymbol{w}^{\star}= \mathbf{0}$. We show that the iterated solution produced by P.1 is also the zero vector. Start with the dual solution $\pmb{\alpha}_{1}$, which minimizes $\| \pmb{\alpha}- \pmb{w}_{0}\|^{2}$ under the constraint $\| \alpha \|_{1}\leq \lambda_{1}$. As $\pmb{\alpha}_{1}= [ \pmb{w}_{0}- \pmb{\theta}_{1}]_{+}$ for some $\theta_{1}\geq 0$, each entry of $\pmb{\alpha}_{1}$ lies between zero and the matching entry of $\pmb{w}_{0}$; hence $\| \pmb{w}_{0}- \pmb{\alpha}_{1}\|_{1}= \| \pmb{w}_{0}\|_{1}- \| \pmb{\alpha}\|_{1}= \| \pmb{w}_{0}\|_{1}- \lambda_{1}\leq \lambda_{2}$. The dual of the second step of P.1 reduces to minimizing $\frac{1}{2}\|\pmb{\alpha}-\big(\pmb{w}_{0}-\pmb{\alpha}_{1}\big)\|^{2}$ under the constraint $\left\| \alpha \right\|_{1}\leq \lambda_{2}$. Having shown $\left\| \pmb{w}_{0}- \pmb{\alpha}\right\|_{1}\le \lambda_{2}$, we obtain $\alpha_{2}={\pmb w}_{0}-{\pmb \alpha}_{1}$, which means $\theta_{2}= 0$. Recalling that the solution of $\mathcal{P}. 1$ is $\min\{w_{0}, \theta_{2}\}$, this equals the zero vector when $\theta_{2}= 0$. Both optimization problems therefore produce the zero vector, which establishes the equivalence of P.1 and P.2 for $q = \infty$.

context.name: Setup and notation: objective f + r, convex and nonnegative (Section 1)
context.statement:
We first fix the notation used throughout the paper. Scalars are written as lower case letters and vectors as bold lower case letters, e.g. w. For two vectors u and v, $\langle{\pmb u},{\pmb v}\rangle$ is their inner product. The p-norm of a vector x is written $\| \pmb{x}\|_{p}$, and ||x|| abbreviates $\| \pmb{x}\|_{2}$.

The paper studies an algorithmic framework for regularized convex programming whose aim is to minimize a sum of two functions,

$$
f({\pmb w})+r({\pmb w}),\tag{1}
$$

in which f and r are both convex and bounded below (so that, with no loss of generality, they are taken to map into $\mathbb{R}_{+}$). Typically f is an empirical loss of the form $\textstyle\sum_{i\in S}\ell_{i}(w)$ built from loss functions $\ell_{i}: \mathbb{R}^{n}\to \mathbb{R}_{+}$, and $r(w)$ is a regularizer that penalizes overly complex vectors, e.g. $r(\mathbf{w})=\lambda\|\mathbf{w}\|_{p}$. Such tasks are common in machine learning, where learning problems for decision and prediction are formulated as convex optimization problems. With this in mind, we study a general and intuitive algorithm called forward-backward splitting for minimizing Eq. (1), with particular emphasis on derivations for, and the use of, regularization functions that are not differentiable.

context.name: Definition: subgradient set
context.statement:
For a function f and a point w, write $\partial f ({\boldsymbol{w}})$ for the subgradient set of f at w, that is,

$$
\partial f(w)=\{g\mid\forall v:f(v)\geq f(w)+\langle g,v-w\rangle\}.
$$

context.name: Algorithm: FoBoS update and forward-looking subgradient, Eqs. (2)-(5) (Section 2)
context.statement:
Our version of Forward-Backward Splitting is driven by the wish that the iterates ${\pmb w}_{t}$ be able to reach points where r is not differentiable. For problems such as $\ell_{1}$-regularization, the method sidesteps the difficulties caused by non-differentiability by alternating subgradient steps with analytical minimization steps. Informally, FoBoS resembles the projected subgradient method, except that the projection step is replaced or augmented by an instantaneous minimization problem whose solution can be derived in closed form. The method is compact: every iteration is made of the two steps below,

$$
\begin{array}{r l r}{{\bf w}_{t + \frac{1}{2}}}&{{}=}&{{\bf w}_{t}- \boldsymbol \eta_{t}{\bf g}_{t}^{f},}\end{array}\tag{2}
$$

$$
\begin{array}{r c l}{{\pmb w}_{t+1}}&{=}&{\displaystyle\operatorname*{argmin}_{{\pmb w}}\left\{\frac{1}{2}\left\|{\pmb w}-{\pmb w}_{t+\frac{1}{2}}\right\|^{2}+\eta_{t+\frac{1}{2}}r({\pmb w})\right\}\ .}\end{array}\tag{3}
$$

Here $g_{t}^{f}$ is an element of $\partial f ({\pmb w}_{t})$, and $\eta_{t}$ denotes the step size used by the algorithm at time step t. What value $\eta_{t}$ takes depends on the particular setting and analysis. The first step is thus nothing more than an unconstrained subgradient step for the function $f$. The second step produces a new vector that balances two aims: (i) remaining near the interim vector $w_{t + \frac{1}{2}}$, and (ii) having small complexity as measured by r. Observe that r is multiplied by an interim step size, written $\eta_{t + \frac{1}{2}}$. The analyses later in the paper fix the particular value of $\eta_{t + \frac{1}{2}}$, which is either $\eta_{t}$ or $\eta_{t + 1}$.

An important property of the solution of Eq. (3), which also explains the name FoBoS, is the necessary optimality condition: at the optimum ${\pmb w}_{t + 1}$, the subgradient set of the objective must contain the zero vector, i.e.

$$
\mathbf{0}\in\partial\left\{\frac{1}{2}\left\|w-w_{t+\frac{1}{2}}\right\|^{2}+\eta_{t+\frac{1}{2}}r(w)\right\}\bigg|_{w=w_{t+1}}.
$$

As $\pmb{w}_{t + \frac{1}{2}}= \pmb{w}_{t}- \eta_{t}\pmb{g}_{t}^{f}$, this condition reads

$$
\mathbf{0}\in\pmb{w}_{t+1}-\pmb{w}_{t}+\eta_{t}\pmb{g}_{t}^{f}+\eta_{t+\frac{1}{2}}\partial r(\pmb{w}_{t+1}).\tag{4}
$$

From $\mathbf{0}\in\pmb{w}_{t+1}-\pmb{w}_{t}+\eta_{t}\pmb{g}_{t}^{f}+\eta_{t+\frac{1}{2}}\partial r(\pmb{w}_{t+1})$ it follows that, as long as ${\pmb w}_{t + 1}$ is taken to be the minimizer of Eq. (3), there is guaranteed to be a vector $\pmb{g}_{t+1}^{r}\in\partial r(\pmb{w}_{t+1})$ with

$$
{\bf 0}={\pmb w}_{t + 1}-{\pmb w}_{t}+ \eta_{t}{\pmb g}_{t}^{f}+ \eta_{t + \frac{1}{2}}{\pmb g}_{t + 1}^{r}\mathrm{~ . ~}
$$

This identity may be read as an update rule in which the new weight vector ${\pmb w}_{t + 1}$ is a linear combination of three vectors: the previous weight vector ${\pmb w}_{t}$, an element of the subgradient set of $f$ at ${\pmb w}_{t}$, and an element of the subgradient of r at the not-yet-known ${\pmb w}_{t + 1}$; this is the origin of the name Forward-Looking Subgradient. In summary, ${\pmb w}_{t + 1}$ can be written as

$$
\pmb{w}_{t + 1}= \pmb{w}_{t}- \eta_{t}\pmb{g}_{t}^{f}- \eta_{t + \frac{1}{2}}\pmb{g}_{t + 1}^{r},\tag{5}
$$

with ${\pmb g}_{t}^{f}\in \partial f ({\pmb w}_{t})$ and $\pmb{g}_{t+1}^{r}\in\partial r(\pmb{w}_{t+1})$. Solving Eq. (3) with r as above brings two main advantages. First, algorithmically, it produces sparse solutions at almost no extra computational cost. Second, thanks to the forward-looking gradient we can reuse existing analyses and prove that the resulting framework inherits the formal convergence guarantees of many existing gradient-based and online convex programming algorithms.

context.name: Setup: choice of the interim step size eta_{t+1/2} (Section 3)
context.statement: At first sight FoBoS appears quite different from subgradient and online convex programming methods. Yet because FoBoS in fact uses a forward-looking subgradient of the regularizer, existing analyses carry over well. In this section we adapt known results, exploiting the forward-looking property of FoBoS, to obtain convergence rate analyses for FoBoS. This requires choosing $\eta_{t + \frac{1}{2}}$ appropriately. As shown below, to get convergence and low regret bounds it suffices to take $\eta_{t + \frac{1}{2}}$ equal to $\eta_{t}$ or to $\eta_{t + 1}$, according to whether the optimization is online or batch. We first analyze FoBoS in the batch setting. There we use the subgradient of $f$, put $\eta_{t + \frac{1}{2}}= \eta_{t + 1}$, and move from ${\pmb w}_{t}$ to ${\pmb w}_{t + 1}$ as specified by Eq. (2) and Eq. (3).

context.name: Assumption: bounded subgradients, Eq. (6)
context.statement:
In this section $w^{\star}$ always denotes the minimizer of $f ({\pmb w}) + r ({\pmb w})$. Below we set $\begin{array}{r}{\|\partial f(\pmb{w})\|\triangleq\operatorname*{sup}_{\pmb{g}\in\partial f(\pmb{w})}\|\pmb{g}\|}\end{array}$. Our first convergence results are derived under the rather general assumption (see, for instance, Langford et al. 2008 or Shalev-Shwartz and Tewari 2009) that the subgradients obey the bounds

$$
\begin{array}{r}{\|\partial f(\pmb{w})\|^{2}\leq Af(\pmb{w})+G^{2},\quad\|\partial r(\pmb{w})\|^{2}\leq Ar(\pmb{w})+G^{2}.}\end{array}\tag{6}
$$

As examples, every Lipschitz loss (for instance the logistic loss, or the hinge loss of support vector machines) meets this condition with $A = 0$ and G the Lipschitz constant, while least squares estimation meets Eq. (6) with $G = 0$ and $A = 4$. The following lemma is technical, but it is the central tool behind every convergence result in this paper.

context.name: Lemma 1 (Bounding Step Differences)
context.statement:
Lemma 1 (Bounding Step Differences) Suppose the subgradient norms of f and r obey the bounds of Eq. (6):

$$
\|\partial f(\pmb{w})\|^{2}\leq Af(\pmb{w})+G^{2},\quad\|\partial r(\pmb{w})\|^{2}\leq Ar(\pmb{w})+G^{2}.
$$

Let $\eta_{t + 1}\leq \eta_{t + \frac{1}{2}}\leq \eta_{t}$, and assume $\eta_{t}\le 2 \eta_{t + \frac{1}{2}}$. Then, when the FoBoS update of Eqs. (2) and (3) is used, for a constant $c \leq 4$ and every vector $\pmb{w}^{\star}$,

$$
\begin{array}{r l r}{{2\boldsymbol\eta_{t}\big(1-cA\boldsymbol\eta_{t}\big)f\big(\boldsymbol{w}_{t}\big)+2\boldsymbol\eta_{t+\frac{1}{2}}\big(1-cA\boldsymbol\eta_{t+\frac{1}{2}}\big)\boldsymbol{r}\big(\boldsymbol{w}_{t+1}\big)}}\\ &{\leq}&{2\boldsymbol\eta_{t}f\big(\boldsymbol{w}^{\star}\big)+2\boldsymbol\eta_{t+\frac{1}{2}}\boldsymbol{r}\big(\boldsymbol{w}^{\star}\big)+\|\boldsymbol{w}_{t}-\boldsymbol{w}^{\star}\|^{2}-\|\boldsymbol{w}_{t+1}-\boldsymbol{w}^{\star}\|^{2}+7\boldsymbol\eta_{t}\boldsymbol\eta_{t+\frac{1}{2}}G^{2}\quad .}\end{array}
$$

context.name: Setup: online learning and regret R_{f+r}(T) (Section 4)
context.statement:
This section gives a regret analysis of FoBoS in online settings. An online learning problem supplies a sequence of functions $f_{t}: \mathbb{R}^{n}\longrightarrow \mathbb{R}$. The aim is that the predictions ${\pmb w}_{t}$ incur low regret relative to one fixed optimal predictor $w^{\star}$. Precisely, $f_{t}({\boldsymbol{w}})$ is the loss incurred on the $t^{t h}$ input loss function by the predictor w. For an online algorithm whose predictors are $\boldsymbol{w}_{1},\ldots,\boldsymbol{w}_{t},\ldots$, the regret with respect to a fixed predictor $\pmb{w}^{\star}$ under a regularization function r is

$$
R_{f+r}(T)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left[f_{t}(\pmb{w}_{t})+r(\pmb{w}_{t})-\left(f_{t}(\pmb{w}^{\star})+r(\pmb{w}^{\star})\right)\right].
$$

The ideal would be zero regret against a stationary $\pmb{w}^{\star}$ for sequences of any length.

To get an online bound for a sequence of convex functions $f_{t}$, we adapt the arguments of Zinkevich (2003). With the bound of Lemma 1 at hand, a theorem on the online regret of FoBoS can be stated and proved directly. The boundedness assumptions in the proof could be dropped (yielding a regret analogue of the bound in Theorem 2), but we do not consider this notably more interesting. Apart from its use of Lemma 1, the proof closely follows Zinkevich's, and so it is postponed to Appendix A.

context.name: Definition: H-strong convexity and Eq. (17)
context.statement:
FoBoS also admits an improved regret bound when the loss functions $f_{t}(\cdot)$ or the function $r(\cdot)$ are strongly convex. Hazan et al. (2006) showed that, for the projected gradient method with strongly convex functions, regret of order ${\cal O}(\log T)$ is attainable by exploiting the curvature of the functions $f_{t}$ instead of relying only on convexity and linearity as in Theorems 2 and 6. These results extend to FoBoS whenever $f_{t}({\pmb w}) + r ({\pmb w})$ is strongly convex, at least on the region $\| \pmb{w}- \pmb{w}^{\star}\| \leq D$. For the sake of completeness we restate some definitions and give the logarithmic regret bound for FoBoS. A function f is said to be H-strongly convex when

$$
f(\pmb{w})\geq f(\pmb{w}_{t})+\langle\nabla f(\pmb{w}_{t}),\pmb{w}-\pmb{w}_{t}\rangle+\frac{H}{2}\|\pmb{w}-\pmb{w}_{t}\|^{2}.
$$

Hence, when r and the functions $f_{t}$ are strongly convex with constants $H_{r}\geq 0$ and $H_{f}\geq 0$ respectively, we get $H = H_{f}+ H_{r}$, and H-strong convexity yields

$$
f_{t}({\boldsymbol{w}}_{t}) - f ({\boldsymbol{w}}^{\star}) + r ({\boldsymbol{w}}_{t}) - r ({\boldsymbol{w}}^{\star}) \leq \left\langle{\boldsymbol{g}}_{t}^{f}+{\boldsymbol{g}}_{t}^{r},{\boldsymbol{w}}_{t}-{\boldsymbol{w}}^{\star}\right\rangle - \frac{H}{2}\|{\boldsymbol{w}}_{t}-{\boldsymbol{w}}^{\star}\|^{2}~ .\tag{17}
$$

It is not necessary for both $f_{t}$ and r to be strongly convex; it is enough that at least one of the two has a positive strong convexity constant. For instance, with $\begin{array}{r}{r ({\bf w}) = \frac{\lambda}{2}\|{\bf w}\|^{2}}\end{array}$ we have $H \geq \lambda$ provided the functions $f_{t}$ are convex. Using Eq. (17), we can build directly on Hazan et al. (2006) to prove a stronger regret bound for the online learning case. Because the proof resembles that of Hazan et al., it too is deferred to Appendix A.

context.name: Setup: proximal step notation, Eq. (18) and [z]_+ (Section 5)
context.statement:
We begin by adjusting the notation. To make the derivations simpler, we write v for the vector $w_{t + \frac{1}{2}}= w_{t}- \eta_{t}g_{t}^{f}$ and write $\tilde{\lambda}$ for $\eta_{t + \frac{1}{2}}\cdot \lambda$. In this notation the problem of Eq. (3) becomes

$$
\operatorname*{minimize}_{\pmb{w}}\frac{1}{2}\|\pmb{w}-\pmb{v}\|^{2}+\widetilde{\lambda}r(\pmb{w}).\tag{18}
$$

We use $[ z ]_{+}$ for $\max\{0,z\}$. Although full derivations are given for every regularization function we consider, to save space we do not formally state well-known technical lemmas. Many of the results below were stated implicitly by Wright et al. (2009).

context.name: Update: l1 regularization (soft thresholding), Eq. (19) (Section 5.1)
context.statement:
Taking $r(\pmb{w})=\lambda\|\pmb{w}\|_{1}$ leads to a simple and intuitive update. To begin with, the objective decomposes, since Eq. (18) can be rewritten as

$$
\operatorname*{minimize}_{\boldsymbol{w}}\ \sum_{j=1}^{n}\left(\frac{1}{2}(w_{j}-v_{j})^{2}+\tilde{\lambda}|w_{j}|\right).
$$

Fix one coordinate of w and, to shorten notation, drop the index $j$. Let $w^{\star}$ be the minimizer of $\frac{1}{2}(w-v)^{2}+\tilde{\lambda}|w|$. Plainly $w^{\star}\cdot v \geq 0$. Otherwise $w^{\star}\cdot v < 0$, but then ${\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{2}}}v^{2}<$ $\begin{array}{r}{\frac{1}{2}v^{2}-w^{\star}\cdot v+\frac{1}{2}(w^{\star})^{2}<\frac{1}{2}(v-w^{\star})^{2}+\tilde{\lambda}|w^{\star}|}\end{array}$, which contradicts the assumed optimality of $w^{\star}$. Since the objective is symmetric in v, we may also take $v \geq 0$; it then remains to minimize $\frac{1}{2}\left(w-v\right)^{2}+\tilde{\lambda}w$ subject to $w \ge 0$. Attaching a Lagrange multiplier $\beta \geq 0$ to this constraint gives the Lagrangian $\frac{1}{2}(w-v)^{2}+\tilde{\lambda}w-\beta w$. Differentiating the Lagrangian in w and equating to zero shows that the optimum is $w^{\star}= v - \tilde{\lambda}+ \beta$. When $w^{\star}> 0$, complementary slackness, which requires the optimal pair $w^{\star}$ and β to satisfy $w^{\star}\beta = 0$ (Boyd and Vandenberghe, 2004), forces $\beta = 0$, hence $w^{\star}= v - \tilde{\lambda}$. When $v < \tilde{\lambda}$, we have $v - \tilde{\lambda}< 0$, so β must be positive and, again by complementary slackness, $w^{\star}= 0$. The case $v \leq 0$ is the same up to a change of signs. Putting this together and returning to the full notation, the coordinates of the optimal solution $\pmb{w}^{\star}= \pmb{w}_{t + 1}$ are obtained from $w_{t + \frac{1}{2}}$ by

$$
w_{t+1,j}=\mathrm{sign}\Big(w_{t+\frac{1}{2},j}\Big)\left[|w_{t+\frac{1}{2},j}| -\widetilde{\lambda}\right]_{+}=\mathrm{sign}\Big(w_{t,j}-\eta_{t}g_{t,j}^{f}\Big)\left[\Big|w_{t,j}-\eta_{t}g_{t,j}^{f}\Big| -\eta_{t+\frac{1}{2}}\cdot\lambda\right]_{+}.\tag{19}
$$

This update can produce sparse solutions: any component of ${\pmb w}_{t +{\frac{1}{2}}}$ whose absolute value is below $\tilde{\lambda}$ yields a zero in the corresponding component of ${\pmb w}_{t + 1}$. Eq. (19) therefore provides a simple online and offline method for minimizing a convex $f$ under $\ell_{1}$ regularization.

context.name: Update: l2^2 regularization, Eq. (20) (Section 5.2)
context.statement:
With $\begin{array}{r}{r(\pmb{w})=\frac{\lambda}{2}\|\pmb{w}\|_{2}^{2}}\end{array}$ the optimization problem is very simple:

$$
\operatorname*{minimize}_{\boldsymbol{w}}\frac{1}{2}\|\boldsymbol{w}-\boldsymbol{v}\|^{2}+\frac{1}{2}\widetilde{\lambda}\|\boldsymbol{w}\|^{2},
$$

where, to make the solution more concise, $\tilde{\lambda}$ has been replaced by $\frac{1}{2}\tilde{\lambda}$. Setting the derivative of this objective to zero gives $\pmb{w}^{\star}- v + \tilde{\lambda}\pmb{w}^{\star}= 0$, and in the original notation this is the update

$$
\pmb{w}_{t + 1}= \frac{\pmb{w}_{t}- \pmb{\eta}_{t}\pmb{g}_{t}^{f}}{1 + \tilde{\lambda}}.\tag{20}
$$

context.name: Update: l2 regularization (Section 5.3)
context.statement:
The $\ell_{2}$ norm of the weight vector is a less commonly used choice of regularizer. Taking $r(\boldsymbol{w})=\tilde{\lambda}\|\boldsymbol{w}\|$, we arrive at the problem

$$
\operatorname*{minimize}_{\boldsymbol{w}}\frac{1}{2}\|\boldsymbol{w}-\boldsymbol{v}\|^{2}+\widetilde{\lambda}\|\boldsymbol{w}\|.\tag{21}
$$

Any solution of Eq. (21) points in the direction of v, i.e. it has the form $\pmb{w}^{\star}= s \pmb{v}$ with $s \geq 0$. To verify this form, suppose for contradiction that $\pmb{w}^{\star}= s \pmb{v}+ \pmb{u}$, where u lies in the null space of v (should u have components parallel to v, these can be added to v, leaving an orthogonal $\pmb{u}^{\prime}$) and s is allowed to be negative. As u is orthogonal to $v$, the objective can be written in terms of $s$, $v$ and u as

$$
\frac 12(1-s)^{2}\|{\pmb v}\|^{2}+\frac 12\|{\pmb u}\|^{2}+\widetilde{\lambda}(\|{\pmb v}\|+\|{\pmb u}\|)\ge\frac 12(1-s)^{2}\|{\pmb v}\|^{2}+\widetilde{\lambda}\|{\pmb v}\|.
$$

So u has to be the zero vector, ${\pmb u}={\bf 0}$, and the optimization problem can be written as

$$
\operatorname*{minimize}_{s}\frac{1}{2}(1-s)^{2}\|\pmb{v}\|^{2}+\widetilde{\lambda}s\|\pmb{v}\|\enspace .
$$

Moreover, no negative s can be optimal. Indeed, when $s < 0$,

$$
\frac{1}{2}(1-s)^{2}\|\pmb{v}\|^{2}+\tilde{\lambda}s\|\pmb{v}\|<\frac{1}{2}\|\pmb{v}\|^{2}.
$$

Hence the choice $s = 0$ attains a smaller objective value, which rules out negative s as an optimal solution. We are thus led once more to a constrained scalar problem, $\operatorname*{minimize}_{s\geq 0}\frac{1}{2}(1-s)^{2}\|\pmb{v}\|^{2}+\tilde{\lambda}s\|\pmb{v}\|$, whose Lagrangian is

$$
\frac{1}{2}(1-s)^{2}\|\pmb{v}\|^{2}+\tilde{\lambda}s\|\pmb{v}\|-\beta s\ ,
$$

with $\beta \geq 0$. Differentiating the Lagrangian in s and setting the derivative to zero gives $(s-1)\|{\pmb v}\|^{2}+\tilde{\lambda}\|{\pmb v}\|-{\beta}=0$, and hence the closed form $s = 1 - \tilde{\lambda}/ \| v \| + \beta / \| v \|^{2}$. If $s > 0$, complementary slackness gives $\beta = 0$, and s simplifies to $s = 1 - \tilde{\lambda}/ \| v \|$. This quantity is positive if and only if $\| v \| > \tilde{\lambda}$. If $\| v \| < \tilde{\lambda}$, then β has to be positive and complementary slackness yields $s = 0$.

In summary, with $\ell_{2}$ regularization the second step of the FoBoS update is

$$
w_{t+1}=\left[1-\frac{\tilde{\lambda}}{\lVert w_{t+\frac{1}{2}}\rVert}\right]_{+}w_{t+\frac{1}{2}}=\left[1-\frac{\tilde{\lambda}}{\lVert w_{t}-\eta_{t}g_{t}^{f}\rVert}\right]_{+}(w_{t}-\eta_{t}g_{t}^{f})\ .
$$

Consequently, $\ell_{2}$ regularization gives the zero weight vector exactly under the condition $\| \pmb{w}_{t}- \pmb{\eta}_{t}\pmb{g}_{t}^{f}\| \le \tilde{\lambda}$. As a requirement for sparsity this is considerably stronger than the one for $\ell_{1}$ (there a single weight becomes sparse depending only on its own value, whereas here sparsity occurs only when the whole weight vector has $\ell_{2}$-norm below $\tilde{\lambda}$), so in high dimensions it is unlikely to be met. It is nonetheless a key building block when a mixed $\ell_{1}/ \ell_{2}$-norm serves as the regularizer, as shown later.

context.name: Update: l-infinity regularization via its dual (l1-ball projection), Eqs. (22)-(25) (Section 5.4)
context.statement:
Next we consider a regularizer that has received less attention, the $\ell_{\infty}$ norm of w. On its own this regularizer cannot offer a strong guarantee against overfitting, because many of the weights of w may go unpenalized. There are, however, settings in which one wants to treat blocks of variables as a group, as in $\ell_{1}/ \ell_{\infty}$ regularization. We postpone the discussion of mixed norms once more and concentrate on the $\ell_{\infty}$ norm alone, since it is a building block. Concretely, we want an efficient solution of the problem

$$
\operatorname*{minimize}_{\boldsymbol{w}}\frac{1}{2}\|\boldsymbol{w}-\boldsymbol{v}\|^{2}+\tilde{\lambda}\|\boldsymbol{w}\|_{\infty}\textrm{.}\tag{22}
$$

An efficient algorithm for the minimizer of Eq. (22) could be derived from properties of the subgradient set of $\| \boldsymbol{w}\|_{\infty}$. The dual form of Eq. (22), however, has a well-known solution. Since the conjugate of a quadratic function is quadratic and the conjugate of the $\ell_{\infty}$ norm is the $\ell_{1}$ barrier function, the dual of the problem in Eq. (22) is immediately seen to be

$$
\operatorname*{maximize}_{\alpha}-\frac{1}{2}\left\|\alpha-\pmb{v}\right\|_{2}^{2}\mathrm{s . t .}\left\|\pmb{\alpha}\right\|_{1}\leq\tilde{\lambda}\mathrm{~.~}\tag{23}
$$

In addition, the dual variables $\pmb{\alpha}$ are related to the primal by ${\pmb{\alpha}}={\pmb{v}}-{\pmb{w}}$. Solving the dual form in Eq. (23) therefore readily gives a solution of Eq. (22). Problem Eq. (23) is the same as Euclidean projection onto the $\ell_{1}$ ball, which many authors have studied. The solution summarized here follows recent work of Duchi et al. (2008). The maximizer of Eq. (23), written $\alpha^{\star}$, has the form

$$
\alpha_{j}^{\star}=\mathrm{sign}(v_{j})\left[|v_{j}| -\theta\right]_{+}\ ,\tag{24}
$$

with θ a non-negative scalar. A linear-time algorithm for computing θ is given by Duchi et al. (2008). We therefore do not analyze that algorithm and instead concentrate on the core properties that affect the solution of the problem in Eq. (22). Computing θ requires finding a pivot element of v, namely the $\rho^{t h}$ order statistic $v_{(\rho)}$ (with $v_{(1)}$ the entry of v of largest magnitude), characterized as follows: $v_{(\rho)}$ is the element of v of smallest magnitude for which

$$
\sum_{j: |v_{j}| > |v_{(\rho)}|}\bigl(|v_{j}| - |v_{(\rho)}|\bigr)<\tilde{\lambda}\ .
$$

When every element of v (with an extra element equal to 0 appended to take care of the smallest entry) satisfies this requirement, θ = 0 is the optimal choice. In the remaining case,

$$
\theta=\frac{1}{\rho}\left(\sum_{j: |v_{j}| > |v_{(\rho)}|}|v_{j}| -\tilde{\lambda}\right).
$$

So θ = 0 is optimal exactly when $\sum_{j = 1}^{n}| v_{j}| \leq \tilde{\lambda}$ (not by coincidence, this is just the subgradient optimality condition for the zero vector in Eq. (22)).

Combining the linear relation $\pmb{\alpha}= \pmb{v}- \pmb{w}\Rightarrow \pmb{w}= \pmb{v}- \pmb{\alpha}$ with the dual solution provided by Eq. (24), the solution of Eq. (22) is

$$
w_{t+1,j}=\mathrm{sign}\Big(w_{t+\frac{1}{2},j}\Big)\operatorname*{min}\left\{\Big|w_{t+\frac{1}{2},j}\Big|\ ,\ \theta\right\}\ .\tag{25}
$$

As noted above, $\theta = 0$ if and only if $\| \pmb{w}_{t + \frac{1}{2}}\|_{1}\leq \tilde{\lambda}$, and otherwise $\theta > 0$ and θ can be computed in $O(n)$ steps. Put in words, the components of ${\pmb w}_{t + 1}$ are obtained by capping every component of ${\pmb w}_{t}$ at θ, with θ equal to zero when the 1-norm of $w_{t + \frac{1}{2}}$ is below $\tilde{\lambda}$. This property mirrors, through duality, the $\ell_{2}$-regularized update, which gives a zero weight vector when the 2-norm (which is self-dual) of v is below $\tilde{\lambda}$. These properties can be used with mixed-norm regularization to obtain sparse solutions for complex prediction problems; this is described later, and preliminary results are given in Sec. 7. Before turning to it, we present one further norm-related regularizer.

context.name: Eq. (36), from the proof of Theorem 6
context.statement:
Proof of Theorem 6 When $\| \partial f \|$ and $\| \partial r \|$ are bounded by G, Lemma 1 gives at once

$$
f_{t}(\boldsymbol{w}_{t})-f_{t}(\boldsymbol{w}^{\star})+r(\boldsymbol{w}_{t+1})-r(\boldsymbol{w}^{\star})\leq\frac{1}{2\eta_{t}}\left(\|\boldsymbol{w}_{t}-\boldsymbol{w}^{\star}\|^{2}-\|\boldsymbol{w}_{t+1}-\boldsymbol{w}^{\star}\|^{2}\right)+\frac{7}{2}G^{2}\eta_{t}.\tag{36}
$$

/-! ### Auxiliary machinery (helper lemmas, proved from Mathlib) -/

section AuxFoBoS
variable {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace ℝ F]

/-- The subgradient inequality, rewritten as `φ x - φ y ≤ ⟪g, x - y⟫`. -/
lemma subgrad_bound {φ : F → ℝ} {g x : F} (h : HasSubgradientAt φ g x) (y : F) :
    φ x - φ y ≤ inner ℝ g (x - y) := by
  have h1 := h y
  have h2 : inner ℝ g (y - x) = -(inner ℝ g (x - y) : ℝ) := by simp [inner_sub_right]
  rw [h2] at h1
  linarith

/-- The sum of subgradients is a subgradient of the sum. -/
lemma subgrad_add {φ ψ : F → ℝ} {g h x : F} (hφ : HasSubgradientAt φ g x)
    (hψ : HasSubgradientAt ψ h x) : HasSubgradientAt (fun z => φ z + ψ z) (g + h) x := by
  intro y
  have h1 := hφ y
  have h2 := hψ y
  have h3 : (inner ℝ (g + h) (y - x) : ℝ) = inner ℝ g (y-x) + inner ℝ h (y-x) := by
    rw [inner_add_left]
  show φ y + ψ y ≥ (φ x + ψ x) + (inner ℝ (g + h) (y - x) : ℝ)
  rw [h3]
  simp only [ge_iff_le] at h1 h2
  linarith

lemma core_id_aux (d a b : F) (η : ℝ) (hη : η ≠ 0) :
    (inner ℝ a d : ℝ) + inner ℝ b (d - η • (a + b))
      = (1/(2*η)) * (‖d‖^2 - ‖d - η • (a+b)‖^2) + (η/2) * (‖a‖^2 - ‖b‖^2) := by
  rw [norm_sub_sq_real, norm_smul, mul_pow, norm_add_sq_real]
  simp only [inner_sub_right, real_inner_smul_right, inner_add_right,
    real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs]
  rw [real_inner_comm b a, real_inner_comm a d, real_inner_comm b d]
  field_simp
  ring

/-- The exact algebraic identity underlying the analysis of a forward-backward splitting step. -/
lemma core_id (wt wt1 wst a b : F) (η : ℝ) (hη : η ≠ 0)
    (hupd : wt1 = wt - η • a - η • b) :
    (inner ℝ a (wt - wst) : ℝ) + inner ℝ b (wt1 - wst)
      = (1/(2*η)) * (‖wt - wst‖^2 - ‖wt1 - wst‖^2) + (η/2) * (‖a‖^2 - ‖b‖^2) := by
  have hd : wt1 - wst = (wt - wst) - η • (a + b) := by rw [hupd, smul_add]; abel
  rw [hd]
  exact core_id_aux (wt - wst) a b η hη

/-- Strong convexity upgrades the subgradient inequality by a quadratic term. -/
lemma strongconvex_subgrad {φ : F → ℝ} {s : Set F} {H : ℝ} (hH : 0 ≤ H)
    (hsc : StrongConvexOn s H φ) {g x : F} (hg : HasSubgradientAt φ g x) (hx : x ∈ s)
    {y : F} (hy : y ∈ s) :
    φ x - φ y ≤ (inner ℝ g (x - y) : ℝ) - (H/2) * ‖x - y‖^2 := by
  set K : ℝ := (H/2) * ‖x - y‖^2 with hK
  have hK0 : 0 ≤ K := by rw [hK]; positivity
  have main : ∀ l : ℝ, 0 < l → l ≤ 1 → φ x - φ y ≤ (inner ℝ g (x - y) : ℝ) - (1 - l) * K := by
    intro l hl hl1
    have h0 : (0:ℝ) ≤ 1 - l := by linarith
    have hcv := hsc.2 hx hy h0 hl.le (by ring)
    have hpt : (1-l) • x + l • y - x = l • (y - x) := by
      rw [smul_sub, sub_smul, one_smul]; abel
    have hsub := hg ((1-l) • x + l • y)
    rw [hpt] at hsub
    have hin : (inner ℝ g (l • (y - x)) : ℝ) = - (l * (inner ℝ g (x - y) : ℝ)) := by
      rw [real_inner_smul_right]
      have h9 : (inner ℝ g (y - x) : ℝ) = -(inner ℝ g (x - y) : ℝ) := by simp [inner_sub_right]
      rw [h9]; ring
    rw [hin] at hsub
    simp only [smul_eq_mul] at hcv
    rw [hK]
    nlinarith [hcv, hsub]
  apply le_of_forall_pos_le_add
  intro ε hε
  have hlt : (0:ℝ) < ε / (K + 1) := by positivity
  set l : ℝ := min 1 (ε / (K+1)) with hlv
  have hl0 : 0 < l := lt_min one_pos hlt
  have hl1 : l ≤ 1 := min_le_left _ _
  have hle : l ≤ ε / (K+1) := min_le_right _ _
  have hm := main l hl0 hl1
  have hKε : l * K ≤ ε := by
    have h1 : l * K ≤ (ε/(K+1)) * K := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hle hK0
    have h2 : (ε/(K+1)) * K ≤ ε := by
      rw [div_mul_eq_mul_div, div_le_iff₀ (by linarith)]
      nlinarith
    linarith
  nlinarith

end AuxFoBoS

lemma sum_Icc_one_eq_range (g : ℕ → ℝ) (T : ℕ) :
    ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, g t = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range T, g (i+1) := by
  induction T with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih => rw [Finset.sum_Icc_succ_top (by omega), Finset.sum_range_succ, ih]

lemma tele (u : ℕ → ℝ) (T : ℕ) :
    ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (u t - u (t+1)) = u 1 - u (T+1) := by
  induction T with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih => rw [Finset.sum_Icc_succ_top (by omega), ih]; ring

/-- Abel-summation bound for a nonincreasing-in-value / nondecreasing-in-weight telescoping sum. -/
lemma abel_bound (a b : ℕ → ℝ) (D2 : ℝ)
    (haD : ∀ t, 1 ≤ t → a t ≤ D2) (hb0 : ∀ t, 0 ≤ b t) (hbm : Monotone b) :
    ∀ T, 1 ≤ T → ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, b t * (a t - a (t+1)) ≤ D2 * b T - b T * a (T+1) := by
  intro T hT
  induction T, hT using Nat.le_induction with
  | base =>
      simp only [Finset.Icc_self, Finset.sum_singleton]
      have h1 : a 1 ≤ D2 := haD 1 le_rfl
      have h2 : 0 ≤ b 1 := hb0 1
      nlinarith
  | succ n hn ih =>
      rw [Finset.sum_Icc_succ_top (by omega)]
      have hbn : b n ≤ b (n+1) := hbm (Nat.le_succ n)
      have h1 : a (n+1) ≤ D2 := haD _ (by omega)
      nlinarith [ih]

lemma sum_inv_sqrt_le (T : ℕ) :
    ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (1:ℝ)/Real.sqrt t ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt T := by
  induction T with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
      rw [Finset.sum_Icc_succ_top (by omega)]
      have hs : Real.sqrt n ≤ Real.sqrt (n+1) := by apply Real.sqrt_le_sqrt; linarith
      have hpos : (0:ℝ) < Real.sqrt (n+1) := by apply Real.sqrt_pos.mpr; positivity
      have key : (1:ℝ)/Real.sqrt ((n:ℝ)+1) ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt ((n:ℝ)+1) - 2 * Real.sqrt n := by
        rw [div_le_iff₀ hpos]
        have h1 : Real.sqrt ((n:ℝ)+1) * Real.sqrt ((n:ℝ)+1) = (n:ℝ)+1 :=
          Real.mul_self_sqrt (by positivity)
        have h2 : Real.sqrt (n:ℝ) * Real.sqrt (n:ℝ) = (n:ℝ) :=
          Real.mul_self_sqrt (by positivity)
        nlinarith [hs, Real.sqrt_nonneg ((n:ℝ)), Real.sqrt_nonneg ((n:ℝ)+1)]
      push_cast
      push_cast at ih
      linarith

lemma sum_inv_le_log (T : ℕ) :
    ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (1:ℝ)/t ≤ 1 + Real.log T := by
  have h1 : ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (1:ℝ)/t = ((harmonic T : ℚ) : ℝ) := by
    rw [sum_Icc_one_eq_range]
    simp [harmonic, Rat.cast_sum]
  rw [h1]
  exact harmonic_le_one_add_log T

theorem theorem6
    (f : ℕ → E → ℝ) (r : E → ℝ) (w gf gr : ℕ → E) (η : ℕ → ℝ) (D G c : ℝ)
    (wstar : E)
    (hconvf : ∀ t, ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (f t)) (hconvr : ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ r)
    (hfnn : ∀ t x, 0 ≤ f t x) (hrnn : ∀ x, 0 ≤ r x)
    (hrun : IsFoBoSOnlineRun f r w gf gr η)
    (hD : ∀ t, 1 ≤ t → ‖w t - wstar‖ ≤ D) (hDnn : 0 ≤ D)
    (hGf : ∀ t x g, HasSubgradientAt (f t) g x → ‖g‖ ≤ G)
    (hGr : ∀ x g, HasSubgradientAt r g x → ‖g‖ ≤ G) (hGnn : 0 ≤ G)
    (hc : 0 < c)
    (hη : ∀ t, 1 ≤ t → η t = c / Real.sqrt t)
    (T : ℕ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    Regret f r w wstar T ≤ 2 * G * D + (D ^ 2 / (2 * c) + 7 * G ^ 2 * c) * Real.sqrt T := by
  obtain ⟨hsf, hsr, hupd⟩ := hrun
  set A : ℕ → ℝ := fun t => ‖w t - wstar‖^2 with hA
  set B : ℕ → ℝ := fun t => Real.sqrt t / (2*c) with hB
  -- per-step bound
  have hstep : ∀ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T,
      f t (w t) - f t wstar + (r (w (t+1)) - r wstar)
        ≤ B t * (A t - A (t+1)) + (c / Real.sqrt t / 2) * G^2 := by
    intro t ht
    rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at ht
    have h1 : 1 ≤ t := ht.1
    have hst : (0:ℝ) < Real.sqrt t := by
      apply Real.sqrt_pos.mpr
      exact_mod_cast h1
    have hηt : η t = c / Real.sqrt t := hη t h1
    have hηpos : 0 < η t := by rw [hηt]; positivity
    have hkey := core_id (w t) (w (t+1)) wstar (gf t) (gr (t+1)) (η t) (ne_of_gt hηpos) (hupd t)
    have hf1 : f t (w t) - f t wstar ≤ inner ℝ (gf t) (w t - wstar) := subgrad_bound (hsf t) wstar
    have hr1 : r (w (t+1)) - r wstar ≤ inner ℝ (gr (t+1)) (w (t+1) - wstar) :=
      subgrad_bound (hsr (t+1)) wstar
    have hG1 : ‖gf t‖ ≤ G := hGf t (w t) (gf t) (hsf t)
    have hBeq : (1:ℝ)/(2*η t) = B t := by
      rw [hηt, hB]
      field_simp
    have hηeq : η t / 2 = c / Real.sqrt t / 2 := by rw [hηt]
    have hsq : ‖gf t‖^2 ≤ G^2 := by nlinarith [norm_nonneg (gf t)]
    have hsq2 : (0:ℝ) ≤ ‖gr (t+1)‖^2 := sq_nonneg _
    have : (η t / 2) * (‖gf t‖^2 - ‖gr (t+1)‖^2) ≤ (c / Real.sqrt t / 2) * G^2 := by
      rw [← hηeq]
      have hh : (0:ℝ) ≤ η t / 2 := by linarith
      nlinarith
    rw [hBeq] at hkey
    have hAeq : A t = ‖w t - wstar‖^2 := rfl
    have hAeq1 : A (t+1) = ‖w (t+1) - wstar‖^2 := rfl
    rw [hAeq, hAeq1]
    linarith [hkey, hf1, hr1, this]
  -- regret decomposition
  have hreg : Regret f r w wstar T
      = (∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (f t (w t) - f t wstar + (r (w (t+1)) - r wstar)))
        + (r (w 1) - r (w (T+1))) := by
    rw [Regret, ← tele (fun t => r (w t)) T, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro t _
    ring
  -- bound the main sum
  have hsum : (∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (f t (w t) - f t wstar + (r (w (t+1)) - r wstar)))
      ≤ ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (B t * (A t - A (t+1)) + (c / Real.sqrt t / 2) * G^2) :=
    Finset.sum_le_sum hstep
  have hsplit : ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (B t * (A t - A (t+1)) + (c / Real.sqrt t / 2) * G^2)
      = (∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, B t * (A t - A (t+1)))
        + ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (c / Real.sqrt t / 2) * G^2 := Finset.sum_add_distrib
  rw [hsplit] at hsum
  -- the harmonic-type sum
  have hsum2 : (∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (c / Real.sqrt t / 2) * G^2) ≤ c * G^2 * Real.sqrt T := by
    have he : (∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (c / Real.sqrt t / 2) * G^2)
        = (c * G^2/2) * ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (1:ℝ)/Real.sqrt t := by
      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro t _
      ring
    rw [he]
    have h1 := sum_inv_sqrt_le T
    have hnn : (0:ℝ) ≤ c * G^2/2 := by positivity
    calc (c * G^2/2) * ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (1:ℝ)/Real.sqrt t
        ≤ (c * G^2/2) * (2 * Real.sqrt T) := by exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h1 hnn
      _ = c * G^2 * Real.sqrt T := by ring
  -- the Abel sum
  have hB0 : ∀ t, 0 ≤ B t := by
    intro t; rw [hB]; positivity
  have hBm : Monotone B := by
    intro x y hxy
    simp only [hB]
    apply div_le_div_of_nonneg_right ?_ (by positivity)
    exact Real.sqrt_le_sqrt (by exact_mod_cast hxy)
  have hAD : ∀ t, 1 ≤ t → A t ≤ D^2 := by
    intro t ht
    have := hD t ht
    have h0 := norm_nonneg (w t - wstar)
    simp only [hA]
    nlinarith
  have habel := abel_bound A B (D^2) hAD hB0 hBm T hT
  have hA0 : (0:ℝ) ≤ A (T+1) := by simp only [hA]; positivity
  have hBT : (0:ℝ) ≤ B T := hB0 T
  have hsum3 : (∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, B t * (A t - A (t+1))) ≤ D^2 * (Real.sqrt T/(2*c)) := by
    have : B T = Real.sqrt T/(2*c) := rfl
    nlinarith [habel]
  -- last term
  have hlast : r (w 1) - r (w (T+1)) ≤ 2*G*D := by
    have h1 : r (w 1) - r (w (T+1)) ≤ inner ℝ (gr 1) (w 1 - w (T+1)) :=
      subgrad_bound (hsr 1) (w (T+1))
    have h2 : (inner ℝ (gr 1) (w 1 - w (T+1)) : ℝ) ≤ ‖gr 1‖ * ‖w 1 - w (T+1)‖ :=
      real_inner_le_norm _ _
    have h3 : ‖gr 1‖ ≤ G := hGr (w 1) (gr 1) (hsr 1)
    have h4 : ‖w 1 - w (T+1)‖ ≤ ‖w 1 - wstar‖ + ‖w (T+1) - wstar‖ := by
      have he : w 1 - w (T+1) = (w 1 - wstar) - (w (T+1) - wstar) := by abel
      rw [he]; exact norm_sub_le _ _
    have h5 : ‖w 1 - wstar‖ ≤ D := hD 1 le_rfl
    have h6 : ‖w (T+1) - wstar‖ ≤ D := hD (T+1) (by omega)
    nlinarith [norm_nonneg (w 1 - w (T+1)), norm_nonneg (gr 1)]
  rw [hreg]
  have hfin : D^2 * (Real.sqrt T/(2*c)) + c * G^2 * Real.sqrt T
      ≤ (D ^ 2 / (2 * c) + 7 * G ^ 2 * c) * Real.sqrt T := by
    have hs : (0:ℝ) ≤ Real.sqrt T := Real.sqrt_nonneg _
    have : D^2 * (Real.sqrt T/(2*c)) = D^2/(2*c) * Real.sqrt T := by ring
    rw [this]
    have h6 : (0:ℝ) ≤ 6 * G^2 * c * Real.sqrt T := by positivity
    nlinarith [h6]
  linarith


theorem theorem8
    (f : ℕ → E → ℝ) (r : E → ℝ) (w gf gr : ℕ → E) (η : ℕ → ℝ) (D G H : ℝ)
    (wstar : E)
    (hconvf : ∀ t, ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (f t)) (hconvr : ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ r)
    (hfnn : ∀ t x, 0 ≤ f t x) (hrnn : ∀ x, 0 ≤ r x)
    (hrun : IsFoBoSOnlineRun f r w gf gr η)
    (hD : ∀ t, 1 ≤ t → ‖w t - wstar‖ ≤ D) (hDnn : 0 ≤ D)
    (hGf : ∀ t x g, HasSubgradientAt (f t) g x → ‖g‖ ≤ G)
    (hGr : ∀ x g, HasSubgradientAt r g x → ‖g‖ ≤ G) (hGnn : 0 ≤ G)
    (hH : 0 < H)
    (hsc : ∀ t, StrongConvexOn (Metric.closedBall wstar D) H (fun x => f t x + r x))
    (hη : ∀ t, 1 ≤ t → η t = 1 / (H * t))
    (T : ℕ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    Regret f r w wstar T
      ≤ 2 * G * D + H * D ^ 2 + (7 * G ^ 2 / (2 * H)) * (1 + Real.log T) := by
  obtain ⟨hsf, hsr, hupd⟩ := hrun
  set A : ℕ → ℝ := fun t => ‖w t - wstar‖^2 with hA
  set u : ℕ → ℝ := fun t => (inner ℝ (gr t) (w t - wstar) : ℝ) with hu
  set v : ℕ → ℝ := fun t => (H/2) * ((t:ℝ) - 1) * A t with hv
  have hwmem : ∀ t, 1 ≤ t → w t ∈ Metric.closedBall wstar D := by
    intro t ht
    rw [Metric.mem_closedBall, dist_eq_norm]
    exact hD t ht
  have hwsmem : wstar ∈ Metric.closedBall wstar D := by
    rw [Metric.mem_closedBall]; simpa using hDnn
  have hstep : ∀ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T,
      f t (w t) + r (w t) - (f t wstar + r wstar)
        ≤ (u t - u (t+1)) + (v t - v (t+1)) + (1/(H*(t:ℝ))/2)*G^2 := by
    intro t ht
    rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at ht
    have h1 : 1 ≤ t := ht.1
    have htR : (1:ℝ) ≤ (t:ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast h1
    have hηt : η t = 1/(H*(t:ℝ)) := hη t h1
    have hηpos : 0 < η t := by rw [hηt]; positivity
    have hsg : HasSubgradientAt (fun z => f t z + r z) (gf t + gr t) (w t) :=
      subgrad_add (hsf t) (hsr t)
    have hscb := strongconvex_subgrad hH.le (hsc t) hsg (hwmem t h1) hwsmem
    simp only [] at hscb
    have hinadd : (inner ℝ (gf t + gr t) (w t - wstar) : ℝ)
        = (inner ℝ (gf t) (w t - wstar) : ℝ) + u t := by
      rw [inner_add_left]
    rw [hinadd] at hscb
    have hkey := core_id (w t) (w (t+1)) wstar (gf t) (gr (t+1)) (η t) (ne_of_gt hηpos) (hupd t)
    have hcoef : (1:ℝ)/(2*η t) = H*(t:ℝ)/2 := by
      rw [hηt]; field_simp
    rw [hcoef] at hkey
    have hG1 : ‖gf t‖ ≤ G := hGf t (w t) (gf t) (hsf t)
    have hsq : ‖gf t‖^2 ≤ G^2 := by nlinarith [norm_nonneg (gf t)]
    have hsq2 : (0:ℝ) ≤ ‖gr (t+1)‖^2 := sq_nonneg _
    have hlast : (η t / 2) * (‖gf t‖^2 - ‖gr (t+1)‖^2) ≤ (1/(H*(t:ℝ))/2)*G^2 := by
      have hh : (0:ℝ) ≤ η t / 2 := by linarith
      have : (1:ℝ)/(H*(t:ℝ))/2 = η t / 2 := by rw [hηt]
      rw [this]
      nlinarith
    have hvv : v t - v (t+1) = (H*(t:ℝ)/2) * (A t - A (t+1)) - (H/2) * A t := by
      simp only [hv]
      push_cast
      ring
    have hAt : A t = ‖w t - wstar‖^2 := rfl
    have hAt1 : A (t+1) = ‖w (t+1) - wstar‖^2 := rfl
    have hut1 : u (t+1) = (inner ℝ (gr (t+1)) (w (t+1) - wstar) : ℝ) := rfl
    rw [hAt, hAt1] at hvv
    rw [hut1]
    linarith [hkey, hscb, hlast, hvv]
  have hsum : Regret f r w wstar T
      ≤ ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, ((u t - u (t+1)) + (v t - v (t+1)) + (1/(H*(t:ℝ))/2)*G^2) :=
    Finset.sum_le_sum hstep
  have hsplit : ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, ((u t - u (t+1)) + (v t - v (t+1)) + (1/(H*(t:ℝ))/2)*G^2)
      = (∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (u t - u (t+1))) + (∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (v t - v (t+1)))
        + (∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (1/(H*(t:ℝ))/2)*G^2) := by
    rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  rw [hsplit, tele u T, tele v T] at hsum
  -- bound u 1 - u (T+1)
  have hu1 : u 1 - u (T+1) ≤ 2*G*D := by
    have e1 : u 1 ≤ ‖gr 1‖ * ‖w 1 - wstar‖ := real_inner_le_norm _ _
    have e2 : |u (T+1)| ≤ ‖gr (T+1)‖ * ‖w (T+1) - wstar‖ := abs_real_inner_le_norm _ _
    have e3 : ‖gr 1‖ ≤ G := hGr (w 1) (gr 1) (hsr 1)
    have e4 : ‖gr (T+1)‖ ≤ G := hGr (w (T+1)) (gr (T+1)) (hsr (T+1))
    have e5 : ‖w 1 - wstar‖ ≤ D := hD 1 le_rfl
    have e6 : ‖w (T+1) - wstar‖ ≤ D := hD (T+1) (by omega)
    have e7 : -u (T+1) ≤ |u (T+1)| := neg_le_abs _
    nlinarith [norm_nonneg (gr 1), norm_nonneg (gr (T+1)), norm_nonneg (w 1 - wstar),
      norm_nonneg (w (T+1) - wstar)]
  -- bound v 1 - v (T+1)
  have hv1 : v 1 - v (T+1) ≤ 0 := by
    have e1 : v 1 = 0 := by simp [hv]
    have e2 : (0:ℝ) ≤ v (T+1) := by
      have he : v (T+1) = (H/2) * (T:ℝ) * ‖w (T+1) - wstar‖^2 := by
        simp only [hv, hA]; push_cast; ring
      rw [he]
      exact mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg (by linarith) (Nat.cast_nonneg T)) (sq_nonneg _)
    linarith
  -- bound the log sum
  have hlog : (∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (1/(H*(t:ℝ))/2)*G^2) ≤ (G^2/(2*H))*(1 + Real.log T) := by
    have he : (∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (1/(H*(t:ℝ))/2)*G^2)
        = (G^2/(2*H)) * ∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 T, (1:ℝ)/t := by
      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro t ht
      rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at ht
      have hne : (t:ℝ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr (by omega)
      field_simp
    rw [he]
    have h1 := sum_inv_le_log T
    have hnn : (0:ℝ) ≤ G^2/(2*H) := by positivity
    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h1 hnn
  have hlogT : (0:ℝ) ≤ Real.log T := Real.log_nonneg (by exact_mod_cast hT)
  have hfin : (G^2/(2*H))*(1 + Real.log T) ≤ (7 * G ^ 2 / (2 * H)) * (1 + Real.log T) := by
    have hnn : (0:ℝ) ≤ 1 + Real.log T := by linarith
    have : G^2/(2*H) ≤ 7 * G^2/(2*H) := by
      apply div_le_div_of_nonneg_right ?_ (by positivity)
      nlinarith [sq_nonneg G]
    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right this hnn
  have hHD : (0:ℝ) ≤ H * D^2 := by positivity
  linarith


/-! ### Machinery for Proposition 11 -/

section Prox
variable {n : ℕ}

/-- Euclidean inner product on `Fin n → ℝ`. -/
def dotp (a b : Fin n → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ i, a i * b i

lemma dotp_comm (a b : Fin n → ℝ) : dotp a b = dotp b a := by
  simp only [dotp]; exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => mul_comm _ _

lemma dotp_self (a : Fin n → ℝ) : dotp a a = sqL2 a := by simp only [dotp, sqL2, sq]

lemma dotp_sub_right (a b c : Fin n → ℝ) : dotp a (b - c) = dotp a b - dotp a c := by
  simp only [dotp, Pi.sub_apply, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring

lemma dotp_neg_right (a b : Fin n → ℝ) : dotp a (-b) = -dotp a b := by
  simp only [dotp, Pi.neg_apply, ← Finset.sum_neg_distrib]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring

lemma sqL2_nonneg (x : Fin n → ℝ) : 0 ≤ sqL2 x := by
  apply Finset.sum_nonneg; intro i _; positivity

lemma sqL2_eq_zero {x : Fin n → ℝ} (h : sqL2 x = 0) : x = 0 := by
  funext i
  have := (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg (fun i _ => sq_nonneg (x i))).mp h i (Finset.mem_univ i)
  simpa using pow_eq_zero_iff (n := 2) (by norm_num) |>.mp this

lemma sqL2_expand (u z x : Fin n → ℝ) :
    sqL2 (u - x) = sqL2 (u - z) + 2 * dotp (u - z) (z - x) + sqL2 (z - x) := by
  simp only [sqL2, dotp, Pi.sub_apply, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring

lemma sqL2_add (a b : Fin n → ℝ) : sqL2 (a + b) = sqL2 a + 2 * dotp a b + sqL2 b := by
  simp only [sqL2, dotp, Pi.add_apply]
  rw [Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring

lemma sqL2_add_smul (a b : Fin n → ℝ) (s : ℝ) :
    sqL2 (a + s • b) = sqL2 a + 2*s*dotp a b + s^2 * sqL2 b := by
  simp only [sqL2, dotp, Pi.add_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
  rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring

lemma sqL2_midpoint (a b : Fin n → ℝ) :
    sqL2 ((1/2 : ℝ) • (a + b)) = (sqL2 a + sqL2 b)/2 - sqL2 (a - b)/4 := by
  simp only [sqL2, Pi.smul_apply, Pi.add_apply, Pi.sub_apply, smul_eq_mul]
  rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_div, Finset.sum_div, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring

/-- Sufficient optimality condition for the prox problem. -/
lemma prox_suff (N : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ) (lam : ℝ) (x z : Fin n → ℝ)
    (h1 : ∀ u, dotp (x - z) u ≤ lam * N u)
    (h2 : dotp (x - z) z = lam * N z) : IsProxNorm N lam x z := by
  rw [IsProxNorm, isMinOn_iff]
  intro u _
  have he := sqL2_expand u z x
  have h3 : dotp (u - z) (z - x) = dotp (x - z) z - dotp (x - z) u := by
    simp only [dotp, Pi.sub_apply, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring
  have h4 := h1 u
  have h5 := sqL2_nonneg (u - z)
  show sqL2 (z - x) / 2 + lam * N z ≤ sqL2 (u - x) / 2 + lam * N u
  rw [he, h3, h2]
  linarith

/-- The variational inequality satisfied by a prox point. -/
lemma prox_VI (N : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ) (lam : ℝ) (hlam : 0 ≤ lam) (x y : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hconv : ∀ (a b : Fin n → ℝ) (s : ℝ), 0 ≤ s → s ≤ 1 →
      N ((1-s) • a + s • b) ≤ (1-s) * N a + s * N b)
    (h : IsProxNorm N lam x y) :
    ∀ u, dotp (x - y) (u - y) ≤ lam * (N u - N y) := by
  intro u
  rw [IsProxNorm, isMinOn_iff] at h
  set K : ℝ := sqL2 (u - y) / 2 with hK
  have hK0 : 0 ≤ K := by rw [hK]; have := sqL2_nonneg (u - y); linarith
  have main : ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ 1 →
      dotp (x - y) (u - y) ≤ lam * (N u - N y) + s * K := by
    intro s hs hs1
    have hpt : (1-s) • y + s • u - x = (y - x) + s • (u - y) := by
      funext i; simp only [Pi.sub_apply, Pi.add_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]; ring
    have hmin := h ((1-s) • y + s • u) (Set.mem_univ _)
    simp only [] at hmin
    rw [hpt, sqL2_add_smul] at hmin
    have hcv := hconv y u s hs.le hs1
    have hdd : dotp (y - x) (u - y) = - dotp (x - y) (u - y) := by
      simp only [dotp, Pi.sub_apply, ← Finset.sum_neg_distrib]
      exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring
    rw [hdd] at hmin
    rw [hK]
    nlinarith [hmin, hcv, sqL2_nonneg (u - y)]
  apply le_of_forall_pos_le_add
  intro ε hε
  have hlt : (0:ℝ) < ε / (K + 1) := by positivity
  set s : ℝ := min 1 (ε / (K+1)) with hsv
  have hs0 : 0 < s := lt_min one_pos hlt
  have hs1 : s ≤ 1 := min_le_left _ _
  have hle : s ≤ ε / (K+1) := min_le_right _ _
  have hm := main s hs0 hs1
  have hKε : s * K ≤ ε := by
    have ha : s * K ≤ (ε/(K+1)) * K := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hle hK0
    have hb : (ε/(K+1)) * K ≤ ε := by
      rw [div_mul_eq_mul_div, div_le_iff₀ (by linarith)]
      nlinarith
    linarith
  linarith

lemma prox_dual {N : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ} {lam : ℝ} {x y : Fin n → ℝ} (hlam : 0 ≤ lam)
    (htri : ∀ a b, N (a + b) ≤ N a + N b)
    (hVI : ∀ u, dotp (x - y) (u - y) ≤ lam * (N u - N y)) :
    ∀ v, dotp (x - y) v ≤ lam * N v := by
  intro v
  have h1 := hVI (y + v)
  have h2 : (y + v) - y = v := by abel
  rw [h2] at h1
  have h3 : N (y + v) ≤ N y + N v := htri y v
  nlinarith

lemma prox_align {N : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ} {lam : ℝ} {x y : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hN0 : N 0 = 0)
    (hVI : ∀ u, dotp (x - y) (u - y) ≤ lam * (N u - N y))
    (hdual : ∀ v, dotp (x - y) v ≤ lam * N v) :
    dotp (x - y) y = lam * N y := by
  have h1 := hVI 0
  have h2 : (0 : Fin n → ℝ) - y = -y := by abel
  rw [h2, hN0, dotp_neg_right] at h1
  have h3 := hdual y
  linarith

lemma prox_unique {N : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ} {lam : ℝ} (hlam : 0 ≤ lam)
    (hmid : ∀ a b : Fin n → ℝ, N ((1/2 : ℝ) • (a + b)) ≤ (N a + N b)/2)
    {x z1 z2 : Fin n → ℝ} (h1 : IsProxNorm N lam x z1) (h2 : IsProxNorm N lam x z2) :
    z1 = z2 := by
  rw [IsProxNorm, isMinOn_iff] at h1 h2
  have e1 := h1 z2 (Set.mem_univ _)
  have e2 := h2 z1 (Set.mem_univ _)
  simp only [] at e1 e2
  set m : Fin n → ℝ := (1/2 : ℝ) • (z1 + z2) with hm
  have hmx : m - x = (1/2 : ℝ) • ((z1 - x) + (z2 - x)) := by
    funext i
    simp only [hm, Pi.sub_apply, Pi.add_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
    ring
  have e3 := h1 m (Set.mem_univ _)
  simp only [] at e3
  rw [hmx, sqL2_midpoint] at e3
  have hd : (z1 - x) - (z2 - x) = z1 - z2 := by abel
  rw [hd] at e3
  have hmn : N m ≤ (N z1 + N z2)/2 := hmid z1 z2
  have hs : sqL2 (z1 - z2) ≤ 0 := by nlinarith
  have hnn := sqL2_nonneg (z1 - z2)
  exact sub_eq_zero.mp (sqL2_eq_zero (le_antisymm hs hnn))

/-- The prox map does not increase `N`. -/
lemma prox_norm_le {N : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ} {lam : ℝ} (hlam : 0 ≤ lam) {x z : Fin n → ℝ}
    (h : IsProxNorm N lam x z) : N z ≤ N x := by
  rw [IsProxNorm, isMinOn_iff] at h
  have e := h x (Set.mem_univ _)
  simp only [] at e
  have h0 : sqL2 (x - x) = 0 := by simp [sqL2]
  rw [h0] at e
  have hnn := sqL2_nonneg (z - x)
  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hlam with h1 | h1
  · have hz : sqL2 (z - x) ≤ 0 := by rw [← h1] at e; linarith
    have : z = x := sub_eq_zero.mp (sqL2_eq_zero (le_antisymm hz hnn))
    rw [this]
  · nlinarith

end Prox

section NormFacts
variable {n : ℕ}

lemma conv_of_tri_hom {N : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ} (htri : ∀ a b, N (a + b) ≤ N a + N b)
    (hhom : ∀ (c : ℝ) (a : Fin n → ℝ), 0 ≤ c → N (c • a) = c * N a) :
    ∀ (a b : Fin n → ℝ) (s : ℝ), 0 ≤ s → s ≤ 1 →
      N ((1-s) • a + s • b) ≤ (1-s) * N a + s * N b := by
  intro a b s h0 h1
  calc N ((1-s) • a + s • b) ≤ N ((1-s) • a) + N (s • b) := htri _ _
    _ = (1-s) * N a + s * N b := by rw [hhom _ _ (by linarith), hhom _ _ h0]

lemma mid_of_conv {N : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ}
    (hconv : ∀ (a b : Fin n → ℝ) (s : ℝ), 0 ≤ s → s ≤ 1 →
      N ((1-s) • a + s • b) ≤ (1-s) * N a + s * N b) (a b : Fin n → ℝ) :
    N ((1/2 : ℝ) • (a + b)) ≤ (N a + N b)/2 := by
  have h := hconv a b (1/2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
  have he : ((1:ℝ)-1/2) • a + (1/2:ℝ) • b = (1/2:ℝ) • (a + b) := by
    funext i
    simp only [Pi.add_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
    ring
  rw [he] at h
  linarith

/-! #### ℓ¹ -/

lemma l1_nonneg (x : Fin n → ℝ) : 0 ≤ l1Norm x :=
  Finset.sum_nonneg fun i _ => abs_nonneg _

lemma l1_zero : l1Norm (0 : Fin n → ℝ) = 0 := by simp [l1Norm]

lemma l1_tri (a b : Fin n → ℝ) : l1Norm (a + b) ≤ l1Norm a + l1Norm b := by
  simp only [l1Norm, Pi.add_apply, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => abs_add_le _ _

lemma l1_hom (c : ℝ) (a : Fin n → ℝ) (hc : 0 ≤ c) : l1Norm (c • a) = c * l1Norm a := by
  simp only [l1Norm, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg hc, Finset.mul_sum]

/-! #### ℓ² -/

lemma l2_nonneg (x : Fin n → ℝ) : 0 ≤ l2Norm x := Real.sqrt_nonneg _

lemma l2_sq (x : Fin n → ℝ) : (l2Norm x)^2 = sqL2 x := Real.sq_sqrt (sqL2_nonneg x)

lemma l2_zero : l2Norm (0 : Fin n → ℝ) = 0 := by simp [l2Norm, sqL2]

lemma dotp_le_l2 (a b : Fin n → ℝ) : dotp a b ≤ l2Norm a * l2Norm b := by
  have h := Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq Finset.univ a b
  have h2 : (dotp a b)^2 ≤ sqL2 a * sqL2 b := by simpa [dotp, sqL2] using h
  have h3 : dotp a b ≤ |dotp a b| := le_abs_self _
  have h4 : |dotp a b| ≤ l2Norm a * l2Norm b := by
    rw [l2Norm, l2Norm, ← Real.sqrt_mul (sqL2_nonneg a)]
    rw [show |dotp a b| = Real.sqrt ((dotp a b)^2) from (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs _).symm]
    exact Real.sqrt_le_sqrt h2
  linarith

lemma l2_tri (a b : Fin n → ℝ) : l2Norm (a + b) ≤ l2Norm a + l2Norm b := by
  have h1 : (l2Norm (a+b))^2 = sqL2 a + 2 * dotp a b + sqL2 b := by rw [l2_sq, sqL2_add]
  have h2 := dotp_le_l2 a b
  have h3 : (l2Norm (a+b))^2 ≤ (l2Norm a + l2Norm b)^2 := by
    rw [h1, ← l2_sq a, ← l2_sq b]; nlinarith
  have h4 : 0 ≤ l2Norm a + l2Norm b := by
    have := l2_nonneg a; have := l2_nonneg b; linarith
  nlinarith [l2_nonneg (a+b)]

lemma l2_hom (c : ℝ) (a : Fin n → ℝ) (hc : 0 ≤ c) : l2Norm (c • a) = c * l2Norm a := by
  have h : sqL2 (c • a) = c^2 * sqL2 a := by
    simp only [sqL2, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, Finset.mul_sum]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring
  rw [l2Norm, h, Real.sqrt_mul (by positivity), Real.sqrt_sq hc, l2Norm]

/-! #### ℓ^∞ -/

lemma linfty_nonneg (x : Fin n → ℝ) : 0 ≤ linftyNorm x := by
  rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty (Fin n) with he | hne
  · rw [linftyNorm, Real.iSup_of_isEmpty]
  · obtain ⟨i⟩ := hne
    show (0:ℝ) ≤ ⨆ j, |x j|
    exact le_trans (abs_nonneg (x i)) (le_ciSup (Finite.bddAbove_range fun j => |x j|) i)

lemma linfty_ge (x : Fin n → ℝ) (i : Fin n) : |x i| ≤ linftyNorm x :=
  le_ciSup (Finite.bddAbove_range fun j => |x j|) i

lemma linfty_le {x : Fin n → ℝ} {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) (h : ∀ i, |x i| ≤ c) :
    linftyNorm x ≤ c := by
  rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty (Fin n) with he | hne
  · rw [linftyNorm, Real.iSup_of_isEmpty]; exact hc
  · exact ciSup_le h

lemma linfty_zero : linftyNorm (0 : Fin n → ℝ) = 0 :=
  le_antisymm (linfty_le le_rfl (by simp)) (linfty_nonneg _)

lemma linfty_tri (a b : Fin n → ℝ) : linftyNorm (a + b) ≤ linftyNorm a + linftyNorm b := by
  apply linfty_le
  · have := linfty_nonneg a; have := linfty_nonneg b; linarith
  · intro i
    calc |(a + b) i| = |a i + b i| := rfl
      _ ≤ |a i| + |b i| := abs_add_le _ _
      _ ≤ linftyNorm a + linftyNorm b := add_le_add (linfty_ge a i) (linfty_ge b i)

lemma linfty_hom (c : ℝ) (a : Fin n → ℝ) (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
    linftyNorm (c • a) = c * linftyNorm a := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · apply linfty_le (by have := linfty_nonneg a; positivity)
    intro i
    calc |(c • a) i| = c * |a i| := by
          simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg hc]
      _ ≤ c * linftyNorm a := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (linfty_ge a i) hc
  · rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hc with h | h
    · rw [← h]; simp [linfty_nonneg]
    · have hb : linftyNorm a ≤ (linftyNorm (c • a))/c := by
        apply linfty_le (by have := linfty_nonneg (c • a); positivity)
        intro i
        rw [le_div_iff₀ h]
        calc |a i| * c = |(c • a) i| := by
              simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg hc]; ring
          _ ≤ linftyNorm (c • a) := linfty_ge _ i
      rw [le_div_iff₀ h] at hb
      linarith [hb]

/-! #### The alignment (★) inequalities -/

lemma dotp_single (a : Fin n → ℝ) (i : Fin n) (c : ℝ) :
    dotp a (fun j => if j = i then c else 0) = a i * c := by
  simp [dotp, mul_ite, Finset.sum_ite_eq']

lemma l1_single (i : Fin n) (c : ℝ) : l1Norm (fun j => if j = i then c else 0) = |c| := by
  simp [l1Norm, apply_ite (fun t : ℝ => |t|), Finset.sum_ite_eq']

lemma coord_bound {l : ℝ} {p : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hd : ∀ v, dotp p v ≤ l * l1Norm v) (i : Fin n) : |p i| ≤ l := by
  rcases le_or_gt 0 (p i) with h | h
  · have hx := hd (fun j => if j = i then 1 else 0)
    rw [dotp_single, l1_single] at hx
    rw [abs_of_nonneg h]
    simpa using hx
  · have hx := hd (fun j => if j = i then -1 else 0)
    rw [dotp_single, l1_single] at hx
    rw [abs_of_neg h]
    simp at hx
    linarith

lemma termwise_eq_l1 {l : ℝ} {p yv : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hb : ∀ i, |p i| ≤ l) (ha : dotp p yv = l * l1Norm yv) :
    ∀ i, p i * yv i = l * |yv i| := by
  have hnn : ∀ i ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)), 0 ≤ l * |yv i| - p i * yv i := by
    intro i _
    have h1 : p i * yv i ≤ |p i * yv i| := le_abs_self _
    have h2 : |p i * yv i| = |p i| * |yv i| := abs_mul _ _
    have h3 : |p i| * |yv i| ≤ l * |yv i| := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hb i) (abs_nonneg _)
    linarith
  have hsum : ∑ i, (l * |yv i| - p i * yv i) = 0 := by
    have he : ∑ i, (l * |yv i| - p i * yv i) = l * l1Norm yv - dotp p yv := by
      simp only [l1Norm, dotp, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    rw [he, ha]; ring
  intro i
  have := (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg hnn).mp hsum i (Finset.mem_univ i)
  linarith

lemma star_l1 {l1 l2 : ℝ} (hl1 : 0 ≤ l1) (hl2 : 0 ≤ l2) {x y z : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hd1 : ∀ v, dotp (x - y) v ≤ l1 * l1Norm v)
    (ha1 : dotp (x - y) y = l1 * l1Norm y)
    (hd2 : ∀ v, dotp (y - z) v ≤ l2 * l1Norm v)
    (ha2 : dotp (y - z) z = l2 * l1Norm z) :
    l1 * l1Norm z ≤ dotp (x - y) z := by
  have hb1 : ∀ i, |(x - y) i| ≤ l1 := coord_bound hd1
  have hb2 : ∀ i, |(y - z) i| ≤ l2 := coord_bound hd2
  have k1 : ∀ i, (x - y) i * y i = l1 * |y i| := termwise_eq_l1 hb1 ha1
  have k2 : ∀ i, (y - z) i * z i = l2 * |z i| := termwise_eq_l1 hb2 ha2
  have main : ∀ i, l1 * |z i| ≤ (x - y) i * z i := by
    intro i
    have e1 := k1 i
    have e2 := k2 i
    simp only [Pi.sub_apply] at e1 e2 ⊢
    rcases lt_trichotomy (z i) 0 with h | h | h
    · rw [abs_of_neg h] at e2
      have hz0 : z i ≠ 0 := ne_of_lt h
      have hfac : (y i - z i + l2) * z i = 0 := by nlinarith [e2]
      have hy : y i = z i - l2 := by
        rcases mul_eq_zero.mp hfac with h' | h'
        · linarith
        · exact absurd h' hz0
      rw [hy, abs_of_neg (show z i - l2 < 0 by linarith)] at e1
      have hfac2 : (x i - (z i - l2) + l1) * (z i - l2) = 0 := by nlinarith [e1]
      have hzl : z i - l2 ≠ 0 := by intro hc; linarith
      have ha : x i - (z i - l2) = -l1 := by
        rcases mul_eq_zero.mp hfac2 with h' | h'
        · linarith
        · exact absurd h' hzl
      rw [hy, ha, abs_of_neg h]
      nlinarith
    · rw [h]; simp
    · rw [abs_of_pos h] at e2
      have hz0 : z i ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt h
      have hfac : (y i - z i - l2) * z i = 0 := by nlinarith [e2]
      have hy : y i = z i + l2 := by
        rcases mul_eq_zero.mp hfac with h' | h'
        · linarith
        · exact absurd h' hz0
      rw [hy, abs_of_pos (show (0:ℝ) < z i + l2 by linarith)] at e1
      have hfac2 : (x i - (z i + l2) - l1) * (z i + l2) = 0 := by nlinarith [e1]
      have hzl : z i + l2 ≠ 0 := by intro hc; linarith
      have ha : x i - (z i + l2) = l1 := by
        rcases mul_eq_zero.mp hfac2 with h' | h'
        · linarith
        · exact absurd h' hzl
      rw [hy, ha, abs_of_pos h]
  calc l1 * l1Norm z = ∑ i, l1 * |z i| := by simp only [l1Norm, Finset.mul_sum]
    _ ≤ ∑ i, (x - y) i * z i := Finset.sum_le_sum (fun i _ => main i)
    _ = dotp (x - y) z := rfl

lemma star_l2 {l1 l2 : ℝ} (hl1 : 0 ≤ l1) (hl2 : 0 ≤ l2) {x y z : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hd1 : ∀ v, dotp (x - y) v ≤ l1 * l2Norm v)
    (ha1 : dotp (x - y) y = l1 * l2Norm y)
    (hd2 : ∀ v, dotp (y - z) v ≤ l2 * l2Norm v)
    (ha2 : dotp (y - z) z = l2 * l2Norm z) :
    l1 * l2Norm z ≤ dotp (x - y) z := by
  have hp : l2Norm (x - y) ≤ l1 := by
    have h := hd1 (x - y)
    rw [dotp_self, ← l2_sq] at h
    rcases eq_or_lt_of_le (l2_nonneg (x-y)) with hh | hh
    · rw [← hh]; exact hl1
    · nlinarith
  have hq : l2Norm (y - z) ≤ l2 := by
    have h := hd2 (y - z)
    rw [dotp_self, ← l2_sq] at h
    rcases eq_or_lt_of_le (l2_nonneg (y-z)) with hh | hh
    · rw [← hh]; exact hl2
    · nlinarith
  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le (l2_nonneg z) with hz | hz
  · have hs : sqL2 z = 0 := by rw [← l2_sq, ← hz]; ring
    have hz0 : z = 0 := sqL2_eq_zero hs
    rw [← hz, hz0]
    simp [dotp]
  · have hq2 : l2 ≤ l2Norm (y - z) := by
      have h := dotp_le_l2 (y - z) z
      rw [ha2] at h
      nlinarith
    have hqe : l2Norm (y - z) = l2 := le_antisymm hq hq2
    have hyzq : y = z + (y - z) := by funext i; simp
    have hny : (l2Norm y)^2 = (l2Norm z + l2)^2 := by
      rw [l2_sq]
      nth_rewrite 1 [hyzq]
      rw [sqL2_add, ← l2_sq z, ← l2_sq (y - z), hqe, dotp_comm z (y - z), ha2]
      ring
    have hnyv : l2Norm y = l2Norm z + l2 := by
      nlinarith [l2_nonneg y, l2_nonneg z]
    have hsplit : dotp (x - y) z = dotp (x - y) y - dotp (x - y) (y - z) := by
      rw [← dotp_sub_right]
      congr 1
      funext i; simp
    have hpq : dotp (x - y) (y - z) ≤ l2Norm (x - y) * l2Norm (y - z) := dotp_le_l2 _ _
    rw [hsplit, ha1, hnyv]
    rw [hqe] at hpq
    nlinarith [hp, l2_nonneg z, hl1, hl2]

lemma l1Norm_le_of_dual {l : ℝ} (hl : 0 ≤ l) {p : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hd : ∀ v, dotp p v ≤ l * linftyNorm v) : l1Norm p ≤ l := by
  set v : Fin n → ℝ := fun j => if 0 ≤ p j then (1:ℝ) else -1 with hv
  have hdv : dotp p v = l1Norm p := by
    simp only [dotp, l1Norm, hv]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    by_cases h : 0 ≤ p i
    · simp [h, abs_of_nonneg h]
    · rw [if_neg h, abs_of_neg (not_le.mp h)]; ring
  have hlv : linftyNorm v ≤ 1 := by
    apply linfty_le zero_le_one
    intro i
    by_cases h : 0 ≤ p i <;> simp [hv, h]
  have hfin := hd v
  rw [hdv] at hfin
  nlinarith [hfin, hlv, hl]

lemma termwise_linfty {l M : ℝ} {p yv : Fin n → ℝ} (hM : M = linftyNorm yv) (hMpos : 0 < M)
    (hp1 : l1Norm p ≤ l) (ha : dotp p yv = l * M) :
    (∀ i, p i * yv i = |p i| * M) ∧ l1Norm p = l := by
  have hnn : ∀ i ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)), 0 ≤ |p i| * M - p i * yv i := by
    intro i _
    have h1 : p i * yv i ≤ |p i * yv i| := le_abs_self _
    have h2 : |p i * yv i| = |p i| * |yv i| := abs_mul _ _
    have h3 : |yv i| ≤ M := hM ▸ linfty_ge yv i
    nlinarith [abs_nonneg (p i)]
  have he : ∑ i, (|p i| * M - p i * yv i) = l1Norm p * M - dotp p yv := by
    simp only [l1Norm, dotp, Finset.sum_mul, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
  rw [ha] at he
  have hge : 0 ≤ ∑ i, (|p i| * M - p i * yv i) := Finset.sum_nonneg hnn
  have hl1eq : l1Norm p = l := by
    rw [he] at hge
    nlinarith
  have hzero : ∑ i, (|p i| * M - p i * yv i) = 0 := by rw [he, hl1eq]; ring
  refine ⟨fun i => ?_, hl1eq⟩
  have := (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg hnn).mp hzero i (Finset.mem_univ i)
  linarith

lemma star_linfty {l1 l2 : ℝ} (hl1 : 0 ≤ l1) (hl2 : 0 ≤ l2) {x y z : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hd1 : ∀ v, dotp (x - y) v ≤ l1 * linftyNorm v)
    (ha1 : dotp (x - y) y = l1 * linftyNorm y)
    (hd2 : ∀ v, dotp (y - z) v ≤ l2 * linftyNorm v)
    (ha2 : dotp (y - z) z = l2 * linftyNorm z)
    (hmono : linftyNorm z ≤ linftyNorm y) :
    l1 * linftyNorm z ≤ dotp (x - y) z := by
  have hp1 : l1Norm (x - y) ≤ l1 := l1Norm_le_of_dual hl1 hd1
  have hq1 : l1Norm (y - z) ≤ l2 := l1Norm_le_of_dual hl2 hd2
  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le (linfty_nonneg z) with hth | hth
  · have hz0 : z = 0 := by
      funext i
      have h1 : |z i| ≤ linftyNorm z := linfty_ge z i
      rw [← hth] at h1
      have h2 := abs_nonneg (z i)
      have h3 : |z i| = 0 := le_antisymm h1 h2
      simpa using abs_eq_zero.mp h3
    rw [← hth, hz0]
    simp [dotp]
  · have hMpos : 0 < linftyNorm y := lt_of_lt_of_le hth hmono
    obtain ⟨k1, hl1eq⟩ := termwise_linfty (rfl) hMpos hp1 ha1
    obtain ⟨k2, hl2eq⟩ := termwise_linfty (rfl) hth hq1 ha2
    have main : ∀ i, (x - y) i * z i = |(x - y) i| * linftyNorm z := by
      intro i
      set p := (x - y) i with hp
      set q := (y - z) i with hq
      have hpy : p * y i = |p| * linftyNorm y := k1 i
      have hqz : q * z i = |q| * linftyNorm z := k2 i
      have hqdef : q = y i - z i := rfl
      by_cases hp0 : p = 0
      · rw [hp0]; simp
      · by_cases hq0 : q = 0
        · have hzy : z i = y i := by rw [hqdef] at hq0; linarith
          have hpabs : 0 < |p| := abs_pos.mpr hp0
          have habs : |p| * linftyNorm y ≤ |p| * |y i| := by
            have h0 : p * y i ≤ |p| * |y i| := by
              calc p * y i ≤ |p * y i| := le_abs_self _
                _ = |p| * |y i| := abs_mul _ _
            rw [hpy] at h0
            exact h0
          have hyM : linftyNorm y ≤ |y i| := le_of_mul_le_mul_left habs hpabs
          have hyM2 : |y i| ≤ linftyNorm y := linfty_ge y i
          have hyeq : |y i| = linftyNorm y := le_antisymm hyM2 hyM
          have hzi : |z i| ≤ linftyNorm z := linfty_ge z i
          rw [hzy] at hzi
          have hMth : linftyNorm y = linftyNorm z := by
            rw [hyeq] at hzi; linarith
          rw [hzy, ← hMth]
          exact hpy
        · have hqabs : 0 < |q| := abs_pos.mpr hq0
          rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hq0 with hqneg | hqpos
          · have hzi : z i = -linftyNorm z := by
              rw [abs_of_neg hqneg] at hqz
              have hh : q * (z i + linftyNorm z) = 0 := by nlinarith [hqz]
              rcases mul_eq_zero.mp hh with h | h
              · exact absurd h hq0
              · linarith
            have hyi : y i = -linftyNorm z + q := by rw [hqdef] at *; linarith
            have hyneg : y i < 0 := by
              rw [hyi]; have := linfty_nonneg z; linarith
            have hpneg : p < 0 := by
              rcases lt_trichotomy p 0 with h | h | h
              · exact h
              · exact absurd h hp0
              · exfalso
                have h1 : 0 < |p| * linftyNorm y := by positivity
                nlinarith [hpy]
            rw [hzi, abs_of_neg hpneg]
            ring
          · have hzi : z i = linftyNorm z := by
              rw [abs_of_pos hqpos] at hqz
              have hh : q * (z i - linftyNorm z) = 0 := by nlinarith [hqz]
              rcases mul_eq_zero.mp hh with h | h
              · exact absurd h hq0
              · linarith
            have hyi : y i = linftyNorm z + q := by rw [hqdef] at *; linarith
            have hypos : 0 < y i := by
              rw [hyi]; have := linfty_nonneg z; linarith
            have hppos : 0 < p := by
              rcases lt_trichotomy p 0 with h | h | h
              · exfalso
                have h1 : 0 < |p| * linftyNorm y := by
                  have : 0 < |p| := abs_pos.mpr hp0
                  positivity
                nlinarith [hpy]
              · exact absurd h hp0
              · exact h
            rw [hzi, abs_of_pos hppos]
    have heq : l1 * linftyNorm z = dotp (x - y) z := by
