### Proof of Theorem 7

To prove (3), it suffices to show that applying the DRERM with a sample size m of the same order as in (3) yields an ε, δ-learner for $\mathcal{H}$.

Proof [Proof of Lemma 5] By definition, $g_{2}(\eta,P)=\eta$ for $\eta \geq 1$ , and

$$
\begin{array}{c}{{g_{2}\left(-\displaystyle\frac{1}{c_{2}-1},P\right)\ge\displaystyle\frac{c_{2}}{c_{2}-1}-\displaystyle\frac{1}{c_{2}-1}}}\\ {{=1=g_{2}(1,P).}}\end{array}
$$

Since $\eta\mapsto g_{2}(\eta,P)$ is convex, this implies the result.

Proof [Proof of Theorem 7] The proof is a modification of the techniques utilized by Koltchinskii and Panchenko (2002). Let $(x_{1},y_{1}),\dots,(x_{m},y_{m})$ be a classification training set, $P_{m}$ denote the corresponding empirical distribution and $h^{*}\in\mathop{\mathrm{argmin}}_{h\in\mathcal{H}}R_{2}(h;P)$ . We begin by decomposing the excess risk:

$$
\begin{array}{r}{R_{2}(\hat{h};P)-R_{2}(h^{*};P)\le R_{2}(\hat{h};P)-R_{2}(\hat{h};P_{m})+R_{2}(h^{*};P_{m})-R_{2}(h^{*};P),}\end{array}
$$

where the last step follows from the definition of $\hat{h}$ Define

$$
\hat{\eta}: =\underset{\eta\in\mathbb{R}}{\mathrm{argmin}}\left\{c_{2}\mathbb{E}_{P_{m}}\left[\left(\varphi_{\eta,\hat{h}}(x,y)\right)_{+}^{2}\right]^{1/2}+\eta\right\},
$$

$$
\eta^{*}: =\underset{\eta\in\mathbb{R}}{\mathrm{argmin}}\left\{c_{2}\mathbb{E}_{P}\left[\left(\varphi_{\eta,h^{*}}(x,y)\right)_{+}^{2}\right]^{1/2}+\eta\right\}.
$$

We can then write

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{R_{2}(\hat{h};P)-R_{2}(\hat{h};P_{m})=\underset{\eta\in\mathbb{R}}{\operatorname*{min}}\left\{c_{2}\mathbb{E}_{P}\left[\left(\varphi_{\eta,\hat{h}}(x,y)\right)_{+}^{2}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}+\eta\right\}-\left(c_{2}\mathbb{E}_{P_{m}}\left[\left(\varphi_{\hat{\eta},\hat{h}}(x,y)\right)_{+}^{2}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}+\hat{\eta}\right)}\\ &{\leq c_{2}\left(\mathbb{E}_{P}\left[\left(\varphi_{\hat{\eta},\hat{h}}(x,y)\right)_{+}^{2}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}-\mathbb{E}_{P_{m}}\left[\left(\varphi_{\hat{\eta},\hat{h}}(x,y)\right)_{+}^{2}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)}\\ &{\leq c_{2}\left|\int\left(\varphi_{\hat{\eta},\hat{h}}(x,y)\right)_{+}^{2}\left(P_{m}-P\right)\left(d x d y\right)\right|^{\frac{1}{2}}.}\end{array}
$$

Following the same logic,

$$
R_{2}(h^{\ast};P_{m})-R_{2}(h^{\ast};P)\leq c_{2}\left|\int\left(\varphi_{\eta^{\ast},h^{\ast}}(x,y)\right)_{+}^{2}\left(P_{m}-P\right)(dxdy)\right|^{\frac{1}{2}}.\tag{15}
$$

By Lemma 5, $\hat{\eta}\in \left[ - \frac{1}{c_{2}- 1}, 1 \right]$ . We now define $\begin{array}{r}{\Phi=\left\{\varphi_{\eta,h}:h\in\mathcal{H},\eta\in\left[-\frac{1}{c_{2}-1},1\right]\right\},\psi(t)=t_{+}^{2}}\end{array}$ and $\psi \circ \Phi = \{\psi \circ \varphi: \varphi \in \Phi\}$ , where $\circ$ denotes the composition of functions. Thus, we can write

$$
R_{2}(\hat{h};P)-R_{2}(\hat{h};P_{m})\leq c_{2}\left(\operatorname*{sup}_{\varphi\in\psi\circ\Phi}\left[\int\varphi(x,y)\left(P-P_{m}\right)(d x d y)\right]\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}.
$$

Since $\mathbb{1}\left[h(x)\neq y\right]\in\left[0,1\right]$ for any $h \in \mathcal H$ and $\begin{array}{r}{\eta \in \left[ - \frac{1}{c_{k}- 1}, 1 \right]}\end{array}$ , then for any $\varphi \in \psi \circ \Phi$ , we have $\begin{array}{r}{\|\varphi\|_{\infty}\le\left(\frac{c_{2}}{c_{2}-1}\right)^{2}}\end{array}$

By a standard symmetrization argument, with probability of at least $1 - \delta / 2$

$$
R_{2}({\hat{h}};P)-R_{2}({\hat{h}};P_{m})\leq c_{2}\left(2\mathcal{R}_{m}(\psi\circ\Phi)+\left(\frac{c_{2}}{c_{2}-1}\right)^{2}\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2/\delta)}{m}}\right)^{\frac 12}
$$

Moreover, from (15) and Hoeffding's inequality, it follows that

$$
R_{2}(h^{\ast};P_{m})-R_{2}(h^{\ast};P)\leq\frac{c_{2}}{c_{2}-1}\left(\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}},\tag{16}
$$

with probability of at least $1 - \delta / 2$

Combining these results, with probability of at least $1 - \delta .$

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{R_{2}(\hat{h};P)-R_{2}(h^{*};P)\leq c_{2}\left[\left(2\mathcal{R}_{m}(\psi\circ\Phi)+\left(\frac{c_{2}}{c_{2}-1}\right)^{2}\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2/\delta)}{m}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}+\frac{c_{2}}{c_{2}-1}\left(\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\right]}\\ &{\qquad\leq c_{2}\left[2\left(\mathcal{R}_{m}(\psi\circ\Phi)\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}+\frac{3c_{2}}{c_{2}-1}\left(\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\right].}\end{array}\tag{17}
$$

Therefore, it suffices to bound $\mathcal{R}_{m}(\psi\circ\Phi)$ . It can be readily observed that $t \mapsto t_{+}^{2}$ is $\displaystyle \frac{2 c_{2}}{c_{2}- 1}$ -Lipschitz on $\textstyle\left[-1,{\frac{c_{2}}{c_{2}-1}}\right]$ ; thus, by invoking Lemma 21, we get:

$$
\mathcal{R}_{m}(\psi\circ\Phi)\leq\frac{2c_{2}}{c_{2}-1}\mathcal{R}_{m}(\Phi).\tag{18}
$$

More specifically,

$$
\begin{array}{r l}\mathcal{R}_{m}(\Phi)&=\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{1}{m}\sup_{h\in\mathcal{H},\eta\in\left[-\frac{1}{c_{2}-1},1\right]}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sigma_{i}\left(\mathbb{1}[h(x)\neq y]-\eta\right)\right]\\ &\le\mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{h\in\mathcal{H}}\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sigma_{i}\mathbb{1}[h(x)\neq y]\right]+\mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{\eta\in\left[-\frac{1}{c_{2}-1},1\right]}\frac{1}{m}\left|\sum_{i=1}^{m}\eta\sigma_{i}\right|\right]\\ &\le\mathcal{R}_{m}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{H}})+\frac{1}{m}\left(\frac{1}{c_{2}-1}\vee 1\right)\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sigma_{i}\right|\right]\\ &\le\mathcal{R}_{m}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{H}})+\frac{1}{m}\left(\frac{1}{c_{2}-1}\vee 1\right)\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sigma_{i}\right)^{2}\right]^{1/2}\\ &\le\mathcal{R}_{m}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{H}})+\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\left(\frac{1}{c_{2}-1}\vee 1\right).\end{array}\tag{19}
$$

To bound $\mathcal{R}_{m}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{H}})$ , we define $\begin{array}{r}{R(A)=\mathbb{E}_{\sigma}\left[\operatorname*{sup}_{h\in\mathcal{H}}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sigma_{i}\mathbb{1}\left[h(x_{i})\neq y_{i}\right]\right]}\end{array}$

Recall that the Sauer-Shelah lemma (Shalev-Shwartz and Ben-David, 2014, Lemma 6.10) tells us that if $\operatorname{vc}(\mathcal{H})=d.$ then

$$
|\{(h(x_{1}),\ldots,h(x_{m})):h\in\mathcal{H}\}|\leq\left(\frac{em}{d}\right)^{d}.
$$

By the Massart Lemma (Shalev-Shwartz and Ben-David, 2014, Lemma 26.8), we have:

$$
\mathcal{R}_{m}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{H}})\leq\sqrt{\frac{2d\log(em/d)}{m}}\tag{20}
$$

Combining (17), (18), (19) and (20), the following holds:

$$
R_{2}({\hat{h}};P)-R_{2}(h^{*};P)\leq C\left({\frac{2d\log(em/d)+\left({\frac{1}{c_{2}-1}}\vee 1\right)^{2}+\log(2/\delta)}{m}}\right)^{1/4}\tag{21}
$$

for some constant C. To ensure that the right-hand side of (21) is smaller than ε, we need:

$$
m\geq\frac{C}{\varepsilon^{4}}\left(d\log(m)+d\log(e/d)+\left(\frac{1}{c_{2}-1}\vee 1\right)^{2}+\log(2/\delta)\right).
$$

Using Lemma 22, a sufficient condition for the inequality to hold is that

$$
m\geq\frac{4Cd}{\varepsilon^{4}}\log(\frac{2Cd}{\varepsilon^{4}})+\frac{2C}{\varepsilon^{4}}\left(\left(\frac{1}{c_{2}-1}\vee 1\right)^{2}+d\log(e/d)+\log(2/\delta)\right),
$$

which concludes our proof.

### Proof of Theorem 9

Proof [Proof of Theorem 9] We will prove the lower bound in two parts. First, we will show that $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{AG}}(\varepsilon,\delta;\mathcal{H},\mathcal{U})\ge\log(\frac{1}{4\delta})/(2\varepsilon^{2})$ ; second, we will show that for every $\delta \leq 1 / 8$ ,we have that $\begin{array}{r}{\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{AG}}(\varepsilon,1/8;\mathcal{H},\mathcal{U})\ge\frac{\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{16}\rho^{1/2}\right)^{2}d}{128\varepsilon^{2}}}\end{array}$ These two bounds will conclude the proof.

We first demonstrate that $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{AG}}(\varepsilon,\delta;\mathcal{H},\mathcal{U})\ge\log(\frac{1}{4\delta})/(2\varepsilon^{2})$

To do so, we show that for a sample with size $\begin{array}{r}{m\leq\log(\frac{1}{4\delta})/(2\varepsilon^{2})}\end{array}$ , $\mathcal{H}$ is not learnable for any $\varepsilon\in\left(0,{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\right)$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$

Let us choose one example that is shattered by $\mathcal{H}$. That is, let c be an example such that there are $h_{+}, h_{-}\in \mathcal{H}$ for which $h_{+}(c)=1$ and $h_{-}(c)= -1$ . Define two distributions, $P_{+}$ and $P_{-}$ , such that for $b\in\{+1,-1\}$ , we have

$$
P_{b}(x,y)=\left\{\begin{array}{l l}{\displaystyle\frac{1+yb\varepsilon}{2},\quad\mathrm{if}\quad x=c,}\\ {\displaystyle~0\quad,\quad\mathrm{otherwise}.}\end{array}\right.
$$

Any training set sampled from $P_{b}$ has the form $S=((c,y_{1}),\dots,(c,y_{m}))$ . Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an arbitrary algorithm. Therefore, the hypothesis that $\mathcal{A}$ outputs receiving sample $S$ is fully characterized by the vector $\mathbf{y}=(y_{1},\dots,y_{m})\in\{+1,-1\}^{m}$ . Upon receiving a training set $S,$ the algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ returns a hypothesis $h_{S}:\mathcal{X}\to\{+1,-1\}$ . Since the error of $h_{S}$ w.r.t. $P_{b}$ depends only on $h(c)$ , we can think of $\mathcal{A}$ as a mapping from $\{+1,-1\}^{m}$ into $\{+1,-1\}$

Therefore, we denote by $\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y})$ the value in $\{+1,-1\}$ corresponding to the prediction $h_{S}(c)$ ; here, $h_{S}$ is the hypothesis that $\mathcal{A}$ outputs upon receiving the training set $S =$ $((c,y_{1}),\dots,(c,y_{m}))$ . Claim 1. The hypothesis $h_{b}(c)=b$ has optimal distributionally robust risk on $P_{b}$

Note that for any hypothesis h, we have

$$
\begin{array}{r l}R_{2}(h;P_{b})&=\sup\big\{\mathbb{E}_{P}\big [\mathbb{1}[h(x)\neq y]\big]:P\ll P_{b},D_{2}(P\|P_{b})\le\rho\big\}\\ &=\inf_{\eta\in\mathbb{R}}\Big\{c_{2}(\rho)\mathbb{E}_{P_{b}}\Big [(\mathbb{1}[h(x)\neq y]-\eta)_{+}^{2}\Big]^{1/2}+\eta\Big\}\\ &=\inf_{\eta\in\mathbb{R}}\Big\{c_{2}(\rho)\Big(\frac{1+\varepsilon}{2}(\mathbb{1}[h(c)\neq b]-\eta)_{+}^{2}+\frac{1-\varepsilon}{2}(\mathbb{1}[h(c)\neq-b]-\eta)^{2}\Big)^{1/2}+\eta\Big\}.\end{array}
$$

Substituting $h_{b}$ into the above formulation, we obtain:

$$
R_{2}(h_{b};P_{b})=\operatorname*{inf}_{\eta\in\mathbb{R}}\Big\{c_{2}(\rho)\Big(\frac{1+\varepsilon}{2}(-\eta)_{+}^{2}+\frac{1-\varepsilon}{2}(1-\eta)_{+}^{2}\Big)^{1/2}+\eta\Big\}.
$$

Noting that $(-\eta)_{+}^{2}\leq(1-\eta)_{+}^{2}$ , we get $R_{2}(h_{b};P_{b})\le R_{2}(h;P_{b})$ for any $h \in \mathcal H$

Invoking Lemma 23, we have

$$
R_{2}(\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y});P_{b})-\inf_{h\in\mathcal{H}}R_{2}(h;P_{b})=\begin{cases}\varepsilon,&\text{if }\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y})(c)\neq b,\\ 0,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
$$

Fix $\mathcal{A}$. For $b\in\{+1,-1\}$ , let $Y^{b}=\{\mathbf{y}\in\{+1,-1\}^{m}:\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y})\neq b\}$ . The distribution $P_{b}$ induces a probability $\mathcal{D}_{b}$ over $\{+1,-1\}^{m}$ Hence,

$$
\mathbb{P}\left[R_{2}(\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y});P_{b})-R_{2}(h_{b};P_{b})=\varepsilon\right]=P_{b}(Y^{b})=\sum_{\mathbf{y}}\mathcal{D}_{b}[\mathbf{y}]\mathbb{1}[\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y})\neq b].
$$

Denote $N^{+}= \{\mathbf{y}: | \{i : y_{i}= + 1 \}| \geq m / 2 \}$ and $N^{-}=\{+1,-1\}^{m}\backslash N^{+}$ . Note that for any $\mathbf{y}\in N^{+}$ , we have ${\mathcal{D}}_{+}[ \mathbf{y}]{\geq}{\mathcal{D}}_{-}[ \mathbf{y}]$ , while for any $\mathbf{y}\in N^{-}$ , we have ${\mathcal{D}}_{-}[ \mathbf{y}]{\geq}{\mathcal{D}}_{+}[ \mathbf{y}]$ . Therefore,

$$
\begin{array}{r l}\max_{b\in\{+1,-1\}}\mathbb{P}\left[R_{2}(\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y});P_{b})-R_{2}(h_{b};P_{b})=\varepsilon\right]&=\max_{b\in\{+1,-1\}}\sum_{\mathbf{y}}\mathcal{D}_{b}[\mathbf{y}]\mathbb{1}[\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y})\neq b]\\ &\geq\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\mathbf{y}}\mathcal{D}_{+}[\mathbf{y}]\mathbb{1}[\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y})\neq+1]+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\mathbf{y}}\mathcal{D}_{-}[\mathbf{y}]\mathbb{1}[\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y})\neq-1]\\ &=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\mathbf{y}\in N^{+}}\left(\mathcal{D}_{+}[\mathbf{y}]\mathbb{1}[\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y})\neq+1]+\mathcal{D}_{-}[\mathbf{y}]\mathbb{1}[\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y})\neq-1]\right)\\ &\quad+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\mathbf{y}\in N^{-}}\left(\mathcal{D}_{+}[\mathbf{y}]\mathbb{1}[\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y})\neq+1]+\mathcal{D}_{-}[\mathbf{y}]\mathbb{1}[\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y})\neq-1]\right)\\ &\geq\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\mathbf{y}\in N^{+}}\left(\mathcal{D}_{-}[\mathbf{y}]\mathbb{1}[\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y})\neq+1]+\mathcal{D}_{-}[\mathbf{y}]\mathbb{1}[\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y})\neq-1]\right)\\ &\quad+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\mathbf{y}\in N^{-}}\left(\mathcal{D}_{+}[\mathbf{y}]\mathbb{1}[\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y})\neq+1]+\mathcal{D}_{+}[\mathbf{y}]\mathbb{1}[\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y})\neq-1]\right)\\ &=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\mathbf{y}\in N^{+}}\mathcal{D}_{-}[\mathbf{y}]+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\mathbf{y}\in N^{-}}\mathcal{D}_{+}[\mathbf{y}].\end{array}
$$

Next, note that $\begin{array}{r}{\sum_{\mathbf{y}\in N^{+}}\mathcal{D}_{-}[ \mathbf{y}] = \sum_{\mathbf{y}\in N^{-}}\mathcal{D}_{+}[ \mathbf{y}]}\end{array}$ , and both values are the probability that a Binomial $(m,(1-\varepsilon)/2)$ random variable will have a value greater than $m / 2$ . Using Lemma 24, this probability is lower bounded by

$$
\frac{1}{2}\left(1-\sqrt{1-\exp(-m\varepsilon^{2}/(1-\varepsilon^{2})}\right)\geq\frac{1}{2}\left(1-\sqrt{1-\exp(-2m\varepsilon^{2})}\right),
$$

where we derive under the assumption that $\varepsilon^{2}\leq 1 / 2$ It follows that if $m\leq 0.5\log(1/(4\delta))/\varepsilon^{2}$ then there exists b such that

$$
\mathbb{P}[R_{2}(\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{y});P_{b})-R_{2}(h_{b};P_{b})=\varepsilon]\ge\frac{1}{2}\left(1-\sqrt{1-\sqrt{4\delta}}\right)\ge\delta,
$$

where the last inequality can be obtained through standard algebraic manipulations. This concludes our proof.

Next, we demonstrate that $\begin{array}{r}{\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{AG}}(\varepsilon,1/8;\mathcal{H},\mathcal{U})\geq\frac{\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{16}\rho^{1/2}\right)^{2}d}{128\varepsilon^{2}}.}\end{array}$

We shall now prove that for every $\varepsilon < \frac{1}{8 \sqrt{2}}$ we have that $\begin{array}{r}{\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{AG}}(\varepsilon,\delta;\mathcal{H},\mathcal{U})\ge\frac{\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{16}\rho^{1/2}\right)^{2}d}{128\varepsilon^{2}}}\end{array}$ Let $r = 8 \varepsilon$ , and note that $r\in(0,1/\sqrt{2})$ . We will construct a family of distributions as follows. First, let $C=\{c_{1},\ldots,c_{d}\}$ be a set of d instances that are shattered by $\mathcal{H}$. Second, for each vector $\mathbf{b}=(b_{1},\ldots,b_{d})\in\{+1,-1\}^{d}$ , define a distribution $P_{\mathbf{b}}$ such that

$$
P_{\mathbf{b}}(x,y)=\left\{\begin{array}{l l}{\displaystyle\frac{1}{d}\cdot\frac{1+yb_{i}r}{2}}&{,\mathrm{if}\ \exists i:x=c_{i}}\\ {\qquad 0}&{,\mathrm{otherwise.}}\end{array}\right.
$$

That is, to sample an example according to $P_{\mathbf{b}}$ , we first sample an element $c_{i}\in C$ uniformly at random, then set the label to be $b_{i}$ with probability $(1+r)/2$ or $- b_{i}$ with probability $(1-r)/2$

Claim 2. The hypothesis $h_{\mathbf{b}}$ satisfying $h(c_{i})=b_{i},\forall i\in [d]$ , has the optimal distributionally robust risk on $P_{\mathbf{b}}$

Recalling the dual formulation (2), $R_{2}(h;{P_{\bf{b}}})$ can be rewritten as follows:

$$
R_{2}(h;P_{\mathbf{b}})=\operatorname*{inf}_{\eta\in\mathbb{R}}\left\{c_{2}\left[\frac{1}{d}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\left(\frac{1+r}{2}(\mathbb{1}[h(c_{i})\neq b_{i}]-\eta)_{+}^{2}+\frac{1-r}{2}(\mathbb{1}[h(c_{i})\neq-b_{i}]-\eta)_{+}^{2}\right)\right]^{1/2}+\eta\right\}.
$$

For each $i\in [d],h_{\mathbf{b}}(c_{i})=b_{i}$ , the summand above can be written as $\begin{array}{r}{\frac{1+r}{2}(-\eta)_{+}^{2}{+}\frac{1-r}{2}(1-\eta)_{+}^{2}}\end{array}$   
for $h(c_{i})\neq b_{i}$ , the summand is $\textstyle\frac{1+r}{2}(1-\eta)_{+}^{2}+\frac{1-r}{2}(-\eta)_{+}^{2}$ . Combining $r > 0$ and $(-\eta)_{+}^{2}\leq(1-\eta)_{+}^{2}$   
we have $\begin{array}{r}{\frac{1+r}{2}(-\eta)_{+}^{2}+\frac{1-r}{2}(1-\eta)_{+}^{2}\leq\frac{1+r}{2}(1-\eta)_{+}^{2}+\frac{1-r}{2}(-\eta)_{+}^{2}}\end{array}$ , which concludes our claim. We denote $d_{+}= |\{i\in [d]:\mathcal{A}(S)(c_{i})=b_{i}\}|$ and $d_{-}= |\{i\in [d]:{\cal A}(S)(c_{i})\neq b_{i}\}|$ , therefore $d_{+}+ d_{-}= d$. Next, we will simplify the distributionally robust risk as follows:

$$
\begin{array}{r l}R_{2}(\mathcal{A}(S);P_{\mathbf{b}})&=\inf_{\eta\in\mathbb{R}}\Bigg\{c_{2}\Bigg[\frac{d_{+}}{d}\left(\frac{1+r}{2}(-\eta)_{+}^{2}+\frac{1-r}{2}(1-\eta)_{+}^{2}\right)+\\ &\qquad\frac{d_{-}}{d}\left(\frac{1+r}{2}(1-\eta)_{+}^{2}+\frac{1-r}{2}(-\eta)_{+}^{2}\right)\Bigg]^{1/2}+\eta\Bigg\}\\ &=\inf_{\eta\in\mathbb{R}}\left\{c_{2}\left[\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{r}{2}\cdot\frac{d_{+}-d_{-}}{d}\right)(-\eta)_{+}^{2}+\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{r}{2}\cdot\frac{d_{+}-d_{-}}{d}\right)(1-\eta)_{+}^{2}\right]^{1/2}+\eta\right\}.\end{array}
$$

Therefore, $R_{2}(A(S);P_{\mathbf{b}})$ can be viewed as the distributionally robust risk of the classifier $h^{\prime}(x)\equiv 1$ on distribution $Q$ ,with

$$
Q(x,y)=\left\{\begin{array}{c l}{\frac{1+yr(d_{+}-d_{-})/d}{2}\quad}&{\mathrm{,if}x=c}\\ {0}&{\mathrm{,otherwise.}}\end{array}\right.
$$

Invoking Lemma 23, we obtain

$$
R_{2}(A(S);P_{\bf b})=\frac{1}{2}\left(1-r\cdot\frac{d_{+}-d_{-}}{d}+\sqrt{2\rho\left(1-r^{2}\cdot\frac{(d_{+}-d_{-})^{2}}{d^{2}}\right)}\right).
$$

Following the same logic, we have $\begin{array}{r}{R_{2}(h_{\mathbf{b}};P_{\mathbf{b}})=\frac{1}{2}\left(1-r+\sqrt{2\rho\left(1-r^{2}\right)}\right)}\end{array}$

Then, after some algebraic manipulations, we have:

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{R_{2}(A(S);P_{\mathbf{b}})-\underset{h\in\mathcal{H}}{\operatorname*{inf}}R_{2}(h;P_{\mathbf{b}})=R_{2}(A(S);P_{\mathbf{b}})-R_{2}(h_{\mathbf{b}};P_{\mathbf{b}})}\\ &{\qquad=r\cdot\frac{d_{-}}{d}+\frac{1}{2}\left(\sqrt{2\rho(1-r^{2}(d_{+}-d_{-})^{2}/d^{2})}-\sqrt{2\rho(1-r^{2})}\right)}\\ &{\qquad\geq r\cdot\frac{d_{-}}{d},}\end{array}\tag{9}
$$

where the last line follows from $(d_{+}-d_{-})^{2}/d^{2}\leq 1$

Next, fix some learning algorithm A, we have that:

$$
\operatorname*{max}_{P_{\mathbf{b}}:\mathbf{b}\in\{+1,-1\}^{d}}\underset{S\sim P_{\mathbf{b}}^{m}}{\mathbb{E}}\left[R_{2}(A(S);P_{\mathbf{b}})-\operatorname*{inf}_{h\in\mathcal{H}}R_{2}(h;P_{\mathbf{b}})\right]\tag{10}
$$

$$
\geq\underset{P_{\mathbf{b}}:\mathbf{b}\sim U(\{+1,-1\}^{d})}{\mathbb{E}}\underset{S\sim P_{\mathbf{b}}^{m}}{\mathbb{E}}\left[R_{2}(A(S);P_{\mathbf{b}})-\underset{h\in\mathcal{H}}{\operatorname*{inf}}\ R_{2}(h;P_{\mathbf{b}})\right]\tag{11}
$$

$$
\geq\underset{P_{\mathbf{b}}:\mathbf{b}\sim U(\{+1,-1\}^{d})}{\mathbb{E}}\underset{S\sim P_{\mathbf{b}}^{m}}{\mathbb{E}}\left[r\cdot{\frac{|\{i\in [d]:A(S)(c_{i})\neq b_{i}\}|}{d}}\right]\tag{12}
$$

$$
=\frac{r}{d}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\underset{P_{\mathbf{b}}:\mathbf{b}\sim U(\{+1,-1\}^{d})}{\mathbb{E}}\underset{S\sim P_{\mathbf{b}}^{m}}{\mathbb{E}}\mathbb{1}[A(S)(c_{i})\neq b_{i}],\tag{13}
$$

where the second inequality follows from (9). In addition, using the definition of $P_{\mathbf{b}}$ , in order to sample $S \sim P_{\mathbf{b}}$ , we can first sample $(j_{1},\ldots,j_{m})\sim U([d])^{m}$ , set $x_{i}= c_{j_{i}}$ , and finally sample $y_{i}$ such that $\mathbb{P}[y_{i}=b_{j_{i}}]=(1+r)/2$ Let us simplify the notation and use $y \sim b$ to denote sampling according to $\mathbb{P}[y=b]=(1+r)/2$ . Therefore, the right-hand side of (13) equals

$$
\frac{r}{d}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\underset{j\sim U([d])^{m}}{\mathbb{E}}\underset{\mathbf{b}\sim U(\{+1,-1\}^{d})}{\mathbb{E}}\underset{\forall k,y_{k}\sim b_{j_{k}}}{\mathbb{E}}\mathbb{1}[A(S)(c_{i})\neq b_{i}].\tag{14}
$$

We now proceed in two steps. First, in Lemma 25, we show that among all learning algorithms, A, the one that minimizes (14) is the Maximum-Likelihood learning rule, denoted as $\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{ML}}$ . Formally, for each $i,\ \mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{ML}}(S)(c_{i})$ is the majority vote among the set $\{y_{k}: k \in$ $[m],x_{k}=c_{i}\}$ . Second, we lower bound (14) for $\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{ML}}$

Fix i. For every $\mathbf{j}\in [ d ]^{m}$ , let $n_{i}(\mathbf{j})= |\{k:\mathbf{j}_{k}=i\}|$ be the number of instances in which the instance is $c_{i}$ . For the Maximum-Likelihood rule, we have that the quantity

$$
\underset{\mathbf{b}\sim U(\{+1,-1\}^{d})}{\mathbb{E}}\underset{\forall k,y_{k}\sim b_{j_{k}}}{\mathbb{E}}\mathbb{1}[A(S)(c_{i})\neq b_{i}]
$$

is exactly equal to the probability that a binomial $(n_{i}(\mathbf{j}),(1-r)/2)$ random variable will be larger than $n_{i}(\mathbf{j})/2$ . Using Lemma 24, and the assumption $r^{2}\leq 1 / 2$ , we have that

$$
\mathbb{P}[B\ge n_{i}(\mathbf{j})/2]\ge\frac{1}{2}\left(1-\sqrt{1-\exp\big(-2n_{i}(\mathbf{j})r^{2}\big)}\right).
$$

We have thus demonstrated that

$$
\frac{r}{d}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\underset{j\sim U([d])^{m}}{\mathbb{E}}\underset{\mathbf{b}\sim U(\{+1,-1\}^{d})}{\mathbb{E}}\underset{\forall k,y_{k}\sim b_{j_{k}}}{\mathbb{E}}\mathbb{1}[A(S)(c_{i})\neq b_{i}]
$$

$$
\geq\frac{r}{2d}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\underset{\mathbf{j}\sim U([d])^{m}}{\mathbb{E}}\left(1-\sqrt{1-\exp\big(-2n_{i}(\mathbf{j})r^{2}\big)}\right)
$$

$$
\geq\frac{r}{2d}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\underset{\mathbf{j}\sim U([d])^{m}}{\mathbb{E}}\left(1-\sqrt{2n_{i}(\mathbf{j})r^{2}}\right),
$$

where the last inequality follows from the fact that $1 - e^{- a}\leq a$

Since the square root function is concave, we can apply Jensen's inequality to obtain that the above is lower bounded by

$$
\begin{array}{l}{\displaystyle\frac{r}{2d}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\left(1-\sqrt{2r^{2}\underset{\mathbf{j}\sim U([d])^{m}}{\mathbb{E}}n_{i}(\mathbf{j})}\right)}\\ {\displaystyle\quad=\frac{r}{2d}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\left(1-\sqrt{2r^{2}m/d}\right)}\\ {\displaystyle=\frac{r}{2}\left(1-\sqrt{2r^{2}m/d}\right).}\end{array}
$$

As long as $m<\frac{{\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{16}\rho^{1/2}\right)}^{2}d}{2r^{2}}$ , this term will be larger than $\begin{array}{r}{\frac{r}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{2}r\rho^{1/2}}{32}}\end{array}$

In summary, we have shown that if $\begin{array}{r}{m<{\frac{\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{16}\rho^{1/2}\right)^{2}d}{2r^{2}}}}\end{array}$ then for any algorithm, there exists a distribution $P_{\mathbf{b}}$ such that

$$
\underset{S\sim P^{m}}{\mathbb{E}}\left[R_{2}(\mathcal{A}(S);P_{\mathbf{b}})-\underset{h\in\mathcal{H}}{\operatorname*{inf}}R_{2}(h;P_{\mathbf{b}})\right]\geq\frac{r}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{2}r\rho^{1/2}}{32}.
$$

Finally, let $\begin{array}{r}{\Delta=\frac{1}{r}\Big(R_{2}(A(S);P_{\mathbf{b}})-\operatorname*{inf}_{h\in\mathcal{H}}R_{2}(h;P_{\mathbf{b}})\Big)}\end{array}$ ; we proof that $\Delta\in [0,1+\sqrt{2}\rho^{1/2}/4]$ in Lemma 26. Therefore, using Lemma 27, we obtain that

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\mathbb{P}\left[R_{2}(\mathcal{A}(S);P_{\mathbf{b}})-\underset{h\in\mathcal{H}}{\operatorname*{inf}}R_{2}(h;P_{\mathbf{b}})\geq\epsilon\right]=\mathbb{P}\left[\Delta>\frac{\varepsilon}{r}\right]\geq\left(1+\sqrt{2}\rho^{1/2}/4\right)^{-1}\left(\mathbb{E}[\Delta]-\frac{\varepsilon}{r}\right)}\\ &{\qquad\geq\left(1+\sqrt{2}\rho^{1/2}/4\right)^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{2}\rho^{1/2}}{32}-\frac{\varepsilon}{r}\right).}\end{array}
$$

Choosing $r = 8 \varepsilon$ , we conclude that if $m<\frac{{\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{16}\rho^{1/2}\right)}^{2}d}{2r^{2}}$ , then with probability of at least $1 / 8 .$ ,we will have that $\begin{array}{r}{R_{2}(A(S);P_{\mathbf{b}})-\operatorname*{inf}_{h\in\mathcal{H}}R_{2}(h;P_{\mathbf{b}})\geq\epsilon}\end{array}$

Proof Recall the definition of $R_{2}(h;P_{b})=\operatorname*{sup}\big\{\mathbb{E}_{P}\big [\mathbb{1}[h(x)\neq y]\big]:P\ll P_{b},D_{2}(P\|P_{b})\le\rho\big\}$

We write P as

$$
P(x,y)=\left\{{\begin{array}{l l}{\displaystyle{\frac{1+\xi}{2}},}&{\text{if } x=c \text{ and } y=b,}\\ {\displaystyle{\frac{1-\xi}{2}},}&{\text{if } x=c \text{ and } y= -b,}\\ {\displaystyle 0}&{,\mathrm{otherwise}.}\end{array}}\right.
$$

Thus, $R_{2}(h;P_{b})$ can be rewritten as

$$
R_{2}(h;P_{b})=\operatorname*{sup}_{\xi}\left\{\frac{1+\xi}{2}\mathbb{1}[h(c)\neq b]+\frac{1-\xi}{2}\mathbb{1}[h(c)\neq-b]:\xi^{2}-2\varepsilon\xi+\varepsilon^{2}-2\rho(1-\varepsilon^{2})\leq 0,\ -1\leq\xi\leq 1\right\}.
$$

Solving the quadratic inequality in the above formulation, we get $\varepsilon-\sqrt{2\rho(1-\varepsilon^{2})}\le\xi\le$ $\varepsilon+\sqrt{2\rho(1-\varepsilon^{2})}$ . Since we assume $\textstyle\rho\in\left(0,{\frac{3-2{\sqrt{2}}}{2}}\right)$ and $\rho\in\left(0,\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$ , the left-hand and right-hand sides can both be achieved.

When $h(c)=b$ ,we have $\begin{array}{r}{\operatorname{er}(h;P)=\frac{1-\xi}{2}}\end{array}$ , and thus $\begin{array}{r}{R_{2}(h;P_{b})=\frac{1-\varepsilon+\sqrt{2\rho(1-\varepsilon^{2})}}{2}}\end{array}$ ; following the same logic, when $h(c)= -b$ ,we have $\begin{array}{r}{R_{2}(h;P_{b})=\frac{1+\varepsilon+\sqrt{2\rho(1-\varepsilon^{2})}}{2}}\end{array}$

Thus, we obtain the desired result.

Proof Fix some $\mathbf{j}\in [ d ]^{m}$ . Note that, given j and $\mathbf{y}\in\{+1,-1\}^{m}$ , the training set S is fully determined; we can therefore write $\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{j},\mathbf{y})$ instead of $\mathcal{A}(S)$ . Let us also fix $i \in [ d ]$ . Denote by $\mathbf{b}^{\lnot i}$ the sequence $( b_{1}, \hdots , b_{i - 1}, b_{i + 1}, \hdots , b_{m})$ . Also, for any $\mathbf{b}\in\{+1,-1\}^{m}$ , let $\mathbf{y}^{I}$ denote the elements of y corresponding to indices for which $j_{k}=i,$ ,and let $\mathbf{y}^{\lnot I}$ be the rest of the elements of y. We therefore have

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&\underset{\mathbf{b}\sim U(\{+1,-1\}^{d})}{\mathbb{E}}\underset{\forall k,y_{k}\sim b_{j_{k}}}{\mathbb{E}}\mathbb{1}[\mathcal{A}(S)(c_{i})\neq b_{i}]\\ &=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{b_{i}\in\{+1,-1\}}\underset{\mathbf{b}^{\neg i}\sim U(\{+1,-1\}^{d-1})}{\mathbb{E}}\sum_{\mathbf{y}}P[\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{b}^{\neg i},b_{i}]\mathbb{1}[\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{j},\mathbf{y})(c_{i})\neq b_{i}]\\ &=\underset{\mathbf{b}^{\neg i}\sim U(\{+1,-1\}^{d-1})}{\mathbb{E}}\sum_{\mathbf{y}^{\neg I}}P[\mathbf{y}^{\neg I}|\mathbf{b}^{\neg i}]\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\mathbf{y}^{I}}\left(\sum_{b_{i}\in\{+1,-1\}}P[\mathbf{y}^{I}|\mathbf{b}_{i}]\mathbb{1}[\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{j},\mathbf{y})(c_{i})\neq b_{i}]\right).\end{array}
$$

The sum within the parentheses is minimized when $\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{j},\mathbf{y})(c_{i})$ is the maximizer of $P [ \mathbf{y}^{I}| b_{i}]$ over $b_{i}\in\{+1,-1\}$ , which is exactly the Maximum-Likelihood rule. Repeating the same argument for all i we conclude our proof.

Proof Recalling (9), we have

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{R_{2}(\mathcal{A}(S);P_{\mathbf{b}})-\underset{h\in\mathcal{H}}{\operatorname*{inf}}R_{2}(h;P_{\mathbf{b}})=R_{2}(\mathcal{A}(S);P_{\mathbf{b}})-R_{2}(h_{\mathbf{b}};P_{\mathbf{b}})}\\ &{\qquad=r\cdot\frac{d_{-}}{d}+\frac{1}{2}\left(\sqrt{2\rho(1-r^{2}(d_{+}-d_{-})^{2}/d^{2})}-\sqrt{2\rho(1-r^{2})}\right).}\end{array}\tag{29}
$$

Next, we upper bound the second term in (29),

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\frac{1}{2}\left(\sqrt{2\rho\left(1-r^{2}(d_{+}-d_{-})^{2}/d^{2}\right)}-\sqrt{2\rho(1-r^{2})}\right)}\\ &{\quad\leq\frac{1}{2}\rho\left(2\rho(1-r^{2})\right)^{-1/2}r^{2}\left(1-\frac{(d_{+}-d_{-})^{2}}{d^{2}}\right)}\\ &{\quad\leq\frac{1}{2}\rho^{1/2}r^{2},}\end{array}
$$

where the first inequality follows from $\begin{array}{r}{\sqrt{x}\leq\frac{1}{2}(\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{y}),\forall x\leq y}\end{array}$ ,while the second follows from the fact that $r^{2}\le 1 / 2$ Thus, $\Delta \le \rho^{1 / 2}r / 2 \le \sqrt{2}\rho^{1 / 2}/ 4$

Proof

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\mathbb{E}[Z]=\mathbb{E}\left[Z\cdot\mathbb{1}[0\leq Z\leq a]\right]+\mathbb{E}\left[Z\cdot\mathbb{1}[a<Z\leq c]\right]}\\ &{\qquad\leq a\left(1-\mathbb{P}[Z>a]\right)+c\mathbb{P}[Z>a].}\end{array}
$$

Following rearrangement, we obtain the desired result.

### Proof of Theorem 12

Our proof is organized as follows: we first show that, for a hypothesis class $\mathcal{H}$ with finite VC dimension, given sufficient samples (the magnitude is provided in Theorem 12), the samples form a Distributionally Robust ε-net for $\mathcal{H}$; subsequently, we prove that such samples is sufficient for distributionally robust learning.

Proposition 18 Let $\mathcal{H}\subseteq \mathcal{Y}^{\mathcal{X}}$ with $v c ({\mathcal{H}}) = d .$ Fix $\varepsilon\in(0,1),\delta\in(0,1/4)$ and let

$$
m\geq\frac{16(1+2\rho)d}{\varepsilon^{2}}\log\left(\frac{8(1+2\rho)d}{\varepsilon^{2}}\right)+\frac{8(1+2\rho)}{\varepsilon^{2}}\left(d\log\left(\frac{2e}{d}\right)+\log\left(\frac{2}{\delta}\right)\right).\tag{22}
$$

Then, with probability of at least $1 - \delta$ over a choice of $S \sim P^{m}$ , we can conclude that $S$ is a Distributionally Robust ε-net for $\mathcal{H}$.

Proof Let $B: =\{S\subseteq\mathcal{X}: |S| =m,\exists h\in\mathcal{H},R_{2}(h;P)\geq\varepsilon,\mathcal{C}_{h}\cap S=\emptyset\}$ be the set of sets that are not a Distributionally Robust ε-net. We need to bound $\mathbb{P}[ S \in B ]$

Define

$$
B^{\prime}: =\left\{\left(S,T\right)\subseteq\mathcal{X}:\left|S\right| =\left|T\right| =m,\exists h\in\mathcal{H},R_{2}(h;P)\geq\varepsilon,\mathcal{C}_{h}\cap S=\varnothing,\left|T\cap\mathcal{C}_{h}\right| >\frac{m\varepsilon^{2}}{2(1+2\rho)}\right\}.
$$

Claim 1. $\mathbb{P}[S\in B]\le 2\cdot\mathbb{P}[(S,T)\in B^{\prime}]$

Since S and T are chosen independently, we can write

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\mathbb{P}[(S,T)\in B^{\prime}]=\underset{(S,T)\sim P^{2m}}{\mathbb{E}}\mathbb{1}[(S,T)\in B^{\prime}]}\\ &{\qquad=\underset{S\sim P^{m}}{\mathbb{E}}\underset{T\sim P^{m}}{\mathbb{E}}\mathbb{1}[(S,T)\in B^{\prime}].}\end{array}
$$

Note that $(S,T)\in B^{\prime}$ implies $S \in B$ , and therefore $\mathbb{1}[(S,T)\in B^{\prime}]=\mathbb{1}[(S,T)\in B^{\prime}]\cdot\mathbb{1}[S\in$ $B ]$ , which yields

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\mathbb{P}[(S,T)\in B^{\prime}]=\underset{(S,T)\sim P^{2m}}{\mathbb{E}}\mathbb{1}[(S,T)\in B^{\prime}]\cdot\mathbb{1}[S\in B]}\\ &{\qquad\underset{S\sim P^{m}}{\mathbb{E}}\mathbb{1}[S\in B]\underset{T\sim P^{m}}{\mathbb{E}}\mathbb{1}[(S,T)\in B^{\prime}].}\end{array}\tag{23}
$$

Fix some S. Then, either $\mathbb{1}[S\in B]=0,{\mathrm{or~}}S\in B$ and then $\exists h_{S}$ such that $R_{2}(h_{S};P)\ge\varepsilon$ and $|{\mathcal{C}}_{h_{S}}\cap S | = 0$ . It follows that a sufficient condition for $(S,T)\in B^{\prime}$ is that $| T \cap \mathcal{C}_{h_{S}}| >$ $\frac{m\varepsilon^{2}}{2(1{+}2\rho)}$ . Therefore, whenever $S \in B$ ,we have

$$
\underset{T\sim P^{m}}{\mathbb{E}}\mathbb{1}\left[\left(S,T\right)\in B^{\prime}\right]\geq\underset{T\sim P^{m}}{\mathbb{P}}\left[\left|T\cap\mathcal{C}_{h_{S}}\right| >\frac{m\varepsilon^{2}}{2(1+2\rho)}\right].\tag{24}
$$

However, since we now assume $S \in B$ , we know that $R_{2}(h_{S};P)\ge\varepsilon;$ accordingly, by Lemma 28, we have $\mathrm{er}(h_{S};P)=p\ge\frac{\varepsilon^{2}}{1+2\rho}$.

Therefore, $| T \cap{\mathcal{C}}_{h_{S}}|$ is a binomial random variable with parameters p (probability of success for a single try) and m (number of tries). Chernoff's inequality implies

$$
\begin{array}{r l}{{\mathbb{P}[|T\cap\mathcal{C}_{h_{S}}|\le\frac{pm}{2}]=\mathbb{P}[|T\cap\mathcal{C}_{h_{S}}| -pm\le-pm/2]}}\\ &{\le\exp(-mp/2)\le\exp(-\frac{m\varepsilon^{2}}{2(1+2\rho)})}\\ &{\le\exp(-d\log(1/\delta)/2)=\delta^{d/2}\le 1/2,}\end{array}
$$

where the first inequality is obtained via Chernoff's inequality and the penultimate inequality follows from our choice of $m$

Thus,

$$
\begin{array}{r}{\mathbb{P}\left[|T\cap\mathcal{C}_{h_{S}}| >\frac{m\varepsilon^{2}}{2\left(1+2\rho\right)}\right]=1-\mathbb{P}\left[|T\cap\mathcal{C}_{h_{S}}|\leq\frac{m\varepsilon^{2}}{2\left(1+2\rho\right)}\right]}\\ {\geq 1-\mathbb{P}\left[|T\cap\mathcal{C}_{h_{S}}|\leq\frac{mp}{2}\right]\geq 1/2.}\end{array}\tag{25}
$$

Combining (23), (24) and (25), we conclude our proof of Claim 1.

Claim 2.(Symmetrization) $\begin{array}{r}{\mathbb{P}\left[(S,T)\in B^{\prime}\right]\leq\exp\left(-\frac{m\varepsilon^{2}}{4(1+2\rho)}\right)\cdot\tau_{\mathcal{H}}(2m)}\end{array}$

For ease of notation, let $\begin{array}{r}{\alpha=\frac{m\varepsilon^{2}}{2(1+2\rho)}}\end{array}$ , and for a sequence $A=(x_{1},\dots,x_{2m})$ , let $A_{0}=$ $(x_{1},\ldots,x_{m})$ . Using the definition of $B^{\prime}$ we get

$$
\begin{array}{r l}\mathbb{P}\left[A\in B^{\prime}\right]&=\underset{A\sim P^{2m}}{\mathbb{E}}\max_{h\in\mathcal{H}}\left\{\mathbb{1}\left[R_{2}(h;P)\geq\varepsilon\right]\cdot\mathbb{1}\left[\left|\mathcal{C}_{h}\cap A_{0}\right| =0\right]\cdot\mathbb{1}\left[\left|\mathcal{C}_{h}\cap A\right|\geq\alpha\right]\right\}\\ &\leq\underset{A\sim P^{2m}}{\mathbb{E}}\max_{h\in\mathcal{H}}\left\{\mathbb{1}\left[\left|\mathcal{C}_{h}\cap A_{0}\right| =0\right]\cdot\mathbb{1}\left[\left|\mathcal{C}_{h}\cap A\right|\geq\alpha\right]\right\}.\end{array}
$$

Now let us denote by $\mathcal{H}_{A}$ the effective number of different hypotheses on $A,$ namely, $\mathcal{H}_{A}: = \{\mathcal{C}_{h}\cap A : h \in \mathcal{H}\}$ . It follows that

$$
\mathbb{P}[ A \in B^{\prime}] \le \underset{A \sim P^{2 m}}{\mathbb{E}}\max_{\mathcal{C}_{h}\in \mathcal{H}_{A}}\left\{{\mathbb{1}}\left[ |{\mathcal{C}}_{h}\cap A_{0}| = 0 \right] \cdot{\mathbb{1}}\left[ |{\mathcal{C}}_{h}\cap A | \ge \alpha \right] \right\}.
$$

Let $J = \{\mathbf{j}\subseteq [ 2 m ] : | \mathbf{j}| = m \}$ . For any $\textbf{j}\in \ J$ and $A=(x_{1},\dots,x_{2m}) $ , define $A_{\mathbf{j}}=$ $( x_{\mathbf{j}_{1}}, \hdots , x_{\mathbf{j}_{m}})$ Since the elements of A are chosen i.i.d., for any $\mathbf{j}\in J$ and any function $f(A,A_{0})$ , it holds that $\underset{A\sim P^{2m}}{\mathbb{E}}[f(A,A_{0})]=\underset{A\sim P^{2m}}{\mathbb{E}}[f(A,A_{\mathbf{j}})]$ . Since this holds for any j, it also holds for the expectation of j chosen at random from J. In particular, it holds for the function $\begin{array}{r}{f(A,A_{0})=\sum_{\mathcal{C}_{h}\in\mathcal{H}_{A}}\mathbb{1}\big [\vert\mathcal{C}_{h}\cap A_{0}\vert=0\big]\cdot\mathbb{1}\big [\vert\mathcal{C}_{h}\cap A\vert\ge\alpha\big]}\end{array}$ . We therefore obtain that

$$
\begin{array}{r l}\mathbb{P}[A\in B^{\prime}]&\leq\underset{A\sim P^{2m}}{\mathbb{E}}\underset{\mathbf{j}\sim U(J)}{\mathbb{E}}\sum_{\mathcal{C}_{h}\in\mathcal{H}_{A}}\mathbb{1}[|\mathcal{C}_{h}\cap A_{\mathbf{j}}| =0]\cdot\mathbb{1}[|\mathcal{C}_{h}\cap A|\geq\alpha]\\ &=\underset{A\sim P^{2m}}{\mathbb{E}}\sum_{\mathcal{C}_{h}\in\mathcal{H}_{A}}\mathbb{1}[|\mathcal{C}_{h}\cap A|\geq\alpha]\underset{\mathbf{j}\sim U(J)}{\mathbb{E}}\mathbb{1}[|\mathcal{C}_{h}\cap A_{\mathbf{j}}| =0].\end{array}
$$

Now fix some $A,$ such that $|{\mathcal{C}}_{h}\cap A | \geq \alpha$ Thus, $\operatorname{\mathbb{E}}_{j\sim U(J)}\mathbb{1}[|\mathcal{C}_{h}\cap A_{\mathbf{j}}| =0]$ represents the probability that when choosing m balls from a bag containing at least α red balls, we will never choose a red ball. This probability is at most

$$
\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2m}\right)^{2}=\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon^{2}}{4(1+2\rho)}\right)^{m}\leq\exp\left(-\frac{m\varepsilon^{2}}{4(1+2\rho)}\right).
$$

We therefore have

$$
\begin{array}{r l r}{{\mathbb{P}[A\in B^{\prime}]\le\underset{A\sim P^{2m}}{\mathbb{E}}\sum_{\mathcal{C}_{h}\in\mathcal{H}_{A}}\exp(-\frac{m\varepsilon^{2}}{4(1+2\rho)})}}\\ &{}&{\le\exp(-\frac{m\varepsilon^{2}}{4(1+2\rho)})\underset{A\sim P^{2m}}{\mathbb{E}}|\mathcal{H}_{A}|}\\ &{}&{\le\exp(-\frac{m\varepsilon^{2}}{4(1+2\rho)})\cdot\tau_{\mathcal{H}}(2m).}\end{array}
$$

By Sauer's lemma, we know that $\tau_{\mathcal{H}}\leq(2em/d)^{d};$ combining this with the above two claims, we obtain that

$$
\mathbb{P}[S\in B]\leq 2(2em/d)^{d}\exp\left(-\frac{m\varepsilon^{2}}{4(1+2\rho)}\right).
$$

We would like the right-hand side of the inequality to be at most $\delta ;$ that is,

$$
2(2em/d)^{d}\exp\left(-\frac{m\varepsilon^{2}}{4(1+2\rho)}\right)\leq\delta .
$$

Through rearrangement, we arrive at

$$
m\geq\frac{4(1+2\rho)d}{\varepsilon^{2}}\log(m)+\frac{4(1+2\rho)d}{\varepsilon^{2}}\log\left(\frac{2e}{d}\right)+\frac{4(1+2\rho)}{\varepsilon^{2}}\log\left(\frac{2}{\delta}\right).
$$

Using Lemma 22, a sufficient condition for the preceding to hold is that

$$
m\geq\frac{16(1+2\rho)d}{\varepsilon^{2}}\log\left(\frac{8(1+2\rho)d}{\varepsilon^{2}}\right)+\frac{8(1+2\rho)}{\varepsilon^{2}}\left(d\log\left(\frac{2e}{d}\right)+\log\left(\frac{2}{\delta}\right)\right).
$$

Next, we derive distributionally robust PAC learnability from the definition of distributionally robust ε-net.

Proposition 19 Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a hypothesis class over $\mathcal{X}$ with $vc(\mathcal{H})$ . Let P be a distribution over $\mathcal{X}$ and let $h^{*}$ be a target hypothesis. Fix $\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1)$ and let m be as defined in Proposition 18; then, with probability of at least $1 - \delta$ over a choice of m i.i.d. instances from $\mathcal{X}$ with labels according to $h^{*},$ , we have that any DRERM hypothesis has a true error of at most ε.

Proof Define the class $\mathcal{H}^{h^{*}}= \{\mathcal{C}_{h^{*}}\triangle \mathcal{C}_{h}: h \in \mathcal{H}\}$ , where $\mathcal{C}_{h^{*}}\triangle\mathcal{C}_{h}=(\mathcal{C}_{h}\backslash\mathcal{C}_{h^{*}})\cup(\mathcal{C}_{h^{*}}\backslash\mathcal{C}_{h})$ It can be readily verified that if some $A \subseteq{\mathcal{X}}$ is shattered by $\mathcal{H}$ then it is also shattered by $\mathcal{H}^{h^{*}}$ , and vice versa. Hence, $\mathrm{vc}(\mathcal{H})=\mathrm{vc}\left(\mathcal{H}^{h^{*}}\right)$ . Therefore, using Proposition 18, we can determine that with probability of at least $1 - \delta$ , the sample S is a distributionally robust ε-net for $\mathcal{H}^{h^{*}}$ , note that

$$
R_{2}(h;P)=\operatorname*{sup}\left\{\mathbb{E}_{Q}[\mathbb{1}[h(x)\neq y]]:Q\ll P,D_{2}(Q\|P)\right\}.
$$

Since $h^{*}$ is the target hypothesis, we have that

$$
\mathbb{E}_{P}[\mathbb{1}[h^{*}(x)\neq y]]=0.
$$

Thus, $R_{2}(h^{*};P)=\operatorname*{inf}_{\eta\in\mathbb{R}}\left\{c_{2}\mathbb{E}_{P}[\left(\mathbb{1}[h^{(}(x)\neq y]-\eta\right)_{+}^{2}]^{1/2}+\eta\right\}\leq c_{2}\mathbb{E}_{P}[(\mathbb{1}[h^{*}(x)\neq y])_{+}^{2}]^{1/2}=0$, which means that for any $Q \ll P$ with $D_{2}(Q\|P)\leq\rho .$ we have $Q[y=h^{\ast}(x)]=1$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{R_{2}(h;P)=\operatorname*{sup}\left\{\mathbb{E}_{Q}[\mathbb{1}[h(x)\neq y]:Q\ll P,D_{2}(Q\|P)\leq\rho\right\}}\\ &{\quad\quad\quad=\operatorname*{sup}\left\{\mathbb{E}_{Q}[\mathbb{1}[h(x)\neq h^{*}(x)]:Q\ll P,D_{2}(Q\|P)\leq\rho\right\}}\\ &{\quad\quad\quad=R_{2}(h\triangle h^{*};P),}\end{array}
$$

where $h \triangle{h^{*}}$ is the hypothesis that satisfies $\mathcal C_{h \triangle h^{*}}= \mathcal C_{h^{*}}\triangle \mathcal C_{h}$ . Therefore, for any $h \in \mathcal H$ with $R_{2}(h;P)\ge\varepsilon$ , we have that $|{\mathcal{C}}_{h^{*}\triangle h}\cap S | > 0 ;$ this which implies that h cannot be a DRERM hypothesis, which concludes our proof.

Proof Recalling the dual formulation of $R_{2}(h;P)$ (Proposition 4), we have

$$
\begin{array}{l}{{R_{2}(h;P)=\operatorname*{inf}_{\eta\in\mathbb{R}}\{c_{2}(\rho)\mathbb{E}_{P}[(\mathbb{1}[h(x)\neq y]-\eta)_{+}^{2}]^{1/2}+\eta\}}}\\ {\quad\le c_{2}(\rho)\mathbb{E}_{P}[(\mathbb{1}[h(x)\neq y])_{+}^{2}]^{1/2}}\\ {\quad=c_{2}(\rho)\mathrm{er}(h;P)^{1/2},}\end{array}
$$

where the first inequality follows by setting $\eta = 0$ and the last line follows from the fact that the indicator $\mathbb{1}\left[h(x)\neq y\right]$ is a 0-1-valued function.

context.statement:
Concretely, let $\mathcal{X}$ be the instance space, while $\mathcal{Y}=\{+1,-1\}$ denotes the label space. We formalize the distributional shift that we would like to protect against as an uncertainty set $\mathcal{U}(P)$ containing distributions with certain constraints, such as moment condition (Delage and Ye, 2010), Wasserstein distance (Gao, 2020) and f-divergence (Duchi and Namkoong, 2021). For a distribution P over $\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}=\{(x,y):x\in\mathcal{X},y\in\mathcal{Y}\}$ , we observe m i.i.d. samples $S \sim P^{m}$ , and distributionally robust learning attempts to learn a predictor $h : \mathcal{X}\to \mathcal{Y}$ having small distributionally robust risk,

$$
R_{\mathcal{U}}(h;P): =\operatorname*{sup}_{Q\in\mathcal{U}(P)}\mathbb{E}_{(x,y)\sim Q}[\mathbb{1}[h(x)\neq y]].\tag{1}
$$

The common approach to distributionally robust learning involves selecting a hypothesis class $\mathcal{H}\subseteq \mathcal{Y}^{\mathcal{X}}$ and learning a predictor $\hat{h}: \mathcal{X}\to \mathcal{Y}$ from $\mathcal{H}$ through Distributionally Robust Empirical Risk Minimization:

$$
\begin{array}{r}{\hat{h}\in\mathrm{DRERM}_{\mathcal{H}}(S): =\underset{h\in\mathcal{H}}{\mathrm{argmin}}\hat{R}_{\mathcal{U}}(h;S),}\end{array}
$$

where $\begin{array}{r}{\hat{R}_{\mathcal{U}}(h;S): =\operatorname*{sup}_{Q\in\mathcal{U}(P_{m})}\mathbb{E}_{(x,y)\sim Q}[\mathbb{1}\left[h(x)\neq y\right]]}\end{array}$ and $P_{m}$ denotes the empirical distribution over samples S.

context.name: Uncertainty set and chi^2-divergence D_2 (Section 1)
context.statement:
Namely, we consider the distributional shift as follows:

$$
\mathcal{U}(P)=\{Q\ll P:D_{2}(Q\|P)\leq\rho\},
$$

where $\begin{array}{r}{D_{2}(Q\|P): =\frac{1}{2}\int\left(\frac{dQ}{dP}-1\right)^{2}dP}\end{array}$ and $Q \ll P$ indicates that distribution Q is absolutely continuous with respect to $P .$ The $\chi^{2}$-divergence is a commonly explored concept in the distributionally robust optimization (DRO) literature (Duchi and Namkoong, 2019). Moreover, it is also a crucial concept in a variety of fields such as information theory, statistics, learning, signal processing, and various branches of mathematics (Park et al., 2011; Saraswat, 2014; Nishiyama and Sason, 2020). The $\chi^{2}$-divergence plays a fundamental role in problems related to source and channel coding, combinatorics, large deviation theory, goodness-of-fit, and independence tests in statistics, as demonstrated by Csiszár et al. (2004). Additionally, it is widely recognized for its computational feasibility and statistical properties, as noted in Tsybakov (2009).

context.name: Problem setup (Section 2)
context.statement: Given a hypothesis class $\mathcal{H}\subseteq \mathcal{Y}^{\mathcal{X}}$ , our goal is to design a learning rule $\mathcal{A}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})^{*}\mapsto\mathcal{Y}^{\mathcal{X}}$ such that for any distribution P over $\mathcal{X}\times \mathcal{Y}$ , the rule $\mathcal{A}$ will find a predictor that can compete with the best predictor $h^{\ast}\in \mathcal{H}$ in terms of the distributionally robust risk using a number of samples that is independent of the distribution P. In this paper, we use $(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})^{*}$ to denote the set of all sequences in the space $\mathcal{X}\times \mathcal{Y}$ . The following definitions formalize the notion of distributionally robust PAC learning under the realizable case and agnostic settings.

context.name: Definition 1 (Agnostic Distributionally Robust PAC Learnability)
context.statement:
Definition 1 (Agnostic Distributionally Robust PAC Learnability) For any $\varepsilon,\delta\in$ (0, 1), the sample complexity of agnostic distributionally robust $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-PAC learning of $\mathcal{H}$ with respect to the distributional shift $\mathcal{U}$, denoted by $\mathcal{M}_{AG}(\varepsilon,\delta;\mathcal{H},\mathcal{U})$ , is defined as the smallest $m \in \mathbb{N}\cup \{0 \}$ for which there exists a learning rule $\mathcal{A}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})^{*}\mapsto\mathcal{Y}^{\mathcal{X}}$ such that, for every data distribution P over $\mathcal{X}\times \mathcal{Y}$ , with probability of at least $1 - \delta$ over $S \sim P^{m}$ ,

$$
R_{\mathcal{U}}(\mathcal{A}(S);P)\leq\operatorname*{inf}_{h\in\mathcal{H}}R_{\mathcal{U}}(h;P)+\varepsilon .
$$

If no such m exists, define $\mathcal{M}_{AG}(\varepsilon,\delta;\mathcal{H},\mathcal{U})=\infty$ . We say that $\mathcal{H}$ is distributionally robustly PAC-learnable in the agnostic setting with respect to the distributional shift $\mathcal{U}$ if $\forall\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1)$ , $\mathcal{M}_{AG}(\varepsilon,\delta;\mathcal{H},\mathcal{U})$ scales polynomially with $1 / \varepsilon$ and $1 / \delta$

context.name: Definition 2 (Realizable Distributionally Robust PAC Learnability)
context.statement:
Definition 2 (Realizable Distributionally Robust PAC Learnability) For any $\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1)$, the sample complexity of realizable distributionally robust $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-PAC learning of $\mathcal{H}$ with respect to the distributional shift $\mathcal{U}$, denoted by $\mathcal{M}_{RE}(\varepsilon,\delta;\mathcal{H},\mathcal{U})$ , is defined as the smallest $m \in \mathbb{N}\cup \{0 \}$ for which there exists a learning rule $\mathcal{A}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})^{*}\mapsto\mathcal{Y}^{\mathcal{X}}$ such that, for every data distribution P over $\mathcal{X}\times \mathcal{Y}$ where there exists a predictor $h^{\ast}\in \mathcal{H}$ with zero distributionally robust risk, $R_{{\mathcal U}}(h^{*};P)=0$ , with probability of at least $1 - \delta$ over $S \sim P^{m}$ ,

$$
R_{\mathcal{U}}(\mathcal{A}(S);P)\leq\varepsilon .
$$

If no such m exists, define $\mathcal{M}_{RE}(\varepsilon,\delta;\mathcal{H},\mathcal{U})=\infty$ . We say that $\mathcal{H}$ is distributionally robustly PAC-learnable in the realizable setting with respect to the distributional shift $\mathcal{U}$ if $\forall\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1)$ , $\mathcal{M}_{RE}(\varepsilon,\delta;\mathcal{H},\mathcal{U})$ scales polynomially with $1 / \varepsilon$ and $1 / \delta$

context.name: Notation: error rate er(h;P) and empirical error
context.statement: We also denote $\mathrm{er}(h;P)=P(h(x)\neq y)$ , the (non-robust) error rate under 0-1 loss, and $\begin{array}{r}{\hat{\mathrm{er}}(h;S)=\frac{1}{|S|}\sum_{(x,y)\in S}\mathbb{1}[h(x)\neq y]}\end{array}$ , the empirical error rate; here, |S| denotes the cardinality of set S, while $\mathbb{1}[\cdot]$ is the indicator function that takes 1 when the statement in the square brackets is true and 0 otherwise. The definition of Vapnik-Chervonenkis dimension (VC dimension) is provided below.

context.name: Definition 3 (VC dimension)
context.statement: Definition 3 (VC dimension) We say that a sequence $\{x_{1},\ldots,x_{k}\}\subseteq{\mathcal{X}}$ is shattered by $\mathcal{H}$ if $\forall y_{1},\ldots,y_{k}\in\mathcal{Y},\exists h\in\mathcal{H}$ such that $\forall i\in [k],h(x_{i})=y_{i}$ . The VC dimension of $\mathcal{H}$ (denoted as $vc(\mathcal{H}))$ is then defined as the largest integer k for which there exists $\{x_{1},\ldots,x_{k}\}\subseteq{\mathcal{X}}$ that is shattered by $\mathcal{H}$. If no such k exists, then $vc(\mathcal{H})$ is said to be infinite.

context.name: Loss class L_H
context.statement:
Denote the loss class of $\mathcal{H}$ by $\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{H}}$ , where

$$
\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{H}}=\Big\{(x,y)\mapsto\mathbb{1}[h(x)\neq y]:h\in\mathcal{H}\Big\}.
$$

context.name: Notation R_2(h;P) (Section 3)
context.statement:
We use $R_{2}(h;P)$ to denote the distributionally robust risk under distributional shift

$$
\begin{array}{r}{\mathcal{U}(P)=\left\{Q\ll P:D_{2}(Q\|P)\leq\rho\right\}.}\end{array}
$$

context.name: Proposition 4 (Duality Formulation), Eq. (2) (Shapiro 2017)
context.statement:
We recall the following duality formulation (Shapiro, 2017, Section 3.2) for distributionally robust risk, which is essential in our derivation.

Proposition 4 (Duality Formulation) For any probability P on $\mathcal{X}\times \mathcal{Y}$ , any $\rho > 0$ , and $c_{2}(\rho): =\sqrt{1+2\rho},$ for all $h \in \mathcal H$ , we have

$$
R_{2}(h;P)=\operatorname*{inf}_{\eta\in\mathbb{R}}\Big\{c_{2}(\rho)\mathbb{E}_{P}\Big [(\mathbb{1}[h(x)\neq y]-\eta)_{+}^{2}\Big]^{1/2}+\eta\Big\},\tag{2}
$$

where $a_{+}: =\operatorname*{max}\left(a,0\right)$

context.name: g_2 and Lemma 5 (compact range for eta), Remark 6
context.statement:
To bring the above proposition into effect, we need the following lemma. In the interests of simplicity, for any fixed $h \in \mathcal H$ , let

$$
\begin{array}{r}{g_{2}(\eta,P): =c_{2}(\rho)\mathbb{E}_{P}\left[(\mathbb{1}\left[h(x)\neq y\right]-\eta)_{+}^{2}\right]^{1/2}+\eta .}\end{array}
$$

Lemma 5 For any distribution $P$ ,

$$
\operatorname*{inf}_{\eta\in\mathbb{R}}g_{2}(\eta,P)=\operatorname*{inf}_{\eta}\left\{g_{2}(\eta,P):\eta\in\left[-\frac{1}{c_{2}(\rho)-1},1\right]\right\}.
$$

Remark 6 The above lemma restricts the domain of η to a compact set, which is crucial to our uniform convergence result.

context.name: Remark 8 (dependence on 1/(c_2(rho)-1))
context.statement: Remark 8 The dependence on $\frac{1}{c_{2}(\rho)-1}$ is due to the lower bound for η in Lemma 5. While more advanced techniques could potentially yield a better dependence on $\rho,$ it is worth noting that the upper bound shows that the finite VC dimension is sufficient for distributionally robust PAC learnability for finite non-zero values of ρ.

context.name: Remark 10 (range of rho in Theorem 9)
context.statement: Remark 10 We derive the result under the assumption that the perturbation size $\rho \in$ $\textstyle\left(0,{\frac{3-2{\sqrt{2}}}{2}}\right)$ . Intuitively, if the perturbation size is prohibitively large, the learning problem can become "easier", since the benchmark in $\inf_{h\in\mathcal{H}}R_{2}(h;P)$ may increase too much. When $\rho$ approaches 0, the lower bound recovers that of the classical statistical learning (Mohri et al., 2012; Shalev-Shwartz and Ben-David, 2014).

context.name: Realizable case setup: C_h and R_2 in primal form (Section 4)
context.statement:
To study the upper bound of the sample complexity under the realizable case, it is necessary to introduce the definition of Distributionally Robust ε-net, which is similar to the definition in (Shalev-Shwartz and Ben-David, 2014, Definition 28.2). In the realizable case, we have a target hypothesis $h^{*}$ that generates the label. We will frequently refer $\mathcal{C}_{h}$ to the set $\{x\in\mathcal{X}:h(x)\neq h^{*}(x)\}$ , where h is a predictor in hypothesis class $\mathcal{H}$. The distributionally robust risk has the following form:

$$
R_{2}(h;P)=\operatorname*{sup}_{Q\ll P}\left\{\mathbb{E}_{x\sim Q}[\mathbb{1}[h(x)\neq h^{\ast}(x)]]:D_{2}(Q\|P)\leq\rho\right\}.
$$

context.name: Definition 11 (Distributionally Robust eps-net), Eq. (5)
context.statement:
Definition 11 (Distributionally Robust ε-net) Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a domain. $S \subseteq{\mathcal{X}}$ is a Distributionally Robust ε-net for $\mathcal{H}\subseteq \mathcal{Y}^{\mathcal{X}}$ with respect to a distribution P over $\mathcal{X}$ if:

$$
\forall h\in{\mathcal{H}}:R_{2}(h;P)\geq\varepsilon\implies\mathcal{C}_{h}\cap S\neq\emptyset .\tag{5}
$$

context.name: Notation phi_{eta,h} (Appendix A.1)
context.statement: We use $\varphi_{\eta,h}(x,y)$ to denote $\mathbb{1}[h(x)\neq y]-\eta$ and $c_{2}$ as the shorthand of $c_{2}(\rho)$ when there is no ambiguity.

context.name: Definition 16 (Rademacher Complexity)
context.statement:
Moreover, we introduce the definition of Rademacher Complexity and Growth Function in order to bound the excess risk in terms of VC dimension.

Definition 16 (Rademacher Complexity) We define the empirical Rademacher Complexity of a hypothesis class $\mathcal{F}$ for a given sample $z_{i}=(x_{i},y_{i}),i=1,\dots,m$ as follows :

$$
\hat{\mathcal{R}}_{m}(\mathcal{F}): =\mathbb{E}_{\sigma}\left[\operatorname*{sup}_{f\in\mathcal{F}}\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sigma_{i}f(z_{i})\right],
$$

where $\sigma=(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{m}) $ is a vector of i.i.d. Rademacher variables. The Rademacher Complexity is defined as the expectation of this quantity:

$$
\mathcal{R}_{m}(\mathcal{F}): =\mathbb{E}_{(z_{1},\ldots,z_{m})\sim P^{m}}\left[\hat{\mathcal{R}}_{m}(\mathcal{F})\right].
$$

context.name: Definition 17 (Growth Function)
context.statement:
Definition 17 (Growth Function) Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a hypothesis class. The growth function of $\mathcal{H}$ ,denoted as $\tau_{\mathcal{H}}: \mathbb{N}\to \mathbb{N}$ , is defined as follows:

$$
\tau_{\mathcal{H}}(m): =\underset{C\subset\mathcal{X}: |C| =m}{max}\left|\mathcal{H}_{C}\right|,
$$

where $\mathcal{H}_{C}: =\left\{(h(x_{1}),\cdot\cdot\cdot,h(x_{|C|})):h\in\mathcal{H}\right\}$ for $C = \{x_{i}: 1 \leq i \leq | C | \}$

context.name: Lemma 20 (Hoeffding's Inequality; Shalev-Shwartz & Ben-David Lemma 4.5)
context.statement:
The following Hoeffding's lemma can be found in (Shalev-Shwartz and Ben-David, 2014, Lemma 4.5).

Lemma 20 (Hoeffding's Inequality) Let $\theta_{1},\ldots,\theta_{m}$ be a sequence of i.i.d. random variables, and assume that for all $i,\mathbb{E}[\theta_{i}]=\mu$ and $\mathbb{P}[ a \leq \theta_{i}\leq b ] = 1$ . Then, for any $\varepsilon > 0$ ,

$$
\mathbb{P}\left[\left|\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\theta_{i}-\mu\right| >\varepsilon\right]\leq 2\exp{(-2m\varepsilon^{2}/(b-a)^{2})}.
$$

context.name: Lemma 21 (Talagrand's Lemma; Mohri et al. Lemma 4.2)
context.statement:
We next recall an important lemma that is useful for bounding the Rademacher complexity and can be found in (Mohri et al., 2012, Lemma 4.2).

Lemma 21 (Talagrand's Lemma) Let ψ be a ρ-Lipschitz function. For any function class $\mathcal{H}$, we have:

$$
\mathcal{R}_{m}(\psi\circ\mathcal{H})\leq\rho\mathcal{R}_{m}(\mathcal{H}).
$$

context.name: Lemma 22 (Shalev-Shwartz & Ben-David Lemma A.1)
context.statement:
The following lemma is fundamental and can be found in (Shalev-Shwartz and Ben-David, 2014, Lemma A.1).

Lemma 22 Let $a > 1$ and $b > 0$ Then: $x\geq 4a\log(2a)+2b\implies x\geq a\log(x)+b.$

context.name: Lemma 23 (closed form of R_2 on two-point distributions)
context.statement: Lemma 23 For $P_{b}(x,y)=\begin{cases}\frac{1+yb\varepsilon}{2},&\text{if } x=c,\\ 0,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$ and $\rho\in\left(0,{\frac{3-2{\sqrt{2}}}{2}}\right)$ , we have $R_{2}(h;P_{b})=$ $\left[1-h(c)b\varepsilon+\sqrt{2\rho(1-\varepsilon^{2})}\right]/2.$

context.name: Lemma 24 (Slud's Inequality; Slud 1977)
context.statement:
We frequently employ the following estimate on the binomial random variable probability (Slud, 1977):

Lemma 24 (Slud's Inequality) Let X be $a\ (m,p)$ binomial random variable and assume that $p=(1-\varepsilon)/2$ . Then,

$$
\mathbb{P}[X\ge m/2]\ge\frac{1}{2}\left(1-\sqrt{1-\exp(-m\varepsilon^{2}/(1-\varepsilon^{2}))}\right).
$$

context.name: Lemma 25 (Maximum-Likelihood rule minimizes (14))
context.statement:
Lemma 25 Among all algorithms, (14) is minimized for $\mathcal{A}$ being the Maximum-Likelihood algorithm, $\mathcal{A}_{M L}$ , defined as

$$
\forall i,\quad\mathcal{A}_{ML}(S)(c_{i})=sign\left(\sum_{k:x_{k}=c_{i}}y_{k}\right).
$$

context.name: Lemma 26 (range of Delta)
context.statement: Lemma 26 Let $\Delta=\frac{1}{r}\left(R_{2}(\mathcal{A}(S);P)-\operatorname*{inf}_{h\in\mathcal{H}}R_{2}(h;P)\right)$ , where r is defined in the proof of Theorem 9. We have $\Delta\in [0,1+\sqrt{2}\rho^{1/2}/4]$

context.name: Lemma 27 (reverse Markov inequality)
context.statement:
Lemma 27 Let Z be a random variable that takes values in $[0,c],c>1$ . Assume that $\mathbb{E}[ Z ] = \mu$ . Then, for any $a\in(0,c)$ ,

$$
\mathbb{P}[ Z > a ] \geq \frac{\mu - a}{c - a}.
$$

context.name: Lemma 28 (R_2 <= c_2(rho) er^{1/2})
context.statement:
Lemma 28 For any probability distribution P and predictor $h \in \mathcal H$ , we have

$$
R_{2}(h;P)\leq c_{2}(\rho)er(h;P)^{1/2}.
$$

import Mathlib

namespace ResearchLevel

open MeasureTheory

structure Predictor (𝒳 𝒴' : Type*) [MeasurableSpace 𝒳] [MeasurableSpace 𝒴'] where

  f : 𝒳 → 𝒴'

  hf : Measurable f

abbrev HypothesisClass (𝒳 𝒴' : Type*) [MeasurableSpace 𝒳] [MeasurableSpace 𝒴'] :=
  Set (Predictor 𝒳 𝒴')

variable {𝒳 : Type*} [MeasurableSpace 𝒳]

def Shatters (H : HypothesisClass 𝒳 Bool) (S : Finset 𝒳) : Prop :=
  ∀ b : S → Bool, ∃ h ∈ H, ∀ x : S, h.f x.val = b x

noncomputable def VCDim (H : HypothesisClass 𝒳 Bool) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨆ (S : Finset 𝒳) (_ : Shatters H S), (S.card : ℕ∞)

noncomputable def c2 (ρ : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.sqrt (1 + 2 * ρ)

noncomputable def etaDomain (ρ : ℝ) : Set ℝ :=
  if ρ = 0 then Set.Iic 1 else Set.Icc (-(1 / (c2 ρ - 1))) 1

noncomputable def robustRisk {𝒳 : Type*} [MeasurableSpace 𝒳]
    (h : Predictor 𝒳 Bool) (P : Measure (𝒳 × Bool)) (ρ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ⨅ η : etaDomain ρ,
    c2 ρ * Real.sqrt
        ((P {z : 𝒳 × Bool | h.f z.1 ≠ z.2}).toReal * (max (1 - (η : ℝ)) 0) ^ 2
          + (P {z : 𝒳 × Bool | h.f z.1 = z.2}).toReal * (max (0 - (η : ℝ)) 0) ^ 2)
      + (η : ℝ)

def AgnosticPACAtSize {𝒳 : Type*} [MeasurableSpace 𝒳]
    (H : HypothesisClass 𝒳 Bool) (ρ ε δ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : (Fin n → 𝒳 × Bool) → Predictor 𝒳 Bool,
    ∀ (P : Measure (𝒳 × Bool)) [IsProbabilityMeasure P],
      (Measure.pi fun _ : Fin n => P)
          {S : Fin n → 𝒳 × Bool |
            (⨅ h : ↥H, robustRisk (h : Predictor 𝒳 Bool) P ρ) + ε < robustRisk (A S) P ρ}
        ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ

noncomputable def agnosticSampleComplexity {𝒳 : Type*} [MeasurableSpace 𝒳]
    (H : HypothesisClass 𝒳 Bool) (ρ ε δ : ℝ) : ℕ∞ :=
  sInf {n : ℕ∞ | ∃ m : ℕ, n = (m : ℕ∞) ∧ AgnosticPACAtSize H ρ ε δ m}

def RealizablePACAtSize {𝒳 : Type*} [MeasurableSpace 𝒳]
    (H : HypothesisClass 𝒳 Bool) (ρ ε δ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : (Fin n → 𝒳 × Bool) → Predictor 𝒳 Bool,
    ∀ (P : Measure (𝒳 × Bool)) [IsProbabilityMeasure P],
      (∃ hstar ∈ H, robustRisk hstar P ρ = 0) →
      (Measure.pi fun _ : Fin n => P)
          {S : Fin n → 𝒳 × Bool | ε < robustRisk (A S) P ρ}
        ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ

noncomputable def realizableSampleComplexity {𝒳 : Type*} [MeasurableSpace 𝒳]
    (H : HypothesisClass 𝒳 Bool) (ρ ε δ : ℝ) : ℕ∞ :=
  sInf {n : ℕ∞ | ∃ m : ℕ, n = (m : ℕ∞) ∧ RealizablePACAtSize H ρ ε δ m}

theorem theorem7 :
    ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ →

      (Measure.pi fun _ : Fin n => P)
          {S : Fin n → 𝒳 × Bool | ε < robustRisk (A S) P ρ}
        ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ

noncomputable def realizableSampleComplexity {𝒳 : Type*} [MeasurableSpace 𝒳]
    (H : HypothesisClass 𝒳 Bool) (ρ ε δ : ℝ) : ℕ∞ :=
  sInf {n : ℕ∞ | ∃ m : ℕ, n = (m : ℕ∞) ∧ RealizablePACAtSize H ρ ε δ m}

/-! ### Helper machinery (added) -/

section Helpers

open scoped ENNReal
open Finset

/-! #### Elementary real analysis -/

theorem le_of_sq_le_sq' {x y : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hy : 0 ≤ y) (hxy : x^2 ≤ y^2) : x ≤ y := by
  have h := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hxy
  rwa [Real.sqrt_sq hx, Real.sqrt_sq hy] at h

theorem one_lt_c2 {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) : 1 < c2 ρ := by
  have h1 : Real.sqrt 1 < Real.sqrt (1+2*ρ) := Real.sqrt_lt_sqrt (by norm_num) (by linarith)
  rwa [Real.sqrt_one] at h1

theorem c2_sq {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) : (c2 ρ)^2 = 1 + 2*ρ := Real.sq_sqrt (by linarith)

/-- The value of the distributionally robust risk as a function of the error probability. -/
noncomputable def psi (ρ a : ℝ) : ℝ := a + Real.sqrt (2*ρ*a*(1-a))

theorem psi_nonneg {ρ a : ℝ} (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) : 0 ≤ psi ρ a := by
  unfold psi; have := Real.sqrt_nonneg (2*ρ*a*(1-a)); linarith

theorem psi_le_one {ρ a : ℝ} (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha1 : a * (1+2*ρ) ≤ 1) :
    psi ρ a ≤ 1 := by
  have ha : a ≤ 1 := by nlinarith
  have h1 : Real.sqrt (2*ρ*a*(1-a)) ≤ Real.sqrt ((1-a)^2) := by
    apply Real.sqrt_le_sqrt; nlinarith
  rw [Real.sqrt_sq (by linarith)] at h1
  unfold psi; linarith

theorem psi_le_c2_sqrt {ρ a : ℝ} (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha1 : a ≤ 1) :
    psi ρ a ≤ c2 ρ * Real.sqrt a := by
  have hnn : 0 ≤ 2*ρ*a*(1-a) :=
    mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg (by linarith : (0:ℝ) ≤ 2*ρ) ha0) (by linarith : (0:ℝ) ≤ 1-a)
  have h2 : (psi ρ a)^2 ≤ (c2 ρ * Real.sqrt a)^2 := by
    have hs : Real.sqrt (2*ρ*a*(1-a)) ^ 2 = 2*ρ*a*(1-a) := Real.sq_sqrt hnn
    have hc : (c2 ρ)^2 = 1 + 2*ρ := Real.sq_sqrt (by linarith)
    have hsa : (Real.sqrt a)^2 = a := Real.sq_sqrt ha0
    have key : Real.sqrt (2*ρ*a*(1-a)) = Real.sqrt (2*ρ*a) * Real.sqrt (1-a) := by
      rw [← Real.sqrt_mul (by positivity)]
    have h1 : Real.sqrt (2*ρ*a) ^2 = 2*ρ*a := Real.sq_sqrt (by positivity)
    have h3 : Real.sqrt (1-a)^2 = 1-a := Real.sq_sqrt (by linarith)
    unfold psi
    rw [key, mul_pow, hc, hsa]
    nlinarith [sq_nonneg (Real.sqrt (1-a) - Real.sqrt (2*ρ*a)), Real.sqrt_nonneg (2*ρ*a),
      Real.sqrt_nonneg (1-a), Real.sqrt_nonneg a]
  have hpos : 0 ≤ c2 ρ * Real.sqrt a := by unfold c2; positivity
  nlinarith [psi_nonneg (ρ := ρ) ha0, h2, hpos]

theorem key_neg {ρ a t : ℝ} (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha1 : a ≤ 1) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    psi ρ a + t ≤ c2 ρ * Real.sqrt (a*(1+t)^2 + (1-a)*t^2) := by
  set u := Real.sqrt (2*ρ) with hu_def
  set v := Real.sqrt a with hv_def
  set w := Real.sqrt (1-a) with hw_def
  have hu : u^2 = 2*ρ := Real.sq_sqrt (by linarith)
  have hv : v^2 = a := Real.sq_sqrt ha0
  have hw : w^2 = 1-a := Real.sq_sqrt (by linarith)
  have hun : 0 ≤ u := Real.sqrt_nonneg _
  have hvn : 0 ≤ v := Real.sqrt_nonneg _
  have hwn : 0 ≤ w := Real.sqrt_nonneg _
  have hpsi : psi ρ a = v^2 + u*v*w := by
    unfold psi
    rw [hv]
    congr 1
    rw [show 2*ρ*a*(1-a) = (u*v*w)^2 by rw [mul_pow, mul_pow, hu, hv, hw]]
    exact Real.sqrt_sq (by positivity)
  have hXeq : a*(1+t)^2 + (1-a)*t^2 = v^2*(1+t)^2 + w^2*t^2 := by rw [hv, hw]
  have hc2 : c2 ρ * Real.sqrt (v^2*(1+t)^2 + w^2*t^2)
      = Real.sqrt ((1+u^2) * (v^2*(1+t)^2 + w^2*t^2)) := by
    rw [c2, Real.sqrt_mul (by nlinarith)]
    congr 2
    linarith [hu]
  rw [hXeq, hc2, hpsi]
  have hid : (1+u^2)*(v^2*(1+t)^2+w^2*t^2) - (v^2+u*v*w+t)^2 = (u*t-v*w+u*v^2)^2 := by
    linear_combination (-((1+u^2)*(v^2-t^2))) * hw + (-((1+u^2)*(v^2-t^2))) * hv
  have hnn : 0 ≤ v^2 + u*v*w + t := by positivity
  rw [show v^2 + u*v*w + t = Real.sqrt ((v^2+u*v*w+t)^2) from (Real.sqrt_sq hnn).symm]
  apply Real.sqrt_le_sqrt
  nlinarith [sq_nonneg (u*t-v*w+u*v^2), hid]

theorem opt_val {ρ a : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha1 : a ≤ 1) :
    c2 ρ * Real.sqrt (a*(1+(Real.sqrt (a*(1-a)/(2*ρ)) - a))^2
      + (1-a)*(Real.sqrt (a*(1-a)/(2*ρ)) - a)^2) - (Real.sqrt (a*(1-a)/(2*ρ)) - a) = psi ρ a := by
  set s := Real.sqrt (a*(1-a)/(2*ρ)) with hs_def
  have hnn : 0 ≤ a*(1-a)/(2*ρ) := by
    apply div_nonneg (mul_nonneg ha0 (by linarith)) (by linarith)
  have hs2 : s^2 = a*(1-a)/(2*ρ) := Real.sq_sqrt hnn
  have hsn : 0 ≤ s := Real.sqrt_nonneg _
  set t := s - a with ht_def
  have hXeq : a*(1+t)^2 + (1-a)*t^2 = (1+2*ρ)/(2*ρ) * (a*(1-a)) := by
    have h0 : a*(1+t)^2 + (1-a)*t^2 = (t+a)^2 + a - a^2 := by ring
    rw [h0, ht_def]
    have h1 : s - a + a = s := by ring
    rw [h1, hs2]
    field_simp
    ring
  rw [hXeq]
  have h1 : Real.sqrt ((1+2*ρ)/(2*ρ) * (a*(1-a))) = Real.sqrt (1+2*ρ) * s := by
    rw [hs_def, ← Real.sqrt_mul (by positivity)]
    congr 1
    field_simp
  rw [h1, c2, ← mul_assoc, Real.mul_self_sqrt (by linarith : (0:ℝ) ≤ 1+2*ρ)]
  have hq : (2*ρ*s)^2 = 2*ρ*a*(1-a) := by
    have h3 : (2*ρ*s)^2 = 4*ρ^2*s^2 := by ring
    rw [h3, hs2]; field_simp; ring
  have h2 : 2*ρ*s = Real.sqrt (2*ρ*a*(1-a)) := by
    rw [← hq, Real.sqrt_sq (mul_nonneg (by linarith) hsn)]
  unfold psi
  linarith [h2]

theorem psi_mono {ρ a₀ a : ℝ} (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) (h0 : 0 ≤ a₀) (hle : a₀ ≤ a) (hsum : a + a₀ ≤ 1) :
    psi ρ a₀ + (a - a₀) ≤ psi ρ a := by
  have hx : 0 ≤ 2*ρ*((a-a₀)*(1-a-a₀)) :=
    mul_nonneg (by linarith) (mul_nonneg (by linarith) (by linarith))
  have h1 : Real.sqrt (2*ρ*a₀*(1-a₀)) ≤ Real.sqrt (2*ρ*a*(1-a)) := by
    apply Real.sqrt_le_sqrt
    nlinarith [hx]
  unfold psi
  linarith

/-! #### The objective function of the robust risk -/

theorem obj_lb {ρ a η : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha1 : a*(1+2*ρ) ≤ 1) (hη : η ≤ 1) :
    psi ρ a ≤ c2 ρ * Real.sqrt (a * (max (1-η) 0)^2 + (1-a) * (max (0-η) 0)^2) + η := by
  have haa : a ≤ 1 := by nlinarith
  rcases le_or_gt η 0 with hc | hc
  · have h1 : max (1-η) 0 = 1 - η := max_eq_left (by linarith)
    have h2 : max (0-η) 0 = -η := by rw [max_eq_left (by linarith)]; ring
    rw [h1, h2]
    have hkey := key_neg (ρ := ρ) (a := a) (t := -η) (by linarith) ha0 haa (by linarith)
    have he : a*(1+(-η))^2 + (1-a)*(-η)^2 = a*(1-η)^2 + (1-a)*(-η)^2 := by ring_nf
    rw [he] at hkey
    linarith
  · have h2 : max (0-η) 0 = 0 := max_eq_right (by linarith)
    have h1 : max (1-η) 0 = 1 - η := max_eq_left (by linarith)
    rw [h1, h2]
    have he : a*(1-η)^2 + (1-a)*0^2 = a*(1-η)^2 := by ring
    rw [he]
    have hsq : Real.sqrt (a*(1-η)^2) = Real.sqrt a * (1-η) := by
      rw [Real.sqrt_mul ha0, Real.sqrt_sq (by linarith)]
    rw [hsq]
    have hcs := psi_le_c2_sqrt (ρ := ρ) (a := a) (by linarith) ha0 haa
    have hpo := psi_le_one (ρ := ρ) (a := a) (by linarith) ha0 ha1
    nlinarith [hcs, hpo, hc, hη]

theorem meas_eq_set {𝒳 : Type*} [MeasurableSpace 𝒳] (h : Predictor 𝒳 Bool) :
    MeasurableSet {z : 𝒳 × Bool | h.f z.1 = z.2} := by
  have he : {z : 𝒳 × Bool | h.f z.1 = z.2}
      = (h.f ⁻¹' {true}) ×ˢ ({true} : Set Bool) ∪ (h.f ⁻¹' {false}) ×ˢ ({false} : Set Bool) := by
    ext ⟨x, y⟩
    cases y <;> cases hh : h.f x <;> simp [hh]
  rw [he]
  exact ((h.hf (by trivial)).prod (by trivial)).union ((h.hf (by trivial)).prod (by trivial))

theorem meas_ne_set {𝒳 : Type*} [MeasurableSpace 𝒳] (h : Predictor 𝒳 Bool) :
    MeasurableSet {z : 𝒳 × Bool | h.f z.1 ≠ z.2} := by
  have he : {z : 𝒳 × Bool | h.f z.1 ≠ z.2} = {z : 𝒳 × Bool | h.f z.1 = z.2}ᶜ := by
    ext z; simp
  rw [he]; exact (meas_eq_set h).compl

/-- Closed form for the χ²-distributionally robust risk of a predictor with error probability `a`,
valid as long as `a (1 + 2ρ) ≤ 1`. -/
theorem robustRisk_eq {𝒳 : Type*} [MeasurableSpace 𝒳] (h : Predictor 𝒳 Bool)
    (P : Measure (𝒳 × Bool)) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {ρ a : ℝ}
    (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hρ8 : ρ ≤ 8) (ha : (P {z : 𝒳 × Bool | h.f z.1 ≠ z.2}).toReal = a)
    (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha1 : a*(1+2*ρ) ≤ 1) :
    robustRisk h P ρ = psi ρ a := by
  have haa : a ≤ 1 := by nlinarith
  have hcorr : (P {z : 𝒳 × Bool | h.f z.1 = z.2}).toReal = 1 - a := by
    have hc : {z : 𝒳 × Bool | h.f z.1 = z.2} = {z : 𝒳 × Bool | h.f z.1 ≠ z.2}ᶜ := by
      ext z; simp
    have hsum := measure_add_measure_compl (μ := P) (meas_ne_set h)
    rw [hc]
    have h1 : P {z : 𝒳 × Bool | h.f z.1 ≠ z.2} ≠ ⊤ := measure_ne_top _ _
    have h2 : P ({z : 𝒳 × Bool | h.f z.1 ≠ z.2}ᶜ) ≠ ⊤ := measure_ne_top _ _
    have h3 := congrArg ENNReal.toReal hsum
    rw [ENNReal.toReal_add h1 h2, ha] at h3
    simp at h3
    linarith
  set s := Real.sqrt (a*(1-a)/(2*ρ)) with hs_def
  have hsn : 0 ≤ s := Real.sqrt_nonneg _
  have hnn2 : 0 ≤ a*(1-a)/(2*ρ) :=
    div_nonneg (mul_nonneg ha0 (by linarith)) (by linarith)
  have hs2 : s^2 = a*(1-a)/(2*ρ) := Real.sq_sqrt hnn2
  have hs2' : s^2 * (2*ρ) = a*(1-a) := by rw [hs2]; field_simp
  set η₀ : ℝ := -(s - a) with hη₀_def
  have hta : a ≤ s := by
    refine le_of_sq_le_sq' ha0 hsn ?_
    nlinarith [hs2', mul_nonneg ha0 (by linarith : (0:ℝ) ≤ 1 - a - 2*ρ*a), hρ]
  have hs_le : s ≤ 1/ρ := by
    have h1 : s^2 ≤ (1/ρ)^2 := by
      rw [hs2, div_pow, one_pow, div_le_div_iff₀ (by linarith) (by positivity)]
      nlinarith [sq_nonneg (a - 1/2), hρ8, hρ]
    exact le_of_sq_le_sq' hsn (by positivity) h1
  have hmem : η₀ ∈ etaDomain ρ := by
    rw [etaDomain, if_neg (ne_of_gt hρ)]
    have hc2 : 1 < c2 ρ := one_lt_c2 hρ
    have hc2le : c2 ρ ≤ 1 + ρ := by nlinarith [c2_sq (le_of_lt hρ), hc2]
    have hfin : 1/ρ ≤ 1/(c2 ρ - 1) := by
      apply one_div_le_one_div_of_le (by linarith) (by linarith)
    constructor
    · simp only [hη₀_def]; linarith
    · simp only [hη₀_def]; linarith
  haveI : Nonempty ↥(etaDomain ρ) := ⟨⟨η₀, hmem⟩⟩
  have hlb : ∀ η : ↥(etaDomain ρ), psi ρ a ≤
      c2 ρ * Real.sqrt (a * (max (1 - (η:ℝ)) 0)^2 + (1-a) * (max (0 - (η:ℝ)) 0)^2) + (η:ℝ) := by
    rintro ⟨η, hη⟩
    apply obj_lb hρ ha0 ha1
    rw [etaDomain, if_neg (ne_of_gt hρ)] at hη
    exact hη.2
  rw [robustRisk, ha, hcorr]
  apply le_antisymm
  · have hbdd : BddBelow (Set.range fun η : ↥(etaDomain ρ) =>
        c2 ρ * Real.sqrt (a * (max (1 - (η:ℝ)) 0)^2 + (1-a) * (max (0 - (η:ℝ)) 0)^2) + (η:ℝ)) := by
      refine ⟨psi ρ a, ?_⟩
      rintro _ ⟨η, rfl⟩
      exact hlb η
    have hci := ciInf_le hbdd (⟨η₀, hmem⟩ : ↥(etaDomain ρ))
    refine le_trans hci (le_of_eq ?_)
    show c2 ρ * Real.sqrt (a * (max (1 - η₀) 0)^2 + (1-a) * (max (0 - η₀) 0)^2) + η₀ = psi ρ a
    have h1 : max (1 - η₀) 0 = 1 + (s - a) := by
      rw [hη₀_def]; rw [max_eq_left (by linarith)]; ring
    have h2 : max (0 - η₀) 0 = s - a := by
      rw [hη₀_def]; rw [max_eq_left (by linarith)]; ring
    rw [h1, h2, hη₀_def]
    have hov := opt_val (ρ := ρ) (a := a) hρ ha0 haa
    rw [← hs_def] at hov
    linarith [hov]
  · exact le_ciInf hlb


noncomputable def droMeas {W : Type*} [Fintype W] [MeasurableSpace W] (w : W → ℝ≥0∞) : Measure W :=
  ∑ v : W, w v • Measure.dirac v

theorem droMeas_apply {W : Type*} [Fintype W] [MeasurableSpace W] [MeasurableSingletonClass W]
    (w : W → ℝ≥0∞) (A : Set W) [DecidablePred (· ∈ A)] :
    droMeas w A = ∑ v ∈ Finset.univ.filter (· ∈ A), w v := by
  classical
  simp only [droMeas, Measure.coe_finset_sum, Finset.sum_apply, Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul,
    Measure.dirac_apply' _ (by measurability : MeasurableSet A)]
  rw [Finset.sum_filter]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun v _ => ?_)
  by_cases hv : v ∈ A <;> simp [hv]

theorem droMeas_singleton {W : Type*} [Fintype W] [MeasurableSpace W] [MeasurableSingletonClass W]
    [DecidableEq W] (w : W → ℝ≥0∞) (u : W) : droMeas w {u} = w u := by
  rw [droMeas_apply]
  rw [show (Finset.univ.filter (· ∈ ({u} : Set W))) = ({u} : Finset W) by ext v; simp]
  simp

theorem droMeas_prob {W : Type*} [Fintype W] [MeasurableSpace W] [MeasurableSingletonClass W]
    (w : W → ℝ≥0∞) (h : ∑ v : W, w v = 1) : IsProbabilityMeasure (droMeas w) := by
  classical
  constructor
  rw [droMeas_apply]
  simpa using h


theorem dro_discrete_lb {W X : Type*} [Fintype W] [MeasurableSpace W] [MeasurableSingletonClass W]
    [MeasurableSpace X]
    (q : Measure W) [IsProbabilityMeasure q] (g : W → X) (hg : Measurable g) (m : ℕ)
    (E : Set (Fin m → X)) (T : Finset (Fin m → W))
    (hT : ∀ S ∈ T, (fun k => g (S k)) ∈ E) :
    ∑ S ∈ T, ∏ k, q {S k} ≤ (Measure.pi fun _ : Fin m => q.map g) E := by
  haveI : IsProbabilityMeasure (q.map g) := Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map hg.aemeasurable
  have hpi : Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin m => q.map g)
      = (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin m => q)).map (fun S i => g (S i)) := by
    refine Measure.pi_eq (μ := fun _ : Fin m => q.map g) ?_
    intro s hs
    rw [Measure.map_apply (by fun_prop) (MeasurableSet.univ_pi hs)]
    have : (fun (S : Fin m → W) (i : Fin m) => g (S i)) ⁻¹' (Set.pi Set.univ s)
        = Set.pi Set.univ (fun i => g ⁻¹' (s i)) := by
      ext S; simp [Set.mem_pi]
    rw [this, Measure.pi_pi]
    exact Finset.prod_congr rfl (fun i _ => (Measure.map_apply hg (hs i)).symm)
  rw [hpi]
  refine le_trans ?_ (Measure.le_map_apply (Measurable.aemeasurable (by measurability)) E)
  have hsub : (↑T : Set (Fin m → W)) ⊆ (fun (S : Fin m → W) (i : Fin m) => g (S i)) ⁻¹' E := by
    intro S hS; exact hT S hS
  refine le_trans ?_ (measure_mono hsub)
  rw [← sum_measure_singleton]
  exact le_of_eq (Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun S _ => (Measure.pi_singleton _ _).symm))


theorem dro_min_eq_half {x y : ℝ} : min x y = (x + y - |x - y|)/2 := by
  rcases le_total x y with h | h
  · rw [min_eq_left h, abs_of_nonpos (by linarith)]; ring
  · rw [min_eq_right h, abs_of_nonneg (by linarith)]; ring

theorem dro_minsum_1 {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] (F₁ F₂ : Ω → ℝ)
    (h1 : ∀ S, 0 ≤ F₁ S) (h2 : ∀ S, 0 ≤ F₂ S)
    (hs1 : ∑ S, F₁ S = 1) (hs2 : ∑ S, F₂ S = 1) :
    (∑ S, Real.sqrt (F₁ S * F₂ S))^2 ≤ 2 * ∑ S, min (F₁ S) (F₂ S) := by
  have key : ∀ S, Real.sqrt (F₁ S * F₂ S)
      = Real.sqrt (min (F₁ S) (F₂ S)) * Real.sqrt (max (F₁ S) (F₂ S)) := by
    intro S
    rw [← Real.sqrt_mul (le_min (h1 S) (h2 S))]
    congr 1
    rcases le_total (F₁ S) (F₂ S) with h | h
    · rw [min_eq_left h, max_eq_right h]
    · rw [min_eq_right h, max_eq_left h]; ring
  have hcs := Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq Finset.univ
      (fun S => Real.sqrt (min (F₁ S) (F₂ S))) (fun S => Real.sqrt (max (F₁ S) (F₂ S)))
  have hmin : ∀ S, Real.sqrt (min (F₁ S) (F₂ S))^2 = min (F₁ S) (F₂ S) :=
    fun S => Real.sq_sqrt (le_min (h1 S) (h2 S))
  have hmax : ∀ S, Real.sqrt (max (F₁ S) (F₂ S))^2 = max (F₁ S) (F₂ S) :=
    fun S => Real.sq_sqrt (le_max_of_le_left (h1 S))
  simp only [hmin, hmax] at hcs
  have hsum : ∑ S, max (F₁ S) (F₂ S) = 2 - ∑ S, min (F₁ S) (F₂ S) := by
    have : ∀ S, max (F₁ S) (F₂ S) = F₁ S + F₂ S - min (F₁ S) (F₂ S) := by
      intro S; rcases le_total (F₁ S) (F₂ S) with h | h
      · rw [min_eq_left h, max_eq_right h]; ring
      · rw [min_eq_right h, max_eq_left h]; ring
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun S _ => this S)]
    rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib, hs1, hs2]
    ring
  have hmnn : 0 ≤ ∑ S, min (F₁ S) (F₂ S) :=
    Finset.sum_nonneg (fun S _ => le_min (h1 S) (h2 S))
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun S _ => key S)]
  nlinarith [hcs, hsum, hmnn]

theorem dro_minsum_2 {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] (F₁ F₂ : Ω → ℝ)
    (h1 : ∀ S, 0 < F₁ S) (h2 : ∀ S, 0 ≤ F₂ S)
    (hs1 : ∑ S, F₁ S = 1) (hs2 : ∑ S, F₂ S = 1) :
    1 - (1/2) * Real.sqrt ((∑ S, (F₂ S)^2/(F₁ S)) - 1) ≤ ∑ S, min (F₁ S) (F₂ S) := by
  have hminabs : ∑ S, min (F₁ S) (F₂ S) = 1 - (1/2) * ∑ S, |F₁ S - F₂ S| := by
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun S _ => dro_min_eq_half (x := F₁ S) (y := F₂ S))]
    rw [← Finset.sum_div, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib, hs1, hs2]
    ring
  have hchi : ∑ S, (F₁ S - F₂ S)^2/(F₁ S) = (∑ S, (F₂ S)^2/(F₁ S)) - 1 := by
    have : ∀ S : Ω, (F₁ S - F₂ S)^2/(F₁ S) = F₁ S - 2 * F₂ S + (F₂ S)^2/(F₁ S) := by
      intro S; have hne := (h1 S).ne'; field_simp; ring
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun S _ => this S)]
    rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, ← Finset.mul_sum, hs1, hs2]
    ring
  have hcs := Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq Finset.univ
      (fun S => Real.sqrt (F₁ S)) (fun S => |F₁ S - F₂ S| / Real.sqrt (F₁ S))
  have hab : ∀ S : Ω, Real.sqrt (F₁ S) * (|F₁ S - F₂ S| / Real.sqrt (F₁ S)) = |F₁ S - F₂ S| := by
    intro S
    rw [mul_div_cancel₀]
    exact ne_of_gt (Real.sqrt_pos.mpr (h1 S))
  have hb2 : ∀ S : Ω, (|F₁ S - F₂ S| / Real.sqrt (F₁ S))^2 = (F₁ S - F₂ S)^2/(F₁ S) := by
    intro S
    rw [div_pow, sq_abs, Real.sq_sqrt (le_of_lt (h1 S))]
  have ha2 : ∀ S : Ω, Real.sqrt (F₁ S)^2 = F₁ S := fun S => Real.sq_sqrt (le_of_lt (h1 S))
  simp only [hab, hb2, ha2] at hcs
  rw [hs1, one_mul, hchi] at hcs
  have habs_nn : 0 ≤ ∑ S, |F₁ S - F₂ S| := Finset.sum_nonneg (fun S _ => abs_nonneg _)
  have hle : ∑ S, |F₁ S - F₂ S| ≤ Real.sqrt ((∑ S, (F₂ S)^2/(F₁ S)) - 1) := by
    exact Real.le_sqrt_of_sq_le hcs
  linarith [hminabs, hle]


open Finset in
theorem dro_sum_prod_pow {W : Type*} [Fintype W] [DecidableEq W] (m : ℕ) (f : W → ℝ) :
    ∑ S : Fin m → W, ∏ k, f (S k) = (∑ w, f w)^m := by
  have := Finset.sum_prod_piFinset (ι := Fin m) (Finset.univ : Finset W) (fun _ w => f w)
  rw [Fintype.piFinset_univ] at this
  rw [this]
  simp

theorem dro_sqrt_prod_eq {W : Type*} [Fintype W] (m : ℕ) (u : Fin m → W) (f₁ f₂ : W → ℝ)
    (h1 : ∀ w, 0 ≤ f₁ w) (h2 : ∀ w, 0 ≤ f₂ w) :
    Real.sqrt ((∏ k, f₁ (u k)) * (∏ k, f₂ (u k))) = ∏ k, Real.sqrt (f₁ (u k) * f₂ (u k)) := by
  rw [show (∏ k, f₁ (u k)) * (∏ k, f₂ (u k)) = ∏ k, (f₁ (u k) * f₂ (u k)) from
    (Finset.prod_mul_distrib).symm]
  rw [show (∏ k, (f₁ (u k) * f₂ (u k))) = (∏ k, Real.sqrt (f₁ (u k) * f₂ (u k)))^2 by
    rw [← Finset.prod_pow]
    exact Finset.prod_congr rfl (fun k _ => (Real.sq_sqrt (mul_nonneg (h1 _) (h2 _))).symm)]
  exact Real.sqrt_sq (Finset.prod_nonneg (fun k _ => Real.sqrt_nonneg _))


theorem dro_prodmin_1 {W : Type*} [Fintype W] [DecidableEq W] (m : ℕ) (f₁ f₂ : W → ℝ)
    (h1 : ∀ w, 0 ≤ f₁ w) (h2 : ∀ w, 0 ≤ f₂ w)
    (hs1 : ∑ w, f₁ w = 1) (hs2 : ∑ w, f₂ w = 1) :
    (1/2) * ((∑ w, Real.sqrt (f₁ w * f₂ w))^m)^2
      ≤ ∑ S : Fin m → W, min (∏ k, f₁ (S k)) (∏ k, f₂ (S k)) := by
  have hp1 : ∑ S : Fin m → W, (∏ k, f₁ (S k)) = 1 := by rw [dro_sum_prod_pow, hs1, one_pow]
  have hp2 : ∑ S : Fin m → W, (∏ k, f₂ (S k)) = 1 := by rw [dro_sum_prod_pow, hs2, one_pow]
  have key := dro_minsum_1 (Ω := Fin m → W) (fun S => ∏ k, f₁ (S k)) (fun S => ∏ k, f₂ (S k))
    (fun S => Finset.prod_nonneg (fun k _ => h1 _)) (fun S => Finset.prod_nonneg (fun k _ => h2 _))
    hp1 hp2
  have hsq : ∑ S : Fin m → W, Real.sqrt ((∏ k, f₁ (S k)) * (∏ k, f₂ (S k)))
      = (∑ w, Real.sqrt (f₁ w * f₂ w))^m := by
    rw [← dro_sum_prod_pow m (fun w => Real.sqrt (f₁ w * f₂ w))]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun S _ => dro_sqrt_prod_eq m S f₁ f₂ h1 h2)
  rw [hsq] at key
  linarith

theorem dro_prodmin_2 {W : Type*} [Fintype W] [DecidableEq W] (m : ℕ) (f₁ f₂ : W → ℝ)
    (h1 : ∀ w, 0 < f₁ w) (h2 : ∀ w, 0 ≤ f₂ w)
    (hs1 : ∑ w, f₁ w = 1) (hs2 : ∑ w, f₂ w = 1) :
    1 - (1/2) * Real.sqrt ((∑ w, (f₂ w)^2/(f₁ w))^m - 1)
      ≤ ∑ S : Fin m → W, min (∏ k, f₁ (S k)) (∏ k, f₂ (S k)) := by
  have hp1 : ∑ S : Fin m → W, (∏ k, f₁ (S k)) = 1 := by rw [dro_sum_prod_pow, hs1, one_pow]
  have hp2 : ∑ S : Fin m → W, (∏ k, f₂ (S k)) = 1 := by rw [dro_sum_prod_pow, hs2, one_pow]
  have key := dro_minsum_2 (Ω := Fin m → W) (fun S => ∏ k, f₁ (S k)) (fun S => ∏ k, f₂ (S k))
    (fun S => Finset.prod_pos (fun k _ => h1 _)) (fun S => Finset.prod_nonneg (fun k _ => h2 _))
    hp1 hp2
  have hchi : ∑ S : Fin m → W, (∏ k, f₂ (S k))^2/(∏ k, f₁ (S k))
      = (∑ w, (f₂ w)^2/(f₁ w))^m := by
    rw [← dro_sum_prod_pow m (fun w => (f₂ w)^2/(f₁ w))]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun S _ => ?_)
    rw [Finset.prod_div_distrib, Finset.prod_pow]
  rw [hchi] at key
  exact key


noncomputable def droW (D : ℕ) (r : ℝ) (b : Fin D → Bool) : Fin D × Bool → ℝ :=
  fun v => (1/(D:ℝ)) * (if v.2 = b v.1 then (1+r)/2 else (1-r)/2)

def droFlip {D : ℕ} (i : Fin D) (b : Fin D → Bool) : Fin D → Bool :=
  fun j => if j = i then !(b j) else b j

theorem droFlip_inv {D : ℕ} (i : Fin D) : Function.Involutive (droFlip i) := by
  intro b; funext j; simp only [droFlip]; by_cases h : j = i <;> simp [h]

theorem dro_sum_bool_if {A B : ℝ} (β : Bool) : (∑ y : Bool, if y = β then A else B) = A + B := by
  cases β <;> simp <;> ring

theorem droW_pos {D : ℕ} {r : ℝ} (hD : 0 < D) (hr : r < 1) (hr0 : -1 < r) (b : Fin D → Bool)
    (v : Fin D × Bool) : 0 < droW D r b v := by
  have hDpos : (0:ℝ) < D := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hD
  simp only [droW]
  apply mul_pos (by positivity)
  by_cases h : v.2 = b v.1 <;> simp [h] <;> linarith

theorem droW_sum {D : ℕ} {r : ℝ} (hD : 0 < D) (b : Fin D → Bool) :
    ∑ v : Fin D × Bool, droW D r b v = 1 := by
  have hDpos : (0:ℝ) < D := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hD
  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
  have : ∀ i : Fin D, ∑ y : Bool, droW D r b (i, y) = 1/(D:ℝ) := by
    intro i
    simp only [droW, ← Finset.mul_sum, dro_sum_bool_if (b i)]
    ring
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => this i)]
  simp
  field_simp

theorem dro_bool_prod (β y : Bool) (A B : ℝ) :
    (if y = β then A else B) * (if y = !β then A else B) = A * B := by
  cases β <;> cases y <;> simp <;> ring

theorem dro_bool_chi (β : Bool) (A B : ℝ) :
    (∑ y : Bool, (if y = !β then A else B)^2/(if y = β then A else B)) = A^2/B + B^2/A := by
  cases β <;> simp <;> ring

theorem droFlip_ne {D : ℕ} {i j : Fin D} (h : j ≠ i) (b : Fin D → Bool) : droFlip i b j = b j := by
  simp [droFlip, h]

theorem droW_sqrt_sum {D : ℕ} {r : ℝ} (hD : 0 < D) (hr : r < 1) (hr0 : -1 < r)
    (b : Fin D → Bool) (i : Fin D) :
    ∑ v : Fin D × Bool, Real.sqrt (droW D r b v * droW D r (droFlip i b) v)
      = (((D:ℝ)-1) + Real.sqrt (1-r^2))/(D:ℝ) := by
  have hDpos : (0:ℝ) < D := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hD
  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type, ← Finset.add_sum_erase _ _ (Finset.mem_univ i)]
  have hpiece1 : ∑ y : Bool, Real.sqrt (droW D r b (i, y) * droW D r (droFlip i b) (i, y))
      = Real.sqrt (1-r^2)/(D:ℝ) := by
    have hval : ∀ y : Bool, droW D r b (i, y) * droW D r (droFlip i b) (i, y)
        = ((1/(D:ℝ)) * (Real.sqrt (1-r^2)/2))^2 := by
      intro y
      simp only [droW, droFlip, eq_self_iff_true, if_true]
      rw [show (1/(D:ℝ) * (if y = b i then (1+r)/2 else (1-r)/2)) *
            (1/(D:ℝ) * (if y = !(b i) then (1+r)/2 else (1-r)/2))
          = (1/(D:ℝ))^2 * ((if y = b i then (1+r)/2 else (1-r)/2) *
            (if y = !(b i) then (1+r)/2 else (1-r)/2)) by ring]
      rw [dro_bool_prod (b i) y ((1+r)/2) ((1-r)/2)]
      have hsq : (Real.sqrt (1-r^2)/2)^2 = (1-r^2)/4 := by
        rw [div_pow, Real.sq_sqrt (by nlinarith : (0:ℝ) ≤ 1 - r^2)]; norm_num
      rw [mul_pow, hsq]; ring
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun y _ => by rw [hval y])]
    rw [Real.sqrt_sq (by positivity)]
    simp [Fintype.sum_bool]
    ring
