targets.label: Lemma 3.1
targets.statement:
Lemma 3.1 (Key self-boundedness properties). Consider the setup of Section 2 and let Assumptions 1-2 hold. Further assume the loss is self-bounded as per Assumption 4. Then, the objective satisfies the following self-boundedness properties for its Gradient and Hessian:

1. Self-bounded gradient: $\begin{array}{r}{\left\|\nabla\widehat{F}_{i}(w)\right\|\leq\ell R\widehat{F}_{i}(w),\forall i\in [n].}\end{array}$

2. Self-bounded weak convexity: $\begin{array}{r}{\lambda_{\operatorname*{min}}\left(\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w)\right)\geq-\frac{L R^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}\widehat{F}(w)}\end{array}$

targets.label: Theorem 3.2
targets.statement:
Theorem 3.2 (Training loss – General bound). Suppose Assumptions $1 \mathrm{-}\mathit{4}$ hold. Fix any training horizon $T \geq 0$ and any step-size $\eta \leq 1 / L_{\widehat{F}}$ where $L_{\widehat{F}}$ is the objective's smoothness parameter. Assume any w $\in \mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}}$ and hidden-layer width m such that $\| w - w_{0}\|^{2}\ge$ max $\{\eta T\widehat{F}(w),\eta\widehat{F}(w_{0})\}$ and $m\geq 18^{2}L^{2}R^{4}\Vert w-w_{0}\Vert^{4}$. Then, the training loss and the parameters' norm satisfy

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\widehat{F}(w_{T})\ \leq\ \displaystyle\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\widehat{F}(w_{t})\ \leq\ 2\widehat{F}(w)+\frac{5\|w-w_{0}\|^{2}}{2\eta T},}\\ &{\forall t\in [T]\ :\ \|w_{t}-w_{0}\|\ \leq\ 4\|w-w_{0}\|.}\end{array}\tag{5}
$$

targets.label: Theorem 3.3
targets.statement:
Theorem 3.3 (Training loss under interpolation). Let Assumptions 1-5 hold. Let $\eta \leq$ min $\begin{array}{r}{\{\frac{1}{L_{\widehat{F}}},g(1)^{2},\frac{g(1)^{2}}{\widehat{F}(w_{0})}\}}\end{array}$ and assume the width satisfies $m\geq 18^{2}L^{2}R^{4}g(\frac{1}{T})^{4}$ for a fixed training horizon T such that $\varepsilon = 1 / T$ is small enough for Assumption 5 to apply. Then,

$$
\widehat{F}(w_{T})\leq\frac{2}{T}+\frac{5g(\frac{1}{T})^{2}}{2\eta T},\tag{6}
$$

$$
\forall t\in [T]\ :\ \|w_{t}-w_{0}\|\ \leq\ 4g(\frac{1}{T}).
$$

nl_proof:
### Proof of Lemma 3.1

Lemma D.1. The following are true for the model (50) under Assumption 2.

1. $\begin{array}{r}{\|\nabla_{1}\Phi(w,x)\|\le\ell R.}\end{array}$

2. $\begin{array}{r}{\|\nabla_{1}^{2}\Phi(w,x)\|\le\frac{LR^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}}\end{array}$

Proof Direct calculation yields that,

$$
\nabla_{1}\Phi(w,x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\left[\begin{array}{c}{a_{1}\sigma^{\prime}(\langle w_{1},x\rangle)x}\\ {.}\\ {.}\\ {a_{m}\sigma^{\prime}(\langle w_{m},x\rangle)x}\end{array}\right]
$$

Noting that $\sigma^{\prime}(\cdot)\leq\ell,$

$$
\begin{array}{r l r}{{\|\nabla_{1}\Phi(w,x)\|^{2}=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\sum_{i=1}^{d}(x(i)\sigma^{\prime}(\langle w_{j},x\rangle))^{2}}}\\ &{}&{\leq\ell^{2}\|x\|^{2}}\\ &{}&{\leq\ell^{2}R^{2}.}\end{array}\tag{53}
$$

For the Hessian,

$$
\frac{\partial^{2}\Phi(w,x)}{\partial w_{ij}\partial w_{k\ell}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}x(j)x(\ell)a_{i}\sigma^{\prime\prime}(\langle w_{i},x\rangle)\mathbf{1}_{\{i=k\}}.\tag{54}
$$

Thus,

$$
\nabla_{1}^{2}\Phi(w,x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\mathrm{diag}\left(a_{1}\sigma^{\prime\prime}(\langle w_{1},x\rangle)x x^{T},\dots,a_{m}\sigma^{\prime\prime}(\langle w_{m},x\rangle)x x^{T}\right)
$$

for any unit norm vector $u \in \mathbb{R}^{m d}$ , define $\bar{u}_{i}: =[u_{(i-1)m+1}:u_{im}]\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ . Moreover, define the matrix $\nabla_{w_{i}}^{2}\Phi(w,x)\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ such that $\begin{array}{r}{[\nabla_{w_{i}}^{2}\Phi(w,x)]_{j\ell}=\frac{\partial^{2}\Phi(w,x)}{\partial w_{ij}\partial w_{i\ell}}}\end{array}$

$$
\begin{array}{r l}{\left\|u^{\top}\nabla_{1}^{2}\Phi(w,x)\right\|^{2}}&{=\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{m}\left\|u_{i}^{\top}\nabla_{w_{i}}^{2}\Phi(w,x)\right\|^{2}}\\ &{\leq\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{m}\left\|\nabla_{w_{i}}^{2}\Phi(w,x)\right\|^{2}\|\bar{u}_{i}\|^{2}}\\ &{\leq\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{m}\frac{L^{2}}{m}\|x\|^{4}\|\bar{u}_{i}\|^{2}}\\ &{\leq\displaystyle\frac{L^{2}R^{4}}{m}.}\end{array}
$$

This completes the proof.

Lemma D.2. Let Assumption 2 hold. Then, the following are true for the loss gradient and Hessian:

$$
\begin{array}{r}{1.\|\nabla\widehat{F}(w)\|\le\ell R\widehat{F}^{\prime}(w).}\end{array}
$$

$$
\begin{array}{r}{2.\|\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w)\|\le\ell^{2}R^{2}\widehat{F}^{\prime\prime}(w)+\frac{LR^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}\widehat{F}^{\prime}(w).}\end{array}
$$

$$
\begin{array}{r}{3.\ \lambda_{\operatorname*{min}}\left(\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w)\right)\geq-\frac{L R^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}\widehat{F}^{\prime}(w).}\end{array}
$$

Proof The loss gradient is derived as follows,

$$
\nabla\widehat{F}(w)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}f^{\prime}(y_{i}\Phi(w,x_{i}))y_{i}\nabla_{1}\Phi(w,x_{i})
$$

Recalling that $y_{i}\in \{\pm 1 \}$ , we can write

$$
\begin{array}{r l}{{\Big\|\nabla\widehat{F}(w)\Big\|=\frac{1}{n}\Big\|\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}f^{\prime}(y_{i}\Phi(w,x_{i}))y_{i}\nabla_{1}\Phi(w,x_{i})\Big\|}}\\ &{\leq\frac{1}{n}\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}\vert f^{\prime}(y_{i}\Phi(w,x_{i}))\vert\Big\|\nabla_{1}\Phi(w,x_{i})\Big\|.}\\ &{\leq\ell RF^{\prime}(w).}\end{array}\tag{55}
$$

For the Hessian of loss, note that

$$
\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}f^{\prime\prime}(y_{i}\Phi(w,x_{i}))\nabla_{1}\Phi(w,x_{i})\nabla_{1}\Phi(w,x_{i})^{\top}+f^{\prime}(y_{i}\Phi(w,x_{i}))y_{i}\nabla_{1}^{2}\Phi(w,x_{i}).\tag{56}
$$

It follows that

$$
\begin{array}{l}{\displaystyle\left\|{\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w)}\right\|=\left\|\frac{1}{n}\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}f^{\prime}(y_{i}\Phi(w,x_{i}))y_{i}{\nabla_{1}^{2}\Phi}(w,x_{i})+f^{\prime\prime}(y_{i}\Phi(w,x_{i}))\nabla_{1}\Phi(w,x_{i})\nabla_{1}\Phi(w,x_{i})^{\top}\right\|}\\ {\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{n}\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}{|f^{\prime}(y_{i}\Phi(w,x_{i}))|}\left\|{\nabla_{1}^{2}\Phi}(w,x_{i})\right\|+ |f^{\prime\prime}(y_{i}\Phi(w,x_{i}))|\left\|\nabla_{1}\Phi(w,x_{i})\nabla_{1}\Phi(w,x_{i})^{\top}\right\|}\\ {\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{n}\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}|f^{\prime}(y_{i}\Phi(w,x_{i}))|\left\|{\nabla_{1}^{2}\Phi}(w,x_{i})\right\|+ |f^{\prime\prime}(y_{i}\Phi(w,x_{i}))|\left\|\nabla_{1}\Phi(w,x_{i})\right\|^{2}}\\ {\displaystyle\leq\frac{LR^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}F^{\prime}(w)+\ell^{2}R^{2}F^{\prime\prime}(w).}\end{array}\tag{57}
$$

To lower-bound the minimum eigenvalue of Hessian, note that f is convex and thus $f^{\prime\prime}(\cdot)\geq 0$ Therefore the first term in (56) is positive semi-definite and the second term can be lowerbounded as follows,

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\lambda_{\operatorname*{min}}(\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w))\geq-\left\|\displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}y_{i}f^{\prime}\big(y_{i}\Phi(w,x_{i})\big)\nabla_{1}^{2}\Phi(w,x_{i})\right\|}\\ &{\qquad\geq-\displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_{i}f^{\prime}\big(y_{i}\Phi(w,x_{i})\big)|\left\|\nabla_{1}^{2}\Phi(w,x_{i})\right\|}\\ &{\qquad\geq-\displaystyle\frac{L R^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}F^{\prime}(w).}\end{array}
$$

Corollary D.2.1 (Self-boundedness of Objective). Let Assumption 2 hold. If the loss satisfies Assumptions 4 (with $\beta_{f}=1)$ and 8, then

1. $\lVert\nabla\widehat{F}(w)\rVert\leq\ell R\widehat{F}(w)$

$$
\begin{array}{r}{2.\|\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w)\|{\le}\left(\ell^{2}R^{2}+\frac{LR^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}\right)\widehat{F}(w).}\end{array}
$$

3. $\begin{array}{r}{\lambda_{\operatorname*{min}}\left(\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w)\right)\geq-\frac{L R^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}\widehat{F}(w).}\end{array}$

If in addition the loss satisfies Assumptions 3.A and 3.B with $L_{f}= G_{f}= 1$ , then

6. $\lVert\nabla\widehat{F}(w)\rVert\leq\ell R.$

$$
\begin{array}{r}{7.\ \|\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w)\|\le\ell^{2}R^{2}+\frac{LR^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}.}\end{array}
$$

Proof For self-bounded losses we have $\widehat{F}^{\prime}(w)\leq\widehat{F}(w)$ and $\widehat{F}^{\prime\prime}(w)\leq\widehat{F}(w)$ . If the loss is 1-Lipschitz and 1-smooth we have $\widehat{F}^{\prime}(w)\leq 1$ and $\widehat{F}^{\prime\prime}(w)\leq 1$ . Thus, the claims immediately follow from Lemma D.2.

### Proof of Theorem 3.2

Because of smoothness and Lipschitz Assumption 3 of $f,$ it turns out that the training objective is $L_{\widehat{F}}$-smooth. Hence, by the descent lemma of GD for smooth functions, the same upper bound holds in Eq. (5) for the value of the loss at time $T$, as well.

## A.1 Proof of Theorem 3.2

We begin with proving the general train-loss and parameter-norm bounds of Theorem 3.2. In fact, we state and prove a slightly more general statement of the theorem which includes non-smooth and non-Lipschitz losses (such as expoential loss) that satisfy a second order self-bounded property described below.

Assumption 8 (2nd order self-boundedness). The convex loss function $f : \mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}_{+}$ satisfies the 2nd order self-boundedness property, i.e.

$$
f^{\prime\prime}(u)\leq f(u),\forall u\in\mathbb{R}.
$$

Theorem A.1 (General statement of Theorem 3.2). Let Assumptions 1-2 hold. Assume the loss function satisfies self-bounded Assumption 4. Moreover, suppose either Assumption 3 or Assumption 8 hold. Fix any $T \geq 0$ . Let the step-size satisfy the assumptions of the descent lemma (Lemma A.2). Assume any w and m such that $\| w - w_{0}\|^{2}\ge$ max $\left\{\eta T\widehat{F}(w),\eta\widehat{F}(w_{0})\right\}$ and $m\geq 18^{2}L^{2}R^{4}\|w-w_{0}\|^{4}$ . Then, the training loss and the parameters' norm satisfy

$$
\begin{array}{r l r}{{\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\widehat{F}(w_{t})\leq 2\widehat{F}(w)+\frac{5\|w-w_{0}\|^{2}}{2\eta T},}}\\ &{}&{\forall t\in [T]\ :\ \|w_{t}-w_{0}\|\leq 4\|w-w_{0}\|.}\end{array}\tag{16}
$$

To prove Theorem A.1, we first state our descent lemma for both self-bounded losses and lipschitz-smooth losses.

Lemma A.2 (Descent lemma). Let Assumptions 1-2 hold. Assume the loss function satisfies self-boundedness Assumptions 4, 8. Then, for any $\begin{array}{r}{\eta<\frac{1}{R^{2}\widehat{F}(w_{t})}\operatorname*{min}\{\frac{1}{\ell^{2}+L},\frac{1}{\sqrt{L}\ell}\}}\end{array}$ the descent property holds, i.e.,

$$
\widehat{F}(w_{t+1})\leq\widehat{F}(w_{t})-\frac{\eta}{2}\|\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t})\|^{2}.
$$

Moreover, if f satisfies Assumption 3 then the descent property holds for any $\eta \leq 1 / L_{\widehat{F}}$ where $\begin{array}{r}{L_{\widehat{F}}: = \ell^{2}R^{2}+ \frac{L R^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}}\end{array}$ is the smoothness parameter of the training objective.

Proof Due to self-boundedness Assumption 8, as well as Assumptions 1-2 the objective is also self-bounded according to Corollary D.2.1, i.e., $\begin{array}{r}{\|\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w)\|\le\left(\ell^{2}R^{2}+\frac{LR^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}\right)\widehat{F}(w),\|\nabla\widehat{F}(w)\|\le}\end{array}$ $\ell R\widehat{F}(w)$

By Taylor's expansion, there exists a $w^{\prime}\in [ w_{t}, w_{t + 1}]$ such that,

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\widehat{F}(w_{t+1})=\widehat{F}(w_{t})+\left\langle\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t}),w_{t+1}-w_{t}\right\rangle+\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\left\langle w_{t+1}-w_{t},\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w^{\prime})\left(w_{t+1}-w_{t}\right)\right\rangle}\\ &{\qquad\leq\widehat{F}(w_{t})+\left\langle\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t}),w_{t+1}-w_{t}\right\rangle+\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\operatorname*{max}_{v\in [w_{t},w_{t+1}]}\left\|\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(v)\right\|\cdot\|w_{t+1}-w_{t}\|^{2}}\\ &{\qquad\leq\widehat{F}(w_{t})-\eta\|\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t})\|^{2}+\displaystyle\frac{\eta^{2}\left(\ell^{2}R^{2}+\frac{L R^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}\right)}{2}\operatorname*{max}_{v\in [w_{t},w_{t+1}]}\widehat{F}(v)\cdot\left\|\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t})\right\|^{2}.}\end{array}
$$

By Corollary A.7.1, for $\sqrt{m}\ge\eta^{2}L\ell^{2}R^{4}\widehat{F}^{2}(w_{t})\ge LR^{2}\|\eta\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t})\|^{2}=LR^{2}\|w_{t+1}-w_{t}\|^{2}$ it holds that

$$
\operatorname*{max}_{v\in [w_{t},w_{t+1}]}\widehat F(v)\leq 2\operatorname*{max}\{\widehat F(w_{t}),\widehat F(w_{t+1})\},
$$

which yields

$$
\widehat{F}(w_{t+1})\leq\widehat{F}(w_{t})-\eta\|\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t})\|^{2}+\eta^{2}\bigg(\ell^{2}R^{2}+\frac{L R^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}\bigg)\operatorname*{max}\Big\{\widehat{F}(w_{t}),\widehat{F}(w_{t+1})\Big\}\cdot\|\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t})\|^{2}.\tag{17}
$$

We note that the condition on m simplifies to $\begin{array}{r}{m\geq 1\mathrm{~if~}\eta\leq\frac{1}{\sqrt{L}\ell R^{2}}\frac{1}{\widehat{F}(w_{t})}}\end{array}$

Back to (17), if $\widehat{F}(w_{t+1})\geq\widehat{F}(w_{t})$ by our condition $\begin{array}{r}{\eta<\frac{1}{\ell^{2}R^{2}+LR^{2}/\sqrt{m}}\frac{1}{\widehat{F}(w_{t})}}\end{array}$ it holds that

$$
\begin{array}{r l r}{{\widehat{F}(w_{t+1})\leq\widehat{F}(w_{t})+\eta\|\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t})\|^{2}(\frac{\widehat{F}(w_{t+1})}{\widehat{F}(w_{t})}-1)}}\\ &{}&{\leq\widehat{F}(w_{t})+\eta\ell^{2}R^{2}\widehat{F}^{2}(w_{t})(\frac{\widehat{F}(w_{t+1})}{\widehat{F}(w_{t})}-1).}\end{array}
$$

Since $\begin{array}{r}{\eta<\frac{1}{\ell^{2}R^{2}}\frac{1}{\widehat{F}(w_{t})}}\end{array}$

$$
\begin{array}{l}{\displaystyle{\widehat F(w_{t+1})<\widehat F(w_{t})+\widehat F(w_{t})\left(\frac{\widehat F(w_{t+1})}{\widehat F(w_{t})}-1\right)}}\\ {\displaystyle{=\widehat F(w_{t+1}),}}\end{array}
$$

which is a contradiction. Thus it holds that $\widehat{F}(w_{t+1})<\widehat{F}(w_{t})$ . Continuing from Eq. (17) with the assumption $\begin{array}{r}{\eta<\frac{1}{\ell^{2}R^{2}+LR^{2}/\sqrt{m}}\frac{1}{\widehat{F}(w_{t})}}\end{array}$ , we conclude that

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\widehat{F}(w_{t+1})\leq\widehat{F}(w_{t})-\eta\|\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t})\|^{2}+\frac{1}{2}\eta^{2}\bigg(\ell^{2}R^{2}+\frac{LR^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}\bigg)\widehat{F}(w_{t})\cdot\|\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t})\|^{2}}\\ &{\qquad\leq\widehat{F}(w_{t})-\frac{\eta}{2}\|\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t})\|^{2}.}\end{array}
$$

This completes the proof for self-bounded losses.

Next, suppose $f$ is 1-smooth and 1-Lipschitz. Then, as per Corollary D.2.1, $\widehat F$ is smooth with the constant

$$
L_{\widehat{F}}: = \ell^{2}R^{2}+ \frac{L R^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}.
$$

Following similar steps as in the beginning of proof and assuming step-size $\eta \leq 1 / L_{\widehat{F}}$ we immediately conclude that,

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\widehat{F}(w_{t+1})\leq\widehat{F}(w_{t})-\eta\|\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t})\|^{2}+\frac{\eta^{2}L_{\widehat{F}}}{2}\|\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t})\|^{2}}\\ &{\qquad\leq\widehat{F}(w_{t})-\displaystyle\frac{\eta}{2}\|\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t})\|^{2}.}\end{array}
$$

This completes the proof.

As a remark, the descent property implies that the loss decreases by each step, i.e., ${\widehat F}(w_{t})\leq{\widehat F}(w_{0})$ . Thus for self-bounded losses the condition $\begin{array}{r}{\eta<\frac{1}{R^{2}\widehat{F}(w_{0})}\operatorname*{min}\{\frac{1}{\ell^{2}+L},\frac{1}{\sqrt{L}\ell}\}}\end{array}$ is sufficient. We also note that the Lipschitz-smoothness and 2nd order self-bounded assumptions are only required for the descent lemma above, which results in conditions on the step-size based on the properties of loss. In the rest of the proof we only use the self-bounded Assumption 4 in order to use the self-bounded weak convexity property of the objective (see Def. 1).

Next lemma finds a general relation for the training loss in terms of an arbitrary point $w \in \mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}}$ and the fluctuations of loss between w and GD iterates $w_{t}$

Lemma A.3. Let Assumptions 1-2 hold. Assume the loss function satisfies the self-bounded Assumption 4. Moreover, suppose $\widehat F$ and step-size η are such that the following descent condition is satisfied for all $t \geq 0$:

$$
\widehat{F}(w_{t+1})\leq\widehat{F}(w_{t})-\frac{\eta}{2}\|\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t})\|^{2}.\tag{18}
$$

Then, for any w $\in \mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}}$ it holds that

$$
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\widehat{F}(w_{t})\leq\widehat{F}(w)+\frac{\|w-w_{0}\|^{2}}{\eta T}+\frac{1}{2}\frac{L R^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\operatorname*{max}_{\alpha\in [0,1]}\widehat{F}(w_{\alpha t})\|w-w_{t}\|^{2},
$$

where we set $w_{\alpha t}: =\alpha w_{t}+(1-\alpha)w$

## Proof

Fix any w. By Taylor, there exists $w_{\alpha t},\alpha\in [0,1]$ such that

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\widehat{F}(w)=\widehat{F}(w_{t})+\left\langle\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t}),w-w_{t}\right\rangle+\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\left\langle w-w_{t},\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w_{\alpha t})\left(w-w_{t}\right)\right\rangle}\\ &{\qquad\geq\widehat{F}(w_{t})+\left\langle\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t}),w-w_{t}\right\rangle+\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\lambda_{\operatorname*{min}}\left(\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w_{\alpha t})\right)\|w-w_{t}\|^{2}}\\ &{\qquad\geq\widehat{F}(w_{t})+\left\langle\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t}),w-w_{t}\right\rangle-\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\frac{L R^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}\widehat{F}(w_{\alpha t})\|w-w_{t}\|^{2}.}\end{array}
$$

The last line is true by Corollary D.2.1. Thus, for any w,

$$
\widehat{F}(w)\geq\widehat{F}(w_{t})+\Big\langle\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t}),w-w_{t}\Big\rangle-\frac{1}{2}\frac{L R^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}\operatorname*{max}_{\alpha\in [0,1]}\widehat{F}(w_{\alpha t})\|w-w_{t}\|^{2}.
$$

Plugging this in (18) gives

$$
\begin{array}{r l r}&{}&{\widehat{F}(w_{t+1})\leq\widehat{F}(w)-\left\langle\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t}),w-w_{t}\right\rangle-\displaystyle\frac{\eta}{2}\left\|\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t})\right\|^{2}+\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\frac{L R^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}\displaystyle\operatorname*{max}_{\alpha\in [0,1]}\widehat{F}(w_{\alpha t})\|w-w_{t}\|^{2}}\\ &{}&{\displaystyle=\widehat{F}(w)+\frac{1}{\eta}\left(\|w-w_{t}\|^{2}-\|w-w_{t+1}\|^{2}\right)+\frac{1}{2}\frac{L R^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}\displaystyle\operatorname*{max}_{\alpha\in [0,1]}\widehat{F}(w_{\alpha t})\|w-w_{t}\|^{2}.\qquad(19)}\end{array}
$$

where the second line follows by completion of squares using $w_{t+1}-w_{t}= -\eta\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t})$

Telescoping the above display for $t=0,\ldots,T-1$ , we arrive at the desired.

Next, when m is large enough so that we can invoke the generalized-local quasiconvexity property, the bound of Lemma A.3 takes the following convenient form

Lemma A.4. Let the assumptions of Lemma A.3 hold. Assume w and m such that $\sqrt{m}\geq 2 L R^{2}\Vert w - w_{t}\Vert^{2}$ for all $t \in [ T - 1 ]$ then

$$
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\widehat{F}(w_{t})\leq 2\widehat{F}(w)+\frac{2\|w-w_{0}\|^{2}}{\eta T}+\frac{\widehat{F}(w_{0})}{2T}.\tag{20}
$$

Proof We invoke Corollary A.7.1 with $\lambda = 4$ to deduce that for all $t \in [ T - 1 ]$

$$
\operatorname*{max}_{\alpha\in [0,1]}\widehat{F}(w_{\alpha t})\leq\frac{4}{3}\operatorname*{max}\{\widehat{F}(w),\widehat{F}(w_{t})\}<\frac{4}{3}\widehat{F}(w_{t})+\frac{4}{3}\widehat{F}(w).\tag{21}
$$

Noting the assumption on m and recalling Lemma A.3,

$$
\begin{array}{r l r}{{\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\widehat{F}(w_{t})\leq\widehat{F}(w)+\frac{\|w-w_{0}\|^{2}}{\eta T}+\frac{1}{2}\frac{L R^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\underset{\alpha\in [0,1]}{\operatorname*{max}}\widehat{F}(w_{\alpha t})\|w-w_{t}\|^{2}}}\\ &{}&{\leq\frac{4}{3}\widehat{F}(w)+\frac{\|w-w_{0}\|^{2}}{\eta T}+\frac{1}{3 T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\widehat{F}(w_{t})}\\ &{}&{\leq\frac{4}{3}\widehat{F}(w)+\frac{\|w-w_{0}\|^{2}}{\eta T}+\frac{1}{3 T}\sum_{t=0}^{T}\widehat{F}(w_{t}).}\end{array}
$$

Arranging terms yields the desired result.

Finally, using the about bounds on the training loss, we can bound the parameter-norm using a recursive argument presented in the lemma below.

Lemma A.5 (Iterates-norm bound). Suppose the assumptions of Lemma A.3 hold. Fix any $T \geq 0$ and assume any w and m such that

$$
\begin{array}{r}{\|w-w_{0}\|^{2}{\ge}\operatorname*{max}\{\eta T\widehat F(w),\eta\widehat F(w_{0})\}.}\end{array}\tag{22}
$$

and

$$
\sqrt{m}\geq 18LR^{2}\Vert w-w_{0}\Vert^{2},\tag{23}
$$

Then, for all $t \in [ T ]$

$$
\| w_{t}- w \| \leq 3 \| w - w_{0}\| .\tag{24}
$$

Proof Denote $A_{t}= \| w_{t}- w \|$ . Start by recalling from (19) that for all t:

$$
A_{t+1}^{2}\leq A_{t}^{2}+\eta\widehat{F}(w)-\eta\widehat{F}(w_{t+1})+\eta\frac{L R^{2}}{2\sqrt{m}}\operatorname*{max}_{\alpha\in [0,1]}\widehat{F}(w_{\alpha t})A_{t}^{2}.\tag{25}
$$

We will prove the desired statement (24) using induction. For $t=0,A_{0}=\|w-w_{0}\|$ Thus, the assumption of induction holds. Now assume (24) is correct for $t \in [ T - 1 ]$ , i.e. $A_{t}\leq 3\|w-w_{0}\|,\forall t\in [T-1]$ . We will then prove it holds for $t = T$

The first observation is that by induction hypothesis $\sqrt{m}\geq 18LR^{2}\|w-w_{0}\|^{2}{\geq}2LR^{2}A_{t}^{2}$ for all $t \in [ T - 1 ]$ . Thus, for all $t \in [ T - 1 ]$ , the condition of the generalized local quasi-convexity Corollary 5.1.1 holds for $\lambda = 4$ implying (see also (21))

$$
\forall t\in [T-1]:\ \operatorname*{max}_{\alpha\in [0,1]}{\widehat{F}}(w_{\alpha t})\leq{\frac{4}{3}}{\widehat{F}}(w_{t})+{\frac{4}{3}}{\widehat{F}}(w).
$$

Using this in (25) we find for all $t \in [ T - 1 ]$ that

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{A_{t+1}^{2}\leq A_{t}^{2}+\eta\widehat{F}(w)-\eta\widehat{F}(w_{t+1})+\eta\frac{LR^{2}\cdot A_{t}^{2}}{2\sqrt{m}}\left(\frac 43\widehat{F}(w_{t})+\frac 43\widehat{F}(w)\right)}\\ &{\qquad\leq A_{t}^{2}+\eta\widehat{F}(w)-\eta\widehat{F}(w_{t+1})+\eta\left(\frac 13\widehat{F}(w_{t})+\frac 13\widehat{F}(w)\right)}\end{array}
$$

where in the second inequality we used again that $\sqrt{m}\geq 2 L R^{2}A_{t}^{2}$ . We proceed by telescoping the above display over $t=0,1,\dots,T-1$ to get

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{A_{T}^{2}\le A_{0}^{2}+\displaystyle\frac{4}{3}\eta T\widehat F(w)+\displaystyle\frac{1}{3}\eta\widehat F(w_{0})+\displaystyle\frac{1}{3}\eta\displaystyle\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\widehat F(w_{t})-\eta\widehat F(w_{T})}\\ &{\qquad\le A_{0}^{2}+\displaystyle\frac{4}{3}\eta T\widehat F(w)+\displaystyle\frac{2}{3}\eta\widehat F(w_{0})+\displaystyle\frac{1}{3}\eta\displaystyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\widehat F(w_{t}),}\end{array}
$$

where the second line follows by nonegativity of the loss.

Now, to bound the last term above, observe that the condition of Lemma A.4 holds since $\sqrt{m}\geq 2 L R^{2}A_{t}^{2}$ for all $t \in [ T - 1 ]$ by induction hypothesis. Hence, using (20), we conclude that

$$
\begin{array}{r l r}{{A_{T}^{2}\le A_{0}^{2}+\frac 43\eta T\widehat F(w)+\frac 23\eta\widehat F(w_{0})+\frac 13\eta T(2\widehat F(w)+\frac{2A_{0}^{2}}{\eta T}+\frac{\widehat F(w_{0})}{2T})}}\\ &{}&{=\frac 53A_{0}^{2}+2\eta T\widehat F(w)+\frac 56\eta\widehat F(w_{0})}\\ &{}&{\le\frac 53\|w-w_{0}\|^{2}+2\|w-w_{0}\|^{2}+\frac 56\|w-w_{0}\|^{2}=\frac 92\|w-w_{0}\|^{2}\qquad\Longrightarrow\ A_{T}\le 3\|w-w_{0}\|.}\end{array}\tag{26}
$$

In the last inequality, we used the assumptions of the lemma on $\lVert w - w_{0}\rVert$ and $A_{0}= \| w - w_{0}\|$ This completes the proof.

## Completing the proof of Theorem A.1.

The proof follows from combining the bounds on the training loss and parameters' growth from Lemmas $\mathrm{{A . 4 – A . 5}}$ and noting that with condition on $\| w - w_{0}\|^{2}$ from Lemma $\mathrm{A . 5}$ we have ${\widehat F}(w_{0})\leq\|w-w_{0}\|^{2}/\eta$ to derive (16). Moreover, we have $\lVert w_{t}- w_{0}\rVert \leq \lVert w_{t}- w \rVert + \lVert w - w_{0}\rVert \leq$ $4 \lVert w - w_{0}\rVert$

## A.3 Generalized local quasi-convexity property

In the remainder of this section, we prove the generalized local quasi-convexity property.

Proposition A.7 (Restatement of Proposition 5.1). Suppose $\widehat{F}: \mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}}\to \mathbb{R}$ satisfies the self-bounded weak convexity property in Eq. 4 with parameter κ. Let $w_{1}, w_{2}\in \mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}}$ be two arbitrary points with distance $\| w_{1}- w_{2}\| \leq D < \sqrt{2 / \kappa}$ . Set $\tau: =\left(1-\kappa D^{2}/2\right)^{-1}$ . Then,

$$
\operatorname*{max}_{v\in [w_{1},w_{2}]}\widehat{F}(v)\leq\tau\cdot\operatorname*{max}\{\widehat{F}(w_{1}),\widehat{F}(w_{2})\}.\tag{27}
$$

Proof Assume the claim of the proposition is incorrect, then

$$
\operatorname*{max}_{v\in [w_{1},w_{2}]}\widehat{F}(v)>\tau\cdot\operatorname*{max}\{\widehat{F}(w_{1}),\widehat{F}(w_{2})\}>\operatorname*{max}\{\widehat{F}(w_{1}),\widehat{F}(w_{2})\}.\tag{28}
$$

Define $\begin{array}{r}{w_{\star}: =\arg\operatorname*{max}_{v\in [w_{1},w_{2}]}\widehat{F}(v)}\end{array}$ . Note that $w_{\star}$ is an interior point. Thus by the optimality condition it holds

$$
\left\langle\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{\star}),w_{1}-w_{2}\right\rangle=0.\tag{29}
$$

By Taylor's approximation theorem for two points w1, $w \in \mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}}$ , there exists a $w_{\beta}\in [w,w_{1}]$ such that

$$
\widehat{F}(w_{1})=\widehat{F}(w)+\left\langle\nabla\widehat{F}(w),w_{1}-w\right\rangle+\frac{1}{2}\left\langle w-w_{1},\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w_{\beta})\left(w-w_{1}\right)\right\rangle\tag{30}
$$

Pick $w=w_{\star}=\alpha_{\star}w_{1}+(1-\alpha_{\star})w_{2}$ in Eq. (30), and note that

$$
\begin{array}{r}{\Big\langle\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{\star}),w_{1}-w_{\star}\Big\rangle= -(1-\alpha_{\star})\Big\langle\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{\star}),w_{1}-w_{2}\Big\rangle=0.}\end{array}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\widehat{F}(w_{1})=\widehat{F}(w_{\star})+\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\left\langle w_{\star}-w_{1},\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w_{\beta})\left(w_{\star}-w_{1}\right)\right\rangle}\\ &{\qquad\quad\geq\widehat{F}(w_{\star})+\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\lambda_{\mathrm{min}}(\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w_{\beta}))\left\|w_{\star}-w_{1}\right\|^{2}}\\ &{\qquad\quad\geq\widehat{F}(w_{\star})-\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\kappa\widehat{F}(w_{\beta})\Big\Vert w_{\star}-w_{1}\Big\Vert^{2}.}\end{array}
$$

where in the last line we used the self-bounded weak convexity property i.e., $\lambda_{\operatorname*{min}}\left(\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(\boldsymbol{w}_{\beta})\right)\geq-\kappa\widehat{F}(w_{\beta})$

This leads to

$$
\begin{array}{l}{\displaystyle\widehat{F}(w_{1})\geq\widehat{F}(w_{\star})-\frac{(1-\alpha_{\star})^{2}}{2}\kappa\widehat{F}(w_{\beta})\Big\|w_{1}-w_{2}\Big\|^{2}}\\ {\displaystyle>\widehat{F}(w_{\star})-\frac{1}{2}\kappa\widehat{F}(w_{\beta})\Big\|w_{1}-w_{2}\Big\|^{2}.}\end{array}
$$

Note that $w_{\beta}\in [ w_{\star}, w_{1}] \subset [ w_{1}, w_{2}]$ , thus $\widehat{F}(w_{\beta})\leq\widehat{F}(w_{\star})$ by definition of $w_{\star}$. Therefore,

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\widehat{F}(w_{\star})<\displaystyle\frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{2}\kappa\|w_{1}-w_{2}\|^{2}}\widehat{F}(w_{1})}\\ &{\qquad\le\displaystyle\frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{2}\kappa D^{2}}\widehat{F}(w_{1}),}\end{array}
$$

which is in contradiction with (28). This proves the statement of the proposition.

Specializing this property to two-layer neural networks yields the following.

Corollary A.7.1 (Restatement of Corollary 5.1.1). Let Assumptions 1,2, 4 hold. Fix arbitrary w1, $w_{2}\in \mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}}$ , any constant $\lambda > 1$ , and m large enough such that $\sqrt{m}\geq \lambda \frac{L R^{2}}{2}\Vert w_{1}-$ $w_{2}\|^{2}$ . Then,

$$
\operatorname*{max}_{v\in [w_{1},w_{2}]}\widehat{F}(v)\leq(1-1/\lambda)^{-1}\cdot\operatorname*{max}\{\widehat{F}(w_{1}),\widehat{F}(w_{2})\}.\tag{31}
$$

Proof By our assumptions and Corollary D.2.1 the objective's Hessian satisfies

$$
\lambda_{\operatorname*{min}}\left(\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w)\right)\geq-\frac{L R^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}\widehat{F}(w).
$$

Invoking Proposition A.7 with $\begin{array}{r}{\kappa : = \frac{L R^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}}\end{array}$ concludes the claim.

### Proof of Theorem 3.3

## A.2 Proof of Theorem 3.3

Here we prove training loss bound for interpolating NN as asserted by Theorem 3.3. Similar to the previous section, we prove a more general result where the loss is not necessarily Lipschitz or smooth. We are now ready to prove Theorem 3.3 for general self-bounded losses. In particular, Theorem 3.3 follows directly from the next result by choosing f to be Lipschitz and smooth.

Theorem A.6 (General statement of Theorem 3.3). Suppose Assumptions 1-2, 4 hold. Moreover, assume the objective and data satisfy the Assumption 5. Let the step-size satisfy the assumptions of Descent Lemma A.2. Moreover, assume $\begin{array}{r}{\eta\le\operatorname*{min}\{g(1)^{2},\frac{1}{L_{\widehat{F}}},\frac{g(1)^{2}}{\widehat{F}(w_{0})}\}}\end{array}$ and $m\geq 18^{2}L^{2}R^{4}g(\frac{1}{T})^{4}$ for a fixed training horizon T. Then,

$$
\widehat{F}(w_{T})\leq\frac{2}{T}+\frac{5g(\frac{1}{T})^{2}}{2\eta T},
$$

$$
\forall t\in [T]\ :\ \|w_{t}-w_{0}\|\ \leq\ 4g(\frac{1}{T}).
$$

Proof According to Assumption 5, for any sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$ , there exists a $w^{(\varepsilon)}$ such that $\widehat{F}(w^{(\varepsilon)})\leq\varepsilon$ and $\lVert\boldsymbol{w}^{(\varepsilon)}-\boldsymbol{w}_{0}\rVert=g(\varepsilon)$ . Pick $\varepsilon = 1 / T$ . With the condition $\eta \leq$ min $\{g(1)^{2},g(1)^{2}/\widehat{F}(w_{0})\}$ we have

$$
\operatorname*{max}\left\{\eta T\widehat{F}(w^{(1/T)}),\eta\widehat{F}(w_{0})\right\}\leq g(1)^{2}\leq g(\frac{1}{T})^{2}=\|w^{(1/T)}-w_{0}\|^{2},
$$

where in the second inequality we used the fact that $g$ is a decreasing function. The desired result is obtained by Theorem A.1.

context.name: Notation
context.statement:
## Notation

We define $[n]: =\{1,2,\cdots,n\}$. We use the standard notation $O(\cdot),\Omega(\cdot)$ and use $\tilde{O}(\cdot),\tilde{\Omega}(\cdot)$ to hide polylogarithmic factors. Occasionally we use $\lesssim$ to hide numerical constants. The Gradient and Hessian of a function $\Phi : \mathbb{R}^{d_{1}\times d_{2}}\to \mathbb{R}$ with respect to the ith input $(i=1,2)$ are denoted by $\nabla_{i}\Phi$ and $\nabla_{i}^{2}\Phi$ , respectively. All logarithms are in base e. We use $\| \cdot \|$ for the $\ell_{2}$ norm of vectors and the operator norm of matrices. We denote $[ w_{1}, w_{2}] : = \{w \ : \ w =$ $\alpha w_{1}+(1-\alpha)w_{2},\alpha\in [0,1]\}$ the line segment between w1, $w_{2}\in \mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}}$ .

context.name: Setup: empirical risk objective (Section 2, eqs. (1)-(2))
context.statement:
## 2. Problem Setup

Given n i.i.d. samples $(x_{i},y_{i})\sim\mathcal{D},i\in [n]$ from data distribution D, we study unconstrained empirical risk minimization with objective $\widehat{F}: \mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}}\to \mathbb{R}$:

$$
\operatorname*{min}_{w\in\mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}}}\Big\{\widehat{F}(w): =\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\widehat{F}_{i}(w)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}f\left(y_{i}\Phi\left(w,x_{i}\right)\right)\Big\}.\tag{1}
$$

This serves as a proxy for minimizing the test loss $F : \mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}}\to \mathbb{R}$:

$$
F(w): =\mathbb{E}_{(x,y)\sim\mathcal{D}}\left[f\left(y\Phi(w,x)\right)\right].\tag{2}
$$

We introduce our assumptions on the data $(x,y)$ , the model $\Phi(\cdot,x)$ , and the loss function $f(\cdot)$ , below. We start by imposing the following mild assumption on the data distribution.

context.name: Assumption 1 (Bounded features)
context.statement: Assumption 1 (Bounded features). Assume any $(x,y)\sim\mathcal{D}$ has almost surely bounded features, i.e. $\| x \| \leq R$ , and binary label $y \in \{\pm 1 \}$.

context.name: Setup: two-layer network model (eq. (3)) and second-layer weights
context.statement:
The model $\Phi:\mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}}\times\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}$ is parameterized by trainable weights $w\in\mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}}$ and takes input $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ . For our main results, we assume $\Phi$ is a one-hidden layer neural-net of m neurons, i.e.

$$
\Phi(w,x): =\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\sum_{j=1}^{m}a_{j}\sigma(\langle w_{j},x\rangle),\tag{3}
$$

where $\sigma:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is the activation function, $w_{j}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ denotes the weight vector of the jth hidden neuron and $\textstyle{\frac{a_{j}}{\sqrt{m}}},j\in [m]$ are the second-layer weights. For the second layer weights, we assume that they are fixed during training taking values $a_{j}\in\{\pm 1\}$ . We assume that for half of second layer weights $a_{j}=1$ and for the other half $a_{j}= -1$ . On the other hand, all the first-layer weights are updated during training. Thus, the total number of trainable parameters is $d^{\prime}=m d$ and we denote $w=[w_{1};w_{2};\ldots;w_{m}]\in\mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}}$ the vector of trainable weights. Throughout, we make the following assumptions on the activation function.

context.name: Assumption 2 (Lipschitz and smooth activation)
context.statement:
Assumption 2 (Lipschitz and smooth activation). The activation function $\sigma : \mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}$ satisfies the following for non-negative constants $\ell,L$:

$$
|\sigma^{\prime}(u)|\leq\ell,\quad|\sigma^{\prime\prime}(u)|\leq L,\qquad\forall u\in\mathbb{R}.
$$

context.name: Loss class and Assumption 3 (Lipschitz and smooth loss)
context.statement:
Next, we discuss conditions on the loss function. Of primal interest is the commonly used logistic loss function $f(u)=\log(1+e^{-u})$ . However, our results hold for a broader class of convex, non-negative and monotonically decreasing functions $(\operatorname*{lim}_{u\to\infty}f(u)=0)$ that satisfy the following:

Assumption 3 (Lipschitz and smooth loss). The convex loss function $f : \mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R_{+}}$ satisfies for all $u \in \mathbb{R}$

3.A: Lipschitzness: $|f^{\prime}(u)|\leq G_{f}$

3.B: Smoothness: $f^{\prime\prime}(u)\leq L_{f}$

context.name: Assumption 4 (Self-bounded loss) and normalization G_f = L_f = beta_f = 1
context.statement:
Assumption 4 (Self-bounded loss). The convex loss function $f : \mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}_{+}$ is self-bounded with some constant $\beta_{f}>0,\ i.e.,\ |f^{\prime}(u)|\leq\beta_{f}f(u),\forall u\in\mathbb{R}$

The self-boundedness Assumption 4 is the key property of the loss that drives our analysis and justifies the polylogarithmic width requirement, as will become evident. Note that the logistic loss naturally satisfies Assumptions 3.A and 3.B (with $G_{f}=1,L_{f}=1/4)$ , as well as, Assumption 4 with $\beta_{f}= 1$ . Other interesting examples of loss functions satisfying those assumptions include polynomial losses, with the tail behavior $f(u)=1/u^{\beta}$ for $\beta > 0$, which we discuss in Remark 2. To lighten the notation and without loss of generality, we set $G_{f}= L_{f}= \beta_{f}= 1$ for the rest of the paper. We remark that our training-loss results also hold for the exponential loss $e^{- u}$ . The exponential loss is self-bounded and while it is not Lipschitz or smooth it satisfies a second-order self-bounded property $f^{\prime\prime}(u)\leq f(u)$ , which we can leverage instead; see Appendix A for details.

context.name: Gradient descent update
context.statement:
We present bounds on the train loss and generalization gap of gradient-descent (GD) under the setting of Section 2. Formally, GD with step-size $\eta > 0$ optimizes (1) by performing the following updates starting from an initialization w0:

$$
\forall t\geq 0:w_{t+1}=w_{t}-\eta\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t}).
$$

context.name: Definition 1 (Self-bounded weak convexity, eq. (4))
context.statement:
Definition 1 (Self-bounded weak convexity). We say a function $\widehat{F}: \mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}}\to \mathbb{R}$ is self-bounded weakly convex if there exists constant $\kappa > 0$ such that for all w,

$$
\lambda_{\mathrm{min}}\left(\nabla^{2}{\widehat F}(w)\right)\geq-\kappa{\widehat F}(w).\tag{4}
$$

Recall a function $G : \mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}}\to \mathbb{R}$ is weakly convex if $\exists \kappa \geq 0$ such that uniformly over all $w\in\mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}},\lambda_{\operatorname*{min}}\left(\nabla^{2}G(w)\right)\geq-\kappa$ . If $\kappa = 0$ , the function is convex. Instead, property (4) lower bounds the curvature by $-\kappa G(w)$ that changes proportionally with the function value $G(w)$. We explain below how this is exploited in our setting.

context.name: Definitions for the gradient/Hessian calculations (Appendix D.1, eqs. (50)-(52b))
context.statement:
## D.1 Definitions

Assume IID data $(x,y)\sim\mathcal{D},x\in\mathbb{R}^{d},y\in\{\pm 1\}$ . Denote for convenience $z : = y x$ . Suppose two-layer neural network model

$$
\Phi(w,x_{i})=\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\sum_{j\in [m]}a_{j}\sigma(\langle w_{j},x\rangle)\tag{50}
$$

$a_{j}\in \{\pm 1 \}, j \in [ m ]$ and first-layer weights trained by GD on

$$
\widehat F(w)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i\in [n]}f(y_{i}\Phi(w,x_{i}))= :\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i\in [n]}f(w,z_{i}).\tag{51}
$$

for loss function $f : \mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}$

For convenience define

$$
\widehat{F}^{\prime}(w)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i\in [n]}\vert f^{\prime}(y_{i}\Phi(w,x_{i}))\vert\tag{52a}
$$

$$
\widehat{F}^{\prime\prime}(w)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i\in [n]}|f^{\prime\prime}\left(y_{i}\Phi(w,x_{i})\right)|\tag{52b}
$$

context.name: Corollary D.2.1 (Self-boundedness of Objective)
context.statement:
Corollary D.2.1 (Self-boundedness of Objective). Let Assumption 2 hold. If the loss satisfies Assumptions 4 (with $\beta_{f}=1)$ and 8, then

1. $\lVert\nabla\widehat{F}(w)\rVert\leq\ell R\widehat{F}(w)$

$$
\begin{array}{r}{2.\|\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w)\|{\le}\left(\ell^{2}R^{2}+\frac{LR^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}\right)\widehat{F}(w).}\end{array}
$$

3. $\begin{array}{r}{\lambda_{\operatorname*{min}}\left(\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w)\right)\geq-\frac{L R^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}\widehat{F}(w).}\end{array}$

If in addition the loss satisfies Assumptions 3.A and 3.B with $L_{f}= G_{f}= 1$ , then

6. $\lVert\nabla\widehat{F}(w)\rVert\leq\ell R.$

$$
\begin{array}{r}{7.\ \|\nabla^{2}\widehat{F}(w)\|\le\ell^{2}R^{2}+\frac{LR^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}.}\end{array}
$$

context.name: Assumption 5 (NN-Realizability)
context.statement:
Assumption 5 (NN-Realizability). There exists a decreasing function $g : \mathbb{R}_{+}\to \mathbb{R}_{+}$ which measures the norm of deviations from initialization of models that achieve arbitrarily small training error.

Formally, for almost surely all n training samples and for any sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $\boldsymbol{w}^{(\varepsilon)}\in\mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}}$ such that

$$
{\widehat F}(w^{(\varepsilon)})\leq\varepsilon,\ and\ g(\varepsilon)=\Big\|w^{(\varepsilon)}-w_{0}\Big\|.
$$

Since Assumption 5 holds for arbitrarily small ε, it guarantees that the model has enough capacity to interpolate the data, i.e., attain train error that is arbitrarily small (ε). Additionally, this is accomplished for model weights whose distance from initialization is managed by the function $g(\varepsilon)$ . By using these model weights to select w in Theorem 3.2 we obtain train loss bounds for interpolating models.

context.name: Assumption 8 (2nd order self-boundedness)
context.statement:
Assumption 8 (2nd order self-boundedness). The convex loss function $f : \mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}_{+}$ satisfies the 2nd order self-boundedness property, i.e.

$$
f^{\prime\prime}(u)\leq f(u),\forall u\in\mathbb{R}.
$$

context.name: Theorem A.1 (General statement of Theorem 3.2)
context.statement:
Theorem A.1 (General statement of Theorem 3.2). Let Assumptions 1-2 hold. Assume the loss function satisfies self-bounded Assumption 4. Moreover, suppose either Assumption 3 or Assumption 8 hold. Fix any $T \geq 0$ . Let the step-size satisfy the assumptions of the descent lemma (Lemma A.2). Assume any w and m such that $\| w - w_{0}\|^{2}\ge$ max $\left\{\eta T\widehat{F}(w),\eta\widehat{F}(w_{0})\right\}$ and $m\geq 18^{2}L^{2}R^{4}\|w-w_{0}\|^{4}$ . Then, the training loss and the parameters' norm satisfy

$$
\begin{array}{r l r}{{\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\widehat{F}(w_{t})\leq 2\widehat{F}(w)+\frac{5\|w-w_{0}\|^{2}}{2\eta T},}}\\ &{}&{\forall t\in [T]\ :\ \|w_{t}-w_{0}\|\leq 4\|w-w_{0}\|.}\end{array}\tag{16}
$$

context.name: Lemma A.2 (Descent lemma)
context.statement:
Lemma A.2 (Descent lemma). Let Assumptions 1-2 hold. Assume the loss function satisfies self-boundedness Assumptions 4, 8. Then, for any $\begin{array}{r}{\eta<\frac{1}{R^{2}\widehat{F}(w_{t})}\operatorname*{min}\{\frac{1}{\ell^{2}+L},\frac{1}{\sqrt{L}\ell}\}}\end{array}$ the descent property holds, i.e.,

$$
\widehat{F}(w_{t+1})\leq\widehat{F}(w_{t})-\frac{\eta}{2}\|\nabla\widehat{F}(w_{t})\|^{2}.
$$

Moreover, if f satisfies Assumption 3 then the descent property holds for any $\eta \leq 1 / L_{\widehat{F}}$ where $\begin{array}{r}{L_{\widehat{F}}: = \ell^{2}R^{2}+ \frac{L R^{2}}{\sqrt{m}}}\end{array}$ is the smoothness parameter of the training objective.

context.name: Remark 1 (Example: linearly-separable data)
context.statement:
Remark 1 (Example: Linearly-separable data). Consider logistic-loss minimization, tanh activation $\begin{array}{r}{\sigma(u)=\frac{e^{u}-e^{-u}}{e^{u}+e^{-u}}}\end{array}$ and data distribution that is linearly separable with margin γ, $i . e .$ , for almost surely all n samples there exists unit-norm vector $v^{\star}\in \mathbb{R}^{d}$ such that $\mathrm{min}_{i\in [n]}y_{i}\langle v^{\star},x_{i}\rangle=\gamma$. We initialize the weights to zero, i.e. $w_{0}~ = ~ 0$ and show that the realizability Assumption 5 naturally holds in this setting. To see this, for any fixed $\varepsilon > 0$ , set $\alpha=2\log(1/\varepsilon)/\gamma\sqrt{m}$ and assume m $\geq 4\log^{2}(1/\varepsilon)$ . With this choice, select weights $\begin{array}{r}{w_{j}^{(\varepsilon)}: =\alpha v^{\star},a_{j}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\ for\ j\in [1,\cdot\cdot\cdot,\frac{m}{2}]}\end{array}$ and $\begin{array}{r}{w_{j}^{(\varepsilon)}: = -\alpha v^{\star},a_{j}=\frac{-1}{\sqrt{m}}\ for\ j\in\{\frac{m}{2}+1,\cdot\cdot\cdot,m\}}\end{array}$ Then, the model output for any sample $(x_{i},y_{i})$ satisfies

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{y_{i}\Phi(w^{(\varepsilon)},x_{i})=\displaystyle\frac{y_{i}\sqrt{m}}{2}\left(\sigma(\alpha\langle v^{\star},x_{i}\rangle)-\sigma(-\alpha\langle v^{\star},x_{i}\rangle)\right)}\\ &{\quad\quad\quad=y_{i}\sqrt{m}\sigma(\alpha\langle v^{\star},x_{i}\rangle)\ge\sqrt{m}\sigma(\alpha\gamma)\ge\displaystyle\frac{\sqrt{m}}{2}\alpha\gamma=\log(1/\varepsilon),}\end{array}
$$

where the second equality uses the fact that tanh is odd, the first inequality follows by the increasing nature of tanh and data separability, and the last inequality follows since $\alpha \gamma \leq 1$ and $\sigma(u)\geq u/2$ for all $u\in [0,1]$ . Thus, the loss satisfies $\widehat{F}(w^{(\varepsilon)})\leq\varepsilon$ since for the logistic function log $\left(1+e^{u}\right)\leq e^{u}$ . Moreover, our choice of α implies $g(\varepsilon)=\|w^{(\varepsilon)}-w_{0}\|=$ $\|w^{(\varepsilon)}\|{=}\alpha\sqrt{m}=2\log(1/\varepsilon)/\gamma$ . To conclude, the NN-Realizability Assumption 5 holds with $g(\varepsilon)=2\log(1/\varepsilon)/\gamma$ and thus applying Theorems 3.3 and 3.5 shows that with $m=\Omega(\log^{4}(T))$ neurons, the training loss and generalization gap are respectively bounded by $\begin{array}{r}{{\tilde{O}}(\frac{1}{\gamma^{2}T})}\end{array}$ and $\begin{array}{r}{{\cal\tilde{O}}(\frac{1}{\gamma^{2}n})}\end{array}$ , which are known to be optimal under this data assumption. We note that the same conclusion as above holds for other smooth activations such as Softmax or GELU.

context.name: Section 4: NTK separability, initialization bound, Proposition 4.1 (eq. (9))
context.statement:
In this section, we interpret our results for NTK-separable data by showing that our realizability condition holds for this class. We recall the definition of NTK-separability below Nitanda et al. (2019); Chen et al. (2020); Cao and Gu (2020).

Assumption 6 (Separability by NTK). For almost surely all n training samples from the data distribution there exists $w^{\star}\in \mathbb{R}^{d^{\prime}}$ and $\gamma > 0$ such that $\| w^{\star}\| = 1$ and for all $i \in [ n ]$ ,

$$
\begin{array}{r}{y_{i}\Bigl\langle\nabla_{1}\Phi(w_{0},x_{i}),w^{\star}\Bigr\rangle\geq\gamma .}\end{array}\tag{8}
$$

We also assume a bound on the model's output at initialization. Similar assumptions, but for the value of the loss, also appear in prior works that study generalization using the algorithmic stability framework Richards and Kuzborskij (2021); Lei et al. (2022).

Assumption 7 (Initialization bound). There exists parameter C such that $\forall i \in [ n ] \ :$ $|\Phi(w_{0},x_{i})|\leq C,$ for almost surely all n training samples from the data distribution

The next proposition relates the NTK-separability assumption to our realizability assumption. The proofs for this section are given in Appendix C.

Proposition 4.1 (Realizability of NTK-separable data). Let Assumptions $1-2,6-7$ hold. Assume f (·) to be the logistic loss. Fix $\varepsilon > 0$ and let $\begin{array}{r}{m\geq\frac{L^{2}R^{4}}{4\gamma^{4}C^{2}}(2C+\log(1/\varepsilon))^{4}}\end{array}$ . Then the realizability Assumption 5 holds with $\begin{array}{r}{g(\varepsilon)=\frac{1}{\gamma}(2C+\log(1/\varepsilon))}\end{array}$ . In other words, there exists $w^{(\varepsilon)}$ such that

$$
\widehat{F}(w^{(\varepsilon)})\leq\varepsilon,\quad and\quad\left\|w^{(\varepsilon)}-w_{0}\right\|=\frac{1}{\gamma}\left(2C+\log(1/\varepsilon)\right).\tag{9}
$$
