targets.label: Theorem 1
targets.statement:
Theorem 1 (Classification-calibration) Let L be the LHS loss. For any x such that $p(\mathbf{x})\in$ (0, 1) with $p(\mathbf{x})\neq 1/2$, a global minimizer of $\operatorname{E}[L(\mathbf{Y}f(\mathbf{X}))\mid\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{x}]$ uniquely exists and is

$$
\bar{f}({\bf x})=\left\{\begin{array}{l l}{-(1-p({\bf x}))(p({\bf x}))^{-1},\quad}&{ifp({\bf x})<1/2,}\\ {+p({\bf x})(1-p({\bf x}))^{-1},\quad}&{ifp({\bf x})>1/2.}\end{array}\right.
$$

Also, sgn $\{{\bar{f}}({\bf x}) \}= f^{*}({\bf x})$ , where $f^{*}(\mathbf{x})=\mathrm{sgn}\{p(\mathbf{x})-1/2\}$ is the Bayes rule.

targets.label: Theorem 2
targets.statement:
Theorem 2 (Existence of global solution) Let $(\mathbf{x}_{i},y_{i})\in\mathbb{R}^{p}\times\{-1,+1\}$ for $i=1,\ldots,n$ be training data. Suppose there exist $i,j$ with $y_{i}= + 1$ and $y_{j}= - 1$ . Then, there exists a global solution to

$$
\operatorname*{min}\mathcal{L}(\beta_{0},\beta)=\operatorname*{min}_{\beta_{0},\beta}\left[\sum_{i=1}^{n}L\left(y_{i}(\beta_{0}+\mathbf{x}_{i}^{T}\beta)\right)/n+\lambda\beta^{T}\beta\right],\tag{2}
$$

where L is the LHS loss and $\lambda > 0$ is a tuning parameter.

targets.label: Theorem 6
targets.statement:
Theorem 6 (Classification-calibration) For any x such that $p(\mathbf{x})\in(0,1)$ with $p(\mathbf{x})\neq 1/2$ , a global minimizer of $\operatorname{E}[L_{r}(\mathbf{Y}f(\mathbf{X}))\mid\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{x}]$ uniquely exists and is

$$
\begin{array}{r l}{-\left\{(1-p({\bf x}))/p({\bf x})\right\}^{r/(r-1)},}&{{}\quad if~p({\bf x})<1/2,}\\ {and+\left\{p({\bf x})/(1-p({\bf x}))\right\}^{r/(r-1)},}&{{}\quad if~p({\bf x})>1/2.}\end{array}
$$

Note that sgn $\{{\bar{f}}({\bf x}) \}= f^{*}({\bf x})$ , where $f^{*}$ is the Bayes rule.

nl_proof:
### Proof of Theorem 1

Fix x and let $\alpha=f(\mathbf{x})$ . We have

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\mathrm{E}[L(\mathbf{Y}\alpha)|\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{x}]=p(\mathbf{x})L(\alpha)+\{1-p(\mathbf{x})\}L(-\alpha)}\\ &{\qquad=\left\{\begin{array}{l l}{p(\mathbf{x})(-\log\alpha)+(1-p(\mathbf{x}))(1+\alpha),}&{\mathrm{if~}\alpha>1,}\\ {p(\mathbf{x})(1-\alpha)+\{1-p(\mathbf{x})\}(1+\alpha),}&{\mathrm{if~}-1\leq\alpha\leq 1,}\\ {p(\mathbf{x})(1-\alpha)+(1-p(\mathbf{x}))(-\log(-\alpha)),}&{\mathrm{if~}\alpha< -1.}\end{array}\right.}\end{array}
$$

If $0<p(\mathbf{x})<1$ , the global minimizer exists because $\mathrm{E}[L(\mathbf{Y}\alpha)|\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{x}]$ is coercive:

$$
\operatorname{E}[L(\mathbf{Y}\alpha)|\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{x}]\to\infty\quad{\mathrm{as~}}|\alpha|\to\infty .
$$

The derivative of $\mathrm{E}[L({\bf Y}\alpha)|{\bf X}={\bf x}]$ with respect to α is

$$
\frac{\partial}{\partial\alpha}\mathrm{E}[L(\mathbf{Y}\alpha)|\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{x}]=\left\{\begin{array}{l l}{-p(\mathbf{x})\frac{1}{\alpha}+\{1-p(\mathbf{x})\},}&{\mathrm{if~}\alpha>1,}\\ {-p(\mathbf{x})+\{1-p(\mathbf{x})\},}&{\mathrm{if~}-1\leq\alpha\leq 1,}\\ {-p(\mathbf{x})-\{1-p(\mathbf{x})\}\frac{1}{\alpha},}&{\mathrm{if~}\alpha< -1.}\end{array}\right.
$$

$\begin{array}{r}{\frac{\partial}{\partial\alpha}\mathrm{E}[L(\mathbf{Y}\alpha)|\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{x}]=0}\end{array}$ holds if and only if

$$
\bar{f}(\mathbf{x})=\alpha=\left\{\begin{array}{l l}{-\frac{1-p(\mathbf{x})}{p(\mathbf{x})},}&{\quad\mathrm{if}p(\mathbf{x})<\frac{1}{2},}\\ {+\frac{p(\mathbf{x})}{1-p(\mathbf{x})},}&{\quad\mathrm{if}p(\mathbf{x})>\frac{1}{2}.}\end{array}\right.
$$

α is the unique minimizer because $\mathrm{E}[L({\bf Y}\alpha)|{\bf X}={\bf x}]$ is convex.

### Proof of Theorem 2

Let $(\hat{\beta}_{0},\hat{\pmb{\beta}})$ be any minimizer if it exists. Without loss of generality, let's say that $p_{+}\geq p_{-}$ where $p_{+}= \# \{i : y_{i}= + 1 \}/ n > 0$ and $p_{-}= \# \{i : y_{i}= - 1 \}/ n > 0$ Assume that,

$$
\begin{array}{r}{\left\|(\hat{\beta}_{0}\hat{\pmb{\beta}}^{T})^{T}\right\|^{2}>C_{1}^{2}+C_{2}^{2},}\end{array}
$$

where,

$$
C_{1}=\left(\frac{p_{+}}{p_{-}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{p_{-}}}+\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |}{2\sqrt{\lambda p_{-}}}\right)^{2}>1,
$$

$$
\mathrm{and}C_{2}=\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |}{\lambda}+\sqrt{\frac{C_{1}}{\lambda}}.
$$

Since $|L(a)-L(b)|\leq|a-b|$ for any a, $b \in \mathbb{R}$

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{L\left(y_{i}(\boldsymbol{\beta}_{0}+\mathbf{x}_{i}^{T}\boldsymbol{\beta})\right)\geq L(y_{i}\boldsymbol{\beta}_{0})- |y_{i}\mathbf{x}_{i}^{T}\boldsymbol{\beta}|}\\ &{\qquad\quad\geq L(y_{i}\boldsymbol{\beta}_{0})- | |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |\cdot| |\boldsymbol{\beta}| |}\\ &{\qquad\quad\geq L(y_{i}\boldsymbol{\beta}_{0})-\underset{i}{\operatorname*{max}}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |\cdot| |\boldsymbol{\beta}| |.}\end{array}
$$

Then, we have

$$
\begin{array}{l}{\displaystyle\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol{\beta}_{0},\boldsymbol{\beta})\geq\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}L(y_{i}\beta_{0})-\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |\cdot| |\boldsymbol{\beta}| | +\lambda| |\boldsymbol{\beta}| |^{2}}\\ {\displaystyle\ =\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}L(y_{i}\beta_{0})+\lambda\left(\|\boldsymbol{\beta}\|-\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |}{2\lambda}\right)^{2}-\lambda\left(\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |}{2\lambda}\right)^{2}.}\end{array}
$$

(Case 1) Suppose that $\hat{\beta}_{0}^{2}\leq C_{1}^{2}$ . It implies that $| | \hat{\pmb{\beta}}| |^{2}> C_{2}^{2}$ and we obtain that,

$$
\begin{array}{r l}{\mathcal{L}(\hat{\beta}_{0},\hat{\pmb{\beta}})\geq\displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}L(y_{i}\hat{\beta}_{0})+\lambda\left(| |\hat{\beta}| | -\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |}{2\lambda}\right)^{2}-\lambda\left(\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |}{2\lambda}\right)^{2}}&{}\\ {\geq\displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}(1-y_{i}\hat{\beta}_{0})+\lambda\left(| |\hat{\beta}| | -\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |}{2\lambda}\right)^{2}-\lambda\left(\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |}{2\lambda}\right)^{2}}&{}\\ {>(1- |\hat{\beta}_{0}|)+\lambda\left(C_{2}-\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |}{2\lambda}\right)^{2}-\lambda\left(\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |}{2\lambda}\right)^{2}}&{}\\ {\geq 1-C_{1}+\lambda\left(\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |}{2\lambda}+\sqrt{\frac{C_{1}}{\lambda}}\right)^{2}-\lambda\left(\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |}{2\lambda}\right)^{2}}&{}\\ {>1=\mathcal{L}(0,\mathbf{0}),}\end{array}
$$

which is a contradiction. The third inequality is because $\begin{array}{r}{\vert\vert\hat{\pmb\beta}\vert\vert>C_{2}>\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}\vert\vert\mathbf{x}_{i}\vert\vert^{2}}{2\lambda}}\end{array}$

(Case 2) Suppose ${\hat{\beta}}_{0}^{2}>C_{1}^{2}\left(>1\right)$ . log $| \hat{\beta}_{0}|$ is bounded by log $\begin{array}{r}{| \hat{\beta}_{0}| \le \frac{| \hat{\beta}_{0}| - 1}{| \hat{\beta}_{0}|^{1 / 2}}}\end{array}$ . Then we obtain that,

$$
\begin{array}{r l}{\mathcal{L}(\hat{\beta}_{0},\hat{\pmb{\beta}})\geq}&{\displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}L(y_{i}\hat{\beta}_{0})+\lambda\left(| |\hat{\pmb{\beta}}| | -\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |}{2\lambda}\right)^{2}-\lambda\left(\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |}{2\lambda}\right)^{2}}\\ {\geq}&{p_{+}\cdot(-\log|\hat{\beta}_{0}|)+p_{-}\cdot(1+ |\hat{\beta}_{0}|)-\lambda\left(\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |}{2\lambda}\right)^{2}}\\ {\geq}&{p_{+}\cdot\left(-\frac{|\hat{\beta}_{0}| -1}{|\hat{\beta}_{0}|^{1/2}}\right)+p_{-}\cdot(1+ |\hat{\beta}_{0}|)-\lambda\left(\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |}{2\lambda}\right)^{2}}\\ {\geq}&{-p_{+}|\hat{\beta}_{0}|^{1/2}+p_{-}|\hat{\beta}_{0}| -\lambda\left(\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |}{2\lambda}\right)^{2}}\\ {=}&{p_{-}\left(|\hat{\beta}_{0}|^{1/2}-\frac{1}{2}\frac{p_{+}}{p_{-}}\right)^{2}-p_{-}\left(\frac{1}{2}\frac{p_{+}}{p_{-}}\right)^{2}-\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |^{2}}{4\lambda}}\\ {>}&{p_{-}\left(C_{1}^{1/2}-\frac{1}{2}\frac{p_{+}}{p_{-}}\right)^{2}-p_{-}\left(\frac{1}{2}\frac{p_{+}}{p_{-}}\right)^{2}-\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |^{2}}{4\lambda}}\\ {=}&{p_{-}\left(\frac{1}{2}\frac{p_{+}}{p_{-}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{p_{-}}}+\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |}{2\sqrt{\lambda p_{-}}}\right)^{2}-p_{-}\left(\frac{1}{2}\frac{p_{+}}{p_{-}}\right)^{2}-\frac{\operatorname*{max}_{i}| |\mathbf{x}_{i}| |^{2}}{4\lambda}}\\ {>}&{1=\mathcal{L}(0,\mathbf{0}),}\end{array}
$$

which is a contradiction.

Therefore, we can conclude that,

$$
\left\|(\hat{\beta}_{0}\hat{\pmb{\beta}}^{T})^{T}\right\|^{2}\leq C_{1}^{2}+C_{2}^{2}.
$$

Eventually, (2) is equivalent to minimizing a continuous function over a non-empty compact region. Therefore, there exists a global minimizer.

### Proof of Theorem 6

Fix x and let $\alpha=f(\mathbf{x})$ . We have

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\mathrm{E}[L_{r}({\mathbf Y}\alpha)|{\mathbf X}={\mathbf x}]=p({\mathbf x})L_{r}(\alpha)+\{1-p({\mathbf x})\}L_{r}(-\alpha)}\\ &{\qquad=\left\{\begin{array}{l l}{p({\mathbf x})r\left(1-\alpha^{1/r}\right)+(1-p({\mathbf x}))(1+\alpha),}&{\mathrm{if~}\alpha>1,}\\ {p({\mathbf x})(1-\alpha)+(1-p({\mathbf x}))(1+\alpha),}&{\mathrm{if~}-1\le\alpha\le 1,}\\ {p({\mathbf x})(1-\alpha)+(1-p({\mathbf x}))r\left(1-(-\alpha)^{1/r}\right),}&{\mathrm{if~}\alpha< -1.}\end{array}\right.}\end{array}
$$

If $0<p(\mathbf{x})<1$ , the global minimizer exists because $\mathrm{E}[L_{r}({\bf Y}\alpha)|{\bf X}={\bf x}]$ is coercive:

$$
\operatorname{E}[L_{r}(\mathbf{Y}\alpha)|\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{x}]\to\infty\quad{\mathrm{as~}}|\alpha|\to\infty .
$$

$\begin{array}{r}{\frac{\partial}{\partial\alpha}\mathrm{E}[L_{r}(\mathbf{Y}\alpha)|\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{x}]=0}\end{array}$ holds if and only if

$$
\bar{f}(\mathbf{x})=\alpha=\left\{\begin{array}{l l}{-\left(\frac{1-p(\mathbf{x})}{p(\mathbf{x})}\right)^{\frac{r}{r-1}},}&{\quad\mathrm{if}p(\mathbf{x})<\frac{1}{2},}\\ {+\left(\frac{p(\mathbf{x})}{1-p(\mathbf{x})}\right)^{\frac{r}{r-1}},}&{\quad\mathrm{if}p(\mathbf{x})>\frac{1}{2}.}\end{array}\right.
$$

α is the unique minimizer because $\mathrm{E}[L_{r}({\bf Y}\alpha)|{\bf X}={\bf x}]$ is convex.

context.name: Setup: binary classification, p(x), Bayes rule (Section 1)
context.statement: This paper concerns binary classification, where the task is to predict an unobserved binary output value $y\in\{-1,1\}$ based on an observed input vector $\mathbf{x}\in \mathbb{R}^{p}$ . The classifier is a mapping from the input space $\mathcal{X}$ to {−1, 1} via a classification function $\hat{f}$, and the predicted y value is $\mathrm{sgn}\{\hat{f}(\mathbf{x})\}$ . The decision boundary is the set $\{\mathbf{x}:{\hat{f}}(\mathbf{x})=0\}$ . Suppose that data are generated from some underlying distribution $\mathrm{pr}(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$ , and let $p(\mathbf{x})=\mathrm{pr}(\mathbf{Y}=1\mid$ $\mathbf{X}= \mathbf{x})$ Under the standard 0-1 loss, the optimal classification rule is sgn $[p(\mathbf{x})-1/2]$ (a.k.a. Bayes rule). Throughout the paper, we assume that $p(\mathbf{X})\neq 1/2$ almost surely. The optimal decision boundary is $\{\mathbf{x}:p(\mathbf{x})=1/2\}$ Given training data, $\{({\bf x}_{i},y_{i}),i=$ $1,\ldots,n\}$ , one aims to develop a classifier that mimics the Bayes rule as closely as possible.

context.name: LHS loss, eq. (1)
context.statement:
In this paper, we provide an affirmative answer and the new function called the leaky hockey stick loss (LHS loss). The expression of the LHS loss is given in (1) and the picture of this loss function is displayed in Figure 1. We use the word 'hockey stick' because our loss function resembles it and is continuously differentiable. We use the term 'leaky' because the right side diverges to negative infinity motivated by the name of leaky ReLU.

$$
L(yf)=\left\{{\begin{array}{l l}{-\log yf,}&{yf>1,}\\ {1-yf,}&{yf\leq 1,}\end{array}}\right.\tag{1}
$$

context.name: Classification-calibration and Fisher consistency (Section 2)
context.statement:
Lin (2004) proposed Fisher consistency as a necessary condition on a loss function. It is defined to be that any global minimizer $\check{f}$ (if it exists) of $\operatorname{E}[L(\mathbf{Y}f(\mathbf{X}))]$ , generally referred to as a population minimizer, has the same sign function as the Bayes rule almost surely. Later, Bartlett et al. (2006) defined classification-calibration. A loss function L is called classification-calibrated if any global minimizer $\bar{f}$ (if it exists) of $\operatorname{E}[L(\mathbf{Y}f(\mathbf{X}))\mid\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{x}]$ has the same sign as the Bayes rule almost surely. For example, the hinge loss is classification-calibrated, which can be directly shown by Theorem 2 of Bartlett et al. (2006).

An unspoken assumption in those two definitions is the existence of a global minimizer. When $\bar{f}$ exists (which can be easily checked) and $|\mathrm{E}[L({\bf Y}\bar{f}({\bf X}))]| <\infty .$ then a population minimizer $\check{f}$ exists. We further see that loss function L is classification-calibrated if and only if it is Fisher consistent. The 'if' statement follows from the fact that any $\bar{f}$ is also a population minimizer and the definition of Fisher consistency. The 'only if' statement comes from the fact that $\operatorname{E}[L(\mathbf{Y}{\bar{f}}(\mathbf{X}))\mid\mathbf{X}]=\operatorname{E}[L(\mathbf{Y}{\check{f}}(\mathbf{X}))\mid\mathbf{X}]$ almost surely and that for any $\delta_{\mathbf{X}}$ such that $\operatorname{sgn}(\delta_{\mathbf{X}})\neq\operatorname{sgn}(p(\mathbf{X})-1/2),\operatorname{E}[L(\mathbf{Y}{\bar{f}}(\mathbf{X}))\mid\mathbf{X}]<\operatorname{E}[L(\mathbf{Y}\delta_{\mathbf{X}})\mid\mathbf{X}]$ almost surely by the definition of classification-calibration.

For a non-negative loss function L, $\operatorname{E}[L(\mathbf{Y}\bar{f}(\mathbf{X}))]$ is always finite. However, the LHS loss does not guarantee the finiteness of $\operatorname{E}[L(\mathbf{Y}\bar{f}(\mathbf{X}))]$ (see Theorem 4 for further information), thereby not ensuring the existence of a global minimizer that Fisher consistency implicitly assumes. Instead, we verify that the LHS loss is classification-calibrated. The LHS loss is the first negatively divergent loss function proven to satisfy the classification-calibration property.

context.name: Remark 1 (why p(x) in (0,1))
context.statement: Remark 1 In general, a global minimizer of $\operatorname{E}[L(\mathbf{Y}f(\mathbf{X}))\mid\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{x}]$ is allowed to take values $\pm \infty$ because what matters is only the sign of the minimizer $(Lin,~2004)$ If we allow the minimum objective to take values $\pm \infty$ , Theorem 1 can be extended to include $p(\mathbf{x})$ equals to 0 and 1. It is because if $p(\mathbf{x})=0$, then $\operatorname{E}[L(\mathbf{Y}\alpha)\mid\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{x}]=L(-\alpha)\to-\infty$ as $\alpha \to - \infty$. If $p ({\bf x}) = 1$ , then $\operatorname{E}[L(\mathbf{Y}f(\mathbf{X}))\mid\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{x}]=L(\alpha)\to-\infty$ as $\alpha \to \infty$.

context.name: Existence approach for the linear LHS classifier (Section 3.1)
context.statement:
When L is a non-negative continuous loss function, there exists a global minimizer to the regularized ERM problem. Proving existence is considered well-understood. The sublevel set of the objective function L of the regularized ERM problem, $\{\beta:{\mathcal{L}}(\beta)\leq c\}$ , is compact for any $c \in \mathbb{R}$ , and the global minimizer of the continuous objective function on a compact set must exist by the extreme value theorem.

In contrast, it is not trivial to show the existence of a global minimizer of the linear LHS classifier. The loss term in the regularized ERM can diverge to negative infinity even though the LHS loss is convex and training data have finite samples. To show the existence, we find a specific compact set D of $\beta,$ so that the objective function of the linear LHS classifier can have a global minimizer on D. Then, we show that the objective value at the global minimizer on D is always smaller than any objective value on $D^{c}$

context.name: Remark 2 (uniqueness of the linear LHS solution)
context.statement:
Remark 2 (Uniqueness) The minimizer $\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}$ is uniquely determined because the LHS loss is convex and the $\ell_{2}$ regularizer is strictly convex. However, $\hat{\beta}_{0}$ may not. Here is an illustrative example. Let the data be

$$
\begin{array}{r l r l r l}{y_{1}= -1,}&{{}y_{2}= -1,}&{}&{{}y_{3}=1,}&{}&{{}y_{4}=1,}\\ {x_{1}=1,}&{{}x_{2}= -1,}&{}&{{}x_{3}=1,}&{}&{{}x_{4}= -1.}\end{array}
$$

Then both $(0,0)$ and $(1,0)$ are global minimizers. Non-uniqueness of the intercept term can also occur in the linear SVM.

context.name: Loss family L_r, eq. (15) (Section 7.2)
context.statement:
We define a negatively divergent loss functions $L_{r}$ as follows: with $r\in(1,\infty)$,

$$
L_{r}(yf)={\left\{\begin{array}{l l}{r\left(1-(yf)^{1/r}\right),}&{yf>1,}\\ {1-yf,}&{yf\leq 1.}\end{array}\right.}\tag{15}
$$

Figure 3 illustrates (15) for various r values. Note the LHS loss is (15) with r diverging to ∞.

import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators

namespace ResearchLevel

noncomputable def lhs (u : ℝ) : ℝ := if 1 < u then -Real.log u else 1 - u

noncomputable def condRisk (p α : ℝ) : ℝ := p * lhs α + (1 - p) * lhs (-α)

noncomputable def fbar (p : ℝ) : ℝ := if p < 1 / 2 then -(1 - p) / p else p / (1 - p)

noncomputable def objective {n p : ℕ} (xs : Fin n → (Fin p → ℝ)) (ys : Fin n → ℝ)
    (lam : ℝ) (b0 : ℝ) (b : Fin p → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (∑ i, lhs (ys i * (b0 + ∑ k, xs i k * b k))) / n + lam * (∑ k, b k * b k)

noncomputable def lhsR (r u : ℝ) : ℝ := if 1 < u then r * (1 - u ^ (1 / r)) else 1 - u

noncomputable def condRiskR (r p α : ℝ) : ℝ := p * lhsR r α + (1 - p) * lhsR r (-α)

noncomputable def fbarR (r p : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if p < 1 / 2 then -(((1 - p) / p) ^ (r / (r - 1))) else (p / (1 - p)) ^ (r / (r - 1))

private lemma lhs_le' {u : ℝ} (h : u ≤ 1) : lhs u = 1 - u := by
  simp only [lhs, if_neg (not_lt.2 h)]

private lemma lhs_gt' {u : ℝ} (h : 1 < u) : lhs u = -Real.log u := by
  simp only [lhs, if_pos h]

private lemma lhsR_le' {r u : ℝ} (h : u ≤ 1) : lhsR r u = 1 - u := by
  simp only [lhsR, if_neg (not_lt.2 h)]

private lemma lhsR_gt' {r u : ℝ} (h : 1 < u) : lhsR r u = r * (1 - u ^ (1/r)) := by
  simp only [lhsR, if_pos h]

private lemma bern {s t : ℝ} (hs0 : 0 < s) (hs1 : s < 1) (ht : 0 < t) (hne : t ≠ 1) :
    t ^ s < 1 + s * (t - 1) := by
  have hlog : Real.log t ≠ 0 := by
    intro h; apply hne; rw [← Real.exp_log ht, h, Real.exp_zero]
  have hc := strictConvexOn_exp.2 (Set.mem_univ (Real.log t)) (Set.mem_univ (0:ℝ))
    hlog hs0 (by linarith : (0:ℝ) < 1 - s) (by ring)
  simp only [smul_eq_mul, mul_zero, add_zero, Real.exp_zero, mul_one, Real.exp_log ht] at hc
  rw [Real.rpow_def_of_pos ht, mul_comm (Real.log t) s]
  linarith

private lemma main1 {p : ℝ} (hq0 : 0 < 1 - p) (hpq : 1 - p < p) (α : ℝ)
    (hne : α ≠ p / (1 - p)) : condRisk p (p / (1 - p)) < condRisk p α := by
  have hp0 : 0 < p := by linarith
  set q : ℝ := 1 - p with hqdef
  set a : ℝ := p / q with hadef
  have ha0 : 0 < a := div_pos hp0 hq0
  have ha1 : 1 < a := (one_lt_div hq0).2 hpq
  have hpa : p = q * a := by rw [hadef]; field_simp
  have hCa : condRisk p a = p * (-Real.log a) + q * (1 + a) := by
    simp only [condRisk, ← hqdef, lhs_gt' ha1, lhs_le' (by linarith : -a ≤ 1)] <;> ring
  -- main inequality for positive α
  have key : ∀ β : ℝ, 0 < β → β ≠ a →
      p * (-Real.log a) + q * (1 + a) < p * (-Real.log β) + q * (1 + β) := by
    intro β hβ hβa
    have hd : Real.log (β / a) < β / a - 1 :=
      Real.log_lt_sub_one_of_pos (div_pos hβ ha0) (by
        intro h; exact hβa (by field_simp at h; linarith))
    have hdiv : Real.log (β / a) = Real.log β - Real.log a :=
      Real.log_div (ne_of_gt hβ) (ne_of_gt ha0)
    have h3 : p * Real.log (β / a) < p * (β / a - 1) := by
      exact mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hd hp0
    have h4 : p * (β / a - 1) = q * (β - a) := by
      rw [hpa]; field_simp
    rw [hdiv] at h3
    linarith
  have h2q : condRisk p a < 2 * q := by
    have h := key 1 one_pos (by intro h; rw [← h] at ha1; linarith)
    rw [Real.log_one] at h
    rw [hCa]
    linarith
  by_cases h1 : 1 < α
  · have hCα : condRisk p α = p * (-Real.log α) + q * (1 + α) := by
      simp only [condRisk, ← hqdef, lhs_gt' h1, lhs_le' (by linarith : -α ≤ 1)] <;> ring
    rw [hCa, hCα]
    exact key α (by linarith) hne
  · push_neg at h1
    by_cases h2 : -1 ≤ α
    · have hCα : condRisk p α = p * (1 - α) + q * (1 + α) := by
        simp only [condRisk, ← hqdef, lhs_le' h1, lhs_le' (by linarith : -α ≤ 1)]
        ring
      rw [hCα]
      nlinarith [h2q]
    · push_neg at h2
      have hCα : condRisk p α = p * (1 - α) + q * (-Real.log (-α)) := by
        simp only [condRisk, ← hqdef, lhs_le' h1, lhs_gt' (by linarith : (1:ℝ) < -α)] <;> ring
      have hl : Real.log (-α) ≤ -α - 1 := Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (by linarith)
      rw [hCα]
      nlinarith [h2q]

private lemma sym1 (p α : ℝ) : condRisk p α = condRisk (1 - p) (-α) := by
  simp only [condRisk, neg_neg]
  ring

private lemma main6 {r p : ℝ} (hr : 1 < r) (hq0 : 0 < 1 - p) (hpq : 1 - p < p) (α : ℝ)
    (hne : α ≠ (p / (1 - p)) ^ (r / (r - 1))) :
    condRiskR r p ((p / (1 - p)) ^ (r / (r - 1))) < condRiskR r p α := by
  have hp0 : 0 < p := by linarith
  have hr0 : 0 < r := by linarith
  have hr1 : 0 < r - 1 := by linarith
  have hrr : r * (1 / r) = 1 := by field_simp
  set q : ℝ := 1 - p with hqdef
  have hs0 : 0 < 1 / r := by positivity
  have hs1 : 1 / r < 1 := by rw [div_lt_one hr0]; linarith
  set x : ℝ := p / q with hxdef
  have hx0 : 0 < x := div_pos hp0 hq0
  have hx1 : 1 < x := (one_lt_div hq0).2 hpq
  set a : ℝ := x ^ (r / (r - 1)) with hadef
  have ha1 : 1 < a := by
    have h := (Real.rpow_lt_rpow_left_iff hx1).2 (show (0:ℝ) < r / (r-1) by positivity)
    rwa [Real.rpow_zero] at h
  have ha0 : 0 < a := by linarith
  have hA0 : 0 < a ^ (1 / r) := Real.rpow_pos_of_pos ha0 _
  have hpa : p * a ^ (1 / r) = q * a := by
    have e1 : a ^ (1 / r) = x ^ (1 / (r - 1)) := by
      rw [hadef, ← Real.rpow_mul hx0.le]
      congr 1
      field_simp
    have e2 : a = x ^ (1 / (r - 1)) * x := by
      rw [hadef, show r / (r - 1) = 1 / (r - 1) + 1 by field_simp; ring, Real.rpow_add hx0,
        Real.rpow_one]
    have hqx : q * x = p := by rw [hxdef]; field_simp
    rw [e1, e2, ← hqx]
    ring
  have hCa : condRiskR r p a = p * (r * (1 - a ^ (1/r))) + q * (1 + a) := by
    simp only [condRiskR, ← hqdef, lhsR_gt' ha1, lhsR_le' (by linarith : -a ≤ 1)] <;> ring
  have key : ∀ β : ℝ, 0 < β → β ≠ a →
      p * (r * (1 - a ^ (1/r))) + q * (1 + a) < p * (r * (1 - β ^ (1/r))) + q * (1 + β) := by
    intro β hβ hβa
    have hb : (β / a) ^ (1/r) < 1 + (1/r) * (β / a - 1) :=
      bern hs0 hs1 (div_pos hβ ha0) (by
        intro h
        apply hβa
        field_simp at h
        linarith)
    have hsplit : β ^ (1/r) = a ^ (1/r) * (β / a) ^ (1/r) := by
      rw [Real.div_rpow hβ.le ha0.le]
      field_simp
    have step : β ^ (1/r) - a ^ (1/r) < a ^ (1/r) * ((1/r) * (β / a - 1)) := by
      rw [hsplit]; nlinarith [hA0, hb]
    have step2 : p * r * (β ^ (1/r) - a ^ (1/r))
        < p * r * (a ^ (1/r) * ((1/r) * (β / a - 1))) :=
      mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left step (by positivity)
    have heq : p * r * (a ^ (1/r) * ((1/r) * (β / a - 1))) = q * (β - a) := by
      have h1 : p * r * (a ^ (1/r) * ((1/r) * (β / a - 1)))
          = (p * a ^ (1/r)) * ((β - a) / a) := by
        field_simp
      rw [h1, hpa]
      field_simp
    rw [heq] at step2
    nlinarith [step2]
  have h2q : condRiskR r p a < 2 * q := by
    have h := key 1 one_pos (by intro h; rw [← h] at ha1; linarith)
    rw [hCa]
    rw [Real.one_rpow] at h
    linarith
  by_cases h1 : 1 < α
  · have hCα : condRiskR r p α = p * (r * (1 - α ^ (1/r))) + q * (1 + α) := by
      simp only [condRiskR, ← hqdef, lhsR_gt' h1, lhsR_le' (by linarith : -α ≤ 1)] <;> ring
    rw [hCa, hCα]
    exact key α (by linarith) hne
  · push_neg at h1
    by_cases h2 : -1 ≤ α
    · have hCα : condRiskR r p α = p * (1 - α) + q * (1 + α) := by
        simp only [condRiskR, ← hqdef, lhsR_le' h1, lhsR_le' (by linarith : -α ≤ 1)]
        ring
      rw [hCα]
      nlinarith [h2q]
    · push_neg at h2
      have hCα : condRiskR r p α = p * (1 - α) + q * (r * (1 - (-α) ^ (1/r))) := by
        simp only [condRiskR, ← hqdef, lhsR_le' h1, lhsR_gt' (by linarith : (1:ℝ) < -α)] <;> ring
      have hb : (-α) ^ (1/r) < 1 + (1/r) * (-α - 1) :=
        bern hs0 hs1 (by linarith) (by intro h; linarith)
      have hmul := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hb hr0
      have hgt : α + 1 < r * (1 - (-α) ^ (1/r)) := by nlinarith [hmul, hrr]
      rw [hCα]
      nlinarith [h2q, hgt]

private lemma sym6 (r p α : ℝ) : condRiskR r p α = condRiskR r (1 - p) (-α) := by
  simp only [condRiskR, neg_neg]
  ring

theorem theorem1 {p : ℝ} (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (hne : p ≠ 1 / 2) :
    (∀ α : ℝ, condRisk p (fbar p) ≤ condRisk p α) ∧
    (∀ α : ℝ, (∀ β : ℝ, condRisk p α ≤ condRisk p β) → α = fbar p) ∧
    Real.sign (fbar p) = Real.sign (p - 1 / 2) := by
  have hstrict : ∀ α : ℝ, α ≠ fbar p → condRisk p (fbar p) < condRisk p α := by
    rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hne with hlt | hgt
    · intro α hα
      have hf : fbar p = -((1 - p) / p) := by
        simp only [fbar, if_pos hlt, neg_div]
      have h := main1 (p := 1 - p) (by linarith) (by linarith)
      simp only [sub_sub_cancel] at h
      rw [hf] at hα ⊢
      rw [sym1 p, neg_neg, sym1 p α]
      exact h (-α) (by intro hc; exact hα (by linarith))
    · intro α hα
      have hf : fbar p = p / (1 - p) := by
        simp only [fbar, if_neg (by push_neg; linarith : ¬ p < 1 / 2)]
      rw [hf] at hα ⊢
      exact main1 (by linarith) (by linarith) α hα
  refine ⟨fun α => ?_, fun α hα => ?_, ?_⟩
  · rcases eq_or_ne α (fbar p) with h | h
    · rw [h]
    · exact (hstrict α h).le
  · by_contra hc
    exact absurd (hα (fbar p)) (not_le.2 (hstrict α hc))
  · rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hne with hlt | hgt
    · have hf : fbar p = -((1 - p) / p) := by
        simp only [fbar, if_pos hlt, neg_div]
      rw [hf, Real.sign_of_neg (by
        have : 0 < (1 - p) / p := div_pos (by linarith) hp0
        linarith), Real.sign_of_neg (by linarith)]
    · have hf : fbar p = p / (1 - p) := by
        simp only [fbar, if_neg (by push_neg; linarith : ¬ p < 1 / 2)]
      rw [hf, Real.sign_of_pos (div_pos hp0 (by linarith)),
        Real.sign_of_pos (by linarith)]

theorem theorem6 {r p : ℝ} (hr : 1 < r) (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (hne : p ≠ 1 / 2) :
    (∀ α : ℝ, condRiskR r p (fbarR r p) ≤ condRiskR r p α) ∧
    (∀ α : ℝ, (∀ β : ℝ, condRiskR r p α ≤ condRiskR r p β) → α = fbarR r p) ∧
    Real.sign (fbarR r p) = Real.sign (p - 1 / 2) := by
  have hstrict : ∀ α : ℝ, α ≠ fbarR r p → condRiskR r p (fbarR r p) < condRiskR r p α := by
    rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hne with hlt | hgt
    · intro α hα
      have hf : fbarR r p = -(((1 - p) / p) ^ (r / (r - 1))) := by
        simp only [fbarR, if_pos hlt]
      have h := main6 (p := 1 - p) hr (by linarith) (by linarith)
      simp only [sub_sub_cancel] at h
      rw [hf] at hα ⊢
      rw [sym6 r p, neg_neg, sym6 r p α]
      exact h (-α) (by intro hc; exact hα (by linarith))
    · intro α hα
      have hf : fbarR r p = (p / (1 - p)) ^ (r / (r - 1)) := by
        simp only [fbarR, if_neg (by push_neg; linarith : ¬ p < 1 / 2)]
      rw [hf] at hα ⊢
      exact main6 hr (by linarith) (by linarith) α hα
  refine ⟨fun α => ?_, fun α hα => ?_, ?_⟩
  · rcases eq_or_ne α (fbarR r p) with h | h
    · rw [h]
    · exact (hstrict α h).le
  · by_contra hc
    exact absurd (hα (fbarR r p)) (not_le.2 (hstrict α hc))
  · rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hne with hlt | hgt
    · have hf : fbarR r p = -(((1 - p) / p) ^ (r / (r - 1))) := by
        simp only [fbarR, if_pos hlt]
      rw [hf, Real.sign_of_neg (by
        have : 0 < ((1 - p) / p) ^ (r / (r - 1)) :=
          Real.rpow_pos_of_pos (div_pos (by linarith) hp0) _
        linarith), Real.sign_of_neg (by linarith)]
    · have hf : fbarR r p = (p / (1 - p)) ^ (r / (r - 1)) := by
        simp only [fbarR, if_neg (by push_neg; linarith : ¬ p < 1 / 2)]
      rw [hf, Real.sign_of_pos (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos (div_pos hp0 (by linarith)) _),
        Real.sign_of_pos (by linarith)]

private lemma lhs_ge_lin (u : ℝ) : 1 - u ≤ lhs u := by
  by_cases h : 1 < u
  · rw [lhs_gt' h]
    have := Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (by linarith : (0:ℝ) < u)
    linarith
  · rw [lhs_le' (not_lt.1 h)]

private lemma lhs_ge_log {u T : ℝ} (h : |u| ≤ T) : -Real.log (1 + T) ≤ lhs u := by
  have hT : 0 ≤ T := le_trans (abs_nonneg u) h
  by_cases h1 : 1 < u
  · rw [lhs_gt' h1]
    have h2 : u ≤ 1 + T := by
      have := le_abs_self u
      linarith
    have := Real.log_le_log (by linarith : (0:ℝ) < u) h2
    linarith
  · rw [lhs_le' (not_lt.1 h1)]
    have : 0 ≤ Real.log (1 + T) := Real.log_nonneg (by linarith)
    have h2 : u ≤ 1 := not_lt.1 h1
    linarith

private lemma sum_lb {m : ℕ} (f : Fin m → ℝ) (i0 : Fin m) (A L : ℝ) (hA : A ≤ f i0)
    (hL : ∀ i, L ≤ f i) (hL0 : L ≤ 0) : A + (m : ℝ) * L ≤ ∑ i, f i := by
  rw [← Finset.add_sum_erase _ f (Finset.mem_univ i0)]
  have h1 : ((Finset.univ.erase i0).card : ℝ) * L ≤ ∑ i ∈ Finset.univ.erase i0, f i := by
    have := Finset.card_nsmul_le_sum (Finset.univ.erase i0) f L (fun i _ => hL i)
    simpa [nsmul_eq_mul] using this
  have h2 : ((Finset.univ.erase i0).card : ℝ) ≤ (m : ℝ) := by
    have := Finset.card_le_card (Finset.erase_subset i0 (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m)))
    simp only [Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin] at this
    exact_mod_cast this
  have h3 : (m : ℝ) * L ≤ ((Finset.univ.erase i0).card : ℝ) * L :=
    mul_le_mul_of_nonpos_right h2 hL0
  linarith

private lemma log_scale_bound {y c : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y) (hc : 0 < c) :
    Real.log y ≤ y / c - 1 + Real.log c := by
  have h : Real.log y = Real.log (y / c) + Real.log c := by
    rw [Real.log_div (ne_of_gt hy) (ne_of_gt hc)]; ring
  have := Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (div_pos hy hc)
  linarith

private lemma lhs_continuous : Continuous lhs := by
  have heq : lhs = fun u : ℝ => if u ≤ 1 then 1 - u else -Real.log (max u 1) := by
    funext u
    simp only [lhs]
    by_cases h : u ≤ 1
    · rw [if_neg (not_lt.2 h), if_pos h]
    · push_neg at h
      rw [if_pos h, if_neg (not_le.2 h), max_eq_left h.le]
  rw [heq]
  have hg : Continuous fun u : ℝ => -Real.log (max u 1) := by
    refine Continuous.neg (Real.continuousOn_log.comp_continuous
      (continuous_id.max continuous_const) ?_)
    intro x
    simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
    have h1 : (1:ℝ) ≤ max x 1 := le_max_right _ _
    intro h
    rw [h] at h1
    linarith
  exact Continuous.if_le (continuous_const.sub continuous_id) hg continuous_id
    continuous_const (fun x hx => by rw [hx]; simp)

set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
theorem theorem2 {n p : ℕ} (xs : Fin n → (Fin p → ℝ)) (ys : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hy : ∀ i, ys i = 1 ∨ ys i = -1)
    (hpos : ∃ i, ys i = 1) (hneg : ∃ j, ys j = -1)
    {lam : ℝ} (hlam : 0 < lam) :
    ∃ b0 : ℝ, ∃ b : Fin p → ℝ, ∀ c0 : ℝ, ∀ c : Fin p → ℝ,
      objective xs ys lam b0 b ≤ objective xs ys lam c0 c := by
  obtain ⟨i0, hi0⟩ := hpos
  obtain ⟨j0, hj0⟩ := hneg
  have hn0 : 0 < n := i0.pos
  have hnR : (0:ℝ) < (n:ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn0
  set M : ℝ := ∑ i, ∑ k, |xs i k| with hMdef
  have hM0 : 0 ≤ M := by
    rw [hMdef]; positivity
  have hlin : ∀ (b : Fin p → ℝ) (i : Fin n), |∑ k, xs i k * b k| ≤ M * ‖b‖ := by
    intro b i
    calc |∑ k, xs i k * b k| ≤ ∑ k, |xs i k * b k| := Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
      _ ≤ ∑ k, |xs i k| * ‖b‖ := by
          refine Finset.sum_le_sum (fun k _ => ?_)
          rw [abs_mul]
          exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
            (by simpa [Real.norm_eq_abs] using norm_le_pi_norm b k) (abs_nonneg _)
      _ = (∑ k, |xs i k|) * ‖b‖ := by rw [Finset.sum_mul]
      _ ≤ M * ‖b‖ := by
          refine mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right ?_ (norm_nonneg b)
          rw [hMdef]
          exact Finset.single_le_sum (f := fun i => ∑ k, |xs i k|)
            (fun i _ => Finset.sum_nonneg (fun k _ => abs_nonneg _)) (Finset.mem_univ i)
  set c : ℝ := 2 * (n:ℝ) * (1 + M) + 1 with hcdef
  have hc0 : 0 < c := by rw [hcdef]; positivity
  set K : ℝ := (1 + M)^2 / (4 * (n:ℝ) * lam) with hKdef
  have hK0 : 0 ≤ K := by rw [hKdef]; positivity
  set R : ℝ := 2 * ((n:ℝ) + K + (n:ℝ) * Real.log c) + 2 with hRdef
  have hbig : ∀ z : ℝ × (Fin p → ℝ), R ≤ ‖z‖ → 1 ≤ objective xs ys lam z.1 z.2 := by
    rintro ⟨b0, b⟩ hz
    simp only at hz ⊢
    set N : ℝ := ‖(b0, b)‖ with hNdef
    have hb0 : |b0| ≤ N := by
      rw [hNdef, Prod.norm_def]
      exact le_trans (le_of_eq (Real.norm_eq_abs b0).symm) (le_max_left _ _)
    have hbn : ‖b‖ ≤ N := by
      rw [hNdef, Prod.norm_def]; exact le_max_right _ _
    have hbn0 : (0:ℝ) ≤ ‖b‖ := norm_nonneg b
    have hN : N ≤ |b0| + ‖b‖ := by
      rw [hNdef, Prod.norm_def, Real.norm_eq_abs]
      exact max_le (by linarith) (by linarith [abs_nonneg b0])
    set T : ℝ := |b0| + M * ‖b‖ with hTdef
    have hT0 : 0 ≤ T := by rw [hTdef]; positivity
    set L : ℝ := -Real.log (1 + T) with hLdef
    have hL0 : L ≤ 0 := by
      rw [hLdef]
      simp only [neg_nonpos]
      exact Real.log_nonneg (by linarith)
    have habs : ∀ i, |ys i * (b0 + ∑ k, xs i k * b k)| ≤ T := by
      intro i
      have h1 : |ys i| = 1 := by rcases hy i with h | h <;> rw [h] <;> simp
      rw [abs_mul, h1, one_mul]
      calc |b0 + ∑ k, xs i k * b k| ≤ |b0| + |∑ k, xs i k * b k| := abs_add_le _ _
        _ ≤ T := by have := hlin b i; rw [hTdef]; linarith
    have hLall : ∀ i, L ≤ lhs (ys i * (b0 + ∑ k, xs i k * b k)) := fun i =>
      lhs_ge_log (habs i)
    set A : ℝ := 1 + |b0| - M * ‖b‖ with hAdef
    have hex : ∃ i, A ≤ lhs (ys i * (b0 + ∑ k, xs i k * b k)) := by
      by_cases hb0s : 0 ≤ b0
      · refine ⟨j0, ?_⟩
        have h1 := lhs_ge_lin (ys j0 * (b0 + ∑ k, xs j0 k * b k))
        rw [hj0] at h1
        have h2 := hlin b j0
        have h3 : |b0| = b0 := abs_of_nonneg hb0s
        rw [hAdef, h3]
        have h4 := abs_le.1 h2
        rw [hj0]
        linarith [h4.1, h4.2]
      · push_neg at hb0s
        refine ⟨i0, ?_⟩
        have h1 := lhs_ge_lin (ys i0 * (b0 + ∑ k, xs i0 k * b k))
        rw [hi0] at h1
        have h2 := hlin b i0
        have h3 : |b0| = -b0 := abs_of_neg hb0s
        rw [hAdef, h3]
        have h4 := abs_le.1 h2
        rw [hi0]
        linarith [h4.1, h4.2]
    obtain ⟨istar, hstar⟩ := hex
    have hsum : A + (n:ℝ) * L ≤ ∑ i, lhs (ys i * (b0 + ∑ k, xs i k * b k)) :=
      sum_lb _ istar A L hstar hLall hL0
    have hnormsq : ‖b‖^2 ≤ ∑ k, b k * b k := by
      have hS : (0:ℝ) ≤ ∑ k, b k * b k := Finset.sum_nonneg (fun k _ => mul_self_nonneg _)
      have h1 : ‖b‖ ≤ Real.sqrt (∑ k, b k * b k) := by
        refine (pi_norm_le_iff_of_nonneg (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)).2 (fun k => ?_)
        rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, ← Real.sqrt_mul_self_eq_abs]
        exact Real.sqrt_le_sqrt
          (Finset.single_le_sum (f := fun k => b k * b k)
            (fun k _ => mul_self_nonneg _) (Finset.mem_univ k))
      have h2 := Real.sq_sqrt hS
      nlinarith [norm_nonneg b, Real.sqrt_nonneg (∑ k, b k * b k)]
    have hobj : (n:ℝ) * objective xs ys lam b0 b
        = (∑ i, lhs (ys i * (b0 + ∑ k, xs i k * b k))) + (n:ℝ) * lam * (∑ k, b k * b k) := by
      simp only [objective]
      field_simp
    have hKeq : 4 * (n:ℝ) * lam * K = (1 + M)^2 := by
      rw [hKdef]; field_simp
    have h5 : 1 + N - K ≤ A + (n:ℝ) * lam * ‖b‖^2 := by
      rw [hAdef]
      nlinarith [sq_nonneg (2 * (n:ℝ) * lam * ‖b‖ - (1 + M)), hKeq, hnR, hlam, hN, hbn0, hM0,
        mul_pos hnR hlam]
    have hN0 : 0 ≤ N := norm_nonneg _
    have hTN : T ≤ (1 + M) * N := by
      rw [hTdef]; nlinarith [hb0, hbn, hM0, abs_nonneg b0]
    have hlog1 : Real.log (1 + T) ≤ Real.log (1 + (1 + M) * N) :=
      Real.log_le_log (by linarith) (by linarith)
    have hlog2 : Real.log (1 + (1 + M) * N) ≤ (1 + (1 + M) * N) / c - 1 + Real.log c :=
      log_scale_bound (by nlinarith [mul_nonneg (by linarith : (0:ℝ) ≤ 1 + M) hN0]) hc0
    have hdiv : (n:ℝ) * ((1 + (1 + M) * N) / c) ≤ (n:ℝ) + N / 2 := by
      rw [← mul_div_assoc, div_le_iff₀ hc0, hcdef]
      nlinarith [hN0, hM0, hnR, mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg hnR.le hnR.le)
        (by linarith : (0:ℝ) ≤ 1 + M), mul_nonneg hnR.le (mul_nonneg hM0 hN0)]
    have h6 : -N / 2 - (n:ℝ) * Real.log c ≤ (n:ℝ) * L := by
      rw [hLdef]
      have := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (le_trans hlog1 hlog2) (le_of_lt hnR)
      nlinarith [hdiv]
    have hfin : (n:ℝ) ≤ (n:ℝ) * objective xs ys lam b0 b := by
      rw [hobj]
      have h7 : (n:ℝ) * lam * ‖b‖^2 ≤ (n:ℝ) * lam * (∑ k, b k * b k) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hnormsq (by positivity)
      have hRle : R ≤ N := hz
      rw [hRdef] at hRle
      linarith [hsum, h5, h6]
    nlinarith [hfin, hnR]
  have hz0 : objective xs ys lam 0 0 = 1 := by
    have h1 : lhs 0 = 1 := by rw [lhs_le' (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) ≤ 1)]; norm_num
    simp only [objective, Pi.zero_apply, mul_zero, Finset.sum_const_zero, add_zero, h1,
      Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one]
    field_simp
  have hcont : Continuous fun z : ℝ × (Fin p → ℝ) => objective xs ys lam z.1 z.2 := by
    simp only [objective]
    refine Continuous.add (Continuous.div_const ?_ _) (continuous_const.mul ?_)
    · refine continuous_finset_sum _ (fun i _ => lhs_continuous.comp ?_)
      exact continuous_const.mul (continuous_fst.add (continuous_finset_sum _ (fun k _ =>
        continuous_const.mul ((continuous_apply k).comp continuous_snd))))
    · exact continuous_finset_sum _ (fun k _ => ((continuous_apply k).comp continuous_snd).mul
        ((continuous_apply k).comp continuous_snd))
  have hev : ∀ᶠ z : ℝ × (Fin p → ℝ) in Filter.cocompact (ℝ × (Fin p → ℝ)),
      objective xs ys lam (0:ℝ) (0 : Fin p → ℝ) ≤ objective xs ys lam z.1 z.2 := by
    have h := (tendsto_norm_cocompact_atTop (E := ℝ × (Fin p → ℝ))).eventually_ge_atTop R
    filter_upwards [h] with z hz
    rw [hz0]
    exact hbig z hz
  obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := hcont.exists_forall_le' ((0:ℝ), (0 : Fin p → ℝ)) hev
  exact ⟨w.1, w.2, fun c0 cc => hw (c0, cc)⟩

end ResearchLevel

$(\langle x, \sigma_\gamma(x)\rangle)^2 / \|\sigma_\gamma(x)\|^2 \ge \|x\|_{1+\gamma}^2 / \|\mathbb{1}\|_p$, with $p = (1+\gamma)/(1-\gamma)$,

### Proof of Theorem 1 (PB-SVRGE, eq. 8)

Proof According to the results in the inequality (6) and $w_{k+1}^{s+1}=w_{k}^{s+1}-\eta_{k}\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})$ , we easily inferred

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{f(w_{k+1}^{s+1})\leq f(w_{k}^{s+1})+\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\cdot(w_{k+1}^{s+1}-w_{k}^{s+1})+\displaystyle\frac{L}{2}\|w_{k+1}^{s+1}-w_{k}^{s+1}\|^{2}}\\ &{\qquad=f(w_{k}^{s+1})-\eta_{k}\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})+\displaystyle\frac{L\eta_{k}^{2}}{2}\|\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}\\ &{\qquad=f(w_{k}^{s+1})-\eta_{k}\nu_{k}^{s+1}\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})+\displaystyle\frac{L\eta_{k}^{2}}{2}\|\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}+\eta_{k}(\nu_{k}^{s+1}}\\ &{\qquad-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1}))\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1}).}\end{array}\tag{9}
$$

Setting $\begin{array}{r}{\eta_{k}=\frac{\nu_{k}^{s+1}\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})}{L\|\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}}\end{array}$ , we further obtained

$$
f(w_{k+1}^{s+1})\leq f(w_{k}^{s+1})-\frac{(\nu_{k}^{s+1}\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1}))^{2}}{2L\|\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}+\eta_{k}(\nu_{k}^{s+1}-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1}))\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1}).\tag{10}
$$

For the last term in the right hand side of (10), we have

$$
\begin{array}{r l}{\eta_{k}\big(\nu_{k}^{s+1}-\nabla f\big(w_{k}^{s+1}\big)\big)\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}\big(\nu_{k}^{s+1}\big)=\displaystyle\frac{\nu_{k}^{s+1}\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}\big(\nu_{k}^{s+1}\big)}{L\|\sigma_{\gamma}\big(\nu_{k}^{s+1}\big)\|^{2}}\big(\nu_{k}^{s+1}-\nabla f\big(w_{k}^{s+1}\big)\big)\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}\big(\nu_{k}^{s+1}\big)}&{}\\ {\leq\displaystyle\frac{|\nu_{k}^{s+1}\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}\big(\nu_{k}^{s+1}\big)|}{L\|\sigma_{\gamma}\big(\nu_{k}^{s+1}\big)\|^{2}}\|\nu_{k}^{s+1}-\nabla f\big(w_{k}^{s+1}\big)\|\|\sigma_{\gamma}\big(\nu_{k}^{s+1}\big)\|}&{}\\ {=\displaystyle\frac{|\nu_{k}^{s+1}\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}\big(\nu_{k}^{s+1}\big)|}{L\|\sigma_{\gamma}\big(\nu_{k}^{s+1}\big)\|}\|\nu_{k}^{s+1}-\nabla f\big(w_{k}^{s+1}\big)\|,}&{}\end{array}\tag{11}
$$

where the first inequality can be satisfied due to the Cauchy-Schwartz inequality.

Further, via utilizing the fact $\textstyle 2 a b \leq \theta a^{2}+{\frac{1}{\theta}}b^{2}$ , where θ denotes any positive real number, and a and b are also two real numbers, we have the following result:

$$
\eta_{k}(\nu_{k}^{s+1}-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1}))\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\leq\frac{1}{2L}\Bigg(\theta\frac{(\nu_{k}^{s+1}\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1}))^{2}}{\|\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}+\frac{1}{\theta}\|\nu_{k}^{s+1}-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}\Bigg).\tag{12}
$$

Combining the inequalities (10) and (12), we obtain

$$
f(w_{k+1}^{s+1})\leq f(w_{k}^{s+1})-\frac{1-\theta}{2L}\frac{(\boldsymbol{\nu}_{k}^{s+1}\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{\gamma}(\boldsymbol{\nu}_{k}^{s+1}))^{2}}{\|\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{\gamma}(\boldsymbol{\nu}_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}+\frac{1}{2L\theta}\|\boldsymbol{\nu}_{k}^{s+1}-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}.\tag{13}
$$

Based on the Hölder's inequality for $\gamma\in(0,1)$ with $\begin{array}{r}{p = \frac{1 + \gamma}{1 - \gamma}}\end{array}$ and $\begin{array}{r}{q = \frac{1 + \gamma}{2 \gamma}}\end{array}$ ,we have the fact

$$
\begin{array}{r l r}{{\|\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}=\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{d}|(\nu_{k}^{s+1})_{i}|^{2\gamma}}}\\ &{}&{\leq(\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{d}1^{p})^{\frac{1}{p}}(\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{d}(|(\nu_{k}^{s+1})_{i}|^{2\gamma})^{q})^{\frac{1}{q}}}\\ &{}&{=\|\mathbf{1}\|_{p}(\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{d}|(\nu_{k}^{s+1})_{i}|^{1+\gamma})^{\frac{2\gamma}{1+\gamma}}.}\end{array}\tag{14}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\frac{(\nu_{k}^{s+1}\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1}))^{2}}{\|\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}\geq\frac{\left(\sum_{i=1}^{d}|(\nu_{k}^{s+1})_{i}|^{1+\gamma}\right)^{2}}{\|\pmb{1}\|_{p}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{d}|\nu_{k}^{s+1}|^{1+\gamma}\right)^{\frac{2\gamma}{1+\gamma}}}}\\ &{\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad=\frac{\|\nu_{k}^{s+1}\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}}{\|\pmb{1}\|_{p}}.}\end{array}\tag{15}
$$

The following results can be derived by utilizing the inequalities (13) and (15) simultaneously:

$$
f(w_{k+1}^{s+1})\leq f(w_{k}^{s+1})-\frac{1-\theta}{2L}\frac{\|\nu_{k}^{s+1}\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}}{\|{\mathbf{1}}\|_{p}}+\frac{1}{2L\theta}\|\nu_{k}^{s+1}-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}.\tag{16}
$$

Now, we consider the second term and the third term of the right hand side of (16), respectively. First, considering $\| \nu_{k}^{s + 1}\|_{1 + \gamma}^{2},$ defining in PB-SVRGE (Algorithm 1), we have

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\|\boldsymbol{\nu}_{k}^{s+1}\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}=\|\nabla f_{S}(\boldsymbol{w}_{k}^{s+1})-\nabla f_{S}(\tilde{\boldsymbol{w}}^{s})+\nabla f(\tilde{\boldsymbol{w}}^{s})\|_{1+r}^{2}}\\ &{\qquad\ge\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\|\nabla f_{S}(\boldsymbol{w}_{k}^{s+1})\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}-\|\nabla f_{S}(\tilde{\boldsymbol{w}}^{s})-\nabla f(\tilde{\boldsymbol{w}}^{s})\|_{1+r}^{2},}\end{array}\tag{17}
$$

where the first inequality holds due to the fact $\begin{array}{r}{\| a \|_{1 + \gamma}^{2}\geq \frac{1}{2}\| b \|_{1 + \gamma}^{2}- \| b - a \|_{1 + \gamma}^{2}.}\end{array}$

Second, considering $\|\nu_{k}^{s+1}-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}$ , we further obtain

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\|\nu_{k}^{s+1}-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}=\|\nabla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})-\nabla f_{S}(\tilde{w}^{s})+\nabla f(\tilde{w}^{s})-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}\\ &{\qquad\le 2\|\nabla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}+2\|\nabla f_{S}(\tilde{w}^{s})-\nabla f(\tilde{w}^{s})\|^{2}}\end{array}\tag{18}
$$

where the first inequality can be satisfied since the fact $\| a + b \|^{2}\leq 2 \| a \|^{2}+ 2 \| b \|^{2}$ holds.

Combining (16), (17) and (18), we conclude that

$$
\begin{array}{l}{\displaystyle f(w_{k+1}^{s+1})\le f(w_{k}^{s+1})-\frac{1-\theta}{4L\|\mathbf 1\|_{p}}\|\nabla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}+\frac{1-\theta}{2L\|\mathbf 1\|_{p}}\|\nabla f_{S}(\tilde{w}^{s})-\nabla f(\tilde{w}^{s})\|_{1+r}^{2}}\\ {\displaystyle\qquad+\frac{1}{L\theta}\left[\|\nabla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}+\|\nabla f_{S}(\tilde{w}^{s})-\nabla f(\tilde{w}^{s})\|^{2}\right].}\end{array}\tag{19}
$$

To hold the inequality (19), it is appropriate to hold the following condition, that is

$$
\begin{array}{l}{f(w_{k+1}^{s+1})\le f(w_{k}^{s+1})-\displaystyle\frac{1-\theta}{4L\|\mathbf{1}\|_{p}}\|\nabla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}+\displaystyle\frac{1}{L\theta}[\|\nabla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}\\ {\displaystyle\qquad+\|\nabla f_{S}(\tilde{w}^{s})-\nabla f(\tilde{w}^{s})\|^{2}].}\end{array}\tag{20}
$$

Taking expectation on both sides of the inequality (20), we have

$$
\mathbb{E}[f(w_{k+1}^{s+1})-f(w_{k}^{s+1})]\leq\mathbb{E}\left[-\frac{1-\theta}{4L\|\mathbf{1}\|_{p}}\|\nabla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}\right]+\frac{2\hat{\sigma}^{2}}{Lb\theta},\tag{21}
$$

where in this inequality, we took the fact in Assumption 2.

By telescoping sum (21) over $k=0,\ldots,K-1$ , we have

$$
\mathbb{E}[f(w_{K}^{s+1})-f(w_{0}^{s+1})]\leq\mathbb{E}\left[-\frac{1-\theta}{4L\|\mathbf{1}\|_{p}}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\|\nabla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}\right]+\frac{2K\hat{\sigma}^{2}}{Lb\theta}.\tag{22}
$$

In addition, according to $\tilde{w}^{s + 1}= w_{K}^{s + 1}$ and $w_{0}^{s + 1}= w_{K}^{s}$ , defined in Algorithm 1, we further obtain

$$
\mathbb{E}[f(\tilde{w}^{s+1})-f(\tilde{w}^{s})]\leq\mathbb{E}\left[-\frac{1-\theta}{4L\|\mathbf{1}\|_{p}}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\|\nabla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}\right]+\frac{2K\hat{\sigma}^{2}}{Lb\theta}.\tag{23}
$$

By telescoping (23) over $s=0,\ldots,\mathfrak{S}-1$ , we have

$$
\begin{array}{r}{\mathbb{E}\left[\displaystyle\sum_{s=0}^{\mathfrak{S}-1}\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\|\nabla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}\right]\leq\displaystyle\frac{4L\|\mathbf{1}\|_{p}}{1-\theta}\mathbb{E}[f(\tilde{w}^{0})-f(w^{*})]+\displaystyle\frac{8K\mathfrak{S}\|\mathbf{1}\|_{p}\hat{\sigma}^{2}}{b\theta(1-\theta)}}\\ {=\displaystyle\frac{4L\|\mathbf{1}\|_{p}}{1-\theta}\mathbb{E}[f(\tilde{w}^{0})-f(w^{*})]+\displaystyle\frac{8T\|\mathbf{1}\|_{p}\hat{\sigma}^{2}}{b\theta(1-\theta)},}\end{array}\tag{24}
$$

where the first inequality holds because of $w^{*}=\mathrm{argmin}_{\scriptscriptstyle w}f(w)$ and the first equality holds due to ${\mathfrak{S}}= T / K$ , defined in Algorithm 1.

By dividing T on both sides of (24), the desired results in Theorem 1 was derived.

### Proof of Theorem 2 (PB-SVRGE-RSBB, eq. 27)

Proof According to the results in the inequality (6) and $w_{k+1}^{s+1}=w_{k}^{s+1}-\eta_{k}\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})$ , we easily inferred

$$
\begin{array}{l}{f(w_{k+1}^{s+1})\le f(w_{k}^{s+1})+\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\cdot(w_{k+1}^{s+1}-w_{k}^{s+1})+\displaystyle\frac{L}{2}\|w_{k+1}^{s+1}-w_{k}^{s+1}\|^{2}}\\ {\displaystyle\qquad=f(w_{k}^{s+1})-\eta_{k}\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})+\displaystyle\frac{L\eta_{k}^{2}}{2}\|\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}\\ {\displaystyle\qquad\le f(w_{k}^{s+1})-\displaystyle\frac{\zeta}{b_{H}\tau}\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})+\displaystyle\frac{L\zeta^{2}}{2b_{H}^{2}\tau^{2}}\|\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}\\ {\displaystyle\qquad=f(w_{k}^{s+1})-\displaystyle\frac{\zeta}{b_{H}\tau}\nu_{k}^{s+1}\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})+\displaystyle\frac{L\zeta^{2}}{2b_{H}^{2}\tau^{2}}\|\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}+\displaystyle\frac{\zeta}{b_{H}\tau}(\nu_{k}^{s+1}}\\ {\displaystyle\qquad-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1}))\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1}),}\end{array}\tag{28}
$$

where the second inequality utilized the fact in Lemma 1.

When setting $\begin{array}{r}{\zeta=\frac{\tau\nu_{k}^{s+1}\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})}{L\|\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}}\end{array}$ , we have

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{f(w_{k+1}^{s+1})\leq f(w_{k}^{s+1})-\displaystyle\frac{(2b_{H}-1)(\nu_{k}^{s+1}\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1}))^{2}}{2Lb_{H}^{2}\|\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}+\displaystyle\frac{\nu_{k}^{s+1}\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})}{b_{H}L\|\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}\cdot(\nu_{k}^{s+1}}\\ &{\qquad-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1}))\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})}\\ &{\qquad\leq f(w_{k}^{s+1})-\displaystyle\frac{(2b_{H}-1)(\nu_{k}^{s+1}\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1}))^{2}}{2Lb_{H}^{2}\|\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}+\displaystyle\frac{|\nu_{k}^{s+1}\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})|}{b_{H}L\|\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\|}\cdot\|\nu_{k}^{s+1}}\\ &{\qquad-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|,}\end{array}\tag{29}
$$

where the last inequality took the Cauchy-Schwartz inequality.

Further, via the condition $2 a b \leq \theta a^{2}+{\textstyle{\frac{1}{\theta}}}b^{2}$ , we have

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{f(w_{k+1}^{s+1})\leq f(w_{k}^{s+1})-\displaystyle\frac{(2b_{H}-1)(\nu_{k}^{s+1}\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1}))^{2}}{2Lb_{H}^{2}\|\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}+\displaystyle\frac{\theta(\nu_{k}^{s+1}\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1}))^{2}}{2b_{H}L\|\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}}\\ &{\qquad+\displaystyle\frac{\|\nu_{k}^{s+1}-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}{2b_{H}L\theta}}\\ &{\qquad=f(w_{k}^{s+1})-\displaystyle\frac{(2b_{H}-\theta b_{H}-1)(\nu_{k}^{s+1}\cdot\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1}))^{2}}{2Lb_{H}^{2}\|\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}+\displaystyle\frac{\|\nu_{k}^{s+1}-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}{2b_{H}L\theta}.}\end{array}\tag{30}
$$

According to the conclusion in the inequality (15), we derived:

$$
f(w_{k+1}^{s+1})\leq f(w_{k}^{s+1})-\frac{(2b_{H}-\theta b_{H}-1)}{2Lb_{H}^{2}}\cdot\frac{\|\boldsymbol{\nu}_{k}^{s+1}\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}}{\|\mathbf{1}\|_{p}}+\frac{\|\boldsymbol{\nu}_{k}^{s+1}-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}{2b_{H}L\theta}\tag{31}
$$

Combining (31), (17) and (18), the following conclusion was obtained

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{f(w_{k+1}^{s+1})\le f(w_{k}^{s+1})-\displaystyle\frac{(2b_{H}-\theta b_{H}-1)}{4Lb_{H}^{2}\|{\mathbf 1}\|_{p}}\cdot\|\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}+\displaystyle\frac{(2b_{H}-\theta b_{H}-1)}{2Lb_{H}^{2}\|{\mathbf 1}\|_{p}}}\\ &{\qquad\cdot\|\nabla f_{S}(\tilde{w}_{s})-\nabla f(\tilde{w}_{s})\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}+\displaystyle\frac{1}{b_{H}L\theta}[\|\nabla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}\\ &{\qquad+\|\nabla f_{S}(\tilde{w}^{s})-\nabla f(\tilde{w}^{s})\|^{2}].}\end{array}\tag{32}
$$

To make the inequality (19) be satisfied, we only keep the following condition

$$
\begin{array}{r l r}{{f(w_{k+1}^{s+1})\le f(w_{k}^{s+1})-\frac{(2b_{H}-\theta b_{H}-1)}{4Lb_{H}^{2}\|{\mathbf 1}\|_{p}}\cdot\|\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}+\frac{1}{b_{H}L\theta}[\|\nabla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})-\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}}}\\ &{}&{\qquad+\|\nabla f_{S}(\tilde{w}^{s})-\nabla f(\tilde{w}^{s})\|^{2}].}\end{array}\tag{33}
$$

Taking expectation on both sides of the inequality (33), we have

$$
\mathbb{E}[f(w_{k+1}^{s+1})-f(w_{k}^{s+1})]\leq\mathbb{E}\left[-\frac{(2b_{H}-\theta b_{H}-1)}{4Lb_{H}^{2}\|{\bf 1}\|_{p}}\|\nabla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}\right]+\frac{2\hat{\sigma}^{2}}{Lb_{H}b\theta},\tag{34}
$$

where in this inequality, we took the fact in Assumption 2 simultaneously.

When summing (34) over $k=0,\ldots,K-1$ recursively, we have

$$
\mathbb{E}[f(w_{K}^{s+1})-f(w_{0}^{s+1})]\leq\mathbb{E}\left[-\frac{(2b_{H}-\theta b_{H}-1)}{4Lb_{H}^{2}\|{\bf 1}\|_{p}}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\|\nabla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}\right]+\frac{2K\hat{\sigma}^{2}}{Lb_{H}b\theta}.\tag{35}
$$

In addition, according to $\tilde{w}^{s + 1}= w_{K}^{s + 1}$ and $w_{0}^{s + 1}= w_{K}^{s}$ , defined in Algorithm 2, we further obtain

$$
\mathbb{E}[f(\tilde{w}^{s+1})-f(\tilde{w}^{s})]\leq\mathbb{E}\left[-\frac{(2b_{H}-\theta b_{H}-1)}{4Lb_{H}^{2}\|{\mathbf 1}\|_{p}}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\|\nabla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}\right]+\frac{2K\hat{\sigma}^{2}}{Lb_{H}b\theta}.\tag{36}
$$

In addition, via telescoping (36) over $s=0,\ldots,\mathfrak{S}-1$ , we derive

$$
\begin{array}{r}{\mathbb{E}\left[\displaystyle\sum_{s=0}^{\mathfrak{S}-1}\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\|\nabla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}\right]\leq\displaystyle\frac{4b_{H}^{2}L\|\mathbf{1}\|_{p}}{2b_{H}-\theta b_{H}-1}\mathbb{E}[f(\tilde{w}^{0})-f(w^{*})]+\displaystyle\frac{8b_{H}K\mathfrak{S}\|\mathbf{1}\|_{p}\hat{\sigma}^{2}}{(2b_{H}-\theta b_{H}-1)b\theta}}\\ {=\displaystyle\frac{4b_{H}^{2}L\|\mathbf{1}\|_{p}}{2b_{H}-\theta b_{H}-1}\mathbb{E}[f(\tilde{w}^{0})-f(w^{*})]+\displaystyle\frac{8\hat{\sigma}^{2}b_{H}T\|\mathbf{1}\|_{p}}{(2b_{H}-\theta b_{H}-1)b\theta},}\end{array}\tag{37}
$$

where the first inequality holds because of $w^{*}=\arg\operatorname*{min}_{w}f(w)$ and the first equality uses ${\mathfrak{S}}= T / K$ defined in Algorithm 2.

Finally, by dividing T on both sides of (37), the desired results in Theorem 2 was obtained.

context.name: Setup: finite-sum problem (1) (Section 1)
context.statement:
Large numbers of applications in machine learning (Le Thi et al., 2022), computer vision (Xu et al., 2021) and numerical optimization (Fehrman et al., 2020) are often implemented to be a finite-sum structure of the form

$$
\operatorname*{min}_{w\in\mathbb{R}^{d}}f(w)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}f_{i}(w),\tag{1}
$$

where n denotes the total number of the instances, w defines the parameter to learn and $f_{i}(\cdot):\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}$ represents a loss function corresponding to the i-th instance with d dimensions. In this work, we are mainly interested in each $f_{i}(w)$ and $f(w)$ that are L-smooth but may be non-convex. More concretely and vividly, the cases Problem (1) referred into logistic regression, eigenvector computation, multi-kernel learning, neural networks, to name a few.

context.name: Notation (Section 1.2)
context.statement: Throughout this work, we take $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ to define the set of d-dimensional real number vectors. For vectors, the mark w · v is used to denote their inner product. Additionally, we use [n] to define the set $\{1,2,\ldots,\mathtt{n}\}$ . The symbol $\| \cdot \|$ and $\| \cdot \|_{p}$ are chosen to represent the Euclidean norm and p-norm on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ respectively. Moreover, Denote by $\nabla f(\boldsymbol{w})$ the gradient of the loss function $f(w)$ . We adopt $\mathbb{E}[ \cdot ]$ to represent the expectation with respect to the underlying probability space. We use $(w)_{i}$ to represent the i-th element of vector $\boldsymbol{w}\in \mathbb{R}^{d}$

context.name: SVRG update (3) and Powerball update (4); definition of σ_γ (Section 3)
context.statement:
Since this work will delve into the theoretical and numerical characteristics of SVRGE in PSO algorithms, we offer some discussions about the updating scheme of the original SVRG algorithm, originally developed in (Johnson and Zhang, 2013). Comparing with the conventional SGD algorithm that worked with the update scheme:

$$
w_{k+1}=w_{k}-\eta_{k}\nabla f_{i}(w_{k}),\tag{2}
$$

for solving Problem (1), the update scheme of SVRG usually took the form:

$$
w_{k+1}=w_{k}-\eta_{k}\big(\nabla f_{i}\big(w_{k}\big)-\nabla f_{i}\big(\tilde{w}\big)+\nabla f\big(\tilde{w}\big)\big),\tag{3}
$$

where $\tilde{w}$ was a snapshot point and $\eta_{k}> 0$ was the learning rate. In general, there were two loops in the SVRG-like approach, where the iterative rule (3) located in the inner loop. The outer loop was used to store the historical information, then transferred it into the inner loop.

The iterative scheme (3), utilizing historical information $(\mathrm{i}.\mathrm{e}.,\nabla f_{i}(\tilde{w})$ and $\nabla f(\tilde{w}))$ , made the stochastic optimization algorithms enjoy a lower variance than classical SGD, and resulted in a faster convergence rate and a better generalization in practice.

In contrast, when dealing with Problem (1), the classical iterative scheme of the PSO algorithm was:

$$
w_{k+1}=w_{k}-\eta_{k}\sigma_{\gamma}(\nabla f_{i}(w_{k})),\tag{4}
$$

where the power coefficient $\gamma\in [0,1),\sigma_{\gamma}(\nabla f_{i}(w_{k}))=\mathrm{sign}(\nabla f_{i}(w_{k}))|\nabla f_{i}(w_{k})|^{\gamma}$ Here $\mathrm{sign}(x)$ backed to the sign of $x$, or 0 if $x = 0$. Also, it was noted that the operations sign(w) and $\sigma_{\gamma}(w)$ was applied to each element if the parameter $y \in \mathbb{R}^{d}$ was a vector. For example, $\sigma_{\gamma}(y)=(\sigma_{\gamma}((y)_{1}),\sigma_{\gamma}((y)_{2}),\dots,\sigma_{\gamma}((y)_{d}))$

context.name: Algorithm 1: PB-SVRGE
context.statement:
Naturally, it was asked whether SVRGE created a positive effect on PSO algorithms? In order to respond to this question, we first proposed the PB-SVRGE algorithm (Algorithm 1) and analyzed its theoretical and empirical properties in the upcoming sections.

Algorithm 1 PB-SVRGE   
Input: $\widetilde{w}^{0}= w_{K}^{0}= w^{0}$ , epoch length $K,$ outer loop size ${\mathfrak{S}}= T / K$ , mini-batch size $b$, learning rate   
$\{\eta_{j}\}_{j = 0}^{K - 1}$ , power coefficient $\gamma .$   
for $s=0,\ldots,{\mathfrak{S}}-1$ do   
$w_{0}^{s + 1}= w_{K}^{s}$   
$g^{s+1}=\nabla f(\tilde{w}^{s})$   
for $k=0,\ldots,K-1$ do   
Randomly choose $S \subseteq [ n ]$ with $|S| =b,$ compute a new stochastic estimate $\nabla f(w_{k}^{s})$   
$\nu_{k}^{s+1}=\nabla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})-\nabla f_{S}(\tilde{w}^{s})+g^{s+1}$   
$w_{k+1}^{s+1}=w_{k}^{s+1}-\eta_{k}\sigma(\nu_{k}^{s+1})$   
end for   
Set $\widetilde{w}^{s + 1}= w_{K}^{s + 1}$   
end for

context.statement:
This work considers the theoretical properties of PB-SVRGE on non-convex optimization problems.   
To proceed the analysis, we make the following standard smoothness assumptions.

Assumption 1. Each cost function $f_{i}(w)$ in Problem (1) is differential and has a L-Lipschitz gradient, that is,

$$
\forall w,\nu\in\mathbb{R}^{d},\quad\|\nabla f_{i}(w)-\nabla f_{i}(\nu)\|\le L\|w-\nu\|.\tag{5}
$$

The conclusion in Assumption 1 indicates that the average function $f(w)$ , presented in Problem (1), has a L-Lipschitz gradient as well.

Clearly, from the smooth property of the cost function, we have the following result:

$$
f(w)\leq f(\nu)+\nabla f(\nu)^{T}(w-\nu)+\frac{L}{2}\parallel w-\nu\parallel^{2}.\tag{6}
$$

context.name: Assumption 2 (unbiased oracle, bounded variance) and the mini-batch variance bound σ̂²/b
context.statement:
Assumption 2. The stochastic gradient oracle is an independent and unbiased estimator of the gradient and satisfies

$$
 egin{array}{r l}&{\mathbb{E}_{\xi_{i}}[
abla f(w,\xi_{i})]=
abla f(w), orall w\in\mathbb{R}^{d},}\ &{\mathbb{E}_{\xi_{i}}[\|
abla f(w,\xi_{i})-
abla f(w)\|^{2}]\le\hat{\sigma}^{2}, orall w\in\mathbb{R}^{d},}\end{array}	ag{7}
$$

where $
abla f_{i}(w)=
abla f(w,\xi_{i})$ and $\xi_{i}$ denotes a random variable.

Two assumptions mentioned above were very common in the most existing studies for finding a first-order stationary point of non-convex or convex loss functions (Ghadimi and Lan, 2013; Wei et al., 2021; Zhou et al., 2018). Observe that, by (5), the gradient of the loss function does not change arbitrary rapid, and by (7), the variance of the random variable $\mathbb{E}[\|
abla f_{i}(w)-
abla f(w)\|^{2}]$ has an upper bound. Notice that, when taking b samples in vanilla SGD at each iterative step, we have $ egin{array}{r}{\mathbb{E}[\|
abla f_{S}(w)-
abla f(w)\|^{2}]\le rac{\hat{\sigma}^{2}}{b}}\end{array}$

context.name: RSBB learning rate (25) (Section 4)
context.statement:
We here briefly discussed the RSBB method. In RSBB, it also employed the similar updating rule to SGD in (2), i.e., $w_{k+1}=w_{k}-\eta_{k}\nabla f_{i}\big(w_{k}\big)$ , but the learning rate

$$
\eta_{k}= \frac{\zeta}{b_{H}}\cdot \frac{\| s_{k}\|^{2}}{s_{k}\cdot y_{k}+ \tau \| s_{k}\|^{2}},\tag{25}
$$

where $s_{k}= w_{k}- w_{k - 1}$ and $y_{k}=\nabla f_{S_{H}}(w_{k})-\nabla f_{S_{H}}(w_{k-1})$ for $k \geq 1$ . Note that, here, $S_{H}\subseteq [ n ]$ with $b_{H}$ samples $(\mathrm{i}.\mathrm{e}.,|S_{H}| =b_{H})$ and $\begin{array}{r}{\nabla f_{S_{H}}(w_{k})=\frac{1}{b_{H}}\sum_{i\in S_{H}}\nabla f_{i}(w_{k})}\end{array}$ . In addition, $\zeta$ and $\tau$ were two positive parameters. Specifically, $\zeta$ was employed to control the convergence speed. The term $\tau \| s_{k}\|^{2}$ was used to avoid the denominator of the original BB step size being zero. For the BB-type technique, it enjoyed a high-order information, resorting employing a simple but a low computational cost way to approximate the Hessian matrix unlike Newton or quasi-Newton type methods.

context.name: Algorithm 2: PB-SVRGE-RSBB
context.statement:
Algorithm 2 PB-SVRGE-RSBB
Input: $\widetilde{w}^{0}= w_{K}^{0}= w^{0},$ epoch length $K,$ outer loop size ${\mathfrak{S}}= T / K$ ,mini-batch size $b$, initial
learning rate $\eta_{0}$, power coefficient $\gamma,$ positive parameters $\zeta$ and $\tau$.
for $s=0,\ldots,\mathfrak{S}-1$ do
$w_{0}^{s + 1}= w_{K}^{s}$
$\boldsymbol{g}^{s+1}=\nabla f(\tilde{w}^{s})$
for $k=0,\ldots,K-1$ do
Randomly choose $S \subseteq [ n ]$ with $|S| =b,$ compute a new stochastic estimate $\nabla f(w_{k}^{s+1})$
$\nu_{k}^{s+1}=\nabla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})-\nabla f_{S}(\tilde{w}^{s})+g^{s+1}$
$w_{k+1}^{s+1}=w_{k}^{s+1}-\eta_{k}\sigma_{\gamma}(\nu_{k}^{s+1})$
Randomly choose $S_{H}\subseteq [ n ]$ with $| S_{H}| = b_{H}$ and compute the learning rate
$\eta_{k+1}=\frac{\zeta}{b_{H}}\cdot\frac{\|w_{k+1}^{s+1}-w_{k}^{s+1}\|^{2}}{(w_{k+1}^{s+1}-w_{k}^{s+1})\cdot(\sigma_{\gamma}(\nabla f_{S_{H}}(w_{k+1}^{s+1}))-\sigma_{\gamma}(\nabla f_{S_{H}}(w_{k}^{s+1})))+\tau\|w_{k+1}^{s+1}-w_{k}^{s+1}\|^{2}}$
end for
Set $\widetilde{w}^{s + 1}= w_{K}^{s + 1}$
end for

context.name: Lemma 1 (step-size bound η_k ≤ ζ/(b_H τ))
context.statement:
The boundary of the learning rate $\eta_{k}$ was first established in the following lemma.

Lemma 1. From the definition of $\eta_{k}$ in PB-SVRGE-RSBB (Algorithm 2), we have the following conclusion

$$
\eta_{k}\leq \frac{\zeta}{b_{H}\tau}.\tag{26}
$$

context.name: Remark after Lemma 1: positivity of s_k·y_k
context.statement: Note that the original BB technique (Barzilai and Borwein, 1988) that used the iterative scheme $\begin{array}{r}{\eta_{k}= \frac{\| s_{k}\|^{2}}{s_{k}^{T}y_{k}}}\end{array}$ to update the learning rate usually kept such the learning rate positive under deterministic optimization background, which meant that the inner product of the vectors $s_{k}$ and $y_{k}$ was positive. Due to the introduction of the mini-batching and variance reduced techniques under stochastic optimization setting, it, here, still almost kept the inner product of the vectors $s_{k}$ and $y_{k}$ positive. This is indeed the case and can be easily confirmed through numerical experiments.

u}_{k}^{s+1}\|_{1+\gamma}^{2}=\|
abla f_{S}( oldsymbol{w}_{k}^{s+1})-
abla f_{S}(	ilde{ oldsymbol{w}}^{s})+
abla f(	ilde{ oldsymbol{w}}^{s})\|_{1+r}^{2}}\ &{\qquad\ge\displaystyle rac{1}{2}\|

abla f_{S}(	ilde{ oldsymbol{w}}^{s})-
abla f(	ilde{ oldsymbol{w}}^{s})\|_{1+r}^{2},}\end{array}	ag{17}
$$

where the first inequality holds due to the fact $ egin{array}{r}{\| a \|_{1 + \gamma}^{2}\geq  rac{1}{2}\| b \|_{1 + \gamma}^{2}- \| b - a \|_{1 + \gamma}^{2}.}\end{array}$

Second, considering $\|
u_{k}^{s+1}-
abla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}$ , we further obtain

$$
 egin{array}{r l}&{\|
u_{k}^{s+1}-
abla f(w_{k}^{s+1})\|^{2}=\|
abla f_{S}(w_{k}^{s+1})-
abla f_{S}(	ilde{w}^{s})+
abla f(	ilde{w}^{s})-

abla f_{S}(	ilde{w}^{s})-

where the first inequality can be satisfied since the fact $\| a + b \|^{2}\leq 2 \| a \|^{2}+ 2 \| b \|^{2}$ holds.
