in $\overset{b}{=}$. Plugging into (18), we have

$$
g_{j}(\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{k+1})-g_{j}(\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{k})\leq-\frac{\theta}{2\eta}|\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{k+1}-\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{k}|^{2}+\frac{\eta}{2}\sum_{t=1}^{k}(1-\theta)^{k-t}|\widetilde\delta_{j}^{t}|^{2}.
$$

Summing over $k=0,1,\cdots,\mathcal{K}-1$ and $j \in S_{2}$ , we have

$$
\begin{array}{r l}{\displaystyle\sum_{j\in{\mathcal{S}}_{2}}g_{j}(\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{\mathcal{K}})-\displaystyle\sum_{j\in{\mathcal{S}}_{2}}g_{j}(\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{0})\le-\displaystyle\sum_{j\in{\mathcal{S}}_{2}}\frac{\theta}{2\eta}\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{\mathcal{K}-1}|\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{k+1}-\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{k}|^{2}+\displaystyle\frac{\eta}{2}\sum_{k=0}^{\mathcal{K}-1}\sum_{t=1}^{k}(1-\theta)^{k-t}\|\widetilde\delta^{t}\|^{2}}&{}\\ {\overset{c}{\le}-\displaystyle\sum_{j\in{\mathcal{S}}_{2}}\frac{\theta}{2\eta}\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{\mathcal{K}-1}|\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{k+1}-\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{k}|^{2}+2\eta\rho^{2}B^{4}\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{\mathcal{K}-1}\sum_{t=1}^{k}(1-\theta)^{k-t}}&{}\\ {\le-\displaystyle\sum_{j\in{\mathcal{S}}_{2}}\frac{\theta}{2\eta}\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{\mathcal{K}-1}|\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{k+1}-\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{k}|^{2}+\displaystyle\frac{2\eta\rho^{2}B^{4}\mathcal{K}}{\theta},}&{}\end{array}
$$

where we use (15) in $\overset{c}{\leq}$.

Proof Summing over (16) and (17), we have

$$
\begin{array}{r l}{g(\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{\mathcal{K}})-g(\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{0})=\displaystyle\sum_{j\in{\cal S}_{1}\cup{\cal S}_{2}}g_{j}(\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{\mathcal{K}})-g_{j}(\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{0})}&{}\\ {\displaystyle\leq-\frac{3\theta}{8\eta}\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{\mathcal{K}-1}\|\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{k+1}-\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{k}\|^{2}+\frac{10\eta\rho^{2}B^{4}\mathcal{K}}{\theta}}&{}\\ {\displaystyle= -\frac{3\theta}{8\eta}\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{\mathcal{K}-1}\|\mathbf{x}^{k+1}-\mathbf{x}^{k}\|^{2}+\frac{10\eta\rho^{2}B^{4}\mathcal{K}}{\theta}}&{}\\ {\displaystyle\overset{a}{\leq}-\frac{3\theta B^{2}}{8\eta\mathcal{K}}+\frac{10\eta\rho^{2}B^{4}\mathcal{K}}{\theta},}\end{array}
$$

where we use (8a) in $\overset{a}{\leq}$. Plugging into (12) and using $\mathcal{K} \leq K$ , we have

$$
\begin{array}{r}{f(\mathbf{x}^{\mathcal{K}})-f(\mathbf{x}^{0})\leq-\displaystyle\frac{3\theta B^{2}}{8\eta\mathcal{K}}+\frac{10\eta\rho^{2}B^{4}\mathcal{K}}{\theta}+4.5\rho B^{3}}\\ {\leq-\displaystyle\frac{3\theta B^{2}}{8\eta\mathcal{K}}+\frac{10\eta\rho^{2}B^{4}K}{\theta}+4.5\rho B^{3}.}\end{array}
$$

Proof Combing Lemmas 8 and 11 and using the parameter settings, we have

$$
f({\bf x}^{\mathcal{K}})-f({\bf x}^{0})\le-\operatorname*{min}\Bigg\{\frac{3\theta B^{2}}{8\eta K}-\frac{10\eta\rho^{2}B^{4}K}{\theta}-4.5\rho B^{3},\frac{B^{2}}{4\eta}\Bigg\}= -\operatorname*{min}\Bigg\{\frac{7\epsilon^{3/2}}{8\sqrt{\rho}},\frac{\epsilon}{4\eta\rho}\Bigg\}.
$$

From $\theta=4(\epsilon\rho\eta^{2})^{1/4}\leq 1$ , we have $\begin{array}{r}{\frac{7 \epsilon^{3 / 2}}{8 \sqrt{\rho}}\le \frac{\epsilon}{4 \eta \rho}}\end{array}$

### Proof of Lemma 13

Proof Denote $\begin{array}{r}{\widetilde{\mathbf{y}}= \mathbf{U}^{T}\hat{\mathbf{y}}= \frac{1}{K_{0}+ 1}\sum_{k = 0}^{K_{0}}\mathbf{U}^{T}\mathbf{y}^{k}= \frac{1}{K_{0}+ 1}\sum_{k = 0}^{K_{0}}\widetilde{\mathbf{y}}^{k}}\end{array}$ . Since g is quadratic, we have

$$
\begin{array}{r l}\|\nabla g(\widetilde{\mathbf{y}})\|&=\left\|\frac{1}{K_{0}+1}\sum_{k=0}^{K_{0}}\nabla g(\widetilde{\mathbf{y}}^{k})\right\|\\ &\overset{a}{=}\frac{1}{\eta(K_{0}+1)}\left\|\sum_{k=0}^{K_{0}}\left(\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{k+1}-\widetilde{\mathbf{y}}^{k}+\eta\widetilde{\delta}^{k}\right)\right\|\\ &=\frac{1}{\eta(K_{0}+1)}\left\|\sum_{k=0}^{K_{0}}\left(\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{k+1}-\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{k}-(1-\theta)(\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{k}-\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{k-1})+\eta\widetilde{\delta}^{k}\right)\right\|\\ &\overset{b}{=}\frac{1}{\eta(K_{0}+1)}\left\|\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{K_{0}+1}-\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{0}-(1-\theta)(\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{K_{0}}-\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{0})+\eta\sum_{k=0}^{K_{0}}\widetilde{\delta}^{k}\right\|\\ &=\frac{1}{\eta(K_{0}+1)}\left\|\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{K_{0}+1}-\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{K_{0}}+\theta(\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{K_{0}}-\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{0})+\eta\sum_{k=0}^{K_{0}}\widetilde{\delta}^{k}\right\|\\ &\le\frac{1}{\eta(K_{0}+1)}\left(\|\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{K_{0}+1}-\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{K_{0}}\|+\theta\|\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{K_{0}}-\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{0}\|+\eta\sum_{k=0}^{K_{0}}\|\widetilde{\delta}^{k}\|\right)\\ &\overset{c}{\le}\frac{2}{\eta K}\|\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{K_{0}+1}-\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{K_{0}}\|+\frac{2\theta B}{\eta K}+2\rho B^{2},\end{array}\tag{21}
$$

where we use (14b) in $\overset{a}{=}$, $\mathbf{x}^{- 1}= \mathbf{x}^{0}$ in $\overset{b}{=}$, $K_{0}+ 1 \geq \frac{K}{2}$, (10a), (15), and (10b) in $\overset{c}{\leq}$. From $K_{0}=\mathrm{argmin}_{\lfloor\frac{K}{2}\rfloor\leq k\leq K-1}\|\mathbf{x}^{k+1}-\mathbf{x}^{k}\|$ , we have

$$
\begin{array}{l}{\displaystyle \|{\mathbf x}^{K_{0}+ 1}-{\mathbf x}^{K_{0}}\|^{2}\leq \frac{1}{K - \lfloor K / 2 \rfloor}\displaystyle \sum_{k = \lfloor K / 2 \rfloor}^{K - 1}\|{\mathbf x}^{k + 1}-{\mathbf x}^{k}\|^{2}}\\ {\displaystyle \leq \frac{1}{K - \lfloor K / 2 \rfloor}\displaystyle \sum_{k = 0}^{K - 1}\|{\mathbf x}^{k + 1}-{\mathbf x}^{k}\|^{2}}\\ {\displaystyle \overset{d}{\leq} \frac{1}{K - \lfloor K / 2 \rfloor}\displaystyle \frac{B^{2}}{K}\leq \frac{2 B^{2}}{K^{2}},}\end{array}\tag{22}
$$

where we use (10a) in $\overset{d}{\leq}$. On the other hand, we also have

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\|\nabla f(\hat{\mathbf{y}})\|=\|\widetilde{\nabla}f(\hat{\mathbf{y}})\|\leq\|\nabla g(\widetilde{\mathbf{y}})\|+\|\widetilde{\nabla}f(\hat{\mathbf{y}})-\nabla g(\widetilde{\mathbf{y}})\|}\\ &{\qquad=\|\nabla g(\widetilde{\mathbf{y}})\|+\|\widetilde{\nabla}f(\hat{\mathbf{y}})-\widetilde{\nabla}f(\mathbf{x}^{0})-\pmb{\Lambda}(\widetilde{\mathbf{y}}-\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{0})\|}\\ &{\qquad=\|\nabla g(\widetilde{\mathbf{y}})\|+\|\nabla f(\hat{\mathbf{y}})-\nabla f(\mathbf{x}^{0})-\mathbf{H}(\hat{\mathbf{y}}-\mathbf{x}^{0})\|}\\ &{\qquad\leq\|\nabla g(\widetilde{\mathbf{y}})\|+\frac{\rho}{2}\|\hat{\mathbf{y}}-\mathbf{x}^{0}\|^{2}\overset{e}{\leq}\|\nabla g(\widetilde{\mathbf{y}})\|+2\rho B^{2},}\end{array}
$$

where we use $\begin{array}{r}{\| \hat{\mathbf{y}}- \mathbf{x}^{0}\| \leq \frac{1}{K_{0}+ 1}\sum_{k = 0}^{K_{0}}\| \mathbf{y}^{k}- \mathbf{x}^{0}\| \leq 2 B}\end{array}$ from (10b) in $\overset{e}{\leq}$. So we have

$$
\|\nabla f(\hat{\mathbf{y}})\|\leq\frac{2\sqrt{2}B}{\eta K^{2}}+\frac{2\theta B}{\eta K}+4\rho B^{2}\leq 82\epsilon .
$$

context.name: Problem setup: problem (1) and approximate stationary point (Section 1)
context.statement:
$$
\operatorname*{min}_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}}f(\mathbf{x}),\tag{1}
$$

where f (x) has Lipschitz continuous gradient and Hessian and it is bounded from below. Our goal is to find an $\epsilon$-approximate first-order stationary point, defined as

$$
\|\nabla f(\mathbf{x})\|\leq\epsilon .
$$

context.name: Notation and Assumption 1 (Section 1.4)
context.statement:
We use lowercase bold letters to represent vectors, uppercase bold letters for matrices, and non-bold (both lowercase and uppercase) letters for scalars. Denote $\mathbf{x}_{j}$ and $\nabla_{j}f(\mathbf{x})$ as the jth element of x and $\nabla f(\mathbf{x})$ , respectively. For the vectors produced in the iterative algorithms, for example, x, denote $\mathbf{x}^{k}$ to be the value at the kth iteration. We denote $\| \cdot \|$ to be the $\ell_{2}$ Euclidean norm for vectors, $\| \cdot \|_{2}$ as the spectral norm and $\| \cdot \|_{F}$ as the Frobenius norm for matrices. We make the following standard assumptions in this paper.

Assumption 1 1. f (x) is L-gradient Lipschitz: $\|\nabla f(\mathbf{x})-\nabla f(\mathbf{y})\|\leq L\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}\|,\forall\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}\in$ $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ ,

2. f (x) is ρ-Hessian Lipschitz: $\begin{array}{r}{\|\nabla^{2}f(\mathbf{x})-\nabla^{2}f(\mathbf{y})\|_{2}\leq\rho\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}\|,\forall\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^{d},}\end{array}$

which yield the following two well-known inequalities:

$$
\begin{array}{r}{|f(\mathbf{y})-f(\mathbf{x})-\langle\nabla f(\mathbf{x}),\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}\rangle|\leq\frac{L}{2}\|\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2},}\end{array}\tag{2}
$$

$$
\begin{array}{r}{\big|f(\mathbf{y})-f(\mathbf{x})-\langle\nabla f(\mathbf{x}),\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}\rangle-(\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x})^{T}\nabla^{2}f(\mathbf{x})(\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x})\big|\leq\frac{\rho}{6}\|\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}\|^{3}.}\end{array}\tag{3}
$$

We also assume that the objective function is lower bounded, that is, $\min_{\mathbf{x}}f(\mathbf{x})> -\infty$

context.name: Nesterov's AGD iteration (Section 2)
context.statement:
Nesterov's classical AGD consists of the following iterations:

$$
\begin{array}{r}{\mathbf{y}^{k}=\mathbf{x}^{k}+(1-\theta)(\mathbf{x}^{k}-\mathbf{x}^{k-1}),\quad\mathbf{x}^{k+1}=\mathbf{y}^{k}-\eta\nabla f(\mathbf{y}^{k}),}\end{array}
$$

context.name: Algorithm 1 (RAGD-NC) and its description
context.statement:
Algorithm 1 Restarted AGD for Nonconvex Optimization (RAGD-NC)   
1: Initialize ${\bf x}^{- 1}={\bf x}^{0}={\bf x}_{i n t}, k = 0$   
2: while $k < K$ do   
3: $\mathbf{y}^{k}=\mathbf{x}^{k}+(1-\theta)(\mathbf{x}^{k}-\mathbf{x}^{k-1})$   
4: $\mathbf{x}^{k+1}=\mathbf{y}^{k}-\eta\nabla f(\mathbf{y}^{k})$   
5: $k = k + 1$   
6: if $k \textstyle \sum_{t = 0}^{k - 1}\|{\bf x}^{t + 1}-{\bf x}^{t}\|^{2}> B^{2}$ then   
7: $\mathbf{x}^{- 1}= \mathbf{x}^{0}= \mathbf{x}^{k}, k = 0$   
8: end if   
9: end while   
10: $K_{0}=\mathrm{argmin}_{\lfloor\frac{K}{2}\rfloor\leq k\leq K-1}\|\mathbf{x}^{k+1}-\mathbf{x}^{k}\|$   
11: Output $\begin{array}{r}{\hat{\mathbf{y}}= \frac{1}{K_{0}+ 1}\sum_{k = 0}^{K_{0}}\mathbf{y}^{k}}\end{array}$

We present our method in Algorithm 1. It runs Nesterov's classical AGD iterations until the "if condition" triggers. Then we reset $\mathbf{x}^{0}$ and $\mathbf{x}^{- 1}$ equal to $\mathbf{x}^{k}$ and continue to the next round of AGD. The method terminates and outputs a specific average when the "if condition" does not trigger in K iterations. To simplify the description, we define one round of AGD between two successive restarts to be one "epoch". The restart trick, first proposed in (O'Donoghue and Candès, 2015), is motivated by (Fang et al., 2019), where a ball-mechanism is proposed as the stopping criteria to analyze SGD.

context.name: Theorem 1 (parameter settings)
context.statement: Theorem 1 Suppose that Assumption 1 holds. Let $\begin{array}{r}{\eta=\frac{1}{4L},B=\sqrt{\frac{\epsilon}{\rho}},\theta=4(\epsilon\rho\eta^{2})^{1/4}\in(0,1].}\end{array}$ and $\begin{array}{r}{K = \frac{1}{\theta}}\end{array}$ . Then Algorithm 1 terminates in at most $\frac{\triangle_{f}L^{1 / 2}\rho^{1 / 4}}{\epsilon^{7 / 4}}$ gradient computations and the output satisfies $\|\nabla f(\hat{\mathbf{y}})\|\leq 82\epsilon$ , where $\begin{array}{r}{\triangle_{f}=f(\mathbf{x}_{i n t})-\operatorname*{min}_{\mathbf{x}}f(\mathbf{x})}\end{array}$

context.name: Epoch quantities: trigger index (7), (8a), (8b), (9), (10a), (10b) (Section 4.1)
context.statement:
We prove the convergence rate of Algorithm 1 in this section. Denote $\mathcal{K}$ to be the iteration number when the "if condition" on line 6 of Algorithm 1 triggers, that is,

$$
\mathcal{K}=\operatorname*{min}_{k}\left\{k\bigg|k\sum_{t=0}^{k-1}\|{\bf x}^{t+1}-{\bf x}^{t}\|^{2}>B^{2}\right\}.\tag{7}
$$

For each epoch consisting of one round of AGD from iterations $k = 0$ to $k = \mathcal{K}$ , we have

$$
1\leq\mathcal{K}\leq K,\qquad\mathcal{K}\sum_{t=0}^{\mathcal{K}-1}\|{\bf x}^{t+1}-{\bf x}^{t}\|^{2}>B^{2},\qquad\mathrm{and}\tag{8a}
$$

$$
\|{\bf x}^{k}-{\bf x}^{0}\|^{2}=\left\|\sum_{t=0}^{k-1}{\bf x}^{t+1}-{\bf x}^{t}\right\|^{2}\leq k\sum_{t=0}^{k-1}\|{\bf x}^{t+1}-{\bf x}^{t}\|^{2}\leq B^{2},\forall k<\mathcal{K},\tag{8b}
$$

where the last inequality comes from the definition of $\mathcal{K}$. From the update of y on line 3 of Algorithm 1, we also have

$$
\|\mathbf{y}^{k}-\mathbf{x}^{0}\|\leq\|\mathbf{x}^{k}-\mathbf{x}^{0}\|+\|\mathbf{x}^{k}-\mathbf{x}^{k-1}\|\leq 2B,\forall k<{\mathcal{K}}.\tag{9}
$$

On the other hand, for the last epoch where the "if condition" does not trigger and the while loop breaks when k increases to $K$ ,we have

$$
\|{\mathbf{x}}^{k}-{\mathbf{x}}^{0}\|^{2}\leq k\sum_{t=0}^{k-1}\|{\mathbf{x}}^{t+1}-{\mathbf{x}}^{t}\|^{2}\leq B^{2},\forall k\leq K,\tag{10a}
$$

$$
\|\mathbf{y}^{k}-\mathbf{x}^{0}\|\leq 2B,\forall k\leq K.\tag{10b}
$$

context.name: Quadratic approximation setup: (12)-(15), S_1, S_2 (Section 4.1.2)
context.statement:
If $\|\nabla f(\mathbf{y}^{\mathcal{K}-1})\|\leq\frac{B}{\eta}$ , then from the AGD iteration on line 4 and (9) we have

$$
\begin{array}{r}{\|{\mathbf{x}}^{\mathcal{K}}-{\mathbf{x}}^{0}\| \leq \|{\mathbf{y}}^{\mathcal{K} - 1}-{\mathbf{x}}^{0}\| + \eta \| \nabla f ({\mathbf{y}}^{\mathcal{K} - 1}) \| \leq 3 B .}\end{array}
$$

For each epoch, denote $\mathbf{H}=\nabla^{2}f(\mathbf{x}^{0})$ to be the Hessian matrix at the starting iterate and $\mathbf{H}= \mathbf{U}\pmb{\Lambda}\mathbf{U}^{T}$ to be its eigenvalue decomposition with U, $\pmb{\Lambda}\in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}$ . Let $\lambda_{j}$ be the jth eigenvalue. Define $\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}= \mathbf{U}^{T}\mathbf{x}, \widetilde{\mathbf{y}}= \mathbf{U}^{T}\mathbf{y}$ ,and $\widetilde{\nabla}f(\mathbf{y})=\mathbf{U}^{T}\nabla f(\mathbf{y})$ . As the Hessian is ρ-Lipschitz, we have

$$
\begin{array}{l}{f({\mathbf x}^{\mathcal{K}})-f({\mathbf x}^{0})\le\left\langle\nabla f({\mathbf x}^{0}),{\mathbf x}^{\mathcal{K}}-{\mathbf x}^{0}\right\rangle+\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}({\mathbf x}^{\mathcal{K}}-{\mathbf x}^{0})^{T}{\mathbf H}({\mathbf x}^{\mathcal{K}}-{\mathbf x}^{0})+\displaystyle\frac{\rho}{6}\|{\mathbf x}^{\mathcal{K}}-{\mathbf x}^{0}\|^{3}}\\ {\displaystyle=\left\langle\widetilde\nabla f({\mathbf x}^{0}),\widetilde{{\mathbf x}}^{\mathcal{K}}-\widetilde{{\mathbf x}}^{0}\right\rangle+\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}(\widetilde{{\mathbf x}}^{\mathcal{K}}-\widetilde{{\mathbf x}}^{0})^{T}\pmb{\Lambda}(\widetilde{{\mathbf x}}^{\mathcal{K}}-\widetilde{{\mathbf x}}^{0})+\displaystyle\frac{\rho}{6}\|{\mathbf x}^{\mathcal{K}}-{\mathbf x}^{0}\|^{3}}\\ {\le g(\widetilde{{\mathbf x}}^{\mathcal{K}})-g(\widetilde{{\mathbf x}}^{0})+4.5\rho B^{3},}\end{array}\tag{12}
$$

where we denote

$$
\begin{array}{l}{g({\pmb x})=\left\langle\widetilde{\nabla}f({\pmb x}^{0}),{\pmb x}-\widetilde{\pmb x}^{0}\right\rangle+\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}({\pmb x}-\widetilde{\pmb x}^{0})^{T}{\pmb\Lambda}({\pmb x}-\widetilde{\pmb x}^{0})=\sum_{j=1}^{d}g_{j}({\pmb x}_{j}),}\\ {g_{j}(x)=\left\langle\widetilde{\nabla}_{j}f({\pmb x}^{0}),x-\widetilde{\pmb x}_{j}^{0}\right\rangle+\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\lambda_{j}(x-\widetilde{\pmb x}_{j}^{0})^{2}.}\end{array}\tag{13}
$$

Denoting

$$
\widetilde{\delta}_{j}^{k}=\widetilde{\nabla}_{j}f(\mathbf{y}^{k})-\nabla g_{j}(\widetilde{\mathbf{y}}_{j}^{k}),\qquad\widetilde{\delta}^{k}=\widetilde{\nabla}f(\mathbf{y}^{k})-\nabla g(\widetilde{\mathbf{y}}^{k}),
$$

then the AGD iterations in Algorithm 1 can be rewritten as

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\widetilde{\mathbf{y}}_{j}^{k}=\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{k}+(1-\theta)(\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{k}-\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{k-1}),}\\ &{\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{k+1}=\widetilde{\mathbf{y}}_{j}^{k}-\eta\widetilde{\nabla}_{j}f(\mathbf{y}^{k})=\widetilde{\mathbf{y}}_{j}^{k}-\eta\nabla g_{j}(\widetilde{\mathbf{y}}_{j}^{k})-\eta\widetilde{\delta}_{j}^{k},}\end{array}\tag{14a}
$$

(14b)

and $\lVert \widetilde{\delta}^{k}\rVert$ can be bounded as

$$
\begin{array}{r l r}{{\|\widetilde{\delta}^{k}\|=\|\widetilde{\nabla}f(\mathbf{y}^{k})-\widetilde{\nabla}f(\mathbf{x}^{0})-\pmb{\Lambda}(\widetilde{\mathbf{y}}^{k}-\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}^{0})\|}}\\ &{}&{=\|\nabla f(\mathbf{y}^{k})-\nabla f(\mathbf{x}^{0})-\mathbf{H}(\mathbf{y}^{k}-\mathbf{x}^{0})\|}\\ &{}&{=\|(\int_{0}^{1}\nabla^{2}f(\mathbf{x}^{0}+t(\mathbf{y}^{k}-\mathbf{x}^{0}))-\mathbf{H})(\mathbf{y}^{k}-\mathbf{x}^{0})dt\|}\\ &{}&{\leq\frac{\rho}{2}\|\mathbf{y}^{k}-\mathbf{x}^{0}\|^{2}\leq 2\rho B^{2}}\end{array}\tag{15}
$$

for any $k < \mathcal{K}$ , where we use the ρ-Lipschitz Hessian assumption and (9) in the last two inequalities, respectively.

Thanks to (12), to prove the decrease from $f(\mathbf{x}^{0})$ to $f(\mathbf{x}^{\mathcal{K}})$ , we only need to study the decrease of g(x). Iterations (14a) and (14b) can be regarded as applying AGD to the quadratic approximation $g(\mathbf{x})$ coordinately with the approximation error $\widetilde{\delta}^{k}$ , where the later can be controlled within $\mathcal{O}(\rho B^{2})$ . The quadratic approximation $g(\mathbf{x})$ equals to the sum of d scalar functions $g_{j}(\mathbf{x}_{j})$ . We decompose $g(\mathbf{x})$ into $\textstyle\sum_{j\in S_{1}}g_{j}(\mathbf{x}_{j})$ and $\textstyle\sum_{j\in S_{2}}g_{j}(\mathbf{x}_{j})$ , where

$$
{\mathcal{S}}_{1}=\left\{j:\lambda_{j}\geq-{\frac{\theta}{\eta}}\right\}\quad{\mathrm{and}}\quad{\mathcal{S}}_{2}=\left\{j:\lambda_{j}< -{\frac{\theta}{\eta}}\right\}.
$$

We see that $g_{j}(x)$ is approximate convex when $j \in S_{1}$ , and strongly concave when $j \in S_{2}$ We will prove the approximate decrease of $g_{j}(\mathbf{x}_{j})$ in the above two cases. We first consider $\textstyle\sum_{j\in S_{1}}g_{j}(\mathbf{x}_{j})$ in the following lemma.

context.name: Lemma 9
context.statement:
Lemma 9 Suppose that Assumption 1 holds. Let $\begin{array}{r}{\eta \le \frac{1}{4 L}}\end{array}$ and $0 < \theta \leq 1$ . In each epoch of Algorithm 1 where the "if condition" triggers, when $\begin{array}{r}{\|\nabla f(\mathbf{y}^{\mathcal{K}-1})\|\le\frac{B}{\eta}}\end{array}$ , we have

$$
\sum_{j\in{\cal S}_{1}}g_{j}(\widetilde{{\bf x}}_{j}^{\mathcal{K}})-\sum_{j\in{\cal S}_{1}}g_{j}(\widetilde{{\bf x}}_{j}^{0})\leq-\sum_{j\in{\cal S}_{1}}\frac{3\theta}{8\eta}\sum_{k=0}^{\mathcal{K}-1}|\widetilde{{\bf x}}_{j}^{k+1}-\widetilde{{\bf x}}_{j}^{k}|^{2}+\frac{8\eta\rho^{2}B^{4}\mathcal{K}}{\theta}.\tag{16}
$$

context.name: Lemma 10
context.statement:
Lemma 10 Suppose that Assumption 1 holds. Let $\begin{array}{r}{\eta \le \frac{1}{4 L}}\end{array}$ and $0 < \theta \leq 1$ . In each epoch of Algorithm 1 where the "if condition" triggers, when $\begin{array}{r}{\|\nabla f(\mathbf{y}^{\mathcal{K}-1})\|\le\frac{B}{\eta}}\end{array}$ , we have

$$
\sum_{j\in S_{2}}g_{j}(\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{\mathcal{K}})-\sum_{j\in S_{2}}g_{j}(\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{0})\leq-\sum_{j\in S_{2}}\frac{\theta}{2\eta}\sum_{k=0}^{\mathcal{K}-1}|\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{k+1}-\widetilde{\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{k}|^{2}+\frac{2\eta\rho^{2}B^{4}\mathcal{K}}{\theta}.\tag{17}
$$

context.name: Lemma 11
context.statement:
Lemma 11 Suppose that Assumption 1 holds. Let $\begin{array}{r}{\eta \le \frac{1}{4 L}}\end{array}$ and $0 < \theta \leq 1$ . In each epoch of Algorithm 1 where the "if condition" triggers, when $\begin{array}{r}{\|\nabla f(\mathbf{y}^{\mathcal{K}-1})\|\le\frac{B}{\eta}}\end{array}$ , we have

$$
f(\mathbf{x}^{\mathcal{K}})-f(\mathbf{x}^{0})\leq-\frac{3\theta B^{2}}{8\eta K}+\frac{10\eta\rho^{2}B^{4}K}{\theta}+4.5\rho B^{3}.\tag{19}
$$

context.name: Remark 14 (role of the averaged output in (22))
context.statement: Remark 14 The purpose of using the specific average as the output and $k \sum_{t = 0}^{k - 1}\| \mathbf{x}^{t + 1}- \mathbf{x}^{t}\|^{2}> B^{2}$ in the "if condition" in Algorithm 1, rather than $\| \mathbf{x}^{k}- \mathbf{x}^{0}\| \geq B$ , is to establish (22).

private lemma le_of_sq_le_sq' {a c : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hc : 0 ≤ c) (h : a^2 ≤ c^2) : a ≤ c := by
  nlinarith

private theorem norm_sum_sq_le {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (v : ι → E) :
    ‖∑ i ∈ s, v i‖^2 ≤ (s.card : ℝ) * ∑ i ∈ s, ‖v i‖^2 := by
  have h1 : ‖∑ i ∈ s, v i‖ ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, ‖v i‖ := norm_sum_le s v
  have h2 : (∑ i ∈ s, ‖v i‖)^2 ≤ (s.card : ℝ) * ∑ i ∈ s, ‖v i‖^2 :=
    sq_sum_le_card_mul_sum_sq
  nlinarith [norm_nonneg (∑ i ∈ s, v i),
    Finset.sum_nonneg (fun i (_ : i ∈ s) => norm_nonneg (v i))]

private theorem grad_taylor
    {f' : E → E} {Hf : E → (E →L[ℝ] E)} {ρ : ℝ}
    (hf'' : ∀ z, HasFDerivAt f' (Hf z) z)

    intro t
    simpa using ((hasDerivAt_id t).smul_const v).const_add a

    intro t

      (hf'' (a + t • v)).comp_hasDerivAt t (hc t)
    have h2 : HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => s • ((Hf a) v)) ((Hf a) v) t := by
      simpa using (hasDerivAt_id t).smul_const ((Hf a) v)
    exact (h1.sub_const (f' a)).sub h2

    intro t

      have h3 : HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => s ^ 2) (2 * t) t := by
        simpa using (hasDerivAt_pow 2 t)
      simpa using ((h3.const_mul (ρ/2)).mul_const (‖v‖ ^ 2))
    convert this using 1
    ring
  have key : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1, ‖F t‖ ≤ Bd t := by
    apply image_norm_le_of_norm_deriv_right_le_deriv_boundary
      (f' := fun t => (Hf (a + t • v)) v - (Hf a) v)
    · exact fun t _ => (hFd t).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · exact fun t _ => (hFd t).hasDerivWithinAt
    · simp [hFdef, hBdef]
    · exact hB
    · intro t ht
      have h1 : ‖(Hf (a + t • v)) v - (Hf a) v‖ ≤ ‖Hf (a + t • v) - Hf a‖ * ‖v‖ := by
        have : (Hf (a + t • v)) v - (Hf a) v = (Hf (a + t • v) - Hf a) v := by simp

        rw [abs_of_nonneg ht.1] at h
        exact h

private theorem taylor_two_sided

  have hc : ∀ t : ℝ, HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => a + s • v) v t := by
    intro t
    simpa using ((hasDerivAt_id t).smul_const v).const_add a
  have hFd : ∀ t : ℝ, HasDerivAt F ((inner ℝ (f' (a + t • v)) v : ℝ) - inner ℝ (f' a) v) t := by
    intro t
    have h1 : HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => f (a + s • v)) (inner ℝ (f' (a + t • v)) v : ℝ) t := by
      simpa using ((hf' (a + t • v)).hasFDerivAt).comp_hasDerivAt t (hc t)
    have h2 : HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => s * (inner ℝ (f' a) v : ℝ)) (inner ℝ (f' a) v : ℝ) t := by
      simpa using (hasDerivAt_id t).mul_const (inner ℝ (f' a) v : ℝ)
    exact (h1.sub_const (f a)).sub h2

    intro t

      have h3 : HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => s ^ 2) (2 * t) t := by
        simpa using (hasDerivAt_pow 2 t)

    convert this using 1
    ring

        simp only [add_sub_cancel_left, norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs] at this
        rw [abs_of_nonneg ht.1] at this

          ≤ ‖f' (a + t • v) - f' a‖ * ‖v‖ := h1
        _ ≤ (L * (t * ‖v‖)) * ‖v‖ := by
            apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right h2 (norm_nonneg _)
        _ = L * t * ‖v‖ ^ 2 := by ring
  have hfin := key 1 (by norm_num)
  simp only [hFdef, hBdef, one_smul, one_mul] at hfin
  have hab : a + v = b := by simp [hv]
  rw [hab] at hfin
  simpa [hv] using hfin

private theorem step_ineq
    {f : E → ℝ} {f' : E → E} {L : ℝ}
    (hf' : ∀ z, HasGradientAt f (f' z) z)
    (hLip : ∀ u v : E, ‖f' u - f' v‖ ≤ L * ‖u - v‖)
    {η : ℝ} (hη : 0 < η) (hLη : L * η ≤ 1/4)
    (xk xk1 yk : E) (hxk1 : xk1 = yk - η • f' yk) :
    f xk1 - f xk ≤ 5/(8*η) * ‖xk - yk‖^2 - 1/(2*η) * ‖xk1 - xk‖^2 - 3*η/8 * ‖f' yk‖^2 := by
  have h1 := taylor_two_sided hf' hLip yk xk1
  have h2 := taylor_two_sided hf' hLip yk xk

  set u := xk - yk with hudef

  have e2 : xk1 - xk = -(u + η • g) := by rw [hxk1, hudef]; abel
  have hi1 : (inner ℝ g (xk1 - yk) : ℝ) = -(η * ‖g‖^2) := by
    rw [e1, inner_neg_right, real_inner_smul_right, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq]
  have hn1 : ‖xk1 - yk‖^2 = η^2 * ‖g‖^2 := by
    rw [e1, norm_neg, norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos hη, mul_pow]
  have hi2 : (inner ℝ g (xk - yk) : ℝ) = (inner ℝ u g : ℝ) := by
    rw [← hudef, real_inner_comm]
  have hn2 : ‖xk1 - xk‖^2 = ‖u‖^2 + 2*η*(inner ℝ u g : ℝ) + η^2*‖g‖^2 := by
    rw [e2, norm_neg, norm_add_sq_real, real_inner_smul_right, norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs,
      abs_of_pos hη, mul_pow]
    ring
  rw [hi1, hn1] at h1
  rw [hi2] at h2
  rw [hn2]
  have hAnn : (0:ℝ) ≤ ‖u‖^2 := sq_nonneg _
  have hGnn : (0:ℝ) ≤ ‖g‖^2 := sq_nonneg _
  have hc1 : L/2 * ‖u‖^2 ≤ 1/(8*η) * ‖u‖^2 := by
    apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right _ hAnn

    nlinarith
  have hc2 : L/2 * (η^2 * ‖g‖^2) ≤ η/8 * ‖g‖^2 := by
    nlinarith [mul_nonneg hGnn (le_of_lt hη)]
  have h1' : f xk1 - f yk - -(η * ‖g‖^2) ≤ L/2 * (η^2 * ‖g‖^2) := (abs_le.mp h1).2
  have h2' : -(L/2 * ‖u‖^2) ≤ f xk - f yk - (inner ℝ u g : ℝ) := (abs_le.mp h2).1
  have expand : 5/(8*η) * ‖u‖^2 - 1/(2*η) * (‖u‖^2 + 2*η*(inner ℝ u g : ℝ) + η^2*‖g‖^2)
      - 3*η/8 * ‖g‖^2 = 1/(8*η)*‖u‖^2 - (inner ℝ u g : ℝ) - 7*η/8*‖g‖^2 := by
    field_simp
    ring
  rw [expand]
  linarith

    have h := Finset.sum_le_sum (s := Finset.range K)

private theorem third_taylor
    {f : E → ℝ} {f' : E → E} {Hf : E → (E →L[ℝ] E)} {ρ : ℝ}
    (hf' : ∀ z, HasGradientAt f (f' z) z)
    (hf'' : ∀ z, HasFDerivAt f' (Hf z) z)
    (hHLip : ∀ u v : E, ‖Hf u - Hf v‖ ≤ ρ * ‖u - v‖)
    (a b : E) :
    |f b - f a - (inner ℝ (f' a) (b - a) : ℝ) - (1/2) * (inner ℝ ((Hf a) (b-a)) (b-a) : ℝ)|
      ≤ ρ/6 * ‖b - a‖ ^ 3 := by
  set v : E := b - a with hv
  set F : ℝ → ℝ := fun t => f (a + t • v) - f a - t * (inner ℝ (f' a) v : ℝ)
      - (t^2/2) * (inner ℝ ((Hf a) v) v : ℝ) with hFdef
  have hc : ∀ t : ℝ, HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => a + s • v) v t := by
    intro t
    simpa using ((hasDerivAt_id t).smul_const v).const_add a
  have hFd : ∀ t : ℝ, HasDerivAt F
      ((inner ℝ (f' (a + t • v)) v : ℝ) - (inner ℝ (f' a) v : ℝ)
        - t * (inner ℝ ((Hf a) v) v : ℝ)) t := by
    intro t
    have h1 : HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => f (a + s • v)) (inner ℝ (f' (a + t • v)) v : ℝ) t := by
      simpa using ((hf' (a + t • v)).hasFDerivAt).comp_hasDerivAt t (hc t)
    have h2 : HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => s * (inner ℝ (f' a) v : ℝ)) (inner ℝ (f' a) v : ℝ) t := by
      simpa using (hasDerivAt_id t).mul_const (inner ℝ (f' a) v : ℝ)
    have h3 : HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => (s^2/2) * (inner ℝ ((Hf a) v) v : ℝ))
        (t * (inner ℝ ((Hf a) v) v : ℝ)) t := by
      have hp : HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => s ^ 2 / 2) t t := by
        simpa using ((hasDerivAt_pow 2 t).div_const 2)
      simpa using hp.mul_const (inner ℝ ((Hf a) v) v : ℝ)
    exact ((h1.sub_const (f a)).sub h2).sub h3
  set Bd : ℝ → ℝ := fun t => ρ/6 * t ^ 3 * ‖v‖ ^ 3 with hBdef
  have hB : ∀ t : ℝ, HasDerivAt Bd (ρ/2 * t ^ 2 * ‖v‖ ^ 3) t := by
    intro t
    have h3 : HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => s ^ 3) (3 * t^2) t := by
      simpa using (hasDerivAt_pow 3 t)
    have := ((h3.const_mul (ρ/6)).mul_const (‖v‖ ^ 3))
    convert this using 1
    ring
  have key : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1, ‖F t‖ ≤ Bd t := by
    apply image_norm_le_of_norm_deriv_right_le_deriv_boundary
      (f' := fun t => (inner ℝ (f' (a + t • v)) v : ℝ) - (inner ℝ (f' a) v : ℝ)
        - t * (inner ℝ ((Hf a) v) v : ℝ))
    · exact fun t _ => (hFd t).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · exact fun t _ => (hFd t).hasDerivWithinAt
    · simp [hFdef, hBdef]
    · exact hB
    · intro t ht
      have hsm : (Hf a) (t • v) = t • ((Hf a) v) := by rw [ContinuousLinearMap.map_smul]
      have hgt := grad_taylor hf'' hHLip a (a + t • v)
      have hred : a + t • v - a = t • v := by abel
      rw [hred] at hgt
      have h1 : (inner ℝ (f' (a + t • v)) v : ℝ) - (inner ℝ (f' a) v : ℝ)
          - t * (inner ℝ ((Hf a) v) v : ℝ)
          = (inner ℝ (f' (a + t • v) - f' a - (Hf a) (t • v)) v : ℝ) := by
        rw [inner_sub_left, inner_sub_left, hsm, real_inner_smul_left]
      rw [h1]
      have h2 : |(inner ℝ (f' (a + t • v) - f' a - (Hf a) (t • v)) v : ℝ)|
          ≤ ‖f' (a + t • v) - f' a - (Hf a) (t • v)‖ * ‖v‖ := abs_real_inner_le_norm _ _
      have h3 : ‖t • v‖ = t * ‖v‖ := by
        rw [norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg ht.1]
      rw [h3] at hgt
      calc ‖(inner ℝ (f' (a + t • v) - f' a - (Hf a) (t • v)) v : ℝ)‖
          ≤ ‖f' (a + t • v) - f' a - (Hf a) (t • v)‖ * ‖v‖ := h2
        _ ≤ (ρ/2 * (t*‖v‖)^2) * ‖v‖ := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hgt (norm_nonneg _)
        _ = ρ/2 * t^2 * ‖v‖^3 := by ring
  have hfin := key 1 (by norm_num)
  simp only [hFdef, hBdef, one_smul, one_mul, one_pow] at hfin
  have hab : a + v = b := by simp [hv]
  rw [hab] at hfin
  simpa using hfin

theorem theorem1_complexity
    (ε ρ L Δ : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hL : 0 < L) (hΔ : 0 ≤ Δ)
    (hK1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (1 : ℝ) / 2 * (L ^ 2 / (ε * ρ)) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 4))
    (N : ℕ) (F : ℕ → ℝ) (Fmin : ℝ)
    (hdec : ∀ i, i < N →
      F (i + 1) ≤ F i - 7 * ε ^ ((3 : ℝ) / 2) / (8 * Real.sqrt ρ))
    (hlb : Fmin ≤ F N)
    (hΔf : F 0 - Fmin ≤ Δ) :
    (N : ℝ) * ((1 : ℝ) / 2 * (L ^ 2 / (ε * ρ)) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 4))
      ≤ Δ * Real.sqrt L * ρ ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 4) / ε ^ ((7 : ℝ) / 4) := by
  set u : ℝ := ε ^ ((1:ℝ)/4) with hu
  set v : ℝ := ρ ^ ((1:ℝ)/4) with hv
  have hu0 : 0 < u := Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hε _
  have hv0 : 0 < v := Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hρ _
  have hsL0 : 0 < Real.sqrt L := Real.sqrt_pos.mpr hL
  have hε32 : ε ^ ((3:ℝ)/2) = u^6 := by
    rw [hu, ← Real.rpow_natCast (ε ^ ((1:ℝ)/4)) 6, ← Real.rpow_mul hε.le]
    norm_num
  have hε74 : ε ^ ((7:ℝ)/4) = u^7 := by
    rw [hu, ← Real.rpow_natCast (ε ^ ((1:ℝ)/4)) 7, ← Real.rpow_mul hε.le]
    norm_num
  have hρs : Real.sqrt ρ = v^2 := by
    rw [hv, ← Real.rpow_natCast (ρ ^ ((1:ℝ)/4)) 2, ← Real.rpow_mul hρ.le, Real.sqrt_eq_rpow]
    norm_num
  have hLrp : (L ^ 2 / (ε * ρ)) ^ ((1:ℝ)/4) = Real.sqrt L / (u * v) := by
    rw [Real.div_rpow (by positivity) (by positivity), Real.mul_rpow hε.le hρ.le]
    congr 1
    rw [← Real.rpow_natCast L 2, ← Real.rpow_mul hL.le, Real.sqrt_eq_rpow]
    norm_num
  -- descent chain
  set c : ℝ := 7 * ε ^ ((3:ℝ)/2) / (8 * Real.sqrt ρ) with hc
  have hc0 : 0 < c := by
    rw [hc]; positivity
  have hstep : ∀ m, m ≤ N → F m ≤ F 0 - (m:ℝ) * c := by
    intro m
    induction m with
    | zero => intro _; simp
    | succ k ih =>
        intro hk
        have h1 := ih (by omega)
        have h2 := hdec k (by omega)
        push_cast
        linarith

    have h := hstep N le_rfl
    linarith
  set R : ℝ := Real.sqrt L * v / u^7 with hR
  have hR0 : 0 ≤ R := by rw [hR]; positivity
  have hAeq : (1:ℝ)/2 * (L ^ 2 / (ε * ρ)) ^ ((1:ℝ)/4) = (4/7) * R * c := by
    rw [hLrp, hR, hc, hε32, hρs]
    field_simp
    ring
  have hgoal : Δ * Real.sqrt L * ρ ^ ((1:ℝ)/4) / ε ^ ((7:ℝ)/4) = Δ * R := by
    rw [hR, ← hv, hε74]
    ring
  rw [hAeq, hgoal]
  have : (N:ℝ) * ((4/7) * R * c) = (4/7) * R * ((N:ℝ) * c) := by ring
  rw [this]
  nlinarith [hR0, hNc, hΔ]

targets.label: Lemma 4 (Simulation Lemma)
targets.statement:
Lemma 4 Suppose $M$ and $\bar{M}$ are SGs on $N$ states and that $\bar{M}$ is an $\frac{\epsilon}{N T R_{m a x}}$ -approximation of $M$. Then, for any state $s$, any policy $\pi$ of the agent and any policy $\rho$ of the adversary,

$$
|U_{\bar{M}}(s,\pi,\rho,T)-U_{M}(s,\pi,\rho,T)|\le\epsilon .
$$

targets.label: Lemma 4 engine (path-distribution total-variation bound)
targets.statement:
**Lemma 4, engine (path-distribution total-variation bound).**

Same setting as Lemma 4: a two-player stochastic game on $N$ states, $k$ actions and horizon $T$, and $\bar{M}$ approximating $M$ to within $\alpha \ge 0$ in the sense that rewards agree and $|\bar{P}(s,a,a',t) - P(s,a,a',t)| \le \alpha$ for all $s, a, a', t$.

Claim: the two induced distributions over length-$T$ trajectories (each trajectory being a sequence of $T+1$ states together with both players' $T$ actions) are close in total variation —

$$
\sum_w |\Pr_{\bar{M}}(w) - \Pr_M(w)| \le N \cdot T \cdot \alpha,
$$

the sum being over all trajectories $w$ from $s_0$. This is the step that carries Lemma 4: a per-transition error of $\alpha$ accumulates to at most $N \cdot T \cdot \alpha$ over the whole path distribution, and bounded rewards then turn that into the value bound.

targets.label: Lemma 6 core (implicit explore-or-exploit value bound)
targets.statement:
**Lemma 6, core (implicit explore-or-exploit value bound).**

Setting: a stochastic game $M$ on $N$ states as in Lemma 4, together with a set $L$ of (state, action, action) triples designated UNKNOWN. Build an auxiliary game on $N+1$ states by adding one absorbing state: from any triple in $L$ the auxiliary game moves to the new state with probability 1 and pays $R_{\max}$; the new state is absorbing and also pays $R_{\max}$; off $L$ the auxiliary game agrees with $M$ in both transitions and rewards. Lift a pair of policies for $M$ to the auxiliary game so that they behave identically on histories that never leave the original $N$ states.

Let the escape probability be the probability, under $M$ and the original policies from $s_0$, that the trajectory uses at least one triple in $L$.

Claim: the values of the two games differ by at most $R_{\max}$ times that probability —

$$
|U_{\mathrm{aux}}(\pi_a', \pi_d', s_0) - U_M(\pi_a, \pi_d, s_0)| \le R_{\max} \cdot \Pr[\text{escape}].
$$

This is the explore-or-exploit dichotomy in quantitative form: optimism about the unknown triples costs nothing unless they are actually reached, so either the auxiliary game's value is nearly the true value, or the unknown set gets visited with substantial probability.

nl_proof:
### Proof of Lemma 4 (Simulation Lemma)

Proof Once the policies of both players are fixed, an MDP and a general SG alike give rise to a probability distribution over the T-step paths through the state space. Since the players' policies may be non-stationary, the resulting process need not be Markov. Still, at every point the transition probabilities are determined by the current state together with the actions chosen, and the probability of a path equals the product of the probabilities of the transitions along it. This holds regardless of whether the policies are pure or mixed.

Our goal is to show

$$
\sum_{p}|\operatorname*{Pr}_{M}(p)U_{M}(p)-\operatorname*{Pr}_{\bar{M}}(p)U_{\bar{M}}(p)|\leq\epsilon
$$

in which $p$ ranges over T-step paths that start at $s$ , $\operatorname*{Pr}_{M}(p)$ (and, correspondingly, $\mathrm{Pr}_{\bar{M}}(p)$ ) denotes the probability of $p$ under the random process generated by M (respectively by $\bar{M}$ ), π, and $\rho,$ and $U_{M}(p)$ (respectively $U_{\bar{M}}(p)$ ) denotes the average payoff collected along $p$. As the average payoff never exceeds $R_{m a x}$ , it follows that

$$
\sum_{p}|\operatorname*{Pr}_{M}(p)U_{M}(p)-\operatorname*{Pr}_{\bar{M}}(p)U_{\bar{M}}(p)|\leq\sum_{p}|\operatorname*{Pr}_{M}(p)-\operatorname*{Pr}_{\bar{M}}(p)|R_{max}.
$$

So the proof will be finished once we verify that

$$
\sum_{p}|\operatorname*{Pr}_{M}(p)-\operatorname*{Pr}_{\bar{M}}(p)|\leq\epsilon/R_{max}
$$

Define the random process $h_{i}$ as follows: begin in state s and play according to $\rho$ and $\pi ;$ during the first i steps, use transition probabilities equal to those of the process just described on $\bar{M}$ , and during the remaining steps use transition probabilities equal to those of $M .$ For the purpose of evaluating probabilities of T-step paths, $h_{0}$ then coincides with the original process on M, and $h_{T}$ coincides with the original process on $\bar{M}$. By the triangle inequality,

$$
\sum_{p}|\operatorname*{Pr}_{M}(p)-\operatorname*{Pr}_{\bar{M}}(p)| =\sum_{p}|\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{0}}(p)-\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{T}}(p)|\leq\sum_{i=0}^{T-1}\sum_{p}|\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i}}(p)-\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i+1}}(p)|
$$

Hence, once we establish $\begin{array}{r}{\sum_{p}|\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i}}(p)-\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i+1}}(p)|\leq\epsilon/TR_{max}}\end{array}$ for every $0 \leq i < T$ , we obtain $\begin{array}{r}{\sum_{p}|\operatorname*{Pr}_{M}(p)-\operatorname*{Pr}_{\bar{M}}(p)|\leq\epsilon/R_{max}}\end{array}$ , which is exactly the required bound.

It therefore remains to show $\begin{array}{r}{\sum_{p}|\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i}}(p)-\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i+1}}(p)|\leq\epsilon/TR_{max}}\end{array}$ . We organise the sum over paths $p$ in four layers: the outermost runs over the N states that may be occupied after i steps; next, for each such state, over the path prefixes leading to it; then over the states that may be occupied after step $i + 1$ ; and innermost, for each of those, over the suffixes beginning there. Each path $p$ then has probability equal to the probability of its prefix, times the probability of the transition from $x_{i}$ to $x_{i + 1}$ , times the probability of its suffix. Here $x_{i}$ stands for the state occupied after i steps, $x_{i + 1}$ for the state occupied after $i + 1$ steps, $pre(x_{i})$ for the i-step prefixes ending at $x_{i}$ , and $suf(x_{j})$ for the suffixes beginning at $x_{j}$ . Accordingly,

$$
\begin{array}{r l}{\underset{p}{\mathop{\sum}}|\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i}}(p)-\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i+1}}(p)| =\underset{x_{i}}{\mathop{\sum}}}&{\underset{pre(x_{i})}{\mathop{\sum}}\underset{x_{i+1}}{\mathop{\sum}}\underset{suf(x_{i+1})}{\mathop{\sum}}|(\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i}}(pre(x_{i}))\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i}}(x_{i}\to x_{i+1})\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i}}(suf(x_{i+1})))-}\\ {\quad}&{(\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i+1}}(pre(x_{i}))\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i+1}}(x_{i}\to x_{i+1})\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i+1}}(suf(x_{i+1})))|}\end{array}
$$

Since $h_{i}$ and $h_{i + 1}$ assign the same probabilities to prefixes and to suffixes, the sum above equals

$$
\begin{array}{l}{\displaystyle\sum_{x_{i}}\displaystyle\sum_{pre(x_{i})}\sum_{x_{i+1}}\sum_{suf(x_{i+1})}\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i}}(pre(x_{i}))\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i}}(suf(x_{i+1}))|\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i}}(x_{i}\to x_{i+1})-\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i+1}}(x_{i}\to x_{i+1})| =}\\ {\displaystyle\sum_{x_{i}}\displaystyle\sum_{pre(x_{i})}\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i}}(pre(x_{i}))\sum_{x_{i+1}}\sum_{suf(x_{i+1})}\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i}}(suf(x_{i+1}))|\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i}}(x_{i}\to x_{i+1})-\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i+1}}(x_{i}\to x_{i+1})|\le}\\ {\displaystyle\qquad [\displaystyle\sum_{x_{i}}\sum_{pre(x_{i})}\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i}}(pre(x_{i}))][\displaystyle\sum_{x_{i+1}}\sum_{suf(x_{i+1})}\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i}}(suf(x_{i+1}))\epsilon/NTR_{max}]}\end{array}
$$

The final expression factors into two independent terms. The first one sums over every i-step prefix (that is, over every prefix that starts at the given $x_{0}$ and ends at $x_{i}$ , whatever $x_{i}$ is), so it equals 1. The second one sums over every suffix starting at $x_{i + 1}$ , whatever $x_{i + 1}$ is. For a fixed value of $x_{i + 1}$ , the suffixes starting there have total probability 1; adding these up over all possible values of $x_{i + 1}$ yields $N$

Consequently,

$$
\sum_{p}|\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i}}(p)-\operatorname*{Pr}_{h_{i+1}}(p)|\leq 1\cdot\epsilon/NTR_{max}\cdot N
$$

and the proof is complete.

### Proof of Lemma 6 core (implicit explore-or-exploit value bound)

To establish the claim, we argue that when R-MAX is played, the agent's reward in M and its reward in $M_{L}$ differ by less than $R_{m a x}$ times the exploration probability. Consequently, a small exploration probability forces R-MAX to obtain a near-optimal payoff; put the other way, failing to obtain a near-optimal payoff forces the exploration probability to be large enough.

Every policy satisfies the decomposition

$$
U_{M}(s,\pi,\rho,T)=\sum_{p}{Pr_{M}^{\pi,s}[p]U_{M}(p)}=\sum_{q}{Pr_{M}^{\pi,s}[q]U_{M}(q)}+\sum_{r}{Pr_{M}^{\pi,s}[r]U_{M}(r)}
$$

in which the three sums range, in order, over all T-paths p in M, over the T-paths q in M none of whose visited entries lies in L, and over the T-paths r in M that visit at least one entry lying in L. It follows that

$$
\begin{array}{l}{{\displaystyle|U_{M}(s,{\mathrm{R-max}},\rho,T)-U_{M_{L}}(s,{\mathrm{R-max}},\rho,T)| = |\sum_{p}Pr_{M}^{{\mathrm{R-max}},\rho,s}[p]U_{M}(p)-\sum_{p}Pr_{M_{L}}^{{\mathrm{R-max}},\rho,s}[p]U_{M_{L}}(p)|}}\\ {~}\\ {{\displaystyle~= |\sum_{q}Pr_{M}^{{\mathrm{R-max}},\rho,s}[q]U_{M}(q)+\sum_{r}Pr_{M}^{{\mathrm{R-max}},\rho,s}[r]U_{M}(r)-}}\end{array}
$$

$$
\begin{array}{c l}{{}}&{{\displaystyle\sum_{q}Pr_{M_{L}}^{\mathrm{R-max},\rho,s}[q]U_{M_{L}}(q)+\sum_{r}Pr_{M_{L}}^{\mathrm{R-max},\rho,s}[r]U_{M_{L}}(r)|}}\\ {{}}&{{\displaystyle\leq|\sum_{q}Pr_{M}^{\mathrm{R-max},\rho,s}[q]U_{M}(q)-\sum_{q}Pr_{M_{L}}^{\mathrm{R-max},\rho,s}[q]U_{M_{L}}(q)|\ +}}\\ {{}}&{{\displaystyle~|\sum_{r}{Pr_{M}^{\mathrm{R-max},\rho,s}[r]U_{M}(r)-\sum_{r}{Pr_{M_{L}}^{\mathrm{R-max},\rho,s}[r]U_{M_{L}}(r)}|}}}\end{array}
$$

The first of these differences,

$$
|\sum_{q}{Pr_{M}^{\mathrm{R-max},\rho,s}[q]U_{M}(q)}-\sum_{q}{Pr_{M_{L}}^{\mathrm{R-max},\rho,s}[q]U_{M_{L}}(q)|}
$$

is necessarily 0: along a path that never visits an unknown entry, M and $M_{L}$ yield the same rewards, and they also assign that path the same probability.

We are therefore left with

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{|U_{M}(s,\mathrm{R-max},\rho,T)-U_{M_{L}}(s,\mathrm{R-max},\rho,T)|\leq|\displaystyle\sum_{r}Pr_{M}^{\mathrm{R-max},\rho,s}[r]U_{M}(r)-\displaystyle\sum_{r}Pr_{M_{L}}^{\mathrm{R-max},\rho,s}[r]U_{M_{L}}(r)|}\\ &{\qquad\leq\displaystyle\sum_{r}Pr_{M}^{\mathrm{R-max},\rho,s}[r]R_{max}}\end{array}
$$

The second inequality holds because the average reward along any path lies between 0 and $R_{m a x}$ ; hence the value of a path in M and its value in $M_{L}$ can differ by at most $R_{m a x}$

The final term equals $R_{m a x}$ multiplied by the probability of reaching an unknown entry.

context.name: Setup: stochastic games (Section 2.1)
context.statement:
A game models how several agents interact. It involves a set of players; each player picks an action to carry out from a prescribed action set. The combination of the players' choices determines an outcome, which is expressed numerically as a payoff vector, namely a vector containing one value per player. Our focus is on fixed-sum games with two players (games where the entries of the payoff vector always add up to the same constant). The player we control is called the agent, and the opposing player is called the adversary.$^{2}$

Games are commonly represented by a matrix; this representation is called the strategic form of the game. Rows of the matrix are indexed by the agent's actions and columns by the adversary's actions. When the agent plays its $i^{t h}$ action and the adversary plays its $j^{t h}$ action, the rewards received by the agent and by the adversary are those recorded in the entry at row i and column $j$ of the game matrix. For simplicity, we assume that the agent and the adversary have action sets of the same size; extending to action sets of different sizes is trivial.

A stochastic game (SG) consists of the players playing, one after another, standard games drawn from a given set of games; this sequence may be infinite. Each time a game is played, the players obtain the payoff prescribed by that game's matrix and then move on to a new game. Which game comes next depends stochastically on the game just played and on the actions the players took in it. Formally:

context.name: Definition 1 (stochastic game)
context.statement:
Definition 1 A fixed-sum, two player, stochastic-game [SG] M with state set $S=\{1,\ldots,N\}$ and action set $A=\{a_{1},\ldots,a_{k}\}$ is made up of the following components:

• Stage Games: to every state $s \in S$ there is attached a two-player, fixed-sum game in strategic form in which each player's action set is A. The reward matrix of stage-game i is written $R^{i}$.

Probabilistic Transition Function: $P_{M}(s,t,a,a^{\prime})$ denotes the probability of moving from state s to state t when the first player (the agent) chooses a and the second player (the adversary) chooses a'.

context.name: SGs vs MDPs (Section 2.1)
context.statement: SGs resemble MDPs: in each model, actions cause the world to move between states. The key distinction is that an MDP's transition is governed by the action of one agent, while an SG's transition is governed by the joint action of the agent and the adversary. Moreover, in an SG the agent's reward for an action depends both on that action and on the adversary's action. To capture this, each state is assigned a game, and for this reason we use the words state and game interchangeably.

context.name: Rewards in [0, R_max], histories, policies, T-step average value (Section 2.1)
context.statement:
To simplify the presentation, the payoffs of both players in every stage game are normalised to be nonnegative real numbers lying between 0 and some constant $R_{m a x}.$ The number of actions is also treated as a constant. A history of length t is an element of $(S\times A^{2}\times R)^{t}\times S$ , that is, t state-action-reward triplets in sequence, followed by the state that is reached. The set H of possible histories is the union, over all $t \geq 0$ , of the sets of histories of length t, where the histories of length 0 are the elements of S.

For a given SG, an agent policy maps H to the set of probability distributions over A. Thus, for every possible history, a policy specifies the probability with which each action is chosen.

Policies are evaluated by the average expected reward criterion, defined as follows. For an SG M and a natural number $T,$ we write $U_{M}(s,\pi,\rho,T)$ for the expected T-step undiscounted average reward of a policy π against an adversary using policy $\rho,$ with both $\pi$ and $\rho$ run from a state $s \in S$ (the subscript naming the SG is dropped when no confusion arises). The value that π can guarantee over T steps from s is denoted $U_{M}(s,\pi,T)=\operatorname*{min}_{\rho \text{ is a policy}}U_{M}(s,\pi,\rho,T)$. We then set $\begin{array}{r}{U_{M}(s,\pi)=\operatorname*{lim}\operatorname*{inf}_{T\to\infty}U_{M}(s,\pi,T)}\end{array}$ , and, lastly, $\begin{array}{r}{U_{M}(\pi)=\operatorname*{min}_{s\in S}U_{M}(s,\pi).}\end{array}$ $^{3}$

context.name: Assumptions: observability and known R_max (Section 2.2)
context.statement: Two assumptions underlie the analysis. The first is that the agent can always identify which state (or stage-game) it has arrived at, though not the payoffs and transition probabilities attached to it, and that once a game has been played the agent knows which action the adversary took and which payoffs resulted. The second is that the largest possible reward $R_{m a x}$ is known in advance; we expect that this second assumption can be dropped.

context.name: Setup and notation for R-MAX (Section 3)
context.statement: As before, M is a stochastic game made up of a set $S=\{G_{1},\ldots,G_{N}\}$ of stage-games, in each of which both the agent and the adversary choose from the action set $A=\{a_{1},\ldots,a_{k}\}$. Each game has a reward matrix $R^{i}$ attached to it, and $R_{m,l}^{i}$ stands for the pair formed by the agent's and the adversary's rewards when actions $a_{m}$ and $a_{l}$ , respectively, are played in game $G_{i}.$ There is also a probabilistic transition function $P_{M}$ , where $P_{M}(s,t,a,a^{\prime})$ gives the probability of moving from $G_{s}$ to $G_{t}$ when the agent plays a and the adversary plays $a^{\prime}.$ It is helpful to regard $P_{M}(i,\cdot,a,a^{\prime})$ as attached to the entry $(a,a^{\prime})$ of the stage-game $G_{i}$ ; in this way every model parameter, reward or transition alike, belongs to a joint action of a specific game. Fix $\epsilon > 0$ . To keep the exposition simple, for most of the analysis we assume that T, the $\epsilon$-return mixing time of the optimal policy, is known; how to relax this assumption is shown later.

context.name: Algorithm R-MAX (Section 3)
context.statement:
The R-MAX algorithm reads as follows.

Input: N – how many stage games there are; k – how many actions each stage game has; $\epsilon$ – the error bound; δ – the probability that the algorithm fails; $R_{m a x}$ – an upper bound on the reward function; T – the $\epsilon$-return mixing time of an optimal policy.

Initialize: Build a model $M'$ with $N{+ 1}$ stage-games $\{G_{0},G_{1},\dots,G_{N}\}$ and k actions $\{a_{1},\ldots,a_{k}\}$ . The games $G_{1},\ldots,G_{N}$ stand for the real games and $\{a_{1},\ldots,a_{k}\}$ for the real actions, while $G_{0}$ is an extra, fictitious game. Every entry of every game matrix is set to $(R_{max},0)$ initially.$^{4}$ Set $P_{M}(G_{i},G_{0},a,a^{\prime})=1$ for every $i=0,\ldots,N$ and every pair of actions $a,a^{\prime}$

Additionally, for every entry of every game $G_{1},\dots,G_{N}$ , keep track of: (1) a boolean flag known/unknown, whose initial value is unknown; (2) the states that have been reached by playing the joint action of this entry (together with the number of times each was reached); (3) the reward received (by both players) for playing the joint action of this entry. At the start, items 2 and 3 are empty.

## Repeat:

Compute and Act: For the current state, find a policy that is optimal over T steps, and follow it for T steps or until some new entry becomes known.

Observe and update: After every joint action, proceed as follows. Let a be your action in $G_{i}$ and $a^{\prime}$ the adversary's action.

When the joint action $(a,a^{\prime})$ is being performed in $G_{i}$ for the first time, set the reward associated with $(a,a^{\prime})$ in $G_{i}$ to the observed one.

Update the record of states that playing $(a,a^{\prime})$ in $G_{i}$ has led to

If the record of states reached from this entry now holds $\begin{array}{r}{K_{1}=\operatorname*{max}((\lceil\frac{4 N T R_{m a x}}{\epsilon})^{3}\rceil,\lceil-6 l n^{3}(\frac{\delta}{6 N k^{2}})\rceil)+1}\end{array}$ elements, flag this entry as known and set its transition probabilities to the observed frequencies.

R-MAX is thus very simple. Its initial estimate of the model parameters assumes that every state and every joint action gives the maximal reward and moves with probability 1 to the fictitious stage-game $G_{0}$ . An optimal T-step policy is computed for the current model and then followed. After each joint action the agent lands in a new stage-game, and the transition is stored in the corresponding place. When enough information has been gathered about where a given joint action leads from a given stage-game, the model entries for that stage-game and joint action are updated. After every update of the model, an optimal policy is recomputed and the steps above are repeated.

context.name: Definition 3 (alpha-approximation)
context.statement:
Definition 3 Suppose M and $\bar{M}$ are SGs sharing the same state space and the same action space. $\bar{M}$ is called an α-approximation of M if every state s satisfies the following:

1. Writing $P_{M}(s,t,a,a^{\prime})$ and $P_{\bar{M}}(s,t,a,a^{\prime})$ for the probability, in M and in $\bar{M}$ respectively, of moving from state s to state t under the joint action $(a,a^{\prime})$ of the agent and the adversary, we have $P_{M}(s,t,a,a^{\prime})-\alpha\le P_{\bar{M}}(s,t,a,a^{\prime})\le P_{M}(s,t,a,a^{\prime})+\alpha$

2. For every state s, $\bar{M}$ and M attach the same stage-game to s (so that the rewards coincide).

context.name: Definition 5 (induced SG M_L) and R-max policy
context.statement:
We now introduce induced SGs. Apart from the role played by $R_{m a x}$ , the definition mirrors the induced MDP of Kearns and Singh (1998). The agent chooses its policy on the basis of the induced SG.

Definition 5 Let M be an SG, and let L denote the set of entries $(G_{i},a,a^{\prime})$ that are marked unknown; in other words, $(G_{i},a,a^{\prime})\in L$ means that the entry for the joint action $(a,a^{\prime})$ in the stage-game $G_{i}$ is marked unknown. The SG $M_{L}$ is defined to coincide with M except that it has one more state, $G_{0}$ . Every entry of $M_{L}$ outside L has the same transitions and rewards as in M. Every entry that is in L or in $G_{0}$ moves to $G_{0}$ with probability 1 and gives reward $R_{m a x}$ to the agent and 0 to the adversary.$^{5}$

For an SG M with a set L of unknown states, $R^{M_{L}}$ -max stands for the optimal policy of the induced SG $M_{L}$ . If $M_{L}$ is clear from context, we just say R-MAX policy in place of $R^{M_{L}}$ -max policy.

context.name: Lemma 6 (implicit explore or exploit)
context.statement:
Lemma 6 Let M be an SG and let L and $M_{L}$ be as above. Let $\rho$ be any adversary policy, s any state, and $0 < \alpha < 1$ . Then at least one of the following holds: (1) $V_{R-max}>Opt(\Pi_{M}(\epsilon,T))-\alpha$ , where $V_{R - m a x}$ denotes the expected T-step average reward of the $R^{M_{L}}$ -max policy on M; or (2) when R-MAX is run on M for T steps, an unknown entry is played with probability at least $\frac{\alpha}{R_{m a x}}$

The adversary's policy $\rho$ cannot be known ahead of time in practice, so we cannot tell in advance whether R-MAX will obtain near-optimal reward or will reach an unknown entry with sufficient probability. What matters is that one of the two will happen, whatever the adversary does.

import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators

namespace ResearchLevel

structure SG (N k : ℕ) where
  P : Fin N → Fin k → Fin k → Fin N → ℝ
  R : Fin N → Fin k → Fin k → ℝ

variable {N k T : ℕ}

abbrev Traj (N k T : ℕ) := (Fin (T + 1) → Fin N) × (Fin T → Fin k) × (Fin T → Fin k)

abbrev Policy (N k T : ℕ) :=
  (i : Fin T) → (Fin (i.val + 1) → Fin N) → (Fin i.val → Fin k) →
    (Fin i.val → Fin k) → (Fin i.val → ℝ) → Fin k → ℝ

def stateHist (w : Traj N k T) (i : Fin T) : Fin (i.val + 1) → Fin N :=
  fun j => w.1 (Fin.castLE (by have := i.isLt; omega) j)

def agentHist (w : Traj N k T) (i : Fin T) : Fin i.val → Fin k :=
  fun j => w.2.1 (Fin.castLE (by have := i.isLt; omega) j)

def advHist (w : Traj N k T) (i : Fin T) : Fin i.val → Fin k :=
  fun j => w.2.2 (Fin.castLE (by have := i.isLt; omega) j)

def rewardHist (M : SG N k) (w : Traj N k T) (i : Fin T) : Fin i.val → ℝ :=
  fun j => M.R (w.1 (Fin.castLE (by have := i.isLt; omega) j).castSucc)
    (w.2.1 (Fin.castLE (by have := i.isLt; omega) j))
    (w.2.2 (Fin.castLE (by have := i.isLt; omega) j))

noncomputable def pathProb (M : SG N k)
    (πa πd : Policy N k T) (s0 : Fin N) (w : Traj N k T) : ℝ :=
  (if w.1 0 = s0 then (1 : ℝ) else 0) *
    ∏ i : Fin T,
      πa i (stateHist w i) (agentHist w i) (advHist w i) (rewardHist M w i) (w.2.1 i) *
      πd i (stateHist w i) (agentHist w i) (advHist w i) (rewardHist M w i) (w.2.2 i) *
      M.P (w.1 i.castSucc) (w.2.1 i) (w.2.2 i) (w.1 i.succ)

noncomputable def pathPayoff (M : SG N k) (w : Traj N k T) : ℝ :=
  (1 / (T : ℝ)) * ∑ i : Fin T, M.R (w.1 i.castSucc) (w.2.1 i) (w.2.2 i)

noncomputable def U (M : SG N k)
    (πa πd : Policy N k T) (s0 : Fin N) : ℝ :=
  ∑ w : Traj N k T, pathProb M πa πd s0 w * pathPayoff M w

def Approximates (Mbar M : SG N k) (α : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ s a a' t, |Mbar.P s a a' t - M.P s a a' t| ≤ α) ∧
  (∀ s a a', Mbar.R s a a' = M.R s a a')

abbrev UnknownSet (N k : ℕ) := Finset (Fin N × Fin k × Fin k)

def inducedSG (M : SG N k) (L : UnknownSet N k) (Rmax : ℝ) : SG (N + 1) k where
  P := fun s a a' t =>
    if hs : (s : ℕ) < N then
      if (⟨s, hs⟩, a, a') ∈ L then (if t = Fin.last N then 1 else 0)
      else if ht : (t : ℕ) < N then M.P ⟨s, hs⟩ a a' ⟨t, ht⟩ else 0
    else if t = Fin.last N then 1 else 0
  R := fun s a a' =>
    if hs : (s : ℕ) < N then
      if (⟨s, hs⟩, a, a') ∈ L then Rmax else M.R ⟨s, hs⟩ a a'
    else Rmax

noncomputable def escapeProb (L : UnknownSet N k) (M : SG N k)
    (πa πd : Policy N k T) (s0 : Fin N) : ℝ :=
  ∑ w : Traj N k T,
    (if ∃ i : Fin T, (w.1 i.castSucc, w.2.1 i, w.2.2 i) ∈ L then
        pathProb M πa πd s0 w else 0)

theorem simulation_lemma
    (hN : 0 < N) (hk : 0 < k) (hT : 0 < T) (Rmax ε : ℝ) (hRmax : 0 < Rmax) (hε : 0 < ε)
    (M Mbar : SG N k)

    (hMP0 : ∀ s a a' t, 0 ≤ M.P s a a' t)
    (hMPsum : ∀ s a a', ∑ t, M.P s a a' t = 1)

    (hMbarP0 : ∀ s a a' t, 0 ≤ Mbar.P s a a' t)
    (hMbarPsum : ∀ s a a', ∑ t, Mbar.P s a a' t = 1)

    (hR0 : ∀ s a a', 0 ≤ M.R s a a')
    (hRle : ∀ s a a', M.R s a a' ≤ Rmax)

    (πa πd : Policy N k T)
    (ha0 : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πa i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hasum : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πa i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (hd0 : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πd i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hdsum : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πd i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (s0 : Fin N)

    (happrox : Approximates Mbar M (ε / ((N : ℝ) * (T : ℝ) * Rmax))) :
    |U Mbar πa πd s0 - U M πa πd s0| ≤ ε := by

theorem path_dist_l1_bound
    (hN : 0 < N) (hk : 0 < k) (hT : 0 < T) (α : ℝ) (hα : 0 ≤ α)
    (M Mbar : SG N k)
    (Rmax : ℝ) (hRmax : 0 < Rmax)

    (hRle : ∀ s a a', M.R s a a' ≤ Rmax)

theorem value_diff_escape_bound
    (hN : 0 < N) (hk : 0 < k) (hT : 0 < T) (Rmax : ℝ) (hRmax : 0 < Rmax)
    (L : UnknownSet N k) (M : SG N k)
    (hMP0 : ∀ s a a' t, 0 ≤ M.P s a a' t)
    (hMPsum : ∀ s a a', ∑ t, M.P s a a' t = 1)
    (hR0 : ∀ s a a', 0 ≤ M.R s a a') (hRle : ∀ s a a', M.R s a a' ≤ Rmax)
    (πa πd : Policy N k T)
    (ha0 : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πa i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hasum : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πa i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (hd0 : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πd i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hdsum : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πd i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (πa' πd' : Policy (N + 1) k T)
    (ha0' : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πa' i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hasum' : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πa' i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (hd0' : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πd' i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hdsum' : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πd' i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (hπa : ∀ (i : Fin T) (hs : Fin (i.val + 1) → Fin N) ha hd hr a,
      πa' i (fun j => (hs j).castSucc) ha hd hr a = πa i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hπd : ∀ (i : Fin T) (hs : Fin (i.val + 1) → Fin N) ha hd hr a,

    (s0 : Fin N) :
