import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators

namespace ResearchLevel

structure SG (N k : ℕ) where
  P : Fin N → Fin k → Fin k → Fin N → ℝ
  R : Fin N → Fin k → Fin k → ℝ

variable {N k T : ℕ}

abbrev Traj (N k T : ℕ) := (Fin (T + 1) → Fin N) × (Fin T → Fin k) × (Fin T → Fin k)

abbrev Policy (N k T : ℕ) :=
  (i : Fin T) → (Fin (i.val + 1) → Fin N) → (Fin i.val → Fin k) →
    (Fin i.val → Fin k) → (Fin i.val → ℝ) → Fin k → ℝ

def stateHist (w : Traj N k T) (i : Fin T) : Fin (i.val + 1) → Fin N :=
  fun j => w.1 (Fin.castLE (by have := i.isLt; omega) j)

def agentHist (w : Traj N k T) (i : Fin T) : Fin i.val → Fin k :=
  fun j => w.2.1 (Fin.castLE (by have := i.isLt; omega) j)

def advHist (w : Traj N k T) (i : Fin T) : Fin i.val → Fin k :=
  fun j => w.2.2 (Fin.castLE (by have := i.isLt; omega) j)

def rewardHist (M : SG N k) (w : Traj N k T) (i : Fin T) : Fin i.val → ℝ :=
  fun j => M.R (w.1 (Fin.castLE (by have := i.isLt; omega) j).castSucc)
    (w.2.1 (Fin.castLE (by have := i.isLt; omega) j))
    (w.2.2 (Fin.castLE (by have := i.isLt; omega) j))

noncomputable def pathProb (M : SG N k)
    (πa πd : Policy N k T) (s0 : Fin N) (w : Traj N k T) : ℝ :=
  (if w.1 0 = s0 then (1 : ℝ) else 0) *
    ∏ i : Fin T,
      πa i (stateHist w i) (agentHist w i) (advHist w i) (rewardHist M w i) (w.2.1 i) *
      πd i (stateHist w i) (agentHist w i) (advHist w i) (rewardHist M w i) (w.2.2 i) *
      M.P (w.1 i.castSucc) (w.2.1 i) (w.2.2 i) (w.1 i.succ)

noncomputable def pathPayoff (M : SG N k) (w : Traj N k T) : ℝ :=
  (1 / (T : ℝ)) * ∑ i : Fin T, M.R (w.1 i.castSucc) (w.2.1 i) (w.2.2 i)

noncomputable def U (M : SG N k)
    (πa πd : Policy N k T) (s0 : Fin N) : ℝ :=
  ∑ w : Traj N k T, pathProb M πa πd s0 w * pathPayoff M w

def Approximates (Mbar M : SG N k) (α : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ s a a' t, |Mbar.P s a a' t - M.P s a a' t| ≤ α) ∧
  (∀ s a a', Mbar.R s a a' = M.R s a a')

abbrev UnknownSet (N k : ℕ) := Finset (Fin N × Fin k × Fin k)

def inducedSG (M : SG N k) (L : UnknownSet N k) (Rmax : ℝ) : SG (N + 1) k where
  P := fun s a a' t =>
    if hs : (s : ℕ) < N then
      if (⟨s, hs⟩, a, a') ∈ L then (if t = Fin.last N then 1 else 0)
      else if ht : (t : ℕ) < N then M.P ⟨s, hs⟩ a a' ⟨t, ht⟩ else 0
    else if t = Fin.last N then 1 else 0
  R := fun s a a' =>
    if hs : (s : ℕ) < N then
      if (⟨s, hs⟩, a, a') ∈ L then Rmax else M.R ⟨s, hs⟩ a a'
    else Rmax

noncomputable def escapeProb (L : UnknownSet N k) (M : SG N k)
    (πa πd : Policy N k T) (s0 : Fin N) : ℝ :=
  ∑ w : Traj N k T,
    (if ∃ i : Fin T, (w.1 i.castSucc, w.2.1 i, w.2.2 i) ∈ L then
        pathProb M πa πd s0 w else 0)

/- A finite autoregressive process, used to isolate the probability calculation
from the concrete trajectory representation. -/
private abbrev Round (N k : ℕ) := Fin k × Fin k × Fin N

private def seqPrefix {X : Type*} {n : ℕ} (z : Fin n → X) (i : Fin n) :
    Fin i.val → X :=
  fun j => z ⟨j.val, lt_trans j.isLt i.isLt⟩

private abbrev DepKernel (X : Type*) (n : ℕ) :=
  (i : Fin n) → (Fin i.val → X) → X → ℝ

private noncomputable def depWeight {X : Type*} {n : ℕ}
    (K : DepKernel X n) (z : Fin n → X) : ℝ :=
  ∏ i : Fin n, K i (seqPrefix z i) (z i)

private theorem depWeight_snoc {X : Type*} {n : ℕ} (K : DepKernel X (n + 1))
    (u : Fin n → X) (x : X) :
    depWeight K (Fin.snoc u x) =
      depWeight (fun i u x => K i.castSucc u x) u * K (Fin.last n) u x := by
  have hp (i : Fin n) :
      seqPrefix (Fin.snoc u x) i.castSucc = seqPrefix u i := by
    funext j
    have hj : j.val < n := lt_trans j.isLt i.isLt
    simp [seqPrefix, Fin.snoc, hj]
  have hl : seqPrefix (Fin.snoc u x) (Fin.last n) = u := by
    funext j
    have hj : j.val < n := j.isLt
    simp [seqPrefix, Fin.snoc, hj]
  simp [depWeight, Fin.prod_univ_castSucc, hp, hl]

private def prefixStates {N k i : ℕ} (s0 : Fin N) (u : Fin i → Round N k) :
    Fin (i + 1) → Fin N :=
  Fin.cases s0 (fun j => (u j).2.2)

private def prefixRewards {N k i : ℕ} (M : SG N k) (s0 : Fin N)
    (u : Fin i → Round N k) : Fin i → ℝ :=
  fun j => M.R (prefixStates s0 u j.castSucc) (u j).1 (u j).2.1

private noncomputable def roundKernel (M : SG N k) (πa πd : Policy N k T)
    (s0 : Fin N) : DepKernel (Round N k) T :=
  fun i u x =>
    πa i (prefixStates s0 u) (fun j => (u j).1) (fun j => (u j).2.1)
        (prefixRewards M s0 u) x.1 *
      πd i (prefixStates s0 u) (fun j => (u j).1) (fun j => (u j).2.1)
        (prefixRewards M s0 u) x.2.1 *
      M.P (prefixStates s0 u (Fin.last i.val)) x.1 x.2.1 x.2.2

private def trajFromRounds (s : Fin N) (z : Fin T → Round N k) : Traj N k T :=
  (Fin.cases s (fun i => (z i).2.2), (fun i => (z i).1), fun i => (z i).2.1)

private def trajRoundEquiv : Traj N k T ≃ Fin N × (Fin T → Round N k) where
  toFun w := (w.1 0, fun i => (w.2.1 i, w.2.2 i, w.1 i.succ))
  invFun p := trajFromRounds p.1 p.2
  left_inv w := by
    rcases w with ⟨st, a, d⟩
    apply Prod.ext
    · funext j
      refine Fin.cases ?_ (fun i => ?_) j
      · rfl
      · rfl
    · apply Prod.ext <;> rfl
  right_inv p := by
    rcases p with ⟨s, z⟩
    apply Prod.ext
    · rfl
    · funext i
      rfl

private theorem stateHist_trajFromRounds (s : Fin N) (z : Fin T → Round N k)
    (i : Fin T) :
    stateHist (trajFromRounds s z) i = prefixStates s (seqPrefix z i) := by
  funext j
  refine Fin.cases ?_ (fun q => ?_) j
  · simp [stateHist, trajFromRounds, prefixStates]
  · simp [stateHist, trajFromRounds, prefixStates, seqPrefix]
    congr 2

private theorem agentHist_trajFromRounds (s : Fin N) (z : Fin T → Round N k)
    (i : Fin T) :
    agentHist (trajFromRounds s z) i = fun j => (seqPrefix z i j).1 := by
  funext j
  simp [agentHist, trajFromRounds, seqPrefix]
  congr 2

private theorem advHist_trajFromRounds (s : Fin N) (z : Fin T → Round N k)
    (i : Fin T) :
    advHist (trajFromRounds s z) i = fun j => (seqPrefix z i j).2.1 := by
  funext j
  simp [advHist, trajFromRounds, seqPrefix]
  congr 2

private theorem rewardHist_trajFromRounds (M : SG N k) (s : Fin N)
    (z : Fin T → Round N k) (i : Fin T) :
    rewardHist M (trajFromRounds s z) i =
      prefixRewards M s (seqPrefix z i) := by
  funext j
  change M.R _ _ _ =
    M.R (prefixStates s (seqPrefix z i) j.castSucc)
      (seqPrefix z i j).1 (seqPrefix z i j).2.1
  rw [show (Fin.castLE (by have := i.isLt; omega) j).castSucc =
      Fin.castLE (by have := i.isLt; omega) j.castSucc by apply Fin.ext; rfl]
  change M.R (stateHist (trajFromRounds s z) i j.castSucc)
      (agentHist (trajFromRounds s z) i j)
      (advHist (trajFromRounds s z) i j) = _
  rw [stateHist_trajFromRounds, agentHist_trajFromRounds,
    advHist_trajFromRounds]

private theorem pathProb_trajFromRounds (M : SG N k) (πa πd : Policy N k T)
    (s0 : Fin N) (z : Fin T → Round N k) :
    pathProb M πa πd s0 (trajFromRounds s0 z) =
      depWeight (roundKernel M πa πd s0) z := by
  unfold pathProb depWeight
  rw [if_pos (by simp [trajFromRounds]), one_mul]
  apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
  intro i _
  have hcur : (trajFromRounds s0 z).1 i.castSucc =
      prefixStates s0 (seqPrefix z i) (Fin.last i.val) := by
    have h := congrFun (stateHist_trajFromRounds s0 z i) (Fin.last i.val)
    simpa [stateHist] using h
  have hnext : (trajFromRounds s0 z).1 i.succ = (z i).2.2 := by
    simp [trajFromRounds]
  rw [stateHist_trajFromRounds, agentHist_trajFromRounds,
    advHist_trajFromRounds, rewardHist_trajFromRounds]
  simp only [roundKernel]
  rw [hcur, hnext]
  simp [trajFromRounds]

private theorem depWeight_nonneg
    {X : Type*} [Fintype X] {n : ℕ} (K : DepKernel X n)
    (hK0 : ∀ i u x, 0 ≤ K i u x) (z : Fin n → X) :
    0 ≤ depWeight K z := by
  exact Finset.prod_nonneg fun i _ => hK0 i (seqPrefix z i) (z i)

private theorem depWeight_sum_eq_one
    {X : Type*} [Fintype X] {n : ℕ} (K : DepKernel X n)
    (hKsum : ∀ i u, ∑ x, K i u x = 1) :
    ∑ z : Fin n → X, depWeight K z = 1 := by
  induction n with
  | zero =>
      simp [depWeight]
  | succ n ih =>
      let K' : DepKernel X n := fun i u x => K i.castSucc u x
      let e : ((Fin n → X) × X) ≃ (Fin (n + 1) → X) :=
        (Equiv.prodComm (Fin n → X) X).trans (Fin.snocEquiv (fun _ => X))
      calc
        (∑ z : Fin (n + 1) → X, depWeight K z) =
            ∑ ux : (Fin n → X) × X, depWeight K (e ux) :=
          (e.sum_comp (depWeight K)).symm
        _ = ∑ u : Fin n → X, ∑ x : X,
              depWeight K' u * K (Fin.last n) u x := by
          rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
          apply Fintype.sum_congr
          intro u
          apply Fintype.sum_congr
          intro x
          change depWeight K (Fin.snoc u x) = _
          simpa [K'] using depWeight_snoc K u x
        _ = ∑ u : Fin n → X, depWeight K' u := by
          apply Fintype.sum_congr
          intro u
          rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
          rw [hKsum]
          simp
        _ = 1 := ih K' (fun i u => hKsum i.castSucc u)

private lemma abs_mul_sub_mul_le (pbar p bbar b : ℝ)
    (hpbar : 0 ≤ pbar) (hb : 0 ≤ b) :
    |pbar * bbar - p * b| ≤ pbar * |bbar - b| + |pbar - p| * b := by
  rw [show pbar * bbar - p * b =
      pbar * (bbar - b) + (pbar - p) * b by ring]
  calc
    |pbar * (bbar - b) + (pbar - p) * b| ≤
        |pbar * (bbar - b)| + |(pbar - p) * b| := abs_add_le _ _
    _ = pbar * |bbar - b| + |pbar - p| * b := by
      rw [abs_mul, abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg hpbar, abs_of_nonneg hb]

private theorem depWeight_l1_bound
    {X : Type*} [Fintype X] {n : ℕ} (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
    (Kbar K : DepKernel X n)
    (hKbar0 : ∀ i u x, 0 ≤ Kbar i u x)
    (hK0 : ∀ i u x, 0 ≤ K i u x)
    (hKbarSum : ∀ i u, ∑ x, Kbar i u x = 1)
    (hKsum : ∀ i u, ∑ x, K i u x = 1)
    (hstep : ∀ i u, ∑ x, |Kbar i u x - K i u x| ≤ δ) :
    ∑ z : Fin n → X, |depWeight Kbar z - depWeight K z| ≤ (n : ℝ) * δ := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [depWeight]
  | succ n ih =>
      let Kbar' : DepKernel X n := fun i u x => Kbar i.castSucc u x
      let K' : DepKernel X n := fun i u x => K i.castSucc u x
      let e : ((Fin n → X) × X) ≃ (Fin (n + 1) → X) :=
        (Equiv.prodComm (Fin n → X) X).trans (Fin.snocEquiv (fun _ => X))
      have hpbar (u : Fin n → X) : 0 ≤ depWeight Kbar' u :=
        depWeight_nonneg Kbar' (fun i v x => hKbar0 i.castSucc v x) u
      have hinner (u : Fin n → X) :
          (∑ x : X,
            |depWeight Kbar' u * Kbar (Fin.last n) u x -
              depWeight K' u * K (Fin.last n) u x|) ≤
            depWeight Kbar' u * δ + |depWeight Kbar' u - depWeight K' u| := by
        calc
          (∑ x : X,
              |depWeight Kbar' u * Kbar (Fin.last n) u x -
                depWeight K' u * K (Fin.last n) u x|) ≤
              ∑ x : X, (depWeight Kbar' u *
                  |Kbar (Fin.last n) u x - K (Fin.last n) u x| +
                |depWeight Kbar' u - depWeight K' u| * K (Fin.last n) u x) := by
            apply Finset.sum_le_sum
            intro x _
            exact abs_mul_sub_mul_le _ _ _ _ (hpbar u) (hK0 (Fin.last n) u x)
          _ = depWeight Kbar' u *
                (∑ x : X, |Kbar (Fin.last n) u x - K (Fin.last n) u x|) +
              |depWeight Kbar' u - depWeight K' u| *
                (∑ x : X, K (Fin.last n) u x) := by
            rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.mul_sum, Finset.mul_sum]
          _ ≤ depWeight Kbar' u * δ +
                |depWeight Kbar' u - depWeight K' u| := by
            rw [hKsum]
            simp only [mul_one]
            exact add_le_add
              (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hstep (Fin.last n) u) (hpbar u)) le_rfl
      calc
        (∑ z : Fin (n + 1) → X,
            |depWeight Kbar z - depWeight K z|) =
            ∑ ux : (Fin n → X) × X,
              |depWeight Kbar (e ux) - depWeight K (e ux)| :=
          (e.sum_comp (fun z => |depWeight Kbar z - depWeight K z|)).symm
        _ = ∑ u : Fin n → X, ∑ x : X,
              |depWeight Kbar' u * Kbar (Fin.last n) u x -
                depWeight K' u * K (Fin.last n) u x| := by
          rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
          apply Fintype.sum_congr
          intro u
          apply Fintype.sum_congr
          intro x
          change |depWeight Kbar (Fin.snoc u x) -
            depWeight K (Fin.snoc u x)| = _
          rw [depWeight_snoc, depWeight_snoc]
        _ ≤ ∑ u : Fin n → X,
              (depWeight Kbar' u * δ +
                |depWeight Kbar' u - depWeight K' u|) := by
          exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun u _ => hinner u
        _ = (∑ u : Fin n → X, depWeight Kbar' u) * δ +
              ∑ u : Fin n → X, |depWeight Kbar' u - depWeight K' u| := by
          rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_mul]
        _ = δ + ∑ u : Fin n → X,
              |depWeight Kbar' u - depWeight K' u| := by
          rw [depWeight_sum_eq_one Kbar'
            (fun i u => hKbarSum i.castSucc u), one_mul]
        _ ≤ δ + (n : ℝ) * δ := by
          exact add_le_add le_rfl <| ih Kbar' K'
            (fun i u x => hKbar0 i.castSucc u x)
            (fun i u x => hK0 i.castSucc u x)
            (fun i u => hKbarSum i.castSucc u)
            (fun i u => hKsum i.castSucc u)
            (fun i u => hstep i.castSucc u)
        _ = ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * δ := by push_cast; ring

private theorem roundKernel_nonneg
    (M : SG N k) (πa πd : Policy N k T) (s0 : Fin N)
    (hP0 : ∀ s a a' t, 0 ≤ M.P s a a' t)
    (ha0 : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πa i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hd0 : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πd i hs ha hd hr a) :
    ∀ i u x, 0 ≤ roundKernel M πa πd s0 i u x := by
  intro i u x
  exact mul_nonneg
    (mul_nonneg
      (ha0 i (prefixStates s0 u) (fun j => (u j).1) (fun j => (u j).2.1)
        (prefixRewards M s0 u) x.1)
      (hd0 i (prefixStates s0 u) (fun j => (u j).1) (fun j => (u j).2.1)
        (prefixRewards M s0 u) x.2.1))
    (hP0 (prefixStates s0 u (Fin.last i.val)) x.1 x.2.1 x.2.2)

private theorem roundKernel_sum_eq_one
    (M : SG N k) (πa πd : Policy N k T) (s0 : Fin N)
    (hPsum : ∀ s a a', ∑ t, M.P s a a' t = 1)
    (hasum : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πa i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (hdsum : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πd i hs ha hd hr a = 1) :
    ∀ i u, ∑ x, roundKernel M πa πd s0 i u x = 1 := by
  intro i u
  simp only [roundKernel, Round]
  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
  simp_rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
  simp_rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
  simp_rw [hPsum, mul_one]
  simp_rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
  simp_rw [hdsum, mul_one]
  exact hasum i (prefixStates s0 u) (fun j => (u j).1) (fun j => (u j).2.1)
    (prefixRewards M s0 u)

private theorem roundKernel_l1_bound
    (α : ℝ) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (M Mbar : SG N k)
    (πa πd : Policy N k T) (s0 : Fin N)
    (ha0 : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πa i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hd0 : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πd i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hasum : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πa i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (hdsum : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πd i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (happrox : Approximates Mbar M α) :
    ∀ i u, ∑ x, |roundKernel Mbar πa πd s0 i u x -
      roundKernel M πa πd s0 i u x| ≤ (N : ℝ) * α := by
  intro i u
  let A : Fin k → ℝ := fun a =>
    πa i (prefixStates s0 u) (fun j => (u j).1) (fun j => (u j).2.1)
      (prefixRewards M s0 u) a
  let D : Fin k → ℝ := fun a =>
    πd i (prefixStates s0 u) (fun j => (u j).1) (fun j => (u j).2.1)
      (prefixRewards M s0 u) a
  let s : Fin N := prefixStates s0 u (Fin.last i.val)
  have hrewards : prefixRewards Mbar s0 u = prefixRewards M s0 u := by
    funext j
    exact happrox.2 _ _ _
  have hA0 (a : Fin k) : 0 ≤ A a := by
    exact ha0 i (prefixStates s0 u) (fun j => (u j).1) (fun j => (u j).2.1)
      (prefixRewards M s0 u) a
  have hD0 (a : Fin k) : 0 ≤ D a := by
    exact hd0 i (prefixStates s0 u) (fun j => (u j).1) (fun j => (u j).2.1)
      (prefixRewards M s0 u) a
  have hAsum : ∑ a, A a = 1 := by
    exact hasum i (prefixStates s0 u) (fun j => (u j).1) (fun j => (u j).2.1)
      (prefixRewards M s0 u)
  have hDsum : ∑ a, D a = 1 := by
    exact hdsum i (prefixStates s0 u) (fun j => (u j).1) (fun j => (u j).2.1)
      (prefixRewards M s0 u)
  have hterm (a d : Fin k) (t : Fin N) :
      |A a * D d * Mbar.P s a d t - A a * D d * M.P s a d t| =
        A a * D d * |Mbar.P s a d t - M.P s a d t| := by
    rw [show A a * D d * Mbar.P s a d t - A a * D d * M.P s a d t =
      A a * D d * (Mbar.P s a d t - M.P s a d t) by ring]
    rw [abs_mul, abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (hA0 a), abs_of_nonneg (hD0 d)]
  have htrans (a d : Fin k) :
      (∑ t : Fin N, |Mbar.P s a d t - M.P s a d t|) ≤ (N : ℝ) * α := by
    calc
      (∑ t : Fin N, |Mbar.P s a d t - M.P s a d t|) ≤ ∑ _t : Fin N, α := by
        exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun t _ => happrox.1 s a d t
      _ = (N : ℝ) * α := by simp [nsmul_eq_mul]
  simp only [roundKernel, Round]
  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
  simp_rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
  rw [hrewards]
  change (∑ a : Fin k, ∑ d : Fin k, ∑ t : Fin N,
    |A a * D d * Mbar.P s a d t - A a * D d * M.P s a d t|) ≤ _
  simp_rw [hterm]
  calc
    (∑ a : Fin k, ∑ d : Fin k, ∑ t : Fin N,
        A a * D d * |Mbar.P s a d t - M.P s a d t|) =
        ∑ a : Fin k, ∑ d : Fin k,
          A a * D d * (∑ t : Fin N, |Mbar.P s a d t - M.P s a d t|) := by
      simp_rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    _ ≤ ∑ a : Fin k, ∑ d : Fin k, A a * D d * ((N : ℝ) * α) := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro a _
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro d _
      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (htrans a d) (mul_nonneg (hA0 a) (hD0 d))
    _ = ∑ a : Fin k, (A a * ((N : ℝ) * α)) * (∑ d : Fin k, D d) := by
      apply Fintype.sum_congr
      intro a
      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
      apply Fintype.sum_congr
      intro d
      ring
    _ = ∑ a : Fin k, A a * ((N : ℝ) * α) := by rw [hDsum]; simp
    _ = (∑ a : Fin k, A a) * ((N : ℝ) * α) := by rw [Finset.sum_mul]
    _ = (N : ℝ) * α := by rw [hAsum, one_mul]

private theorem path_l1_eq_depWeight
    (M Mbar : SG N k) (πa πd : Policy N k T) (s0 : Fin N) :
    (∑ w : Traj N k T,
        |pathProb Mbar πa πd s0 w - pathProb M πa πd s0 w|) =
      ∑ z : Fin T → Round N k,
        |depWeight (roundKernel Mbar πa πd s0) z -
          depWeight (roundKernel M πa πd s0) z| := by
  let f : Traj N k T → ℝ := fun w =>
    |pathProb Mbar πa πd s0 w - pathProb M πa πd s0 w|
  calc
    (∑ w : Traj N k T, f w) =
        ∑ p : Fin N × (Fin T → Round N k), f (trajRoundEquiv.symm p) := by
      exact Fintype.sum_equiv trajRoundEquiv _ _ (fun w => by simp)
    _ = ∑ s : Fin N, ∑ z : Fin T → Round N k,
        |pathProb Mbar πa πd s0 (trajFromRounds s z) -
          pathProb M πa πd s0 (trajFromRounds s z)| := by
      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
      rfl
    _ = ∑ z : Fin T → Round N k,
        |pathProb Mbar πa πd s0 (trajFromRounds s0 z) -
          pathProb M πa πd s0 (trajFromRounds s0 z)| := by
      apply Fintype.sum_eq_single s0
      intro s hs
      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
      intro z _
      simp [pathProb, trajFromRounds, hs]
    _ = ∑ z : Fin T → Round N k,
        |depWeight (roundKernel Mbar πa πd s0) z -
          depWeight (roundKernel M πa πd s0) z| := by
      apply Fintype.sum_congr
      intro z
      rw [pathProb_trajFromRounds, pathProb_trajFromRounds]

private theorem pathPayoff_eq_of_reward_eq (M Mbar : SG N k)
    (hR : ∀ s a a', Mbar.R s a a' = M.R s a a') (w : Traj N k T) :
    pathPayoff Mbar w = pathPayoff M w := by
  unfold pathPayoff
  congr 1
  apply Fintype.sum_congr
  intro i
  exact hR _ _ _

private theorem abs_pathPayoff_le (hT : 0 < T) (Rmax : ℝ)
    (M : SG N k)
    (hR0 : ∀ s a a', 0 ≤ M.R s a a')
    (hRle : ∀ s a a', M.R s a a' ≤ Rmax)
    (w : Traj N k T) :
    |pathPayoff M w| ≤ Rmax := by
  have hTc : 0 < (T : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hT
  have hsum0 : 0 ≤ ∑ i : Fin T,
      M.R (w.1 i.castSucc) (w.2.1 i) (w.2.2 i) :=
    Finset.sum_nonneg fun i _ => hR0 _ _ _
  have hsumle : (∑ i : Fin T,
      M.R (w.1 i.castSucc) (w.2.1 i) (w.2.2 i)) ≤
      ∑ _i : Fin T, Rmax :=
    Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => hRle _ _ _
  rw [abs_of_nonneg]
  · unfold pathPayoff
    calc
      (1 / (T : ℝ)) * ∑ i : Fin T,
          M.R (w.1 i.castSucc) (w.2.1 i) (w.2.2 i) ≤
          (1 / (T : ℝ)) * ∑ _i : Fin T, Rmax :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hsumle (by positivity)
      _ = (1 / (T : ℝ)) * ((T : ℝ) * Rmax) := by
        simp [nsmul_eq_mul]
      _ = Rmax := by field_simp
  · unfold pathPayoff
    exact mul_nonneg (by positivity) hsum0

private theorem model_path_l1_bound
    (α : ℝ) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (M Mbar : SG N k)
    (hMP0 : ∀ s a a' t, 0 ≤ M.P s a a' t)
    (hMPsum : ∀ s a a', ∑ t, M.P s a a' t = 1)
    (hMbarP0 : ∀ s a a' t, 0 ≤ Mbar.P s a a' t)
    (hMbarPsum : ∀ s a a', ∑ t, Mbar.P s a a' t = 1)
    (πa πd : Policy N k T)
    (ha0 : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πa i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hasum : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πa i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (hd0 : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πd i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hdsum : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πd i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (s0 : Fin N) (happrox : Approximates Mbar M α) :
    ∑ w : Traj N k T,
        |pathProb Mbar πa πd s0 w - pathProb M πa πd s0 w|
      ≤ (N : ℝ) * (T : ℝ) * α := by
  rw [path_l1_eq_depWeight M Mbar πa πd s0]
  calc
    (∑ z : Fin T → Round N k,
        |depWeight (roundKernel Mbar πa πd s0) z -
          depWeight (roundKernel M πa πd s0) z|)
        ≤ (T : ℝ) * ((N : ℝ) * α) :=
      depWeight_l1_bound ((N : ℝ) * α) (mul_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg N) hα)
        (roundKernel Mbar πa πd s0) (roundKernel M πa πd s0)
        (roundKernel_nonneg Mbar πa πd s0 hMbarP0 ha0 hd0)
        (roundKernel_nonneg M πa πd s0 hMP0 ha0 hd0)
        (roundKernel_sum_eq_one Mbar πa πd s0 hMbarPsum hasum hdsum)
        (roundKernel_sum_eq_one M πa πd s0 hMPsum hasum hdsum)
        (roundKernel_l1_bound α hα M Mbar πa πd s0 ha0 hd0 hasum hdsum happrox)
    _ = (N : ℝ) * (T : ℝ) * α := by ring

private theorem pathProb_nonneg (M : SG N k) (πa πd : Policy N k T)
    (s0 : Fin N)
    (hP0 : ∀ s a a' t, 0 ≤ M.P s a a' t)
    (ha0 : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πa i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hd0 : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πd i hs ha hd hr a)
    (w : Traj N k T) : 0 ≤ pathProb M πa πd s0 w := by
  unfold pathProb
  apply mul_nonneg
  · split_ifs <;> positivity
  · apply Finset.prod_nonneg
    intro i _
    exact mul_nonneg
      (mul_nonneg (ha0 _ _ _ _ _ _) (hd0 _ _ _ _ _ _))
      (hP0 _ _ _ _)

private theorem pathProb_sum_eq_one (M : SG N k) (πa πd : Policy N k T)
    (s0 : Fin N)
    (hPsum : ∀ s a a', ∑ t, M.P s a a' t = 1)
    (hasum : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πa i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (hdsum : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πd i hs ha hd hr a = 1) :
    ∑ w : Traj N k T, pathProb M πa πd s0 w = 1 := by
  calc
    (∑ w : Traj N k T, pathProb M πa πd s0 w) =
        ∑ p : Fin N × (Fin T → Round N k),
          pathProb M πa πd s0 (trajRoundEquiv.symm p) := by
      exact Fintype.sum_equiv trajRoundEquiv _ _ (fun w => by simp)
    _ = ∑ s : Fin N, ∑ z : Fin T → Round N k,
          pathProb M πa πd s0 (trajFromRounds s z) := by
      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
      rfl
    _ = ∑ z : Fin T → Round N k,
          pathProb M πa πd s0 (trajFromRounds s0 z) := by
      apply Fintype.sum_eq_single s0
      intro s hs
      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
      intro z _
      simp [pathProb, trajFromRounds, hs]
    _ = ∑ z : Fin T → Round N k,
          depWeight (roundKernel M πa πd s0) z := by
      apply Fintype.sum_congr
      exact fun z => pathProb_trajFromRounds M πa πd s0 z
    _ = 1 := depWeight_sum_eq_one _
      (roundKernel_sum_eq_one M πa πd s0 hPsum hasum hdsum)

theorem simulation_lemma
    (hN : 0 < N) (hk : 0 < k) (hT : 0 < T) (Rmax ε : ℝ) (hRmax : 0 < Rmax) (hε : 0 < ε)
    (M Mbar : SG N k)

    (hMP0 : ∀ s a a' t, 0 ≤ M.P s a a' t)
    (hMPsum : ∀ s a a', ∑ t, M.P s a a' t = 1)

    (hMbarP0 : ∀ s a a' t, 0 ≤ Mbar.P s a a' t)
    (hMbarPsum : ∀ s a a', ∑ t, Mbar.P s a a' t = 1)

    (hR0 : ∀ s a a', 0 ≤ M.R s a a')
    (hRle : ∀ s a a', M.R s a a' ≤ Rmax)

    (πa πd : Policy N k T)
    (ha0 : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πa i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hasum : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πa i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (hd0 : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πd i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hdsum : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πd i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (s0 : Fin N)

    (happrox : Approximates Mbar M (ε / ((N : ℝ) * (T : ℝ) * Rmax))) :
    |U Mbar πa πd s0 - U M πa πd s0| ≤ ε := by
  have hNc : 0 < (N : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hN
  have hTc : 0 < (T : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hT
  have hden : 0 < (N : ℝ) * (T : ℝ) * Rmax :=
    mul_pos (mul_pos hNc hTc) hRmax
  have hα : 0 ≤ ε / ((N : ℝ) * (T : ℝ) * Rmax) :=
    (div_pos hε hden).le
  have hdist := model_path_l1_bound
    (ε / ((N : ℝ) * (T : ℝ) * Rmax)) hα M Mbar
    hMP0 hMPsum hMbarP0 hMbarPsum πa πd ha0 hasum hd0 hdsum s0 happrox
  unfold U
  simp_rw [pathPayoff_eq_of_reward_eq M Mbar happrox.2]
  rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
  calc
    |∑ w : Traj N k T,
        (pathProb Mbar πa πd s0 w * pathPayoff M w -
          pathProb M πa πd s0 w * pathPayoff M w)| ≤
        ∑ w : Traj N k T,
          |pathProb Mbar πa πd s0 w * pathPayoff M w -
            pathProb M πa πd s0 w * pathPayoff M w| := by
      exact Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
    _ = ∑ w : Traj N k T,
        |pathProb Mbar πa πd s0 w - pathProb M πa πd s0 w| *
          |pathPayoff M w| := by
      apply Fintype.sum_congr
      intro w
      rw [← sub_mul, abs_mul]
    _ ≤ ∑ w : Traj N k T,
        |pathProb Mbar πa πd s0 w - pathProb M πa πd s0 w| * Rmax := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro w _
      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (abs_pathPayoff_le hT Rmax M hR0 hRle w)
        (abs_nonneg _)
    _ = (∑ w : Traj N k T,
        |pathProb Mbar πa πd s0 w - pathProb M πa πd s0 w|) * Rmax := by
      rw [Finset.sum_mul]
    _ ≤ ((N : ℝ) * (T : ℝ) *
        (ε / ((N : ℝ) * (T : ℝ) * Rmax))) * Rmax :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hdist hRmax.le
    _ = ε := by field_simp

theorem path_dist_l1_bound
    (hN : 0 < N) (hk : 0 < k) (hT : 0 < T) (α : ℝ) (hα : 0 ≤ α)
    (M Mbar : SG N k)
    (Rmax : ℝ) (hRmax : 0 < Rmax)
    (hR0 : ∀ s a a', 0 ≤ M.R s a a')
    (hRle : ∀ s a a', M.R s a a' ≤ Rmax)
    (hMP0 : ∀ s a a' t, 0 ≤ M.P s a a' t)
    (hMPsum : ∀ s a a', ∑ t, M.P s a a' t = 1)
    (hMbarP0 : ∀ s a a' t, 0 ≤ Mbar.P s a a' t)
    (hMbarPsum : ∀ s a a', ∑ t, Mbar.P s a a' t = 1)
    (πa πd : Policy N k T)
    (ha0 : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πa i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hasum : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πa i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (hd0 : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πd i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hdsum : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πd i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (s0 : Fin N)
    (happrox : Approximates Mbar M α) :
    ∑ w : Traj N k T,
        |pathProb Mbar πa πd s0 w - pathProb M πa πd s0 w|
      ≤ (N : ℝ) * (T : ℝ) * α := by
  rw [path_l1_eq_depWeight M Mbar πa πd s0]
  calc
    (∑ z : Fin T → Round N k,
        |depWeight (roundKernel Mbar πa πd s0) z -
          depWeight (roundKernel M πa πd s0) z|)
        ≤ (T : ℝ) * ((N : ℝ) * α) :=
      depWeight_l1_bound ((N : ℝ) * α) (mul_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg N) hα)
        (roundKernel Mbar πa πd s0) (roundKernel M πa πd s0)
        (roundKernel_nonneg Mbar πa πd s0 hMbarP0 ha0 hd0)
        (roundKernel_nonneg M πa πd s0 hMP0 ha0 hd0)
        (roundKernel_sum_eq_one Mbar πa πd s0 hMbarPsum hasum hdsum)
        (roundKernel_sum_eq_one M πa πd s0 hMPsum hasum hdsum)
        (roundKernel_l1_bound α hα M Mbar πa πd s0 ha0 hd0 hasum hdsum happrox)
    _ = (N : ℝ) * (T : ℝ) * α := by ring

private def liftedSG (M : SG N k) (Rmax : ℝ) : SG (N + 1) k where
  P := fun s a a' t =>
    if hs : (s : ℕ) < N then
      if ht : (t : ℕ) < N then M.P ⟨s, hs⟩ a a' ⟨t, ht⟩ else 0
    else if t = Fin.last N then 1 else 0
  R := fun s a a' =>
    if hs : (s : ℕ) < N then M.R ⟨s, hs⟩ a a' else Rmax

private theorem liftedSG_P_nonneg (M : SG N k) (Rmax : ℝ)
    (hP0 : ∀ s a a' t, 0 ≤ M.P s a a' t) :
    ∀ s a a' t, 0 ≤ (liftedSG M Rmax).P s a a' t := by
  intro s a a' t
  simp only [liftedSG]
  split_ifs <;> try positivity
  exact hP0 _ _ _ _

private theorem liftedSG_P_sum (M : SG N k) (Rmax : ℝ)
    (hPsum : ∀ s a a', ∑ t, M.P s a a' t = 1) :
    ∀ s a a', ∑ t, (liftedSG M Rmax).P s a a' t = 1 := by
  intro s a a'
  rw [Fin.sum_univ_castSucc]
  by_cases hs : (s : ℕ) < N
  · simp [liftedSG, hs, hPsum]
  · have hslast : s = Fin.last N := by
      apply Fin.ext
      simp
      omega
    subst s
    simp [liftedSG]

private theorem inducedSG_P_nonneg (L : UnknownSet N k) (M : SG N k) (Rmax : ℝ)
    (hP0 : ∀ s a a' t, 0 ≤ M.P s a a' t) :
    ∀ s a a' t, 0 ≤ (inducedSG M L Rmax).P s a a' t := by
  intro s a a' t
  simp only [inducedSG]
  split_ifs <;> try positivity
  exact hP0 _ _ _ _

private theorem inducedSG_P_sum (L : UnknownSet N k) (M : SG N k) (Rmax : ℝ)
    (hPsum : ∀ s a a', ∑ t, M.P s a a' t = 1) :
    ∀ s a a', ∑ t, (inducedSG M L Rmax).P s a a' t = 1 := by
  intro s a a'
  rw [Fin.sum_univ_castSucc]
  by_cases hs : (s : ℕ) < N
  · by_cases hL : (⟨s, hs⟩, a, a') ∈ L
    · simp [inducedSG, hs, hL]
    · simp [inducedSG, hs, hL, hPsum]
  · have hslast : s = Fin.last N := by
      apply Fin.ext
      simp
      omega
    subst s
    simp [inducedSG]

private theorem liftedSG_R_bounds (M : SG N k) (Rmax : ℝ) (hRmax : 0 ≤ Rmax)
    (hR0 : ∀ s a a', 0 ≤ M.R s a a')
    (hRle : ∀ s a a', M.R s a a' ≤ Rmax) :
    (∀ s a a', 0 ≤ (liftedSG M Rmax).R s a a') ∧
      ∀ s a a', (liftedSG M Rmax).R s a a' ≤ Rmax := by
  constructor <;> intro s a a' <;> simp only [liftedSG] <;> split_ifs
  · exact hR0 _ _ _
  · exact hRmax
  · exact hRle _ _ _
  · exact le_rfl

private theorem inducedSG_R_bounds (L : UnknownSet N k) (M : SG N k) (Rmax : ℝ)
    (hRmax : 0 ≤ Rmax) (hR0 : ∀ s a a', 0 ≤ M.R s a a')
    (hRle : ∀ s a a', M.R s a a' ≤ Rmax) :
    (∀ s a a', 0 ≤ (inducedSG M L Rmax).R s a a') ∧
      ∀ s a a', (inducedSG M L Rmax).R s a a' ≤ Rmax := by
  constructor <;> intro s a a' <;> simp only [inducedSG] <;> split_ifs
  · exact hRmax
  · exact hR0 _ _ _
  · exact hRmax
  · exact le_rfl
  · exact hRle _ _ _
  · exact le_rfl

private def extBad (L : UnknownSet N k) (w : Traj (N + 1) k T) : Prop :=
  (∃ (i : Fin T) (s : Fin N),
      w.1 i.castSucc = s.castSucc ∧ (s, w.2.1 i, w.2.2 i) ∈ L) ∨
    ∃ j : Fin (T + 1), w.1 j = Fin.last N

private theorem not_extBad_state_embedded {L : UnknownSet N k}
    {w : Traj (N + 1) k T} (hgood : ¬ extBad L w) (j : Fin (T + 1)) :
    ∃ s : Fin N, w.1 j = s.castSucc := by
  have hne : w.1 j ≠ Fin.last N := by
    intro heq
    exact hgood (Or.inr ⟨j, heq⟩)
  have hslt : (w.1 j : ℕ) < N := by
    by_contra hn
    apply hne
    apply Fin.ext
    simp
    omega
  exact ⟨⟨w.1 j, hslt⟩, Fin.ext rfl⟩

private theorem not_extBad_not_mem {L : UnknownSet N k}
    {w : Traj (N + 1) k T} (hgood : ¬ extBad L w) (i : Fin T)
    (s : Fin N) (hs : w.1 i.castSucc = s.castSucc) :
    (s, w.2.1 i, w.2.2 i) ∉ L := by
  intro hmem
  exact hgood (Or.inl ⟨i, s, hs, hmem⟩)

private theorem induced_lift_R_eq_of_not_bad
    (L : UnknownSet N k) (M : SG N k) (Rmax : ℝ)
    (w : Traj (N + 1) k T) (hgood : ¬ extBad L w) (i : Fin T) :
    (inducedSG M L Rmax).R (w.1 i.castSucc) (w.2.1 i) (w.2.2 i) =
      (liftedSG M Rmax).R (w.1 i.castSucc) (w.2.1 i) (w.2.2 i) := by
  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := not_extBad_state_embedded hgood i.castSucc
  have hmem := not_extBad_not_mem hgood i s hs
  rw [hs]
  simp [inducedSG, liftedSG, hmem]

private theorem induced_lift_P_eq_of_not_bad
    (L : UnknownSet N k) (M : SG N k) (Rmax : ℝ)
    (w : Traj (N + 1) k T) (hgood : ¬ extBad L w) (i : Fin T) :
    (inducedSG M L Rmax).P (w.1 i.castSucc) (w.2.1 i) (w.2.2 i) (w.1 i.succ) =
      (liftedSG M Rmax).P (w.1 i.castSucc) (w.2.1 i) (w.2.2 i) (w.1 i.succ) := by
  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := not_extBad_state_embedded hgood i.castSucc
  have hmem := not_extBad_not_mem hgood i s hs
  rw [hs]
  simp [inducedSG, liftedSG, hmem]

private theorem induced_lift_rewardHist_eq_of_not_bad
    (L : UnknownSet N k) (M : SG N k) (Rmax : ℝ)
    (w : Traj (N + 1) k T) (hgood : ¬ extBad L w) (i : Fin T) :
    rewardHist (inducedSG M L Rmax) w i = rewardHist (liftedSG M Rmax) w i := by
  funext j
  exact induced_lift_R_eq_of_not_bad L M Rmax w hgood
    (Fin.castLE (by have := i.isLt; omega) j)

private theorem induced_lift_pathProb_eq_of_not_bad
    (L : UnknownSet N k) (M : SG N k) (Rmax : ℝ)
    (πa' πd' : Policy (N + 1) k T) (s0 : Fin N)
    (w : Traj (N + 1) k T) (hgood : ¬ extBad L w) :
    pathProb (inducedSG M L Rmax) πa' πd' s0.castSucc w =
      pathProb (liftedSG M Rmax) πa' πd' s0.castSucc w := by
  unfold pathProb
  congr 1
  apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
  intro i _
  rw [induced_lift_rewardHist_eq_of_not_bad L M Rmax w hgood i,
    induced_lift_P_eq_of_not_bad L M Rmax w hgood i]

private theorem induced_lift_pathPayoff_eq_of_not_bad
    (L : UnknownSet N k) (M : SG N k) (Rmax : ℝ)
    (w : Traj (N + 1) k T) (hgood : ¬ extBad L w) :
    pathPayoff (inducedSG M L Rmax) w = pathPayoff (liftedSG M Rmax) w := by
  unfold pathPayoff
  congr 1
  apply Fintype.sum_congr
  exact fun i => induced_lift_R_eq_of_not_bad L M Rmax w hgood i

private theorem pathPayoff_nonneg (hT : 0 < T) (M : SG N k)
    (hR0 : ∀ s a a', 0 ≤ M.R s a a') (w : Traj N k T) :
    0 ≤ pathPayoff M w := by
  unfold pathPayoff
  exact mul_nonneg (by positivity) (Finset.sum_nonneg fun i _ => hR0 _ _ _)

private theorem expectation_diff_le_bad
    {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] (bad : Ω → Prop) [DecidablePred bad]
    (Rmax : ℝ) (p p' q q' : Ω → ℝ)
    (hp0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ p x) (hp'0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ p' x)
    (hpsum : ∑ x, p x = 1) (hp'sum : ∑ x, p' x = 1)
    (hq0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ q x) (hqle : ∀ x, q x ≤ Rmax)
    (hq'0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ q' x) (hq'le : ∀ x, q' x ≤ Rmax)
    (hgoodp : ∀ x, ¬ bad x → p' x = p x)
    (hgoodq : ∀ x, ¬ bad x → q' x = q x) :
    |(∑ x, p' x * q' x) - ∑ x, p x * q x| ≤
      Rmax * ∑ x, if bad x then p x else 0 := by
  let bp : ℝ := ∑ x, if bad x then p x else 0
  let bp' : ℝ := ∑ x, if bad x then p' x else 0
  let gp : ℝ := ∑ x, if bad x then 0 else p x
  let gp' : ℝ := ∑ x, if bad x then 0 else p' x
  let be : ℝ := ∑ x, if bad x then p x * q x else 0
  let be' : ℝ := ∑ x, if bad x then p' x * q' x else 0
  let ge : ℝ := ∑ x, if bad x then 0 else p x * q x
  let ge' : ℝ := ∑ x, if bad x then 0 else p' x * q' x
  have hp_split : bp + gp = 1 := by
    rw [← hpsum]
    simp only [bp, gp, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    apply Fintype.sum_congr
    intro x
    by_cases hx : bad x <;> simp [hx]
  have hp'_split : bp' + gp' = 1 := by
    rw [← hp'sum]
    simp only [bp', gp', ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    apply Fintype.sum_congr
    intro x
    by_cases hx : bad x <;> simp [hx]
  have hgp : gp' = gp := by
    apply Fintype.sum_congr
    intro x
    by_cases hx : bad x
    · simp [gp', gp, hx]
    · simp [gp', gp, hx, hgoodp x hx]
  have hbp : bp' = bp := by linarith
  have hge : ge' = ge := by
    apply Fintype.sum_congr
    intro x
    by_cases hx : bad x
    · simp [ge', ge, hx]
    · simp [ge', ge, hx, hgoodp x hx, hgoodq x hx]
  have he_split : (∑ x, p x * q x) = be + ge := by
    simp only [be, ge, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    apply Fintype.sum_congr
    intro x
    by_cases hx : bad x <;> simp [hx]
  have he'_split : (∑ x, p' x * q' x) = be' + ge' := by
    simp only [be', ge', ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    apply Fintype.sum_congr
    intro x
    by_cases hx : bad x <;> simp [hx]
  have hbp0 : 0 ≤ bp := by
    apply Finset.sum_nonneg
    intro x _
    by_cases hx : bad x <;> simp [bp, hx, hp0 x]
  have hbp'0 : 0 ≤ bp' := by rw [hbp]; exact hbp0
  have hbe0 : 0 ≤ be := by
    apply Finset.sum_nonneg
    intro x _
    by_cases hx : bad x <;> simp [be, hx, mul_nonneg (hp0 x) (hq0 x)]
  have hbe'0 : 0 ≤ be' := by
    apply Finset.sum_nonneg
    intro x _
    by_cases hx : bad x <;> simp [be', hx, mul_nonneg (hp'0 x) (hq'0 x)]
  have hbe_le : be ≤ Rmax * bp := by
    calc
      be ≤ ∑ x, if bad x then p x * Rmax else 0 := by
        apply Finset.sum_le_sum
        intro x _
        by_cases hx : bad x
        · simp only [be, hx, if_true]
          exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hqle x) (hp0 x)
        · simp [be, hx]
      _ = Rmax * bp := by
        simp only [bp]
        rw [Finset.mul_sum]
        apply Fintype.sum_congr
        intro x
        by_cases hx : bad x <;> simp [hx] <;> ring
  have hbe'_le : be' ≤ Rmax * bp := by
    calc
      be' ≤ ∑ x, if bad x then p' x * Rmax else 0 := by
        apply Finset.sum_le_sum
        intro x _
        by_cases hx : bad x
        · simp only [be', hx, if_true]
          exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hq'le x) (hp'0 x)
        · simp [be', hx]
      _ = Rmax * bp' := by
        simp only [bp']
        rw [Finset.mul_sum]
        apply Fintype.sum_congr
        intro x
        by_cases hx : bad x <;> simp [hx] <;> ring
      _ = Rmax * bp := by rw [hbp]
  rw [he'_split, he_split, hge]
  rw [show be' + ge - (be + ge) = be' - be by ring]
  apply abs_sub_le_iff.mpr
  constructor
  · exact (sub_le_self _ hbe0).trans hbe'_le
  · exact (sub_le_self _ hbe'0).trans hbe_le

private def embedTraj (w : Traj N k T) : Traj (N + 1) k T :=
  (fun j => (w.1 j).castSucc, w.2.1, w.2.2)

private theorem stateHist_embedTraj (w : Traj N k T) (i : Fin T) :
    stateHist (embedTraj w) i = fun j => (stateHist w i j).castSucc := by
  rfl

private theorem agentHist_embedTraj (w : Traj N k T) (i : Fin T) :
    agentHist (embedTraj w) i = agentHist w i := by
  rfl

private theorem advHist_embedTraj (w : Traj N k T) (i : Fin T) :
    advHist (embedTraj w) i = advHist w i := by
  rfl

private theorem lifted_rewardHist_embedTraj (M : SG N k) (Rmax : ℝ)
    (w : Traj N k T) (i : Fin T) :
    rewardHist (liftedSG M Rmax) (embedTraj w) i = rewardHist M w i := by
  funext j
  simp [rewardHist, embedTraj, liftedSG]

private theorem lifted_pathProb_embedTraj
    (M : SG N k) (Rmax : ℝ) (πa πd : Policy N k T)
    (πa' πd' : Policy (N + 1) k T)
    (hπa : ∀ (i : Fin T) (hs : Fin (i.val + 1) → Fin N) ha hd hr a,
      πa' i (fun j => (hs j).castSucc) ha hd hr a = πa i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hπd : ∀ (i : Fin T) (hs : Fin (i.val + 1) → Fin N) ha hd hr a,
      πd' i (fun j => (hs j).castSucc) ha hd hr a = πd i hs ha hd hr a)
    (s0 : Fin N) (w : Traj N k T) :
    pathProb (liftedSG M Rmax) πa' πd' s0.castSucc (embedTraj w) =
      pathProb M πa πd s0 w := by
  unfold pathProb
  have hinit : ((embedTraj w).1 0 = s0.castSucc) ↔ w.1 0 = s0 := by
    simp [embedTraj]
  rw [if_congr hinit rfl rfl]
  congr 1
  apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
  intro i _
  rw [stateHist_embedTraj, agentHist_embedTraj, advHist_embedTraj,
    lifted_rewardHist_embedTraj]
  rw [hπa, hπd]
  simp [embedTraj, liftedSG]

private theorem lifted_pathPayoff_embedTraj (M : SG N k) (Rmax : ℝ)
    (w : Traj N k T) :
    pathPayoff (liftedSG M Rmax) (embedTraj w) = pathPayoff M w := by
  unfold pathPayoff
  congr 1
  apply Fintype.sum_congr
  intro i
  simp [embedTraj, liftedSG]

private theorem extBad_embedTraj_iff (L : UnknownSet N k) (w : Traj N k T) :
    extBad L (embedTraj w) ↔
      ∃ i : Fin T, (w.1 i.castSucc, w.2.1 i, w.2.2 i) ∈ L := by
  simp only [extBad, embedTraj]
  constructor
  · rintro (⟨i, s, hs, hmem⟩ | ⟨j, hj⟩)
    · have hstate : w.1 i.castSucc = s := Fin.castSucc_inj.mp hs
      subst s
      exact ⟨i, hmem⟩
    · exact False.elim (Fin.castSucc_ne_last _ hj)
  · rintro ⟨i, hmem⟩
    exact Or.inl ⟨i, w.1 i.castSucc, rfl, hmem⟩

private def allEmbedded (w : Traj (N + 1) k T) : Prop :=
  ∀ j : Fin (T + 1), w.1 j ≠ Fin.last N

private def embedTrajEquiv :
    Traj N k T ≃ {w : Traj (N + 1) k T // allEmbedded w} where
  toFun w := ⟨embedTraj w, by
    intro j
    simp [embedTraj]⟩
  invFun w :=
    (fun j => ⟨w.1.1 j, Fin.val_lt_last (w.2 j)⟩, w.1.2.1, w.1.2.2)
  left_inv w := by
    apply Prod.ext
    · funext j
      apply Fin.ext
      rfl
    · rfl
  right_inv w := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    apply Prod.ext
    · funext j
      apply Fin.ext
      rfl
    · rfl

private theorem exists_step_to_last
    (st : Fin (T + 1) → Fin (N + 1))
    (h0 : st 0 ≠ Fin.last N) (hex : ∃ j, st j = Fin.last N) :
    ∃ i : Fin T, st i.castSucc ≠ Fin.last N ∧ st i.succ = Fin.last N := by
  let P : ℕ → Prop := fun n => ∃ hn : n < T + 1, st ⟨n, hn⟩ = Fin.last N
  have hP : ∃ n, P n := by
    obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hex
    exact ⟨j.val, j.isLt, hj⟩
  let m := Nat.find hP
  obtain ⟨hmT, hmstate⟩ := Nat.find_spec hP
  change m < T + 1 at hmT
  change st ⟨m, hmT⟩ = Fin.last N at hmstate
  have hm0 : m ≠ 0 := by
    intro heq
    apply h0
    have hidx : (⟨m, hmT⟩ : Fin (T + 1)) = 0 := by
      apply Fin.ext
      simp [heq]
    rw [← hidx]
    exact hmstate
  have hmpos : 0 < m := Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hm0
  have himT : m - 1 < T := by omega
  let i : Fin T := ⟨m - 1, himT⟩
  refine ⟨i, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro hprev
    have hprevP : P (m - 1) := by
      refine ⟨by omega, ?_⟩
      have hidx : (⟨m - 1, by omega⟩ : Fin (T + 1)) = i.castSucc := by
        apply Fin.ext
        rfl
      simpa [hidx] using hprev
    exact (Nat.find_min hP (by omega)) hprevP
  · have hidx : i.succ = (⟨m, hmT⟩ : Fin (T + 1)) := by
      apply Fin.ext
      simp [i]
      omega
    rw [hidx]
    exact hmstate

private theorem lifted_pathProb_zero_of_not_allEmbedded
    (M : SG N k) (Rmax : ℝ) (πa' πd' : Policy (N + 1) k T)
    (s0 : Fin N) (w : Traj (N + 1) k T) (hnot : ¬ allEmbedded w) :
    pathProb (liftedSG M Rmax) πa' πd' s0.castSucc w = 0 := by
  by_cases hinit : w.1 0 = s0.castSucc
  · have h0 : w.1 0 ≠ Fin.last N := by
      rw [hinit]
      exact Fin.castSucc_ne_last _
    have hex : ∃ j, w.1 j = Fin.last N := by
      simpa [allEmbedded] using hnot
    obtain ⟨i, hi, hinext⟩ := exists_step_to_last w.1 h0 hex
    have his : (w.1 i.castSucc : ℕ) < N := Fin.val_lt_last hi
    unfold pathProb
    rw [if_pos hinit, one_mul]
    apply Finset.prod_eq_zero (Finset.mem_univ i)
    rw [hinext]
    simp [liftedSG, his]
  · simp [pathProb, hinit]

private theorem sum_over_extended_eq_sum_embed
    (F : Traj (N + 1) k T → ℝ)
    (hzero : ∀ w, ¬ allEmbedded w → F w = 0) :
    (∑ w : Traj (N + 1) k T, F w) = ∑ w : Traj N k T, F (embedTraj w) := by
  classical
  calc
    (∑ w : Traj (N + 1) k T, F w) =
        ∑ w : Traj (N + 1) k T, if allEmbedded w then F w else 0 := by
      apply Fintype.sum_congr
      intro w
      by_cases hw : allEmbedded w
      · simp [hw]
      · simp [hw, hzero w hw]
    _ = ∑ w ∈ (Finset.univ.filter allEmbedded), F w := by
      rw [Finset.sum_filter]
    _ = ∑ w : {w : Traj (N + 1) k T // allEmbedded w}, F w := by
      exact Finset.sum_subtype _ (by simp) F
    _ = ∑ w : Traj N k T, F (embedTraj w) := by
      exact (Fintype.sum_equiv embedTrajEquiv
        (fun w => F (embedTraj w)) (fun w => F w.1) (fun w => rfl)).symm

private noncomputable def cutOn (p : Prop) (x : ℝ) : ℝ := by
  classical
  exact if p then x else 0

private theorem lifted_U_eq_original
    (M : SG N k) (Rmax : ℝ) (πa πd : Policy N k T)
    (πa' πd' : Policy (N + 1) k T)
    (hπa : ∀ (i : Fin T) (hs : Fin (i.val + 1) → Fin N) ha hd hr a,
      πa' i (fun j => (hs j).castSucc) ha hd hr a = πa i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hπd : ∀ (i : Fin T) (hs : Fin (i.val + 1) → Fin N) ha hd hr a,
      πd' i (fun j => (hs j).castSucc) ha hd hr a = πd i hs ha hd hr a)
    (s0 : Fin N) :
    U (liftedSG M Rmax) πa' πd' s0.castSucc = U M πa πd s0 := by
  unfold U
  rw [sum_over_extended_eq_sum_embed]
  · apply Fintype.sum_congr
    intro w
    rw [lifted_pathProb_embedTraj M Rmax πa πd πa' πd' hπa hπd s0 w,
      lifted_pathPayoff_embedTraj]
  · intro w hw
    rw [lifted_pathProb_zero_of_not_allEmbedded M Rmax πa' πd' s0 w hw]
    simp

private theorem lifted_bad_mass_eq_escapeProb
    (L : UnknownSet N k) (M : SG N k) (Rmax : ℝ)
    (πa πd : Policy N k T) (πa' πd' : Policy (N + 1) k T)
    (hπa : ∀ (i : Fin T) (hs : Fin (i.val + 1) → Fin N) ha hd hr a,
      πa' i (fun j => (hs j).castSucc) ha hd hr a = πa i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hπd : ∀ (i : Fin T) (hs : Fin (i.val + 1) → Fin N) ha hd hr a,
      πd' i (fun j => (hs j).castSucc) ha hd hr a = πd i hs ha hd hr a)
    (s0 : Fin N) :
    (∑ w : Traj (N + 1) k T,
      cutOn (extBad L w) (pathProb (liftedSG M Rmax) πa' πd' s0.castSucc w)) =
        escapeProb L M πa πd s0 := by
  classical
  unfold escapeProb
  rw [sum_over_extended_eq_sum_embed]
  · apply Fintype.sum_congr
    intro w
    simp only [cutOn]
    rw [lifted_pathProb_embedTraj M Rmax πa πd πa' πd' hπa hπd s0 w]
    rw [if_congr (extBad_embedTraj_iff L w) rfl rfl]
  · intro w hw
    simp only [cutOn]
    rw [lifted_pathProb_zero_of_not_allEmbedded M Rmax πa' πd' s0 w hw]
    split_ifs <;> rfl

theorem value_diff_escape_bound
    (hN : 0 < N) (hk : 0 < k) (hT : 0 < T) (Rmax : ℝ) (hRmax : 0 < Rmax)
    (L : UnknownSet N k) (M : SG N k)
    (hMP0 : ∀ s a a' t, 0 ≤ M.P s a a' t)
    (hMPsum : ∀ s a a', ∑ t, M.P s a a' t = 1)
    (hR0 : ∀ s a a', 0 ≤ M.R s a a') (hRle : ∀ s a a', M.R s a a' ≤ Rmax)
    (πa πd : Policy N k T)
    (ha0 : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πa i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hasum : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πa i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (hd0 : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πd i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hdsum : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πd i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (πa' πd' : Policy (N + 1) k T)
    (ha0' : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πa' i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hasum' : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πa' i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (hd0' : ∀ i hs ha hd hr a, 0 ≤ πd' i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hdsum' : ∀ i hs ha hd hr, ∑ a, πd' i hs ha hd hr a = 1)
    (hπa : ∀ (i : Fin T) (hs : Fin (i.val + 1) → Fin N) ha hd hr a,
      πa' i (fun j => (hs j).castSucc) ha hd hr a = πa i hs ha hd hr a)
    (hπd : ∀ (i : Fin T) (hs : Fin (i.val + 1) → Fin N) ha hd hr a,
      πd' i (fun j => (hs j).castSucc) ha hd hr a = πd i hs ha hd hr a)
    (s0 : Fin N) :
    |U (inducedSG M L Rmax) πa' πd' (Fin.castSucc s0) - U M πa πd s0|
      ≤ Rmax * escapeProb L M πa πd s0 := by
  classical
  have hLiftP0 := liftedSG_P_nonneg M Rmax hMP0
  have hLiftPsum := liftedSG_P_sum M Rmax hMPsum
  have hIndP0 := inducedSG_P_nonneg L M Rmax hMP0
  have hIndPsum := inducedSG_P_sum L M Rmax hMPsum
  have hLiftR := liftedSG_R_bounds M Rmax hRmax.le hR0 hRle
  have hIndR := inducedSG_R_bounds L M Rmax hRmax.le hR0 hRle
  have hbound := expectation_diff_le_bad (extBad L) Rmax
    (fun w : Traj (N + 1) k T =>
      pathProb (liftedSG M Rmax) πa' πd' s0.castSucc w)
    (fun w : Traj (N + 1) k T =>
      pathProb (inducedSG M L Rmax) πa' πd' s0.castSucc w)
    (fun w : Traj (N + 1) k T => pathPayoff (liftedSG M Rmax) w)
    (fun w : Traj (N + 1) k T => pathPayoff (inducedSG M L Rmax) w)
    (fun w => pathProb_nonneg (liftedSG M Rmax) πa' πd' s0.castSucc
      hLiftP0 ha0' hd0' w)
    (fun w => pathProb_nonneg (inducedSG M L Rmax) πa' πd' s0.castSucc
      hIndP0 ha0' hd0' w)
    (pathProb_sum_eq_one (liftedSG M Rmax) πa' πd' s0.castSucc
      hLiftPsum hasum' hdsum')
    (pathProb_sum_eq_one (inducedSG M L Rmax) πa' πd' s0.castSucc
      hIndPsum hasum' hdsum')
    (fun w => pathPayoff_nonneg hT (liftedSG M Rmax) hLiftR.1 w)
    (fun w => (le_abs_self _).trans
      (abs_pathPayoff_le hT Rmax (liftedSG M Rmax) hLiftR.1 hLiftR.2 w))
    (fun w => pathPayoff_nonneg hT (inducedSG M L Rmax) hIndR.1 w)
    (fun w => (le_abs_self _).trans
      (abs_pathPayoff_le hT Rmax (inducedSG M L Rmax) hIndR.1 hIndR.2 w))
    (fun w hw => induced_lift_pathProb_eq_of_not_bad L M Rmax πa' πd' s0 w hw)
    (fun w hw => induced_lift_pathPayoff_eq_of_not_bad L M Rmax w hw)
  calc
    |U (inducedSG M L Rmax) πa' πd' s0.castSucc - U M πa πd s0| =
        |U (inducedSG M L Rmax) πa' πd' s0.castSucc -
          U (liftedSG M Rmax) πa' πd' s0.castSucc| := by
      rw [lifted_U_eq_original M Rmax πa πd πa' πd' hπa hπd s0]
    _ ≤ Rmax * (∑ w : Traj (N + 1) k T,
        cutOn (extBad L w)
          (pathProb (liftedSG M Rmax) πa' πd' s0.castSucc w)) := by
      simpa only [U, cutOn] using hbound
    _ = Rmax * escapeProb L M πa πd s0 := by
      rw [lifted_bad_mass_eq_escapeProb L M Rmax πa πd πa' πd' hπa hπd s0]
end ResearchLevel

targets.label: Proposition 4
targets.statement:
Proposition 4 For any distribution D, there exist a majority vote $B_{Q}$ such that

$$
R_{D}(B_{Q})\leq\mathcal{C}_{Q}^{D}=\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}\left(\underset{y\sim D_{\mathcal{Y}|x}}{\mathbf{Var}}(y)\right).
$$

Moreover, there is no majority vote which can produce a lower C-bound.

targets.label: Proposition 3
targets.statement:
Proposition 3 (Proposition 15 in Germain et al. (2015) corrected) For any countable set of voters $\mathcal{H}$, any distribution Q on ${\mathcal{H}},$ and any distribution D on $\mathcal{X}\times\{-1,1\}$ such that there exists a function $g:\mathcal{X}\to\{-1,1\}$ for which $y=g(x)$ and $yf(x)>0$ for all $(x,y)\sim D$ and $f \in \mathcal H$ , we have

$$
\mathbf{Var}(M_{Q}^{D})\leq\sum_{f\in\mathcal{H}}Q^{2}(f)+\sum_{f_{1}\in\mathcal{H}}\sum_{f_{2}\in\mathcal{H}\atop f_{2}\neq f_{1}}Q(f_{1})Q(f_{2})\mathbf{Cov}_{(x,y)\sim D}(f_{1}(x),f_{2}(x)).
$$

targets.label: Counter-example (Section 4, falsifying Corollary 2)
targets.statement: Counter-example falsifying Corollary 2 (Corollary 16 in Germain et al. 2015). Corollary 2 claimed that for $n$ independent voters under a uniform distribution $Q$, the C-bound satisfies $R_D(B_Q) \le C_Q^D \le 1/(n(1-2 d_Q^D)) = 1/(n(1-2 R_D(G_Q)))$, and thus decreases asymptotically to 0 as $n$ grows. The erratum disproves this with a concrete construction (Section 4): the label $y$ is independent of the input $x$ with $\Pr(y=1)=0.8$ (so $\mathbb{E}[y]=3/5$), and there are $n$ mutually independent deterministic voters $f_1,\dots,f_n$ each with $\Pr(f_i=1)=0.8$ (so $\mathbb{E}[f_i]=3/5$, $\mathbb{E}[f_i^2]=1$, and $\mathbb{E}[f_i f_j]=\mathbb{E}[f_i]\mathbb{E}[f_j]=9/25$ for $i \neq j$), each given uniform weight $Q(f_i)=1/n$, giving the aggregated score $S(x)=(1/n) \sum_i f_i(x)$. For this majority vote the first two margin moments are $\mu_1 = \mathbb{E}[y \cdot S] = (3/5)(3/5) = 9/25$ and $\mu_2 = \mathbb{E}[S^2] = (16+9n)/(25n)$, so the C-bound equals $C_Q^D = 1 - \mu_1^2/\mu_2 = (400 + 144 n)/(400 + 225 n)$. In particular $C_Q^D > 0.64 = 16/25$ for every $n > 0$; hence the C-bound does not tend to 0 as the number of independent voters grows, contradicting Corollary 2 (and therefore Proposition 1).

nl_proof:
### Proof of Proposition 4

Proof Let $h(x)=\mathbf{E}_{y\sim D_{\mathcal{Y}|x}}(y)$ and consider a majority vote $B_{Q}$ defined by a set of voters $\mathcal{H}$ and a distribution $Q$ over this set. The score given to any input x by said majority vote $B_{Q}$ is given by $\textstyle\sum_{f\in{\mathcal{H}}}Q(f)f(x)$ . We first notice that this majority vote is equivalent to a majority vote comprised of a single voter $\begin{array}{r}{k(x)=\sum_{f\in\mathcal{H}}Q(f)f(x)}\end{array}$ as the margin of both majority vote would follow the same distribution. To see this, let $M_{Q^{\prime}}(x,y)$ be the margin function of this new majority vote where $Q^{\prime}$ is a dirac distribution on the single voter $k(x)$. We then have

$$
M_{Q}(x,y)=\underset{f\sim Q}{\mathbf{E}}\left[yf(x)\right]=y\underset{f\sim Q}{\mathbf{E}}\left[f(x)\right]=yk(x)=\underset{k\sim Q^{\prime}}{\mathbf{E}}\left[yk(x)\right]=M_{Q^{\prime}}(x,y).
$$

Since both functions $M_{Q}(x,y)$ and $M_{Q^{\prime}}(x,y)$ are equal for any value $(x,y)$ , both margins $(M_{Q^{\prime}}^{D}$ and $M_{Q}^{D})$ will have the same distribution. We remind that the C-bound can be defined using only the moments of its margin. Therefore, as both majority votes lead to the same margin, they will possess the same C-bound. We therefore adopt this equivalent majority vote which uses a single voter $k(x)$ and the margin $M_{Q}^{D}$ for the remainder of the proof. We then consider the definition of the C-bound and proceed as follows (recall that $y\in\{-1,1\}$ , and therefore $y^{2}=1)$

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\mathcal{C}_{Q}^{D}=1-\frac{\big(\mu_{1}(M_{Q}^{D})\big)^{2}}{\mu_{2}(M_{Q}^{D})}}\\ &{\qquad=1-\frac{\Big(\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}(yk(x))\Big)^{2}}{\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}(y^{2}k(x)^{2})}}\\ &{\qquad=1-\frac{\Big(\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}(k(x)h(x))\Big)^{2}}{\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}(k(x)^{2})}}\\ &{\qquad\geq 1-\frac{\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}(k(x)^{2})\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}(h(x)^{2})}{\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}(k(x)^{2})}}\\ &{\qquad=1-\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}(h(x)^{2}).}\end{array}
$$

The above inequality is given by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. We can easily see that by choosing k such that $k(x)\ =\ h(x)$ for all $x,$ the inequality becomes an equality. This means that the value of the C-bound for a given distribution D is lower-bounded by

$1-\mathbf{E}_{(x,y)\sim D}(h(x)^{2})$ , which is always achievable. We can simplify this expression as follows:

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\mathcal{C}_{Q}^{D}=1-\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}(h(x)^{2})}\\ &{\quad=1-\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}\Big [\Big(\underset{y\sim D_{\mathcal{Y}|x}}{\mathbf{E}}(y)\Big)^{2}\Big]}\\ &{\quad=\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}\Big [1-\Big(\underset{y\sim D_{\mathcal{Y}|x}}{\mathbf{E}}(y)\Big)^{2}\Big]}\\ &{\quad=\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}\Big [\underset{y\sim D_{\mathcal{Y}|x}}{\mathbf{E}}(y^{2})-\Big(\underset{y\sim D_{\mathcal{Y}|x}}{\mathbf{E}}(y)\Big)^{2}\Big]}\\ &{\quad=\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}\Big(\underset{y\sim D_{\mathcal{Y}|x}}{\mathbf{Var}}(y)\Big).}\end{array}
$$

### Proof of Proposition 3

Proof Let $g(x)$ be the labelling function assigning each value x to its true, and noiseless, label $y$ and let $f_{i}(x)$ be any voter taken from $\mathcal{H}$. Since $yf_{i}(x)>0$ for any voter $f_{i}\in \mathcal{H}$ and for any given x, we have that the true labelling function $g(x)$ and the voter $f_{i}(x)$ are of the same sign. Thus, we always have $g(x)f_{i}(x)\geq f_{i}(x)\geq-g(x)f_{i}(x)$ , which gives us the following inequality:

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}\left(g(x)f_{i}(x)\right)\geq\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}\left(f_{i}(x)\right)\geq-\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}\left(g(x)f_{i}(x)\right)}\\ {\iff}&{\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}\left(g(x)f_{i}(x)\right)\geq\left|\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}\left(f_{i}(x)\right)\right|}\\ {\implies}&{\left[\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}\left(g(x)f_{i}(x)\right)\right]^{2}\geq\left[\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}\left(f_{i}(x)\right)\right]^{2}.}\end{array}
$$

Since this inequality is true for each voter in $\mathcal{H}$, we consider the previous inequality using the functions $f_{i}$ and $f_{j}$ . Using the fact that for values $a,b,c,d>0$ we have the implication $a<c,b<d\Rightarrow ab<cd$ , we get the following:

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\left[\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}(g(x)f_{i}(x))\right]^{2}\left[\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}(g(x)f_{j}(x))\right]^{2}\geq\left[\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}(f_{i}(x))\right]^{2}\left[\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}(f_{j}(x))\right]^{2}}\\ &{\implies\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}(g(x)f_{i}(x))\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}(g(x)f_{j}(x))\geq\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}(f_{i}(x))\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}(f_{j}(x)).}\end{array}
$$

Since $g(x)f_{i}(x)>0$ for any x, we have that both terms on the left side of the inequality are positive prior to being squared. Knowing this guarantees that the inequality still holds as we take the square root on both sides. This inequality can then be used as follows:

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{Cov}}(y f_{i}(x),y f_{j}(x))}\\ &{=\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}(y^{2}f_{i}(x)f_{j}(x))-\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}(y f_{i}(x))\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}(y f_{j}(x))}\\ &{=\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}(1 f_{i}(x)f_{j}(x))-\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}(g(x)f_{i}(x))\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}(g(x)f_{j}(x))}\\ &{\leq\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}(f_{i}(x)f_{j}(x))-\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}(f_{i}(x))\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}(f_{j}(x))}\\ &{=\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{Cov}}(f_{i}(x),f_{j}(x))}\\ &{=\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{Cov}}(f_{i}(x),f_{j}(x)).}\end{array}
$$

The last equality only serves to highlight that since y is absent from both $f_{i}(x)$ and $f_{j}(x)$ computing the covariance according to either the joint distribution D or the marginal distribution $D_{\mathcal{X}}$ does not affect the result. We have now proven that under our new set of hypothesis, the inequality $\mathbf{Cov}_{(x,y)\sim D}\left(y f_{1}(x),y f_{2}(x)\right)\le\mathbf{Cov}_{(x,y)\sim D}\left(f_{1}(x),f_{2}(x)\right)$ always stands. We note that the original proof erroneously assumed this to be an equality. Nonetheless, we can apply this new inequality to the original proof as follows:

$$
\begin{array}{r l}{\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{Var}}(M_{Q}(x,y))=\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{Var}}\left(\underset{f\in\mathcal{H}}{\sum}Q(f)y f(x)\right)}&{}\\ &{=\underset{f\in\mathcal{H}}{\sum}Q^{2}(f)\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{Var}}y f(x)+\underset{f_{1}\in\mathcal{H}}{\sum}\underset{f_{2}\in\mathcal{H}\atop f_{2}\neq f_{1}}{\sum}Q(f_{1})Q(f_{2})\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{Cov}}(y f_{1}(x),y f_{2}(x))}\\ &{\leq\underset{f\in\mathcal{H}}{\sum}Q^{2}(f)\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{Var}}y f(x)+\underset{f_{1}\in\mathcal{H}}{\sum}\underset{f_{2}\in\mathcal{H}\atop f_{2}\neq f_{1}}{\sum}Q(f_{1})Q(f_{2})\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{Cov}}(f_{1}(x),f_{2}(x))}\\ &{\leq\underset{f\in\mathcal{H}}{\sum}Q^{2}(f)+\underset{f_{1}\in\mathcal{H}}{\sum}\underset{f_{2}\in\mathcal{H}\atop f_{2}\neq f_{1}}{\sum}Q(f_{1})Q(f_{2})\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{Cov}}(f_{1}(x),f_{2}(x)).}\end{array}
$$

The final inequality is given by the fact that $\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{Var}}{y f(x)}\leq 1$ for all voters $f \in \mathcal H$

### Proof of Counter-example (Section 4, falsifying Corollary 2)

Counter-example. Suppose a binary classification problem where each example $(x,y){\sim}D$ is such that x is drawn from the uniform distribution over a one dimensional input space $\mathcal{X}=[0,1]$ , and the output is either $y = 1$ with probability $p=0.8$ or $y = - 1$ with probability $1-p=0.2$ (that is, y is independent of x). Let us now consider a majority vote classifier made from the set of deterministic voters $\mathcal{H}: =\{f_{i}(x)\}$ for $i\in\{1,2,...,n\}$ such that $f_{i}(x)=1$ if the $i^{t h}$ decimal of x is greater or equal than 2, and $f_{i}(x)= -1$ otherwise. As x follows a uniform distribution over [0, 1], every decimal value will be taken from $0,1,2,...,9$ with probability 0.1 for each value. Furthermore, the value of every decimal positions are independent from one another, rendering the output of each voter mutually independent. Finally, each voter $f_{i}\in \mathcal{H}$ is given an equal weight of $Q(f_{i})=1/n$

According to Corollary 2, this majority vote should yield a C-bound that decreases asymptotically to 0 as the number of voters n increases. Because $R_{D}(B_{Q})\leq\mathcal{C}_{Q}^{D}$ this implies that given a large enough amount of voters, it would be possible to predict with almost certainty the noisy label y, which is uncorrelated to both the input x and the voters. However, this result is clearly incorrect, as there is always a minimal probability of $2/10$ to make a false prediction, i.e., $R_{D}(B_{Q})\geq 0.2$ . Moreover, given the construction of data distribution and the voters, we obtain from the definition of the C-bound $\begin{array}{r}{\mathcal{C}_{Q}^{D}=\frac{400+144n}{400+225n}}\end{array}$ . It is easy to see that the value $\mathcal{C}_{Q}^{D}$ does not go to 0 as n grows as we have $\mathcal{C}_{Q}^{D}>0.64$ for any value $n > 0$ . Thus, the C-bound does not possess the property stated by Corollary 2.

In other words, the result of said corollary is incorrect as we have now given a counterexample. Since the only argument in the demonstration of the corollary is the use of Proposition 1, this implies that Proposition 1 is also incorrect.

context.name: Setup: binary classification, voters, weighted majority vote, Bayes and Gibbs risk (Section 2, eq. 1)
context.statement:
Throughout this paper, we employ the same notation and definitions used by Germain et al. (2015) unless specified otherwise. That is, we consider a binary classification problem in which each example $(x,y)$ consists of an input x and output y belonging to the spaces $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}=\{-1,1\}$ respectively. The examples are sampled i.i.d. according to a true unknown distribution D over $\mathcal{X}\times\{-1,1\}$ . We consider $\mathcal{H}$, a finite set of functions $f:\mathcal{X}\to [-1,1]$. Each such $f$ defines a "voter" in the context of majority vote rules. One may see the output of a given voter $f$ as a measurement of the confidence of the voter toward a given label. For example, say we have two voters $f_{1}(x)=0.1$ and $f_{2}(x)=0.9$ , then both voters lean towards the label 1, but the former less confidently then the latter.

A weighted majority vote is defined by a distribution $Q$ over $\mathcal{H}.$ Such a distribution defines the weight given to each voter, denoted $Q(f)$ , which gives rise to the majority vote classifier $B_{Q}(x)=\mathrm{sgn}\left[\mathbf{E}_{f\sim Q}f(x)\right]$ . This majority vote is also called the Bayes classifier$^{1}$ in the PAC-Bayesian literature, as opposed to the stochastic Gibbs Classifier $G_{Q}$; with $\begin{array}{r}{\operatorname*{Pr}(G_{Q}(x)=y)=\frac{1}{2}(1+y\mathbf{E}_{f\sim Q}f(x))}\end{array}$ for $y\in\{-1,1\}$ . The probability that the majority vote will make an incorrect prediction of the output for a given example drawn from distribution D is called the risk of the majority vote, or Bayes risk$^{2}$, and is denoted $R_{D}(B_{Q})$ :

$$
R_{D}(B_{Q})=\operatorname*{Pr}_{(x,y)\sim D}(B_{Q}(x)\neq y)=\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}I\left(\underset{f\sim Q}{\mathbf{E}}yf(x)\leq 0\right),
$$

where $I(\cdot)$ is the indicator function taking value 0 if the input is false and 1 otherwise. Correspondingly, the probability that the Gibbs classifier makes an error is called the Gibbs risk and is denoted $R_{D}(G_{Q})$ :

$$
R_{D}(G_{Q})=\operatorname*{Pr}_{(x,y)\sim D}(G_{Q}(x)\neq y)=\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\underset{f\sim Q}{\mathbf{E}}yf(x)\right).
$$

context.name: Margin, its moments, and the C-bound (Section 2; Lacasse et al. 2006 / Germain et al. 2015)
context.statement:
The term $\mathbf{E}_{f\sim Q}yf(x)$ shared by both Bayes risk and Gibbs risk definitions is a commonly occurring expression in the context of majority votes. It is referred to as the margin of the majority vote and is denoted $M_{Q}(x,y)$ . Given that $(x,y){\sim}D$ , Germain et al. (2015) study the margin as a random variable which they denote $M_{Q}^{D}$ . A longstanding intermediate result in PAC-Bayes analyses is the factor two bound between the Bayes Risk and the Gibbs risk (Langford and Shawe-Taylor, 2002; McAllester, 2003). That is, for fixed distributions D and $Q$, we have $R_{D}(B_{Q})\leq 2R_{D}(G_{Q})$ . The C-bound (Lacasse et al., 2006; Germain et al., 2015) is a finer upper bound on the Bayes risk and is defined using the variance and first two moments of the margin $M_{Q}^{D}$ (denoted $\mu_{1}(M_{Q}^{D})$ and $\mu_{2}(M_{Q}^{D})$ respectively, with $\mu_{i}(M_{Q}^{D})={\bf E}_{(x,y)\sim D}[M_{Q}(x,y)]^{i})$ . Equivalently, the C-bound can be expressed in terms of the Gibbs risk $R_{D}(G_{Q})$ and the expected disagreement (denoted $d_{Q}^{D}$ and defined below):

$$
R_{D}(B_{Q})\leq{\mathcal C}_{Q}^{D}=\frac{\mathbf{Var}(M_{Q}^{D})}{\mu_{2}(M_{Q}^{D})}=1-\frac{\left(\mu_{1}(M_{Q}^{D})\right)^{2}}{\mu_{2}(M_{Q}^{D})}=1-\frac{(1-2 R_{D}(G_{Q}))^{2}}{1-2 d_{Q}^{D}},
$$

where

$$
\begin{array}{c c}{{\displaystyle\mu_{1}\big(M_{Q}^{D}\big)=\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{E}}\,\underset{f\sim Q}{\mathbf{E}}y f(x),}}&{{\qquad\mu_{2}\big(M_{Q}^{D}\big)=\underset{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}{\mathbf{E}}\left[\underset{f\sim Q}{\mathbf{E}}f(x)\right]^{2},}}\\ {{\displaystyle{\mathbf{Var}\big(M_{Q}^{D}\big)=\mu_{2}\big(M_{Q}^{D}\big)-\big(\mu_{1}\big(M_{Q}^{D}\big)\big)^{2},}}}&{{\qquad d_{Q}^{D}=\frac{1}{2}\left(1-\mu_{2}\big(M_{Q}^{D}\big)\right).}}\end{array}
$$

In these definitions, $D_{\mathcal{X}}$ denotes the marginal distribution on $\mathcal{X}$ for a given distribution $D .^{1}$ We adopt this notation throughout the paper, as well as the use of $D_{\mathcal{Y}| x}$ to denote the conditional distribution on the output space $\mathcal{Y}$ given a fixed input $x \in \mathcal{X}$

context.name: Sources of stochasticity: label noise, stochastic voters, stochastic majority vote (Section 2)
context.statement:
An important note has to be made about the notions of stochasticity and determinism as they appear in the original paper. The generic use of these terms can be confusing to the reader as it is sometimes unclear what is meant to be stochastic or deterministic in some passages. To alleviate this ambiguity we differentiate three distinct sources of stochasticity that are of importance in the studied framework.

Label noise. The stochasticity of the labels arises when for a given value of $x \sim D_{\mathcal{X}}$ , there is a non-zero probability of observing more than one value of $y \sim D_{\mathcal{Y}| x}$.

Stochastic voters. Of note, Germain et al. (2015) introduced voters as functions of the form $f:\mathcal{X}\to [-1,1]$, implying they were deterministic predictors. Nevertheless, the property that a given voter is deterministic remains unused in their analysis of majority votes. We may wish to consider stochastic voters, such as voters for which the output follows some distribution. Say we consider a stochastic voter $f^{*}$ such that for any given input $x,$ the output of the voter is a random variable $f^{*}(x)\sim W_{x}$ , where $W_{x}$ is a distribution over [−1, 1] that depends of the value $x .$ To apply the work of Germain et al. (2015), one needs only to consider $f(x)$ as the expected output of the stochastic voter $f^{*}$ given by $f(x)=\mathbf{E}_{f^{*}(x)\sim W_{x}}~f^{*}(x)$ . Doing so, the value $f(x)$ will be deterministic. Moreover, this is coherent with the idea that $f(x)$ is the confidence of the voter towards a given label. The discussion in this erratum henceforth encompasses both deterministic and stochastic voters and we use the general term voter to refer to voters of both natures.

Stochastic majority vote. We specified that the Bayes classifier $B_{Q}$ is deterministic while the Gibbs classifier $G_{Q}$ is stochastic. This distinction, made by Germain et al. (2015), is meant to distinguish between the stochasticity that arises from sampling a single voter (Gibbs) as opposed to averaging over the value of each voter $f \in \mathcal H$ (Bayes). It is not meant to refer to the nature of the individual voters as we remind that both Germain et al. (2015) and this erratum consider deterministic voters only.

We remind that this erratum is valid when considering the deterministic majority vote classifier that embed the expected value of its voters for the Bayes risk of Equation (1). The interested reader may note that the recent work of Zantedeschi et al. (2021) provide PAC-Bayes bounds for stochastic majority votes where the voters weights are random variables. While this is a related line of work, it differs from ours and Germain et al. (2015) as we only consider majority votes for which the weight of each voter is fixed.

context.name: Proposition 1 (Proposition 15 in Germain et al. 2015; erroneous)
context.statement:
## Erroneous result

Proposition 1 (Proposition 15 in Germain et al. (2015)) For any countable set of voters $\mathcal{H}$, any distribution Q on $\mathcal{H}$, and any distribution D on $\mathcal{X}\times\{-1,1\}$ , we have

$$
\mathbf{Var}(M_{Q}^{D})\leq\sum_{f\in\mathcal{H}}Q^{2}(f)+\sum_{f_{1}\in\mathcal{H}}\sum_{f_{2}\in\mathcal{H}\atop f_{2}\neq f_{1}}Q(f_{1})Q(f_{2})\mathbf{Cov}_{(x,y)\sim D}(f_{1}(x),f_{2}(x)).
$$

context.name: Original proof of Proposition 1 (Germain et al. 2015) and its flaw
context.statement:
Proof We begin with the definition of the margin, which can be seen as a sum of random variables, and develop the variance of the sum into the sum of covariances:

$$
\mathbf{Var}\left(M_{Q}^{D}\right)=\mathbf{Var}_{(x,y)\sim D}\left(M_{Q}(x,y)\right)
$$

$$
=\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{Var}}\left(\sum_{f\in\mathcal{H}}Q(f)y f(x)\right)
$$

$$
\begin{array}{r l}&{=\displaystyle\sum_{f\in\mathcal{H}}Q^{2}(f)\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{Var}}y f(x)+\displaystyle\sum_{f_{1}\in\mathcal{H}}\displaystyle\sum_{f_{2}\in\mathcal{H}\atop f_{2}\neq f_{1}}Q(f_{1})Q(f_{2})\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{Cov}}(y f_{1}(x),y f_{2}(x))}\\ &{=\displaystyle\sum_{f\in\mathcal{H}}Q^{2}(f)\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{Var}}y f(x)+\displaystyle\sum_{f_{1}\in\mathcal{H}}\displaystyle\sum_{f_{2}\in\mathcal{H}\atop f_{2}\neq f_{1}}Q(f_{1})Q(f_{2})\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{Cov}}(f_{1}(x),f_{2}(x))}\\ &{\leq\displaystyle\sum_{f\in\mathcal{H}}Q^{2}(f)+\displaystyle\sum_{f_{1}\in\mathcal{H}}\displaystyle\sum_{f_{2}\in\mathcal{H}\atop f_{2}\neq f_{1}}Q(f_{1})Q(f_{2})\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{Cov}}(f_{1}(x),f_{2}(x)).}\end{array}
$$

The inequality is given by the fact that the definitions of $y$ and $f(x)$ implie $yf(x)\in [-1,1]$, from which we infer that $\underset{(x,y)\sim D}{\mathbf{Var}}{y f(x)}\leq 1$ for all voters $f \in{\mathcal{H}}$.

The problem in this demonstration arises when we simplify $\mathbf{Cov}_{(x,y)\sim D}\left(y f_{1}(x),y f_{2}(x)\right)$ to $\mathbf{Cov}_{(x,y)\sim D}\left(f_{1}(x),f_{2}(x)\right)$ , which could also be written as $\mathbf{Cov}_{x\sim D_{\mathcal{X}}}\left(f_{1}(x),f_{2}(x)\right)$ . As this final writing is independent of y, this equality would imply that the value y has no effect in the expression $\mathbf{Cov}_{(x,y)\sim D}\left(y f_{1}(x),y f_{2}(x)\right)$ . This simplification does not stand in the general case as it is possible to find various examples of functions $f_{i}$ and distributions D that do not satisfy this equality. As an example, consider $f_{1}(x)=1,f_{2}(x)= -1$ and $\operatorname*{Pr}_{y\sim D_{\mathcal{Y}|x}}(y{=}1)=\operatorname*{Pr}_{y\sim D_{\mathcal{Y}|x}}(y{=}-1)=\textstyle\frac{1}{2}$ for any given value $x \in \mathcal{X}$ . Using these values, we get the following, which disproves the equality assumed in the said simplification:

$$
\begin{array}{r}{\mathbf{Cov}(f_{1}(x),f_{2}(x))=\mathbf{Cov}(1,-1)=0\qquad}\\ {\mathbf{Cov}(y f_{1}(x),y f_{2}(x))=\mathbf{Cov}(y,-y)= -\mathbf{Cov}(y,y)= -1 .}\end{array}
$$

context.name: Corollary 2 (Corollary 16 in Germain et al. 2015; erroneous) and its motivation
context.statement:
Even though the demonstration of Proposition 1 is flawed, this does not necessarily imply that the proposition itself does not stand. In principle, the proposition might be valid due to a different argument. However, in order to show that Proposition 15 of Germain et al. (2015) is indeed false, we introduce the following corollary. If Proposition 1 were true, then so would Corollary 2 which follows directly from it.

## Erroneous result

Corollary 2 (Corollary 16 in Germain et al. (2015)) Given n independent voters under a uniform distribution $Q,$ we have

$$
R_{D}(B_{Q})\leq\mathcal{C}_{Q}^{D}\leq\frac{1}{n(1-2d_{Q}^{D})}=\frac{1}{n(1-2R_{D}(G_{Q}))}.
$$

To prove the above corollary, Germain et al. (2015) note that under the hypothesis that the n voters are independents under a uniform distribution, Proposition 1 implies that $\mathbf{Var}(M_{Q}^{D})\leq 1/n;$ the result then follows from the definition of the C-bound.

At first glance, the corollary seems intuitive. Increasing the number of voters should improve the quality of the classification. Therefore, we would expect the C-bound to decrease. The main problem with this result is that it implies that as the number of independent voters n goes to infinity, the right side goes to 0. This means that for any binary classification problem, the risk of the majority vote can be made arbitrarily small by using a sufficiently large set of independent voters. Though this may seem like a desirable property, it is not realistic in the presence of label noise. In such case, the noise associated with the output y given a certain x will induce a minimum amount of erroneous classification (i.e., irreducible error). Notice that the label noise is an inherent property of a given distribution D, and the irreducible error (also known as Bayes error in the literature) is achieved by an optimal prediction rule for D. This irreducible error is not 0 in the presence of label noise, which contradicts the statement of Corollary 2. To clearly illustrate this contradiction, consider the following example.

context.name: Assumptions 1-2: deterministic labels and sufficiently accurate voters (Section 5)
context.statement:
We have now shown that Proposition 1 is incorrect as stated in the general case, namely when the labelling task includes label noise. The aim of the current section is to rectify Proposition 1 in a setting devoid of label noise, by introducing new assumptions on the data distribution and the voters. In the following section we build upon this knowledge a new, correct and improved result that stands in the general case.

Even though the assumption that a given problem is devoid of label noise might not be realistic in most applications, we can see this case as an easy classification problem where an error of 0 should be achievable for some classifier. Given this assumption, we would thus desire a majority vote made with "good enough" voters to come arbitrarily close to null classification error. Moreover, we would expect a good bound on the risk of majority votes to reflect this fact by being potentially arbitrarily small in this setting.

We begin by noting that the assumption that distribution D is devoid of label noise implies that there exists a function that maps each input x to its correct label.

Assumption 1: Deterministic labels. The data distribution D is such that there exists a function $g:\mathcal{X}\to\{-1,1\}$ for which $y=g(x)$ for all $(x,y)\sim D$ , or equivalently $\operatorname*{Pr}_{y\sim D_{\mathcal{Y}|x}}\left(y{=}g(x)\right)=1$ for all $x \in \mathcal{X}$

The counter-example of the previous section also illustrates that uncorrelated voters do not necessarily result in an accurate majority vote, as it does not imply that the input-output correlation is taken into account. Thus, we need a second assumption, capturing the fact that the majority vote must be made of "good enough" voters. Namely, we want each voter to classify this input correctly with a probability larger than $1 / 2$

Assumption 2: Sufficiently accurate voters. For any given pair $(x,y)\sim D$ , for any voter $f_{i}\in\mathcal{H},yf_{i}(x)>0;$ in other words, all voters are leaning towards the right label (although with scores, i.e., varying confidence levels) in a non ambivalent manner (i.e., $f_{i}(x)\neq 0)$

Given the definition of a voter $f_{i}$, Assumption 2 implies that for any given input $x$ in $\mathcal{X}$ and any given voter $f_{i}$ in $\mathcal{H}$ , the expected output of $f_{i}(x)$ will agree with the true value of $y,$ meaning they will share the same sign. This assumption is very strong, as it will break when a single voter does not classify a given x with sufficient probability. It may seem trivial that under this assumption the majority vote will be correct every time and will thus have an actual risk of 0. Recall however that the majority vote risk $R_{D}(B_{Q})$ only considers the sign of the margin $[y\,\mathbf{E}_{f\sim Q}f(x)]$ on $(x,y)\sim D$ while the computation of the C-bound depends on the value of the margin itself. In other words, the risk $R_{D}(B_{Q})$ depends on which label the majority vote is most confident in but the C-bound further considers how confident the vote is. This implies that various majority votes which make the same prediction (same risk $R_{D}(B_{Q}))$ may have different C-bound as they may have different margins. Therefore, the C-bound is not trivially 0 under the above assumptions.

We now show that an updated Proposition 1 holds given these two new assumptions, namely that the labels are deterministic and the voters are sufficiently accurate.

context.name: Section 6 introduction (goal of Proposition 4)
context.statement: The counter-example given in Section 4 was based on the knowledge that the risk of the majority vote should never be inferior to minimal risk induced by the label noise in D. We have shown in Section 5 that the C-bound can converge to the minimal risk in a setting deprived of label noise by proving that in such a setting, using voters of sufficient quality renders Corrolary 2 true. In this section, we aim to generalise this result to problems which contain label noise. To do so, we introduce in Proposition 4 a theoretical lower-bound for the C-bound for a given distribution D as well as the majority vote which achieves this bound.
