noncomputable def supDevTruth {Ω 𝒳 ι : Type*} [MeasurableSpace 𝒳] (n : ℕ) (C : ι → Set 𝒳) (μ𝒳 : Measure 𝒳) (X : Fin n → Ω → 𝒳) (ω : Ω) : ℝ :=
  ⨆ i' : ι, |empFreq n C X i' ω - (μ𝒳 (C i')).toReal|

noncomputable def supDevGhost {Ω 𝒳 ι : Type*} (n : ℕ) (C : ι → Set 𝒳) (X X' : Fin n → Ω → 𝒳) (ω : Ω) : ℝ :=
  ⨆ i' : ι, |empFreq n C X i' ω - empFreq n C X' i' ω|

/-! ### Elementary facts about indicators and empirical frequencies -/

private lemma ind_nonneg {𝒳 : Type*} (s : Set 𝒳) (x : 𝒳) :
    0 ≤ s.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) x := by
  by_cases h : x ∈ s <;> simp [h]

private lemma ind_le_one {𝒳 : Type*} (s : Set 𝒳) (x : 𝒳) :
    s.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) x ≤ 1 := by
  by_cases h : x ∈ s <;> simp [h]

private lemma ind_sq {𝒳 : Type*} (s : Set 𝒳) (x : 𝒳) :
    (s.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) x) ^ 2 = s.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) x := by
  by_cases h : x ∈ s <;> simp [h]

private lemma empFreq_nonneg {Ω 𝒳 ι : Type*} (n : ℕ) (C : ι → Set 𝒳) (X : Fin n → Ω → 𝒳)
    (i : ι) (ω : Ω) : 0 ≤ empFreq n C X i ω := by
  unfold empFreq
  have : (0:ℝ) ≤ ∑ k : Fin n, (C i).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) (X k ω) :=
    Finset.sum_nonneg (fun k _ => ind_nonneg _ _)
  positivity

private lemma empFreq_le_one {Ω 𝒳 ι : Type*} {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (C : ι → Set 𝒳)
    (X : Fin n → Ω → 𝒳) (i : ι) (ω : Ω) : empFreq n C X i ω ≤ 1 := by
  have hnR : (0:ℝ) < (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
  unfold empFreq
  have h1 : ∑ k : Fin n, (C i).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) (X k ω) ≤ (n : ℝ) := by
    calc ∑ k : Fin n, (C i).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) (X k ω)
        ≤ ∑ _k : Fin n, (1:ℝ) := Finset.sum_le_sum (fun k _ => ind_le_one _ _)
      _ = (n : ℝ) := by simp
  rw [inv_mul_le_iff₀ hnR, mul_one]
  exact h1

private lemma measurable_empFreq {Ω 𝒳 ι : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace 𝒳]
    (n : ℕ) (C : ι → Set 𝒳) (hC : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (C i)) (X : Fin n → Ω → 𝒳)
    (hX : ∀ k, Measurable (X k)) (i : ι) : Measurable (fun ω => empFreq n C X i ω) := by
  unfold empFreq
  refine Measurable.const_mul ?_ _
  refine Finset.measurable_sum _ (fun k _ => ?_)
  exact (measurable_const.indicator (hC i)).comp (hX k)

private lemma integral_ind_comp {Ω 𝒳 : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace 𝒳]
    (μ : Measure Ω) (μ𝒳 : Measure 𝒳)
    (s : Set 𝒳) (hs : MeasurableSet s) (Z : Ω → 𝒳) (hZ : Measurable Z)
    (hlaw : Measure.map Z μ = μ𝒳) :
    ∫ ω, s.indicator (fun _ => (1:ℝ)) (Z ω) ∂μ = (μ𝒳 s).toReal := by
  have h1 : ∫ x, s.indicator (fun _ => (1:ℝ)) x ∂(μ.map Z)
      = ∫ ω, s.indicator (fun _ => (1:ℝ)) (Z ω) ∂μ :=
    integral_map hZ.aemeasurable ((measurable_const.indicator hs).aestronglyMeasurable)
  rw [← h1, hlaw, integral_indicator_const _ hs]
  simp [measureReal_def]

/-- Chebyshev's inequality for the empirical frequency of an i.i.d. sample. -/
private lemma cheb_empFreq {Ω 𝒳 ι : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace 𝒳]
    (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (μ𝒳 : Measure 𝒳)
    {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (C : ι → Set 𝒳) (hC : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (C i))
    (Z : Fin n → Ω → 𝒳) (hZmeas : ∀ k, Measurable (Z k))
    (hZlaw : ∀ k, Measure.map (Z k) μ = μ𝒳) (hZindep : iIndepFun Z μ)
    (i : ι) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) :
    (μ {ω | s ≤ |empFreq n C Z i ω - (μ𝒳 (C i)).toReal|}).toReal ≤ 1 / (4 * n * s ^ 2) := by
  classical
  have hnR : (0:ℝ) < (n:ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
  set p : ℝ := (μ𝒳 (C i)).toReal with hpdef
  set Y : Fin n → Ω → ℝ := fun k ω => (C i).indicator (fun _ => (1:ℝ)) (Z k ω) with hYdef
  have hYmeas : ∀ k, Measurable (Y k) := fun k =>
    (measurable_const.indicator (hC i)).comp (hZmeas k)
  have hYLp : ∀ k, MemLp (Y k) 2 μ := by
    intro k
    refine MemLp.of_bound (hYmeas k).aestronglyMeasurable 1 (.of_forall (fun ω => ?_))
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (ind_nonneg _ _)]
    exact ind_le_one _ _
  have hYint : ∀ k, ∫ ω, Y k ω ∂μ = p := fun k =>
    integral_ind_comp μ μ𝒳 (C i) (hC i) (Z k) (hZmeas k) (hZlaw k)
  have hYvar : ∀ k, Var[Y k; μ] = p - p ^ 2 := by
    intro k
    rw [variance_eq_sub (hYLp k), hYint k]
    congr 1
    have h2 : (Y k) ^ 2 = Y k := by
      funext ω
      simpa [hYdef] using ind_sq (C i) (Z k ω)
    rw [h2, hYint k]
  -- pairwise independence of the indicators
  have hYindep : Set.Pairwise (↑(Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n))) fun k l => Y k ⟂ᵢ[μ] Y l := by
    intro k _ l _ hkl
    exact (hZindep.indepFun hkl).comp (measurable_const.indicator (hC i))
      (measurable_const.indicator (hC i))
  have hsumvar : Var[∑ k : Fin n, Y k; μ] = (n : ℝ) * (p - p ^ 2) := by
    rw [IndepFun.variance_sum (fun k _ => hYLp k) hYindep]
    simp only [hYvar, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul]
  -- the empirical frequency as a rescaled sum
  have hEF : (fun ω => empFreq n C Z i ω) = fun ω => (n:ℝ)⁻¹ * (∑ k : Fin n, Y k) ω := by
    funext ω
    simp [empFreq, hYdef, Finset.sum_apply]
  have hEFmean : ∫ ω, empFreq n C Z i ω ∂μ = p := by
    rw [hEF]
    have hint : ∀ k : Fin n, Integrable (Y k) μ := fun k => (hYLp k).integrable (by norm_num)
    have : ∫ ω, (n:ℝ)⁻¹ * (∑ k : Fin n, Y k) ω ∂μ = (n:ℝ)⁻¹ * ∫ ω, (∑ k : Fin n, Y k) ω ∂μ :=
      integral_const_mul _ _
    rw [this]
    have h2 : ∫ ω, (∑ k : Fin n, Y k) ω ∂μ = ∑ k : Fin n, ∫ ω, Y k ω ∂μ := by
      simp only [Finset.sum_apply]
      exact integral_finset_sum _ (fun k _ => hint k)
    rw [h2]
    simp [hYint]
    field_simp
  have hEFvar : Var[fun ω => empFreq n C Z i ω; μ] ≤ 1 / (4 * n) := by
    rw [hEF, variance_const_mul, hsumvar]
    have h1 : ((n:ℝ)⁻¹)^2 * ((n:ℝ) * (p - p^2)) = (p - p^2) / n := by
      field_simp
    rw [h1]
    have h2 : (p - p^2) ≤ 1/4 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (p - 1/2)]
    calc (p - p^2)/(n:ℝ) ≤ (1/4)/(n:ℝ) := by gcongr
      _ = 1/(4*(n:ℝ)) := by rw [div_div]
  have hSmeas : Measurable (fun ω => empFreq n C Z i ω) := by
    unfold empFreq
    refine Measurable.const_mul ?_ _
    exact Finset.measurable_sum _ (fun k _ => (measurable_const.indicator (hC i)).comp (hZmeas k))
  have hSLp : MemLp (fun ω => empFreq n C Z i ω) 2 μ := by
    refine MemLp.of_bound hSmeas.aestronglyMeasurable 1 (.of_forall (fun ω => ?_))
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (empFreq_nonneg n C Z i ω)]
    exact empFreq_le_one hn C Z i ω
  have hcheb := meas_ge_le_variance_div_sq hSLp hs
  simp only [hEFmean] at hcheb
  have hvnn : 0 ≤ Var[fun ω => empFreq n C Z i ω; μ] := variance_nonneg _ _
  have h1 : (μ {ω | s ≤ |empFreq n C Z i ω - p|}).toReal
      ≤ Var[fun ω => empFreq n C Z i ω; μ] / s ^ 2 := by
    have := ENNReal.toReal_mono ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top hcheb
    rwa [ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (by positivity)] at this
  refine h1.trans ?_
  calc Var[fun ω => empFreq n C Z i ω; μ] / s ^ 2 ≤ (1/(4*(n:ℝ))) / s^2 := by gcongr
    _ = 1 / (4 * n * s ^ 2) := by rw [div_div]

/-- The slice estimate: if the truth-deviation at `ω` is at least `t`, then with probability at
least `1/2` over the ghost sample the ghost-deviation is at least `t/2`. -/
private lemma key_slice {Ω 𝒳 ι : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace 𝒳]
    (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (μ𝒳 : Measure 𝒳) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ𝒳]
    {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (C : ι → Set 𝒳) (hC : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (C i))
    (X X' : Fin n → Ω → 𝒳)
    (hX'meas : ∀ k, Measurable (X' k)) (hX'law : ∀ k, Measure.map (X' k) μ = μ𝒳)
    (hX'indep : iIndepFun X' μ)
    {t : ℝ} (ht : Real.sqrt (2 / (n : ℝ)) ≤ t)
    (ω : Ω) (hω : t ≤ supDevTruth n C μ𝒳 X ω)
    (B : Set Ω)
    (hBdef : ∀ ω' : Ω, ω' ∈ B ↔ t / 2 ≤ ⨆ i, |empFreq n C X i ω - empFreq n C X' i ω'|) :
    (1 : ℝ≥0∞) / 2 ≤ μ B := by
  classical
  have hnR : (0:ℝ) < (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
  have ht0 : 0 < t := lt_of_lt_of_le (Real.sqrt_pos.mpr (by positivity)) ht
  have ht2 : 2 / (n:ℝ) ≤ t ^ 2 := by
    have h := Real.sq_sqrt (show (0:ℝ) ≤ 2 / (n:ℝ) by positivity)
    nlinarith [Real.sqrt_nonneg (2 / (n:ℝ))]
  by_contra hcon
  push_neg at hcon
  have hBne : μ B ≠ ⊤ := measure_ne_top _ _
  set c : ℝ := (μ B).toReal with hcdef
  have hc0 : 0 ≤ c := ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
  have hclt : c < 1 / 2 := by
    have h1 : (μ B).toReal < ((1:ℝ≥0∞)/2).toReal :=
      (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal hBne (by norm_num)).mpr hcon
    simpa using h1
  have h1c : (1:ℝ)/2 < 1 - c := by linarith
  -- the threshold `u`
  have hm_pos : 0 < 1 / (4 * (n:ℝ) * (1 - c)) := by positivity
  have hmr : 1 / (4 * (n:ℝ) * (1 - c)) < (t/2)^2 := by
    have hA : 1 / (4 * (n:ℝ) * (1 - c)) < 1 / (2 * (n:ℝ)) := by
      apply one_div_lt_one_div_of_lt (by positivity)
      nlinarith
    have hB : 1 / (2 * (n:ℝ)) ≤ (t/2)^2 := by
      have he : 1 / (2*(n:ℝ)) = (2/(n:ℝ))/4 := by
        field_simp
        norm_num
      have he2 : (t/2)^2 = t^2/4 := by ring
      rw [he, he2]
      linarith
    linarith
  set u : ℝ := Real.sqrt ((1 / (4 * (n:ℝ) * (1 - c)) + (t/2)^2) / 2) with hudef
  have hu0 : 0 < u := Real.sqrt_pos.mpr (by linarith)
  have husq : u ^ 2 = (1 / (4 * (n:ℝ) * (1 - c)) + (t/2)^2) / 2 :=
    Real.sq_sqrt (by linarith)
  have hult : u < t / 2 := by nlinarith
  -- pick an index nearly attaining the supremum
  have hne : Nonempty ι := by
    by_contra hemp
    rw [not_nonempty_iff] at hemp
    have h0 : supDevTruth n C μ𝒳 X ω = 0 := Real.iSup_of_isEmpty _
    rw [h0] at hω
    linarith
  have hlt : t/2 + u < ⨆ i, |empFreq n C X i ω - (μ𝒳 (C i)).toReal| := by
    have h1 : t/2 + u < t := by linarith
    exact lt_of_lt_of_le h1 hω
  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := exists_lt_of_lt_ciSup hlt
  -- Chebyshev for the ghost sample at index `i`
  have hchebS := cheb_empFreq μ μ𝒳 hn C hC X' hX'meas hX'law hX'indep i hu0
  -- the complement of the bad set is contained in `B`
  have hsub : (Set.univ : Set Ω)
      ⊆ B ∪ {ω' | u ≤ |empFreq n C X' i ω' - (μ𝒳 (C i)).toReal|} := by
    intro ω' _
    by_cases hmem : ω' ∈ {ω' | u ≤ |empFreq n C X' i ω' - (μ𝒳 (C i)).toReal|}
    · exact Or.inr hmem
    · left
      rw [Set.mem_setOf_eq, not_le] at hmem
      rw [hBdef]
      have hbdd2 : BddAbove (Set.range fun i' => |empFreq n C X i' ω - empFreq n C X' i' ω'|) := by
        refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
        rintro x ⟨i', rfl⟩
        have h1 := empFreq_nonneg n C X i' ω
        have h2 := empFreq_le_one hn C X i' ω
        have h3 := empFreq_nonneg n C X' i' ω'
        have h4 := empFreq_le_one hn C X' i' ω'
        rw [abs_le]
        constructor <;> linarith
      have hterm : t/2 ≤ |empFreq n C X i ω - empFreq n C X' i ω'| := by
        have habs := abs_sub_abs_le_abs_sub
          (empFreq n C X i ω - (μ𝒳 (C i)).toReal)
          (empFreq n C X' i ω' - (μ𝒳 (C i)).toReal)
        have heq : (empFreq n C X i ω - (μ𝒳 (C i)).toReal)
            - (empFreq n C X' i ω' - (μ𝒳 (C i)).toReal)
            = empFreq n C X i ω - empFreq n C X' i ω' := by ring
        rw [heq] at habs
        linarith
      exact le_trans hterm (le_ciSup hbdd2 i)
  -- combine
  have hSne : μ {ω' | u ≤ |empFreq n C X' i ω' - (μ𝒳 (C i)).toReal|} ≠ ⊤ := measure_ne_top _ _
  have hmeasle : (1:ℝ≥0∞) ≤ μ B + μ {ω' | u ≤ |empFreq n C X' i ω' - (μ𝒳 (C i)).toReal|} := by
    calc (1:ℝ≥0∞) = μ (Set.univ : Set Ω) := measure_univ.symm
      _ ≤ μ (B ∪ {ω' | u ≤ |empFreq n C X' i ω' - (μ𝒳 (C i)).toReal|}) := measure_mono hsub
      _ ≤ _ := measure_union_le _ _
  have hreal : (1:ℝ) ≤ c + (μ {ω' | u ≤ |empFreq n C X' i ω' - (μ𝒳 (C i)).toReal|}).toReal := by
    have h := ENNReal.toReal_mono (ENNReal.add_ne_top.mpr ⟨hBne, hSne⟩) hmeasle
    rwa [ENNReal.toReal_add hBne hSne, ENNReal.toReal_one] at h
  have hlast : 1 / (4 * (n:ℝ) * u ^ 2) < 1 - c := by
    have hum : 1 / (4 * (n:ℝ) * (1 - c)) < u ^ 2 := by rw [husq]; linarith
    have h1 : 1 < u ^ 2 * (4 * (n:ℝ) * (1 - c)) :=
      (div_lt_iff₀ (show (0:ℝ) < 4 * (n:ℝ) * (1 - c) by positivity)).mp hum
    rw [div_lt_iff₀ (by positivity)]
    nlinarith
  linarith

theorem ch10_lemma_10_1
    {Ω 𝒳 ι : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace 𝒳]
    (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (μ𝒳 : Measure 𝒳)
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (hn : 0 < n)
    (C : ι → Set 𝒳) (hC : ∀ i' : ι, MeasurableSet (C i'))
    (X X' : Fin n → Ω → 𝒳)
    (hXmeas : ∀ k, Measurable (X k)) (hX'meas : ∀ k, Measurable (X' k))
    (hXlaw : ∀ k, Measure.map (X k) μ = μ𝒳)
    (hX'law : ∀ k, Measure.map (X' k) μ = μ𝒳)
    (hXindep : iIndepFun X μ) (hX'indep : iIndepFun X' μ)
    (hmTruth : Measurable
      (fun p : Ω × Ω => supDevTruth n C μ𝒳 (fun (k : Fin n) (q : Ω × Ω) => X k q.1) p))
    (hmGhost : Measurable
      (fun p : Ω × Ω =>
        supDevGhost n C (fun (k : Fin n) (q : Ω × Ω) => X k q.1)
          (fun (k : Fin n) (q : Ω × Ω) => X' k q.2) p))
    (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≥ Real.sqrt (2 / (n : ℝ))) :
    ((μ.prod μ)
        {p : Ω × Ω | supDevTruth n C μ𝒳 (fun (k : Fin n) (q : Ω × Ω) => X k q.1) p ≥ t}).toReal
      ≤ 2 * ((μ.prod μ)
        {p : Ω × Ω |
          supDevGhost n C (fun (k : Fin n) (q : Ω × Ω) => X k q.1)
            (fun (k : Fin n) (q : Ω × Ω) => X' k q.2) p ≥ t / 2}).toReal := by
  classical
  have hnR : (0:ℝ) < (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
  have ht0 : 0 < t := lt_of_lt_of_le (Real.sqrt_pos.mpr (by positivity)) ht
  -- `Ω` is nonempty
  have hΩ : Nonempty Ω := by
    by_contra h
    rw [not_nonempty_iff] at h
    have h1 : μ (Set.univ : Set Ω) = 1 := measure_univ
    rw [Set.univ_eq_empty_iff.mpr h, measure_empty] at h1
    exact zero_ne_one h1
  obtain ⟨ω₀⟩ := hΩ
  -- `μ𝒳` is a probability measure
  have hprob𝒳 : IsProbabilityMeasure μ𝒳 := by
    rw [← hXlaw ⟨0, hn⟩]
    exact Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map (hXmeas _).aemeasurable
  -- the two events, described intrinsically
  set A : Set Ω := {ω : Ω | supDevTruth n C μ𝒳 X ω ≥ t} with hAdef
  set G : Set (Ω × Ω) :=
    {p : Ω × Ω |
      supDevGhost n C (fun (k : Fin n) (q : Ω × Ω) => X k q.1)
        (fun (k : Fin n) (q : Ω × Ω) => X' k q.2) p ≥ t / 2} with hGdef
  have hGmeas : MeasurableSet G := hmGhost measurableSet_Ici
  have hmeasT : Measurable (fun ω : Ω => supDevTruth n C μ𝒳 X ω) := by
    have h : Measurable (fun ω : Ω => (ω, ω₀)) := measurable_id.prodMk measurable_const
    have h2 := hmTruth.comp h
    exact h2
  have hAmeas : MeasurableSet A := hmeasT measurableSet_Ici
  -- the key slice estimate
  have key : ∀ ω ∈ A, (1 : ℝ≥0∞) / 2 ≤ μ (Prod.mk ω ⁻¹' G) := by
    intro ω hω
    refine key_slice μ μ𝒳 hn C hC X X' hX'meas hX'law hX'indep ht ω hω _ ?_
    intro ω'
    exact Iff.rfl
  -- Fubini
  have hfub : (1 : ℝ≥0∞) / 2 * μ A ≤ (μ.prod μ) G := by
    rw [Measure.prod_apply hGmeas]
    calc (1 : ℝ≥0∞) / 2 * μ A
        = ∫⁻ ω, A.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ≥0∞) / 2) ω ∂μ :=
          (lintegral_indicator_const hAmeas _).symm
      _ ≤ ∫⁻ ω, μ (Prod.mk ω ⁻¹' G) ∂μ := by
          refine lintegral_mono (fun ω => ?_)
          by_cases hω : ω ∈ A
          · rw [Set.indicator_of_mem hω]
            exact key ω hω
          · rw [Set.indicator_of_notMem hω]
            exact zero_le _
  have hfub' : μ A ≤ 2 * (μ.prod μ) G := by
    have hhalf : (2 : ℝ≥0∞) * ((1 : ℝ≥0∞) / 2) = 1 := by
      rw [one_div, ENNReal.mul_inv_cancel (by norm_num) (by norm_num)]
    have h2 : (2 : ℝ≥0∞) * ((1 : ℝ≥0∞) / 2 * μ A) = μ A := by
      rw [← mul_assoc, hhalf, one_mul]
    calc μ A = 2 * ((1 : ℝ≥0∞) / 2 * μ A) := h2.symm
      _ ≤ 2 * (μ.prod μ) G := by gcongr
  -- identify the left-hand event
  have hLHS : (μ.prod μ)
      {p : Ω × Ω | supDevTruth n C μ𝒳 (fun (k : Fin n) (q : Ω × Ω) => X k q.1) p ≥ t}
      = μ A := by
    have hset : {p : Ω × Ω | supDevTruth n C μ𝒳 (fun (k : Fin n) (q : Ω × Ω) => X k q.1) p ≥ t}
        = A ×ˢ (Set.univ : Set Ω) := by
      ext p
      simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_prod, Set.mem_univ, and_true, hAdef]
      rfl
    rw [hset, Measure.prod_prod, measure_univ, mul_one]
  rw [hLHS]
  have hfin : (2 : ℝ≥0∞) * (μ.prod μ) G ≠ ⊤ := by
    refine ENNReal.mul_ne_top (by norm_num) (measure_ne_top _ _)
  have := ENNReal.toReal_mono hfin hfub'
  rwa [ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat] at this

end GraduateLevel

targets.label: ch4_theorem_4_12
targets.statement:
Assume that \(\phi(w, z) \in [0,1]\) for all \(w\) and \(z\). Then given \(\delta \in (0,1)\), with probability at least \(1 - \delta\), the following inequality holds:
\[
\forall w\in\Omega:\phi(w,\mathcal{D})\leq\phi(w,\mathcal{S}_{n})+\epsilon_{n}(\delta),
\]
where
\[
\epsilon_{n}(\delta)=\inf_{\epsilon>0}\left[2\epsilon+3\sqrt{\frac{\ln(3 N_{1}(\epsilon,\mathcal{G},2 n)/\delta)}{2 n}}\right].
\]
Moreover, for any \(\gamma \in (0,1)\), with probability at least \(1 - \delta\), the following inequality holds:
\[
\forall w\in\Omega:(1-\gamma)^{2}\phi(w,\mathcal{D})\leq\phi(w,\mathcal{S}_{n})+\epsilon_{n}(\delta),
\]
where
\[
\epsilon_{n}(\delta)=\inf_{\epsilon>0}\left[2\epsilon+\frac{(5-4\gamma)\ln(3 N_{1}(\epsilon,\mathcal{G},n)/\delta)}{2\gamma n}\right].
\]

nl_proof:
Let \(\mathcal{F} = \{f(z) = \phi(w,z) - 0.5 : w \in \Omega\}\). Given \(S_{n}\), we consider an \(\epsilon-L_{1}(S_{n})\) cover \(\mathcal{F}_{\epsilon}(S_{n})\) of \(\mathcal{F}\), of size no more \(N = N_{1}(\epsilon, \mathcal{G}, n)\). We may assume that \(f(Z_{i}) \in [-0.5, 0.5]\) for \(f \in \mathcal{F}_{\epsilon}(S_{n})\). From Corollary 2.27 (with \(a_{i} = 0.5\)) and the union bound, we obtain the following uniform convergence result over \(\mathcal{F}_{\epsilon}(S_{n})\). With probability \(1-\delta\):
\[
\forall f\in\mathcal{F}_{\epsilon}(\mathcal{S}_{n}):f(\sigma,\mathcal{S}_{n})\leq\sqrt{\frac{\ln(N/\delta)}{2 n}}.
\]
Since for all \( f \in \mathcal{F} \), we can find \( f' \in \mathcal{F}_{\epsilon}(\mathcal{S}_n) \) so that \( n^{-1} \sum_{Z \in \mathcal{S}_n} |f(Z) - f'(Z)| \leq \epsilon \) for all \( Z \in \mathcal{S}_n \). It follows that
\[
f(\sigma,\mathcal{S}_{n})\leq f^{\prime}(\sigma,\mathcal{S}_{n})+\epsilon\leq\epsilon+\sqrt{\frac{\ln(N/\delta)}{2 n}}.
\]
Using Lemma 4.8 with \(\psi = 0\), this uniform convergence result for the symmetrized
empirical process implies the following uniform convergence result. With probability at least \(1 - \delta_{1}\) over \((S_n, S'_n) \sim \mathcal{D}^{2n}\):
\[
\forall w\in\Omega:\underbrace{\phi(w,\mathcal{S}_{n}^{\prime})}_{\psi_{\mathrm{val}}}\leq\underbrace{\phi(w,\mathcal{S}_{n})}_{\psi_{\mathrm{trn}}}+\underbrace{2\epsilon+\sqrt{\frac{2\ln(2 N/\delta_{1})}{n}}}_{\epsilon_{n}^{1}(\delta_{1})}.
\]
The standard additive Chernoff bound implies that for all \( w \in \Omega \), with probability at least \( 1 - \delta_2 \):
\[
\underbrace{\phi(w,\mathcal{D})}_{\psi_{\mathrm{tst}}}\leq\underbrace{\phi(w,\mathcal{S}_{n}^{\prime})}_{\psi_{\mathrm{val}}}+\underbrace{\sqrt{\frac{\ln(1/\delta_{2})}{2 n}}}_{\epsilon_{n}^{2}(\delta_{2})}.
\]
Therefore in Lemma 4.11, we can take symbols as defined above, together with \(\delta_1 = 2\delta /3\) and \(\delta_{2} = \delta /3\) to obtain the desired bound.
Similarly, we consider \(\mathcal{F} = \{f(z) = \phi (w,z):w\in \Omega \}\). Given \(S_{n}\), we consider an \(\epsilon -L_{1}(S_{n})\) cover \(\mathcal{F}_{\epsilon}(\mathcal{S}_n)\) of \(\mathcal{F}\), of size no more \(N=N_{1}(\epsilon,\mathcal{G},n)\). We assume that \(f(Z_{i})\in [0,1]\) for all \(f\in \mathcal{F}_{\epsilon}(\mathcal{S}_n)\). From Corollary 2.27 and the union bound, we obtain the following uniform convergence result over \(\mathcal{F}_{\epsilon}(\mathcal{S}_n)\). With probability at least \(1 - \delta\):
\[
\begin{array}{l}\forall f\in\mathcal{F}_{\epsilon}(\mathcal{S}_{n}):f(\sigma,\mathcal{S}_{n})\leq\sqrt{\frac{2\sum_{Z\in\mathcal{S}_{n}}f(Z)^{2}\ln(N/\delta)}{n^{2}}}\\ \leq\gamma^{\prime}\frac{1}{n}\sum_{Z\in\mathcal{S}_{n}}f(Z)+\frac{\ln(N/\delta)}{2\gamma^{\prime}n}.\\ \end{array}
\]
The first inequality used Corollary 2.27. The second inequality used \(\sqrt{2ab} \leq \gamma' a + b / (2\gamma')\) and \(f(Z)^2 \leq f(Z)\). Since for all \(f \in \mathcal{F}\), we can find \(f' \in \mathcal{F}_{\epsilon}(\mathcal{S}_n)\) so that \(\frac{1}{n} \sum_{Z \in \mathcal{S}_n} |f(Z) - f'(Z)| \leq \epsilon\). It follows that
\[
\begin{array}{l}f(\sigma,\mathcal{S}_{n})\leq f^{\prime}(\sigma,\mathcal{S}_{n})+\epsilon\\ \leq\gamma^{\prime}\frac{1}{n}\sum_{Z\in\mathcal{S}_{n}}f^{\prime}(Z)+\frac{\ln(N/\delta)}{2\gamma^{\prime}n}+\epsilon\\ \leq\gamma^{\prime}\frac{1}{n}\sum_{Z\in\mathcal{S}_{n}}f(Z)+\frac{\ln(N/\delta)}{2\gamma^{\prime}n}+(1+\gamma^{\prime})\epsilon .\\ \end{array}
\]
Now, with \(\psi(f, \mathcal{S}_n) = \widetilde{\psi}(f, \mathcal{S}_n) = \gamma' \frac{1}{n} \sum_{Z \in \mathcal{S}_n} f(Z)\), we obtain from Lemma 4.8 the following uniform convergence result. With probability at least \(1 - \delta_1\) over \((\mathcal{S}_n, \mathcal{S}_n') \sim \mathcal{D}^{2n}\):
\[
\forall w\in\Omega:(1-\gamma^{\prime})\phi(w,\mathcal{S}_{n}^{\prime})\leq(1+\gamma^{\prime})\phi(w,\mathcal{S}_{n})+2(1+\gamma^{\prime})\epsilon+\frac{\ln(2 N/\delta_{1})}{\gamma^{\prime}n}.
\]
Let \(\gamma' = \gamma / (2 - \gamma)\), then it is easy to check algebraically that \((1 - \gamma') / (1 + \gamma') = 1 - \gamma\)
and \(1 / (\gamma^{\prime}(1 + \gamma^{\prime})) = (2 - \gamma)^{2} / (2\gamma)\). We thus obtain:
\[
\forall w\in\Omega:\underbrace{(1-\gamma)\phi(w,\mathcal{S}_{n}^{\prime})}_{\psi_{\mathrm{val}}}\leq\underbrace{\phi(w,\mathcal{S}_{n})}_{\psi_{\mathrm{trn}}}+\underbrace{2\epsilon+\frac{(2-\gamma)^{2}\ln(2 N/\delta_{1})}{2\gamma n}}_{\epsilon_{n}^{1}(\delta_{1})}.\tag{4.1}
\]
The standard multiplicative Chernoff bound in (2.11) implies that with probability \( 1 - \delta_2 \):
\[
\underbrace{(1-\gamma)(1-\gamma)\phi(w,\mathcal{D})}_{\psi_{\mathrm{tst}}}\leq\underbrace{(1-\gamma)\phi(w,\mathcal{S}_{n}^{\prime})}_{\psi_{\mathrm{val}}}+\underbrace{(1-\gamma)\frac{\ln(1/\delta_{2})}{2\gamma n}}_{\epsilon_{n}^{2}(\delta_{2})}.
\]
Therefore in Lemma 4.11, we can use symbols as displayed above, together with \(\delta_1 = 2\delta /3\) and \(\delta_{2} = \delta /3\) to obtain the desired bound.

context.name: corollary 2.27
context.statement:
Let \(\sigma_{i} = \{\pm 1\}\) be independent Bernoulli random variables ( each takes value \(\pm 1\) with equal probability). Let \(a_{i}\) be fixed numbers \((i=1,\dots,n)\) Then for all \(\epsilon >0\) ..
\[
\Pr\left(n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sigma_{i}a_{i}\geq\epsilon\right)\leq\exp\left[-\frac{n\epsilon^{2}}{2 n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_{i}^{2}}\right].
\]

context.name: Lemma 4.8
context.statement:
(Symmetrization) Consider a real valued function family \(F = \{f : Z \rightarrow \mathbb{R}\}\). Assume there exists a function \(\psi : F \times Z^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}\) and \(\epsilon_{n} : (0,1) \rightarrow \mathbb{R}\) so that with probability at least \(1-\delta\):
\[
\forall f \in F, \qquad f(\sigma, S_{n}) \leq \psi(f, S_{n}) + \epsilon_{n}(\delta),
\]
where the randomness is over both \(S_{n} \sim D^{n}\) and \(\sigma\). If there exists \(\tilde{\psi}(f, S_{n} \cup S_{n}^{\prime})\) so that the following superadditive inequality holds for all \((S_{n}, S_{n}^{\prime})\)
\[
\psi(f, S_{n}) + \psi(f, S_{n}^{\prime}) \leq \tilde{\psi}(f, S_{n} \cup S_{n}^{\prime}),
\]
then with probability at least \(1-\delta\) over independent random data \((S_{n}, S_{n}^{\prime}) \sim D^{2n}\):
\[
\forall f \in F, \qquad f(S_{n}^{\prime}) \leq f(S_{n}) + \tilde{\psi}(f, S_{n} \cup S_{n}^{\prime}) + 2\epsilon_{n}(\delta/2).
\]

context.name: lemma 4.11
context.statement:
Let \(\psi_{\mathrm{trn}}: \mathcal{F} \times \mathcal{Z}^n \to \mathbb{R}\), \(\psi_{\mathrm{val}}: \mathcal{F} \times \mathcal{Z}^n \to \mathbb{R}\), \(\psi_{\mathrm{tst}}: \mathcal{F} \times \mathcal{D} \to \mathbb{R}\) be appropriately training (where \(\mathcal{D}\) denotes probability distributions on \(\mathcal{Z}\)), validation, and test statistics. Assume that for any \(\delta_1 \in (0,1)\), the following uniform convergence result holds. With probability at least \(1 - \delta_1\) over randomly drawn training and validation sets \((S_n, S_n') \sim \mathcal{D}^{2n}\):
\[
\forall f\in\mathcal{F}:\psi_{\mathrm{val}}(f,\mathcal{S}_{n}^{\prime})\leq\psi_{\mathrm{trn}}(f,\mathcal{S}_{n})+\epsilon_{n}^{1}(\delta_{1}).
\]
Moreover, assume \(\forall f\in \mathcal{F}\), we have with probability \(1 - \delta_{2}\) over randomly drawn \(\mathcal{S}_n^\prime \sim \mathcal{D}\):
\[
\psi_{\mathrm{tst}}(f,\mathcal{D})\leq\psi_{\mathrm{val}}(f,\mathcal{S}_{n}^{\prime})+\epsilon_{n}^{2}(\delta_{2}).
\]
Then the following uniform convergence statement holds. With probability at least \(1 - \delta_1 - \delta_2\),
\[
\forall f\in\mathcal{F}:\psi_{\mathrm{tst}}(f,\mathcal{D})\leq\psi_{\mathrm{trn}}(f,\mathcal{S}_{n})+\epsilon_{n}^{1}(\delta_{1})+\epsilon_{n}^{2}(\delta_{2}).
\]

context.name: Union Bound
context.statement:
(Union Bound) Consider \(m\) events \(E_1, \ldots, E_m\). The following probability inequality holds:
\[
\Pr (E_1 \cup \cdots \cup E_m) \leq \sum_{j=1}^{m} \Pr(E_j).
\]

The union bound has an alternative expression, which is often used in the learning theory analysis. If each \(E_j\) occurs with probability at least \(1-\delta_j\) for \(j=1, \ldots, m\), then with probability at least \(1-\sum_{j=1}^{m} \delta_j\), all of events \(\{E_j\}\) occur simultaneously for \(j=1, \ldots, m\).

context.name: definition 4.1
context.statement:
Let \((\mathcal{V},d)\) be a pseudometric space with metric \(d(\cdot,\cdot)\). A finite
set \(\mathcal{G}(\epsilon) \subset \mathcal{V}\) is an \(\epsilon\)-cover (or \(\epsilon\)-net) of \(\mathcal{G} \subset \mathcal{V}\) if, for all \(\phi \in \mathcal{G}\), there exists \(\phi' \in \mathcal{G}(\epsilon)\) so that \(d(\phi', \phi) \leq \epsilon\). The \(\epsilon\)-covering number of \(\mathcal{G}\) with metric \(d\) is the smallest cardinality \(N(\epsilon, \mathcal{G}, d)\) of such \(\mathcal{G}(\epsilon)\). The number \(\ln N(\epsilon, \mathcal{G}, d)\) is called the \(\epsilon\)-entropy.
For a function class \(\mathcal{G}\) with seminorm \(L_{p}(\mathcal{D})\) in (3.19), we denote the corresponding \(L_{p}(\mathcal{D})\)-covering number as \(N(\epsilon, \mathcal{G}, L_{p}(\mathcal{D}))\). When \(1 \leq p \leq q\), we have
\[
N(\epsilon,\mathcal{G},L_{p}(\mathcal{D}))\leq N(\epsilon,\mathcal{G},L_{q}(\mathcal{D})).
\]

context.name: definition 3.8
context.statement:
We define
\[
\phi(w,z)=L\left(f(w,x),y\right)-L_{*}(x,y),\tag{3.4}
\]
for \( w \in \Omega \) and \( z = (x, y) \in \mathcal{Z} = \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{Y} \), and a pre-chosen \( L_{*}(x, y) \) of \( z = (x, y) \) that does not depend on \( w \).
For training data \( S_{n}=\{Z_{i}=(X_{i},Y_{i}):i=1,\ldots,n\} \), we define the training loss for \( w\in \Omega \) as
\[
\phi(w,\mathcal{S}_{n})=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\phi(w,Z_{i}).\tag{3.5}
\]
Moreover, for a distribution \(\mathcal{D}\) on \(\mathcal{Z}\), we define the test loss for \(w \in \Omega\) as:
\[
\phi(w,\mathcal{D})=\mathbb{E}_{Z\sim\mathcal{D}}\phi(w,Z).\tag{3.6}
\]
Since \( L_{*}(x,y) \) does not depend on \( w \), the ERM solution with respect to the loss \( L(\cdot) \) is equivalent to the ERM solution with respect to \( \phi (w,\cdot) \). Therefore with the simplified notations, the approximate ERM method (3.3) is a special case of the following method:
\[
\phi(\hat{w},\mathcal{S}_{n})\leq\inf_{w\in\Omega}\phi(w,\mathcal{S}_{n})+\epsilon^{\prime}.\tag{3.7}
\]
In general, we may simply take \( L_{*}(x,y) = 0 \) in (3.4). However, for some applications, we may choose a non-zero \( L_{*}(x,y) \) so that
\[
L(f(w,x),y)-L_{*}(x,y)
\]
has a small variance. For least squares loss, this can be achieved with \( L_{*}(x,y) = L(f_{*}(x),y) \) where \( f_{*}(x) \) is the optimal prediction function that minimizes the test loss as shown in Example 3.9. The smaller variance, combined with Bernstein's inequality, implies better generalization bound (see Section 3.6 for more details).

context.name: Empirical and Uniform Covering Number
context.statement:
Given an empirical distribution \( S_{n}=\{Z_{1},\ldots,Z_{n}\} \), we define the pseudometric \( d = L_{p}(S_{n}) \) as
\[
d(\phi,\phi^{\prime})=\left[\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|\phi(Z_{i})-\phi^{\prime}(Z_{i})|^{p}\right]^{1/p}.
\]
The corresponding metric covering number \(N(\epsilon, \mathcal{G}, L_p(\mathcal{S}_n))\) is referred to as the
empirical \( L_{p} \) covering number. Given \( n \), the largest \( L_{p} \) covering number over empirical distribution \( S_{n} \) is referred to as the uniform \( L_{p} \) covering number
\[
N_{p}(\epsilon,\mathcal{G},n)=\sup_{\mathcal{S}_{n}}N(\epsilon,\mathcal{G},L_{p}(\mathcal{S}_{n})).
\]

context.name: Bracketing Number
context.statement:
Let \(\mathcal{G} = \{\phi(w, \cdot) : w \in \Omega\}\) be a real-valued function class, equipped with a pseudometric \(d\). We say
\[
\mathcal{G}(\epsilon)=\left\{\left[\phi_{1}^{L}(z),\phi_{1}^{U}(z)\right],\dots,\left[\phi_{N}^{L}(z),\phi_{N}^{U}(z)\right]\right\}
\]
is an \(\epsilon\)-bracket of \(\mathcal{G}\) under metric \(d\) if for all \(w \in \Omega\), there exists \(j = j(w)\) such that \(\forall z\):
\[
\phi_{j}^{L}(z)\leq\phi(w,z)\leq\phi_{j}^{U}(z),\quad d(\phi_{j}^{L},\phi_{j}^{U})\leq\epsilon .
\]
The \(\epsilon\)-bracketing number is the smallest cardinality \(N_{\mathbb{I}}(\epsilon, \mathcal{G}, d)\) of such \(\mathcal{G}(\epsilon)\). The quantity \(\ln N_{\mathbb{I}}(\epsilon, \mathcal{G}, d)\) is called \(\epsilon\) bracketing entropy.
In particular, given a distribution \(\mathcal{D}\) and \(p \geq 1\), we define \(L_{p}\)-seminorm in function space as
\[
\left\|f-f^{\prime}\right\|_{L_{p}(\mathcal{D})}=\left[\mathbb{E}_{Z\sim\mathcal{D}}|f(Z)-f^{\prime}(Z)|^{p}\right]^{1/p}.\tag{3.19}
\]
It induces a pseudometric, denoted as \( d = L_{p}(\mathcal{D}) \), and the corresponding bracketing number is \( N_{\parallel}(\epsilon, \mathcal{G}, L_{p}(\mathcal{D})) \).
For \(p = \infty\), the \(L_{\infty}(\mathcal{D})\)-seminorm is defined as the essential supremum seminorm, which leads to the pseudometric
\[
d(f,f^{\prime})=\inf\left\{\omega:\Pr_{\mathcal{D}}[|f(Z)-f^{\prime}(Z)|\leq\omega]=1\right\}.
\]
However, when \( p = \infty \), instead of using the \( L_{\infty} \) bracketing number, it is more conventional to use the equivalent notion of \( L_{\infty} \) covering number (see Proposition 4.3).
